title: Leviticus 4:1–12
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 4:1–12 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 4:1–12 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 4:1–12 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

At the end of the book of Exodus, the storyteller told us that the Israelite people finished building the Tent of Meeting. At the beginning of the book of Leviticus, Yahweh meets with Moses in the Tent of Meeting to tell Moses the laws and instructions for the people of Israel. Yahweh wants to teach the Israelites how to live and how to be close to Yahweh. Yahweh's rules also show the Israelites what is important to Yahweh. So far in Leviticus, Yahweh gave laws and instructions on whole burnt offerings, grain offerings, and peace or fellowship offerings. Yahweh's instructions for the Israelites often teach the people how to be ritually clean and how not to get ritually dirty. Israelites need to be "clean" ritually and spiritually to worship Yahweh.

In Leviticus 4, Yahweh gives Moses instructions about sin or purification offerings. If an Israelite person was ritually dirty, that person needed to give a sin offering to become ritually clean again. Yahweh says that this offering is for Israelites who sinned accidentally, through a mistake or error. This mistake could happen in two different ways. An Israelite person might become ritually dirty because they touched or ate something that they did not know was ritually dirty. For example, Yahweh told the Israelite people what kinds of animal meat the people should eat. An Israelite person might become ritually dirty if they ate some cooked food, and later found out that the meat in the food was forbidden or ritually dirty. In other circumstances, an Israelite person might accidentally touch something that was ritually dirty. Then the Israelite person would become dirty too. For example, an Israelite man would know that he should not touch a dead body. But if a person died unexpectedly next to the Israelite man, the man might accidentally touch the dead body. In this case, the Israelite man did not want to become ritually dirty, but the man still became ritually dirty.

If an Israelite person did not know that what he did was wrong when he did it, then that person could give a sin or purification offering to become clean again. If an Israelite person knew inside himself, in his thoughts, that he was doing something wrong, then that person needed to give a guilt offering. A guilt offering was a bigger offering than a sin offering. We will hear about the guilt offering later. In this passage, Yahweh gave the Israelite people instructions for the sin or purification offering so that the people could become ritually clean, or pure, again. Because of this, we will call this offering the sin or purification offering.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Describe a time in your life when you only had good intentions, but you accidentally did something wrong anyway. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh has told Moses in the first chapters of Leviticus that some offerings are mandatory, which means the Israelite people must give these offerings. Yahweh also gave instructions about other offerings, such as the fellowship or peace offerings. An Israelite person could choose when they wanted to give a fellowship or peace offering. However, Yahweh commanded that the Israelite people must give the sin or purification offering. Yahweh commanded that the Israelite people give the sin or purification offering every time they became ritually dirty. To give a sin offering was the only way for an Israelite person to become ritually clean again.

Yahweh gives instructions on how a high priest should offer a sin or purification offering if he unintentionally sins. The high priest must give a young male bull for his offering. This is a big offering! In the next passage, we find that this offering is the same as the offering for the whole group of Israelites if they all sinned together. The offering for the high priest was the same as the one for the people of Israel because the high priest was a representative of the people to Yahweh. The young male bull was physically mature and old enough to reproduce, but still young. The high priest had to bring the young male bull to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, which was on the east side.

Stop here and look at a picture of the Tent of Meeting as a group. Discuss a process in your own culture where people have to follow special instructions in a specific order. Pause this audio here.

When the high priest needed to offer a sacrifice, the high priest had to bring the young male bull to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. There, the high priest would lay his hands on the head of the young male bull. We are not sure exactly why Yahweh commanded this, but it probably connected the high priest to the offering in a special way. The high priest would kill the young male bull and collect its blood. The high priest would take some of the blood in a bowl or pot and carry it into the Tent of Meeting.

Stop here and look at a picture of the Tent of Meeting as a group. Find the curtain of the sanctuary and the altar of fragrant incense. Pause this audio here.

The curtain of the sanctuary was a thick curtain. Yahweh commanded certain Israelite people to make the curtain of the sanctuary out of special woven threads. This curtain separated the area where the priests worked in the Tent of Meeting from the Holy of Holies, where Yahweh's presence lived on top of the ark of the covenant. The high priest would take the blood to the curtain of the sanctuary. The high priest would dip his finger into the blood and sprinkle or throw the blood in front of the curtain of the sanctuary seven times. The high priest would also smear the blood on the altar of incense. When a priest sprinkled the blood during a sin or purification offering, the blood symbolized that the dirty person was now clean and able to worship Yahweh again. Yahweh wanted the people of Israel to understand that sin makes humans ritually dirty and unable to worship Yahweh, even when people sin accidentally. But Yahweh gave the Israelite people the instructions for the sin offering so that they could become clean again and again. But Yahweh also wanted the Israelite people to know that in order to be ritually clean, they needed the blood of a sacrifice.

After putting the blood on the altar of fragrant incense, the high priest would go back outside. The high priest would pour out the rest of the bull's blood at the bottom of the bronze altar of burnt offering. Next, the high priest had to take certain body parts from the dead body of the young male bull. The high priest had to remove these body parts from the bull's dead body: the fat that covers the internal organs; the two kidneys, and the fat on the kidneys; the best part of the liver that is attached to the kidneys.

Stop here and look at pictures of the fat and the organs of the bull, the kidneys of the bull, and the liver of the bull as a group. Pause this audio here.

The high priest took all these parts of the bull's dead body and burned them on the altar of burnt offering. Then there is another list of all the rest of the bull's body that the high priest had to carry away: the hide or skin of the bull, the flesh or meat parts of the bull, the head of the bull, the legs of the bull, the internal organs of the bull, and the dung of the bull.

The high priest took all these parts of the bull's dead body that were not part of the offering on the altar and carried them away. The high priest took the bull's dead body to a ritually clean place where the priests would dump the ashes from sacrifices. There, the priest burned the bull's dead body on a wood fire. This place was outside the camp, away from the Tent of Meeting and the places where the Israelite people lived.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 4:1–12 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has three scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh is talking to Moses in the Tent of Meeting. Yahweh gives more instructions to Moses about how the Israelites should live. Yahweh tells Moses to tell the Israelites what Yahweh says. Yahweh tells Moses that an Israelite person who accidentally sins or becomes ritually dirty must offer a sin or purification offering.

In the second scene: Yahweh tells Moses what to do if a high priest accidentally sins. The high priest must lay his hands on a young bull. Then the high priest must kill the young bull and sprinkle the bull's blood in a special way. The high priest also must take certain pieces of the animal's dead body and burn them with fire on the altar.

In the third scene: The high priest must carry the rest of the dead bull's body to a clean place outside the camp and burn the body.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelite people
  • And the Israelite high priest

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

When the Israelite high priest offers a purification offering, the high priest will do different actions at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, the altar of burnt offering, the Tent of Meeting, the curtain of the sanctuary, and the altar of fragrant incense.

Stop here and look at a map of the Tent of Meeting. Trace the path that the high priest would walk while doing the offering. Point to the locations in this order: the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, the altar of the burnt offering, the Tent of Meeting, the curtain of the sanctuary, the altar of fragrant incense, and again the altar of the burnt offering. Describe how the priest walks from the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting inside to the Tent of Meeting and then walks back outside again. Pause the audio here.

In scene one, Yahweh speaks to Moses in the Tent of Meeting. Yahweh is still telling Moses the rules, laws, and instructions that the Israelites need to obey. This is the second time the storyteller uses this special phrase: "And Yahweh spoke to Moses and said, 'Speak to the sons of Israel and say....'" When a listener hears this phrase, the listener knows that everything that follows is what Yahweh told Moses and also what Moses told the Israelite people. The narrator uses this phrase over and over in Leviticus, so it may be helpful to have a special phrase in your language that introduces these instructions.

Stop here and, as an activity, have one person in the group tell another person in the group something important. After that, the second person should tell a new person the same words. What words would you use to re-tell someone else's words? Pause the audio here.

Yahweh gives Moses instructions about how to give purification offerings. Remember, an Israelite person gave a purification offering when that person accidentally became ritually dirty. Try to translate the term "purification offering" in a way so that listeners will understand that this offering was for accidental sin, error, or when a person became ritually dirty. You may want to use a phrase like "purity offering," or "cleaning offering," or another phrase that means that these offerings made people spiritually clean again.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What is the best way to translate "purification offering" in your language? Pause the audio here.

In scene two, Yahweh talks about the anointed priest. The high priest was the leading priest whom Yahweh specially anointed for the role, so sometimes the narrator calls the high priest the anointed priest. Yahweh explains what a high priest should do if the high priest accidentally disobeys one of Yahweh's rules, makes a mistake, or accidentally becomes ritually "dirty." Yahweh explains what the high priest must do to become ritually clean. The high priest needed to do this every time that the high priest accidentally sinned or became ritually "dirty."

Stop here and discuss: Think of a ritual, ceremony, or process that people in your culture do in a special way and in a certain order. Talk about those actions as if you were explaining them to someone who has never seen the ceremony before. Pause the audio here.

First, the high priest must select a young bull that is perfect, healthy, and strong. The high priest must lead this young male bull through the entrance of the courtyard to the altar of the burnt offering. When a person presents their offering in the place of worship, that person comes close, or comes near to, the place of worship. The person who offered the animal had to come close to Yahweh to offer the sacrifice. Yahweh's law said that the right place to give Yahweh an offering was at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

Stop and find the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and the altar of the burnt offering on the map. Pause the audio here.

There, the high priest must lay his hand on the head of the young male bull and kill it. The high priest also must then collect the blood from the dead animal's body in some sort of bowl or pot.

The high priest must carry the bowl with some of the blood into the Tent of Meeting. In the Tent of Meeting, the high priest will then walk to the curtain of the sanctuary.

Stop and find the Tent of Meeting, the curtain of the sanctuary, and the altar of fragrant incense on the map. Pause the audio here.

There, the high priest must dip his finger in the blood and splash or sprinkle the blood seven times in front of the curtain of the sanctuary. The high priest must also put some of the blood onto the horns of the altar of fragrant incense. Then the high priest should go back outside to the altar of the burnt offering.

Stop here and find the altar of the burnt offering on the map again. Pause audio here.

The high priest must pour out the rest of the young bull's blood at the bottom of the altar of the burnt offering. Then the high priest has to remove certain parts of the animal carcass. The high priest must remove all of the fat that covers and surrounds the internal organs of the bull, the two kidneys and the fat on them near the back part of the animal, and the best part of the liver.

The high priest must take all of these special pieces of the bull's dead body and burn them with fire on the altar of the burnt offering.

In scene three, the high priest should take the rest of the dead bull's body, including the bull's skin, the flesh, head, legs, the rest of the bull's internal organs, and the bull's dung. The high priest must carry all of the remaining dead body parts outside the camp to a special place that was ritually clean. There, the high priest must burn the dead body on a wood fire.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 4:1–12 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has three scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelite people
  • And the Israelite high priest

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language. Act out the high priest's actions as if he was following Yahweh's instructions.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

In scene one, Yahweh tells Moses to do offerings when someone sins accidentally.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Moses, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am happy and relieved that Yahweh made a plan for when we become unclean or ritually dirty; or
  • I realize that even when humans try to do good, we still make mistakes that make Yahweh unhappy.
Continue the drama.

In scene two, Yahweh gives special instructions about what a high priest must do if the high priest accidentally sins. The high priest must take a young bull and lay his hand on the head of the young bull. The high priest must kill the young bull. Then the high priest must gather the blood into a special bowl and take the blood into the Tent of Meeting. Inside, the high priest must dip his finger in the blood and splash it seven times in front of the curtain of the sanctuary. The high priest also must put some blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense. Then the high priest must go outside and pour out the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar of the burnt offering. Then the high priest has to cut out certain special parts of the insides of the bull carcass and burn them on the altar of the burnt offering.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the high priest, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I feel embarrassed to have to admit in front of everyone that I did something wrong; or
  • I am the spiritual leader of my people. If I make a mistake, it impacts all my people, too. That is a big responsibility!
Continue the drama.

In scene three, the high priest has to carry the rest of the bull's dead body through the camp to an area outside the camp.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing one of the people of Israel, "What are you feeling or thinking when you see the high priest carrying the bull's dead body out of the camp?" The person might answer things like:

  • I feel bad when I see the dead animal. When people sin, things have to die, like these animals! or
  • I am glad my spiritual leader is clean again; or
  • It is very serious when a person sins! or
  • Every sin, even accidental sin, makes us ritually dirty and keeps us from Yahweh.
Continue the drama.

The high priest must take the bull's body to a ceremonially clean place and burn it on a wood fire.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 4:1–12 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

Yahweh speaks to Moses. Use the same word for Yahweh as you used in previous passages. For more information on Yahweh, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh commands Moses to repeat these instructions to the people of Israel. Use the same word or phrase for people of Israel, or Israelite people, as you used in previous passages. For more information on Israelite, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh's laws tell a difference between when a person chooses to sin against Yahweh and when a person sins against Yahweh and does not know that they sinned. The offering in this passage was for a high priest who did an accidental sin. The high priest still sinned, but it was a lesser kind of sin since the high priest did not know that he had sinned and became ritually "dirty."

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for accidental sin. Look up sin in the Master Glossary for more information. Discuss how you might show the difference in your language between when a person purposefully sins and accidentally sins. Pause this audio here.

In this passage, Yahweh gives some of his special rules for the Israelite people to follow. These are Yahweh's commandments.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for commandment. Look up commandment in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

This passage talks specifically about what the high priest should do if he accidentally sins. The storyteller calls the high priest the "anointed priest," because this is the priest that Yahweh anoints, or chooses, to be the leader of all the priests and to make special sacrifices for the Israelite people. You may also simply call this priest the "high priest."

Stop here and discuss as a group: What word or phrase will you use for anointed priest or high priest? For more information on anoint, priest, and high priest, refer to the Master Glossary. Pause this audio here.

When the anointed priest or high priest sins, the high priest brings guilt on the people. Remember that when someone sins against Yahweh or disobeys Yahweh, that person becomes guilty. In other words, that person is no longer in a right relationship with Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for guilt. See the Master Glossary for more information about guilt. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

The high priest must offer a young bull. This word refers to a male animal that is physically mature and able to reproduce. Use the same word for bull as you used in previous passages.

The high priest offers the bull as a sin or purification offering. This offering makes someone pure after they have become ritually dirty or unfit for service to God. In previous passages, you have words like "burnt offering" and "fellowship or peace offering." Remember that this is the "accidental sin offering," so you might want to use your word for "accidental sin" in this passage rather than your regular word for "sin." Or you may want to use a phrase like purification offering or purity offering that reminds listeners that the Israelite people made this offering to become ritually clean.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for sin or purification offering. Look up "sin or purification offering" in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

The high priest presents his offering at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. Use the same word or phrase to describe the person coming close to the Tent of Meeting as you have used in previous passages.

The high priest takes the blood into the Tent of Meeting to the Holy Place or the sanctuary. Yahweh only allowed priests to go inside the Tent of Meeting. Use the same word or phrase for the Tent of Meeting as you used in previous passages. For more information on the Tent of Meeting, refer to "tabernacle" in the Master Glossary.

The high priest uses a bowl or pot, a special container, to carry the blood into the Tent of Meeting. The narrator does not mention this bowl in the passage, so we do not know what kind of bowl this is. But you can include this bowl if it is helpful in your language to describe how the high priest carried the blood.

Stop here and look at a picture of a bowl as a group. Pause this audio here.

The high priest has to put his finger into the blood so the high priest can sprinkle or throw the blood of the sacrifice in certain places. The high priest carefully uses his fingers to make the blood fall on certain places.

Stop here and get a bowl of water. Have someone put their finger or hand in the water and then hold their wet finger over an object so the water falls from their finger onto the object. Talk about what words you would use to explain the actions of when the priest dips or puts his finger in the blood, and when the high priest sprinkles the blood. You may use the same word you used in Leviticus 1 for throwing the blood. Pause the audio here.

The high priest sprinkles the blood in front of the curtain of the sanctuary. The word sanctuary means a holy place. The curtain of the sanctuary was a thick piece of woven fabric that hung in the Tent of the Meeting, between the Holy Place and the Holy of Holies, where Yahweh's covenant ark was. The curtain protected the priests from Yahweh's power and glory.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for the curtain of the sanctuary. See the Master Glossary for more information about sanctuary. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

The high priest smears some blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant or sweet incense. The high priest would pour the rest of the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offerings. Use the same phrase for the altar of burnt offerings as you used in previous passages. For more information on altar and burnt offerings, refer to the Master Glossary.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for the horns of the altar of fragrant incense. You may look at the picture of the altar of fragrant incense again. This altar is in the first room of the tabernacle. This altar is the place where the priests burn incense for Yahweh. Pause this audio here.

The high priest removes the fat from the internal organs, the kidney and its fat, and the best part of the liver. Use the same words and phrases for these parts of the bull as you have used in previous passages. The high priest removes this fat just like he does from the sacrifice of the peace or fellowship offering. Use the same words or phrases for sacrifice and peace or fellowship offering as you have used previously, and refer to the Master Glossary for more information about these words.

The high priest burns parts of the bull's body, then takes the rest of the bull's body to the place "where people throw the ashes out." Earlier, in Leviticus 1, Yahweh talks about a place "where the fat ashes go" beside the altar. These two places are not the same. The place in Leviticus 1 was near the altar. In this passage, Yahweh mentions a place "where people throw the ashes out" that was not in the Israelite camp. It was in a ritually clean place. In the Bible, a clean place means a place that is fit for service to God. But this place was not close to the Tent of Meeting, and it was not close to places where the Israelite people lived.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for the place where people throw out ashes. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for clean or ritually clean. See the Master Glossary for more information about clean. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 4:13–26
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 4:13–26 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 4:13–26 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 4:13–26 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In Leviticus chapter 4, Yahweh gives Moses instructions for offerings for accidental sins or ways people accidentally become ritually dirty. The Israelites could learn about Yahweh and about sin by understanding what Yahweh wanted and what was important to Yahweh. Rules about accidental sins remind us that even when people want to do good things, people still disappoint Yahweh sometimes. Yahweh said that the Israelites had to be ritually clean to be close to Yahweh and have a relationship with Yahweh. But Yahweh chose not to punish the Israelites for their sin and ritual dirtiness. Instead, Yahweh made a way for the Israelite people to become clean again. When the Israelite people did not have a good relationship with Yahweh, Yahweh made a way for the Israelite people to come close to Yahweh again.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Describe a time when you felt like you did not have a good relationship with a close relative. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh required that all the animals for the offering were perfect. The animals must be healthy and strong, not missing body parts or hurt badly. Yahweh did not want the Israelite people to give Yahweh the animals that no one wanted. The Israelite people showed Yahweh that the Israelites were really sorry when they gave Yahweh their best animals.

In Leviticus 4, Yahweh required that an Israelite person give a sin or purification offering after the person realized that they had sinned. In this passage, Yahweh gives instructions for how to do a purification offering to clean all the Israelite people as a whole group. The instructions for the purification offering for all the people of Israel are almost the same as the instructions for the purification offering for the high priest. Why was this the case? The high priest represented all of Israel to Yahweh. So these two purification offerings were the biggest purification offerings. For these offerings, Yahweh required a young bull that was healthy, strong, and whole.

In this passage, the elders or leaders of the Israelites are the ones who must give the purification offering for all of Israel. The elders are the men whom people respected because these men were wise, experienced, and older. These men made important decisions for the whole community and represented different families. Because these men were often older men, people called these leaders the elders.

Stop here and discuss: Who are the spiritual leaders in your community? Describe the responsibilities these people have for the whole community. How is your spiritual leaders' work similar to the Israelite elders' work? How is their work different? Pause the audio here.

The elders or leaders of Israel would lead the young bull to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting in front of the altar of burnt offering. There, the leaders would lay their hands on the head of the young bull. Then a person would kill the bull. We do not know exactly who killed the bull, but it was probably one of the Israelite elders.

The high priest would carry some of the blood in a bowl from the bull into the Tent of Meeting. There, the high priest would sprinkle or throw the blood in front of the curtain of the sanctuary seven times. The high priest would also put some blood on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense. The altars for the Tent of Meeting had points on their corners, which people called horns.

Stop here and look at a picture of the altar of fragrant incense. Find the horns on the altar. Pause this audio here.

After the high priest put the blood on the altar of fragrant incense, the high priest would go back outside. The high priest would pour out the rest of the bull's blood at the bottom of the altar of burnt offering. Next, the high priest had to take the fat from the bull and follow the same process that the high priest would do for his own purification offering. So the high priest must take the fat that covers the internal organs, the two kidneys, the fat on the kidneys, and the best part of the liver.

The high priest took all these parts of the bull's dead body and burned them on the altar of burnt offering. In this way, the high priest made atonement for the people. Remember that atonement makes people clean and restores their relationship with Yahweh. Then Yahweh would forgive the people who had accidentally sinned.

Then the high priest would take all the parts of the bull's dead body that the high priest did not burn on the altar and carry those parts away. The high priest took the rest of the bull's dead body to a ritually clean place where the priests could dump the ashes of the Tent of Meeting. There, the high priest burned the rest of the bull's dead body on a wood fire.

Next, Yahweh gives instructions for the purification offering for a tribal leader of Israel who accidentally sins or becomes ritually dirty. The Israelite tribal leader who accidentally sins must bring a young male goat for his purification offering. This goat must also be perfect, healthy, and strong.

Stop here and look at a picture of a young male goat as a group. Pause this audio here.

The Israelite tribal leader must bring the young male goat to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. The Israelite leader had to lay his hand on the head of the goat in front of the altar of burnt offering. Then the leader had to kill the goat.

The priest who was helping with the offering would take the goat's blood and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering. The priest would then pour the rest of the goat's blood out at the bottom of the altar of burnt offering.

Stop here and look at a picture of the altar of burnt offering. Find the horns on the altar. Talk about where the priest would pour the goat's blood. Pause this audio here.

The priest had to take the fat from the goat and follow the same process that the priest would do for a fellowship offering. So the priest had to take the fat that covers the internal organs, the two kidneys, the fat on the kidneys, and the best part of the liver. The priest would burn all of these parts of the goat on the altar of burnt offering in order to make atonement for the tribal leader. Then Yahweh would forgive the leader who had accidentally sinned.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 4:13–26 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has two scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh gives Moses instructions for how to do a sin or purification offering for all the people of Israel if the whole community accidentally sins.

In the second scene: Yahweh gives Moses instructions for how to do a purification offering if a leader of the Israelite people accidentally sins.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • All of the Israelite people, which is the whole community
  • The Israelite elders
  • The Israelite high priest
  • The Israelite tribal leaders
  • And an Israelite priest

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

The people should follow Yahweh's instructions at the same places as in the last few passages: at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, the altar of the burnt offering, the Tent of Meeting, the curtain of the sanctuary, the altar of fragrant incense, and a ceremonially clean place outside the camp where the priests dump ashes.

Stop here and look at a map of the Tent of Meeting. Pick locations in your space to represent the different locations. For example, if someone is representing Yahweh, that person may stand in the Holy of Holies. Pause the audio here.

In this passage, you might hear the narrator mention two different words: "congregation" and "assembly." The narrator uses the word congregation, or community, to refer to the whole group of Israelite people. Sometimes this word refers to the representatives or leaders of the whole group of Israelites who act on behalf of the Israelite people and make decisions for the Israelite people. The word assembly refers to a smaller group of people who performed religious duties for the Israelite people. The assembly was likely the elders of the Israelite people and prominent religious leaders.

Stop here and discuss: In your language, what words do you use to refer to whole groups of people? Do you have any way to refer to a group of people who are representatives who make decisions for the whole group? Pause the audio here.

Scene one answers an important question: What happens if all the people of Israel accidentally become ritually "dirty" by sinning or making a mistake? How can the whole group of Israelites become clean again? This passage explains what the Israelite people must do to become clean again as a whole group.

Stop here and discuss: In your culture, what happens when your entire community sins against God or your gods? What kinds of things do your people do all together against God? What happens to the people when they sin like that? Pause the audio here.

When the Israelite community realizes that the community has sinned, the Israelite elders must offer a purification offering on behalf of all the Israelite people. These leaders must bring a young bull to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and lay their hands on the bull's head.

Then someone, probably one of the Israelite elders, would kill the young bull. The high priest would collect the bull's blood, probably in a bowl or a pot, and carry the blood into the Tent of Meeting. The narrator calls the high priest the "anointed priest" here because this is the special priest that Yahweh has chosen to lead the Israelite people.

The high priest stands before the curtain of the sanctuary, dips his finger in the blood, and sprinkles it seven times before the curtain of the sanctuary. The high priest also takes some blood and puts it on the horns of the altar of fragrant incense. Then the high priest goes back outside.

The high priest pours the rest of the bull's blood at the bottom of the altar of burnt offering. Then Yahweh says that the high priest must remove all the fat from the bull and burn it on the altar, and follow the same process that the high priest would do for his own purification offering. This means that the high priest would first remove all that fat that covers and surrounds the internal organs of the bull. These internal organs were probably the stomach and the intestines. Then the high priest would also remove the two kidneys, the fat on the kidneys, and the best part of the liver. The high priest would then burn all these pieces on the altar of the burnt offering.

To do this, the priest would arrange these pieces of the bull's body on top of the wood that was on the altar. Finally, the priest was supposed to burn these parts of the bull on the altar with fire. In this way, the priest makes atonement for the people. Then Yahweh forgives the people of Israel for their accidental sin.

Then the high priest takes the rest of the bull's dead body, including the bull's skin, flesh, head, legs, the rest of the bull's internal organs, and the bull's dung outside the camp. Then the high priest would burn these pieces of the bull just like the high priest burned the bull for the high priest's purification offering. That means the high priest would burn those pieces on a wood fire in a ritually clean place where the priests put the ashes.

Scene two answers an important question: What if a leader of the Israelites sins accidentally? The leader of the Israelites who sins accidentally must bring a male goat as a purification offering. The narrator says the Israelite leader should lay his hand on the goat's head and kill it at the place where people kill animals for the burnt offering. This is at the same place as for the purification offering for the Israelites. So the Israelite leader brings the male goat to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting by the altar of the burnt offering. There, the leader puts his hand on the goat's head and then kills the goat. Then an Israelite priest dips his own finger into the goat's blood and puts the blood on the horns of the altar of the burnt offering. The priest pours out the rest of the goat's blood at the bottom of the altar of burnt offering.

Yahweh says that the priest must burn all of the goat's fat on the altar and follow the same process that the priest would do for a fellowship offering. This means that the priest would first remove all the fat that covers and surrounds the internal organs of the goat. These internal organs were probably the stomach and the intestines. Then the priest would also remove the two kidneys, the fat on the kidneys, and the best part of the liver. The priest would then burn all these pieces on the altar of the burnt offering.

To do this, the priest would arrange these animal body parts or inside organs on top of the wood that was on the altar. Finally, the priest was then supposed to burn these animal body parts on the altar with fire. In this way, the priest makes atonement for the leader. Then Yahweh forgives the Israelite leader for his accidental sin.

Stop here and discuss: Talk about the purification offering for all the people of Israel and the purification offering for an Israelite leader. How are the two offerings the same? How are the two offerings different? Pause the audio here.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it. Pay special attention to which person does each action.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 4:13–26 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has two scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • All of the Israelite people, which is the whole community
  • The Israelite elders
  • The Israelite high priest
  • The Israelite tribal leaders
  • And an Israelite priest

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

In the first scene, Yahweh gives instructions for what to do when the whole community of Israelites accidentally sins or becomes ritually dirty. When the people of Israel realize that the community has sinned, the leaders of the Israelites must offer a purification offering of a young bull.

Pause the drama.

Ask all the people playing Israelite people, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am glad I am not the one who has to offer the sacrifice; or
  • I am sad that we did something that makes Yahweh angry; or
  • Those other people did the bad thing, not me! or
  • I realize that even when humans try to do good, we still make mistakes that make Yahweh unhappy.
Continue the drama.

The leaders of the Israelites bring a young bull to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. The leaders of the Israelites put their hands on the head of the young bull. Then one of the leaders of the Israelites kills the young bull. The high priest takes some of the bull's blood into the Tent of Meeting. The high priest dips his finger in the blood and sprinkles it seven times in front of the curtain of the sanctuary. The high priest also puts some of the blood onto the horns on the altar of fragrant incense. Then the high priest goes back outside.

The high priest pours the rest of the bull's blood at the bottom of the altar of burnt offering. Then the high priest has to remove and burn the fat from the bull on the altar in the same way that the high priest would do for the high priest's purification offering. This is how the high priest makes atonement for the Israelites, and Yahweh forgives the Israelites for their accidental sin.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am happy that my people are ritually clean again; or
  • I was sad that my people were not in close relationship with me, but now I am happy that my people have a good relationship with me again.
Continue the drama.

Then the high priest would take the rest of the bull's dead body outside the camp and burn it just like the high priest burned the bull for the high priest's purification offering. This is how the high priest offers a purification offering for the community.

In scene two, Yahweh gives instructions on what to do if a leader of the Israelites accidentally sins. When the Israelite leader realizes he has sinned, that leader must bring a male goat as a purification offering. The male goat must be perfect. The leader brings the male goat through the entrance of the Tent of Meeting to the altar of the burnt offering. There, the leader puts his hand on the goat's head and then kills the goat as a purification offering. Then an Israelite priest dips his own finger into the goat's blood and puts the blood on the horns of the altar of the burnt offering. The priest pours out the rest of the goat's blood at the bottom of the altar of burnt offering.

Then the priest has to remove and burn the fat from the goat on the altar in the same way that the priest would do for a fellowship offering. This is how the priest makes atonement for the Israelite leader, and Yahweh forgives the Israelite leader for his accidental sin.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 4:13–26 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

In this passage, the whole Israelite community may accidentally sin and need to give an offering to become clean again. The Israelites realize that the Israelites are guilty. The narrator uses two words, "congregation" and "assembly," to refer to all the people of Israel as a whole. The word "congregation" refers to the Israelite people as a whole, but could also refer to a smaller group of Israelite people whose actions impacted the whole community. The word "assembly" often refers to a smaller group of Israelite people, most likely the elders and important religious people. These leaders did religious ceremonies and made important decisions on behalf of all of the Israelites. For more information on Israelite, guilt, and sin, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same words or phrases for Israelite, guilt, and accidental sin as you have used before.

Stop here and discuss as a group different ways to refer to "the people of Israel" in this passage. Discuss how to refer to them in a way that emphasizes them as a group. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh talks about what the Israelites should do if the Israelites do not obey Yahweh's commandments. Use the same word for Yahweh and commandment as you used in previous passages. For more information on Yahweh and commandment, refer to the Master Glossary.

In this passage, the elders or leaders of the Israelites must give the purification offering for all of Israel. These are the men whom people deeply respected because of those men's age and experience. These leaders made important decisions for the whole community and represented different families. People often called these leaders elders because these men were usually old men.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for elder. Look up elder in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

The elders give the purification offering for all of Israel. Use the same phrase for sin or purification offering as you used in previous passages. Remember that this is the "accidental sin offering," so use your word for "accidental sin" in this passage rather than your regular word for "sin." For more information, refer to sin or purification offering in the Master Glossary.

The elders bring a bull to the Tent of Meeting. Use the same words for bull and for Tent of Meeting as you used in previous passages. For more information on the Tent of Meeting, refer to tabernacle in the Master Glossary.

Remember the way you have talked about the people coming close to the place of worship when people present the animal to Yahweh to kill it. Talk about that in the same way here as you did in previous passages. Also, talk about killing an animal in the same way you have in previous passages.

During the purification offering for the whole community of Israel, the high priest takes the blood of the dead bull into the Tent of Meeting. The narrator calls the high priest the "anointed priest," because this is the priest that Yahweh specially anoints, or chooses, to be the leader of all the priests and to make special sacrifices for the Israelite people. Use the same words or phrases for anoint and high priest as you have previously, and remember that anoint and high priest are in the Master Glossary.

The high priest uses a bowl or pot, a special container, to carry the blood into the Tent of Meeting. The narrator does not mention this bowl in the passage, but you can include it if it is helpful in your language to describe how the priest carried the blood. Use the same word for bowl or pot as you used in previous passages.

The high priest has to dip or put his finger into the blood so the high priest can sprinkle it. Use the same word or phrase for dip as you used in previous passages.

The high priest would sprinkle the blood of the sacrificed animal in front of the curtain of the sanctuary. Use the same word or phrase for sprinkle and "curtain of the sanctuary" as you used in previous passages. Look at sanctuary in the Master Glossary for more information.

The high priest would put some blood on the altar of fragrant incense. The high priest would pour the rest of the blood at the base of the altar of burnt offerings. Use the same phrases for the altar of fragrant incense and the altar of burnt offerings as you used in previous passages. For more information on altar and burnt offering, refer to the Master Glossary.

The high priest makes atonement for the sins of the people when the high priest burns the bull's body on the altar. In this way, the people become ritually clean from their sin because Yahweh forgives the people for their sin. When you forgive someone who has done something bad to you, you stop being angry with that person. You no longer want to take revenge or to give punishment. So people's relationship with Yahweh is right again. See the Master Glossary for more information about atonement, and translate this in the same way as you have previously.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for forgive. Look up forgive in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

If an Israelite leader sinned, the leader must bring a male goat for a purification offering. This male goat must be physically perfect. That meant that the animal had no physical defects. The animal must not be blind or deformed or have any bruises or injuries. The animal must not have any kind of skin disease or be missing any body part. Use the same words for male goat and perfect that you used in previous passages. For more information on perfect, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh says a priest will help the Israelite leader with the purification offering. This would not be the high priest, but one of the other priests. Use the same word for priest that you used in previous passages. For more information on priest, refer to the Master Glossary.

For the Israelite leader's purification offering, the priest removes and burns the goat's fat, just like the priest did for the sacrifice of the fellowship offerings. Use the same words for sacrifice and fellowship or peace offering as you used in previous passages. For more information on sacrifice and fellowship offerings, refer to the Master Glossary.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 4:27–35
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 4:27–35 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 4:27–35 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 4:27–35 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In Leviticus 4, Yahweh is giving Moses instructions about the different kinds of accidental sin or purification offerings. This passage gives instructions for purification offerings for all the rest of the Israelite people. Any person who was not a priest or a leader would follow these instructions to become ritually clean again.

In this passage, an Israelite can bring a young female goat or a young female sheep for a purification offering. The instructions for both offerings are almost the same, just with a different kind of animal.

Stop here and look at a picture of a young female goat and a young female sheep as a group. Pause this audio here.

When an Israelite person picks an animal to sacrifice, that animal needs to be a healthy animal that has no physical defects. The animal must not be blind or deformed or have any bruises or injuries. The animal must not have any kind of skin disease or be missing any body part. The animal has to be physically perfect. This is true for all the sin offerings. Yahweh requires the best animals and crops for the offerings. This is one of the ways that the Israelite people honored Yahweh.

One difference between offering a young female goat and offering a young female sheep is that the special parts that the priest would burn as a fat offering are slightly different. The priest would burn the same parts of sheep that the priest would burn for the fellowship offering. We know from Leviticus 3:9 that when someone offered a sheep for a fellowship offering, the priest had to include the fatty tail. So the priest would have to include the tail for the purification offering also.

This is what Yahweh says an Israelite must do for a purification offering. The Israelite person who accidentally sinned must bring a healthy young female goat or a young female sheep through the courtyard entrance from the east into the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting. The Israelite person must put their hand on the head of the animal, then kill the animal at the altar of burnt offering. An Israelite priest must put some of the animal's blood on the horns of the altar of burnt offering and then pour out the rest of the blood at the bottom of the altar of burnt offering.

Then the priest must remove certain body parts from the dead animal's body, just like the priest does for a fellowship offering. If the Israelite was offering a sheep, the priest would need to also remove the tail. The priest burns those body parts on the altar of burnt offering. When the offering is burning, it is a pleasing smell to Yahweh. This is how the priest makes atonement for the Israelite person's sin. Remember that atonement makes people clean and restores their relationship with Yahweh. And Yahweh forgives the Israelite person for the accidental sin.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What is different about the purification offerings in this passage compared to the other purification offerings? What is the same?

Yahweh gave the Israelites rules for the purification offerings to help the Israelites become ritually clean from sin. Yahweh wanted the Israelites to understand that sin makes people ritually or spiritually dirty. When people are ritually dirty, those people are not fit to worship Yahweh. When a person sinned, that person could not hide the sin from Yahweh. A person could only become ritually clean again if the person made the right offering. The priest would put the blood of the offering on the horns of the altar to atone, or to cover, the person's sin. When the priest put the blood on the horns of the altar, an Israelite person might remember the story in Exodus, when Yahweh passed over the houses that had blood on the doorposts. Yahweh was teaching the Israelites a pattern and a truth. This is the truth: something must die in order for the person to have a good relationship with Yahweh again.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 4:27–35 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has two scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh gives instructions to Moses about how an Israelite person could bring a young female goat as an accidental sin or purification offering.

In the second scene: Yahweh gives instructions to Moses about how an Israelite person could bring a young female sheep as a purification offering.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • An Israelite person who accidentally sinned
  • And an Israelite priest

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

The people should follow Yahweh's instructions at the same places as in the last few passages: at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting and the altar of the burnt offering.

Stop here and look at a diagram of the Tent of Meeting. Pause the audio here.

This passage answers an important question: What happens if one person accidentally becomes ritually "dirty" by sinning or making a mistake? How can the person be clean again? Yahweh explains in this passage what the Israelite person must do to become ritually clean again. The Israelite person can offer a young female goat or a young female lamb as a purification offering.

In scene one, an Israelite person has learned that they have accidentally sinned or become ritually "dirty." So the Israelite person must bring a young female goat to the Tent of Meeting. The storyteller says the Israelite person should lay their hand on the goat's head and kill it at the place where people kill animals for the burnt offering. This is at the same place as for the other purification offering for the Israelites. So the Israelite person should bring the female goat to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting by the altar of the burnt offering. There, the Israelite person must put their hand on the head of the young female goat. Then the Israelite person must kill the young female goat.

An Israelite priest must then dip his own finger into the young female goat's blood and put the blood on the horns of the altar of the burnt offering. The priest pours out the rest of the goat's blood at the bottom of the altar of burnt offering.

Then the storyteller says that the priest will remove all of the goat's fat in the same way that a priest would for a fellowship offering. This means the priest would first remove all the fat that covers and surrounds the goat's internal organs. These internal organs were probably the stomach and the intestines. Then the priest would also remove the two kidneys, the fat on the kidneys, and the best part of the liver.

The priest takes all of these special pieces of the goat's dead body and burns the special pieces with fire on the altar of the burnt offering. This smell pleases Yahweh. This is how the priest makes atonement for the Israelite person's accidental sin. Yahweh forgives the Israelite person, and the person becomes ritually clean again.

In scene two, the process is the same, but this time the Israelite person brings a young female sheep for the sin offering.

Stop here and discuss: When someone tells a story in your language, how do you repeat information? If you are describing a process that is the same as a process you recently described, do you repeat all the details of the process, or do you have a special way to talk about repeated processes? What information do you choose not to repeat? Are there any special phrases that will help your listeners understand? Pause the audio here.

In scene two, an Israelite person has learned that they have accidentally sinned or become ritually "dirty." Again, the Israelite person brings the animal to the same place as for a fellowship offering, so the Israelite takes the young female sheep to the altar of burnt offering. The Israelite person puts their hand on the head of the young female sheep. Then the Israelite kills the young female sheep.

An Israelite priest dips his own finger into the young female sheep's blood and puts the blood on the horns of the altar of the burnt offering. The priest pours out the rest of the sheep's blood at the bottom of the altar of burnt offering.

Again, the priest has to remove the same parts of the sheep's dead body as a priest would for a fellowship offering. This is the sheep's tail, the fat that covers and surrounds the internal organs of the sheep, the two kidneys and the fat on them, and the best part of the liver.

The priest takes all of these special pieces and burns the special pieces with fire on the altar of the burnt offering. Yahweh says the priest needs to put those parts on the other fire offerings on the altar. This is how the priest makes atonement for the Israelite person's accidental sin. Yahweh forgives the Israelite person's accidental sin, so that person becomes ritually clean again.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 4:27–35 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has two scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • An Israelite person who accidentally sinned
  • And an Israelite priest

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

In scene one, Yahweh tells Moses what an Israelite person should do when the Israelite person has accidentally sinned and become ritually dirty.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am sad because I know that that person did not want to become dirty; or
  • I want the person to be clean again so they can have a good relationship with me again.

Ask the person playing the Israelite person who sinned, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I feel shame about what people will think of me; or
  • I am worried because my sin keeps me from Yahweh; or
  • I want to be ritually clean again!
Continue the drama.

The Israelite should bring a young female goat to the altar of the burnt offering. The Israelite should lay their hand on the goat and then kill the goat. The priest should take some of the dead goat's blood and should put the blood on the horns of the altar of burnt offering.

The priest must remove the fat in the same way that the priest would for a fellowship offering.

The priest takes all of these special pieces of the goat's dead body and burns the special pieces with fire on the altar of the burnt offering. Yahweh considered the smoke from this fire to be a pleasing aroma.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the Israelite who accidentally sinned, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • There is so much blood; or
  • I do not understand why this is what Yahweh wants; or
  • I know I need to do this to be clean again, but I wish there was something else I could do.
Continue the drama.

This is how the priest makes atonement for the Israelite person's accidental sin. Yahweh will forgive the Israelite person's unintentional sin, and the ritually dirty Israelite will be clean again.

In scene two, Yahweh gives instructions for an Israelite person when they offer a young female sheep as a purification offering. The Israelite person should get a young female sheep and bring the sheep to the altar of the burnt offering. The Israelite person should lay their hand on the sheep and then kill the sheep. A priest should take some of the dead sheep's blood and put the blood on the horns of the altar of burnt offering.

The priest must remove the fat in the same way that the priest would for a fellowship offering.

The priest should take all of these special pieces of the sheep's dead body and burn the special pieces with fire on the altar of the burnt offering on the other fire offerings. This is how the priest will make atonement for the Israelite person's accidental sin. Yahweh will forgive the Israelite person's unintentional sin, and the ritually dirty Israelite person will be clean again.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 4:27–35 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

In this passage, a member of the Israelite people may accidentally sin and need to give an offering to become clean again. The Israelite realizes that the Israelite is guilty. Use the same words for accidental sin and for guilt as you used in previous passages. Remember that this is about the "accidental sin offering," so if you have a word for "accidental sin," use that word in this passage rather than your regular word for "sin." For more information about sin and guilt, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh talks about what the Israelites should do if the Israelites do not obey Yahweh's commandments. Use the same word for Yahweh and commandment as you used in previous passages. For more information on Yahweh and commandment, refer to the Master Glossary.

Remember the way you have talked about the people coming close to the place of worship when people present the animal to Yahweh to kill the animal. Talk about that and about killing an animal in the same way here as you did in previous passages.

In this passage, the Israelite person has the option to bring a young female goat for a sin offering. Think of the word you used for goat in previous passages. But notice that the word you used before was for a male goat. If possible, use a word for goat here that means a female goat.

Stop here and discuss as a group the best way to say "female goat" in your language. Pause this audio here.

In this passage, Yahweh gives instructions for sin or purification offerings, which are offerings for Israelite people to offer when a person accidentally sins or becomes ritually dirty. Use the same phrase for purification offering as you used in previous passages. For more information on purification offering, refer to the Master Glossary.

The priest would sacrifice animals for the purification offering on the altar of burnt offering. Use the same word for "altar of burnt offering" as you used in previous passages. For more information on "altar" and "burnt offering," refer to the Master Glossary.

The priest would put the blood from the dead animal on the horns of the altar. Use the same word for horn, as in "the horn of the altar," as you used in previous passages. For more information on priest, refer to the Master Glossary.

When the priest burns the parts of the goat on the altar of burnt offering, it will be a pleasing smell to Yahweh. Use the same phrase for "a pleasing smell to Yahweh" as you have used previously.

The priest will make atonement for the people, and Yahweh will forgive the people. Use the same words or phrases for atonement and for forgive as you used in previous passages. For more information about atonement and forgiveness, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh compares the process for making a purification offering to making a sacrifice for the peace or fellowship offering. Use the same word for sacrifice and fellowship offering as you used in previous passages. Refer to peace or fellowship offering in the Master Glossary for more information.

In this passage, the Israelite person has the option to bring a young female lamb for a sin offering. Think of the word you used for lamb in previous passages. But notice that the word you used before was for a male lamb. If possible, use a word for lamb here that means a female lamb.

Stop here and discuss as a group the best way to say "female lamb" in your language.

The priest will burn the parts of the lamb on top of the other fire offerings. Use the same word or phrase for fire offerings as you have used previously. For more information, refer to fire offerings in the Master Glossary.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.
