title: Leviticus 7:28–28
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 7:28–38 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 7:28–38 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 7:28–38 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this story, Yahweh tells Moses to tell all the Israelites more instructions about the peace or fellowship offering. Just like people sometimes eat together to show their good relationship with one another, the Israelites are supposed to eat most of the fellowship offering to show the Israelites' good relationship with Yahweh. However, there are parts of the animal that the Israelites do not eat. Those are the parts that Yahweh is talking about in this story.

When the Israelites bring a fellowship offering, the Israelites need to bring the offering with their own hands. This means that an Israelite cannot send someone else to give the animal instead of the Israelite. It is important that an Israelite personally bring the offering that the Israelite wants to give to Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: When you need to do something important, do you do it yourself or do you send someone else to do it? Why do you do it like that? Pause this audio here.

The Israelites are supposed to give the fat and the meat from the animal's breast to Yahweh.

Stop here and look at a picture of an animal's breast meat and a picture of an animal with the breast area circled. Pause this audio here.

The Israelites give the meat to Yahweh with a wave offering. A wave offering was a specific way to give an offering to Yahweh, just like burning up the meat on the altar was a specific way to give an offering to Yahweh. For a wave offering, the priest would wave the meat back and forth in the air in front of Yahweh to show that the meat belonged to Yahweh now.

Stop here and look at a picture of a priest making a wave offering. Pause this audio here.

After the priest finishes with the wave offering, the priest would burn up the fat on the altar. Aaron and Aaron's sons would get to cook and eat the animal's breast meat. It is important to remember that Aaron and Aaron's sons are supposed to be Israel's priests, so all of the priests can eat the animal's breast meat.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What jobs does your community have that belong to specific families forever? Pause this audio here.

The other piece of meat that belongs to the priests is the animal's right thigh. The thigh is the top half of the animal's leg. The Israelites thought that the right side of the body was better than the left side of the body, so the right thigh was a more important piece of meat.

Stop here and look at a picture of thigh meat and a picture of an animal with a right thigh circled. Pause this audio here.

The Israelite who makes the offering should give the right thigh to the priest who kills the animal, burns the animal fat on the altar, and sprinkles the animal's blood on the altar. It is a specific gift for the priest who helps offer the fellowship offering. All the priests may eat the breast meat, but only the priest who sacrifices the animal can eat the right thigh meat. The Israelites thought that the breast meat and thigh meat were the tastiest meat of the animal.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What meat does your community think is the tastiest meat? Who is allowed to eat that meat in your community? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that Yahweh is giving the breast meat that the offeror gave to Yahweh with a wave offering and the thigh meat to the priests. The Israelites give the fellowship offering to Yahweh, and Yahweh gives the right thigh and the breast meat to the priests. Aaron, Aaron's sons, and the sons' descendants can eat that meat every time an Israelite gives Yahweh a fellowship offering forever.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Who in your community gets special gifts or honor? Are these people whole families or individuals? Why do those people get those gifts or honor? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh made this rule about what meat the Israelites need to give Aaron and Aaron's descendants on the same day that Yahweh made Aaron and Aaron's descendants into Yahweh's priests. When Yahweh officially made Aaron and Aaron's descendants into priests, Yahweh also told the Israelites to give the priests the right thigh and the breast of the animal every time the Israelites make a fellowship offering. This rule is supposed to last forever.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What are some rules in your community that it is important for everyone to follow forever? Pause this audio here.

The story ends with a summary. The story says that all these laws tell what the Israelites and the priests must do when the Israelites offer a burnt offering, a grain offering, a purification offering, a guilt offering, an ordination offering, or a fellowship offering. The Israelites made ordination offerings when Yahweh appointed new priests. Yahweh gave all the rules for all of these offerings to Moses at Mount Sinai in the Wilderness of Sinai. Yahweh told Moses all these rules on the same day that Yahweh told the Israelites to bring offerings to Yahweh.

Stop here and look at a picture of Mount Sinai and the Wilderness of Sinai as a group.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 7:28–38 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has three scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh gives Moses more instructions about the peace or fellowship offering. Yahweh explains how the Israelites are supposed to give the priests the meat that the priests may eat.

In the second scene: The story explains that Yahweh gave the instructions that the priests should receive specific kinds of meat on the same day that Aaron and Aaron's sons officially became Yahweh's priests.

In the third scene: The storyteller summarizes all the kinds of offerings that Yahweh told Moses about on Mount Sinai.

The characters in this passage are:

  • The storyteller
  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelites
  • Aaron
  • Aaron's sons
  • All of Aaron's descendants
  • And the specific priest who sacrifices the fellowship offering

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

In the first scene, Yahweh gives Moses more instructions to tell all the Israelites. Yahweh is not speaking directly to all the Israelites, but Yahweh is telling Moses what to do so that Moses can tell the other Israelites. These instructions are different from the last instructions. It is important to remember that the last instructions were about the food that Yahweh does not allow the Israelites to eat. This time, Yahweh is giving the Israelites more instructions about the fellowship offering.

It is important to remember that the Israelites eat most of the fellowship offering. When Yahweh starts giving the instructions about the fellowship offering, Yahweh reminds Moses that the Israelites are still supposed to sacrifice part of the meat to Yahweh. When the Israelites bring the fellowship offering to sacrifice, the Israelites need to make sure to bring the right parts of the animal to give to Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will show that Yahweh is talking about the parts of the fellowship offering that the Israelites will give to Yahweh. Pause this audio here.

The Israelites are supposed to bring the fat and the animal's breast to God with their own hands. Yahweh repeats over and over again that the Israelite who is making the offering needs to bring the special parts of the animal to Yahweh. The Israelite cannot send someone else to bring the offering.

Stop here and talk about a rule in your community that is very important for everyone to follow. How do you show how important that rule is when you talk about the rule? Pause this audio here.

When an Israelite brings the fat and the animal's breast, the Israelite must wave the breast in the air as a way to give those things to Yahweh. We do not know exactly how the Israelite waves the breast.

Stop here to do this activity as a group: Find an object that you can use to wave in the air. If you can use actual meat, use actual meat. How would you wave the object to show that you are giving it to Yahweh? How will you describe how the Israelite waves the breast? Pause this audio here.

The priest takes the fat from the Israelite and burns the fat on the altar. Then the priest takes the breast meat and shares the breast meat with the other priests. Then the Israelite gives the priest who burned the fat the right thigh of the animal. Yahweh explains that this is the special gift that the Israelites are supposed to give the priest who helped the Israelite make the sacrifice. The priest who burned the fat on the altar and threw the blood on the altar gets to eat the right thigh. Yahweh explains that the Israelites are giving the fellowship offering to Yahweh, and then Yahweh gives the breast meat and the right thigh to Yahweh's priests.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time where someone gave you something and then you gave part of that gift to someone else. Pause this audio here.

In the second scene, the storyteller talks about the specific day when Yahweh gave these instructions. In some translations, the storyteller is the only person who talks in this scene, and the scene is a summary of what Yahweh said. In other translations, Yahweh is still the person talking here. It is not clear in the original languages which option is correct, so choose the option that works best for your language or is the most like other translations in your area.

Stop here and discuss as a group whether Yahweh will tell this part of the story in your translation or whether the storyteller will tell the story. Pause this audio here.

The storyteller explains again that the Israelites gave the fellowship offering to Yahweh and then Yahweh gave specific meat from the fellowship offering to Yahweh's priests. Yahweh made this rule about what meat the priests could eat on the same day that Yahweh officially made Aaron and Aaron's sons the priests of the Israelites. Yahweh makes Aaron and Aaron's sons priests when Yahweh anoints Aaron and Aaron's sons. A person anoints another person when they pour or smear oil on that person to show that the person has a new job and things to do. Then the storyteller repeats the same information again. On the same day that Aaron and Aaron's sons became the priests of the Israelites, Yahweh said that all the Israelites need to give the priests these kinds of meat every time the Israelites make a fellowship offering. The rules will last forever. Every time an Israelite gives a fellowship offering to Yahweh, Aaron and Aaron's sons get to eat the animal's breast meat and the right thigh as their special portion of the sacrifice.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: How will you act out that the storyteller repeats the rules for the fellowship offering when you act the story in the next step? How will you show that Yahweh gave these rules on the same day that Aaron and Aaron's sons became priests? Pause this audio here.

In the third scene, the storyteller summarizes everything that has happened since Yahweh gave Moses instructions about the purification offering.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Tell a long, complicated story as a group. Where do you summarize information when you tell stories? Pause this audio here.

The storyteller explains that all these instructions, since Yahweh gave the instructions about the purification offerings, are how the Israelites are supposed to offer the burnt offerings, grain offerings, purification offerings, guilt offerings, ordination offerings for appointing the priests, and fellowship offerings. These are the different kinds of offerings that the Israelites regularly make to Yahweh. Each offering gives the Israelites a different way to interact with Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Make a list of different activities your community does regularly. What words, phrases, or other features do you use to make it clear that the activities in the list are things your community does regularly? Pause this audio here.

The storyteller explains that Yahweh gave all these instructions to Moses while Moses was on Mount Sinai. It is important to remember that the first story in Leviticus talks about Yahweh giving instructions to Moses in the Tent of Meeting. Now the storyteller says that Yahweh gave Moses these instructions when Moses was on Mount Sinai. As you will remember, Leviticus has two groups of instructions. Yahweh may have given instructions to Moses about how to make the burnt offering, the grain offering, the fellowship offering, and the purification offerings when Moses was in the Tent of Meeting, after Moses came down from Mount Sinai. Yahweh may have given instructions to Moses about how to make guilt offerings, what to do with the daily offerings, how to prepare someone to be a new priest, and what parts of the offerings the Israelites and priests can eat when Moses was still on Mount Sinai. Then Moses came down and had the people build the Tent of Meeting. This might mean that Yahweh gave the instructions in Leviticus chapters 6 and 7 before Yahweh gave the instructions in Leviticus chapters 1 to 5.

Stop here and discuss as a group: How will you show the new location and time when you act this out? Tell a story about a thing that happened in the past. How do you show that you have changed time or location in the story? Pause this audio here.

The storyteller also says that Yahweh gave the instructions to Moses on the same day that Yahweh commanded the Israelites to bring the Israelites' offerings to Yahweh while all the Israelites were living in the Wilderness of Sinai. The day the storyteller is describing is the first day the Israelites brought offerings to Yahweh. After this day, the Israelites could bring offerings to Yahweh on any day.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Talk about an important event or tradition in your community. How did the event start? How do you talk about the event today? Pause this audio here.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 7:28–38 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has three scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • The storyteller
  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelites
  • Aaron
  • Aaron's sons
  • All of Aaron's descendants
  • And the specific priest who sacrifices the peace offering

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

It is important to remember that Yahweh is telling Moses to give these instructions to the Israelites, so the Israelites are not actually making these sacrifices while Yahweh is talking to Moses. You may still act out the Israelites making the sacrifices in order to remember the story well.

The story starts when Yahweh tells Moses to give these instructions to the Israelites about the fellowship offering.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Moses, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • Why are we talking about the fellowship offering again? or
  • I did not know Yahweh would give more instructions about the fellowship offering. I need to make sure I write these instructions down.
Continue the drama.

Yahweh explains that an Israelite who brings the fellowship offering needs to bring part of the offering specifically to Yahweh. The Israelite needs to bring the animal's fat and the animal's breast meat to Yahweh and give it to Yahweh as a wave offering.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I want to make sure Yahweh knows that this gift is from me; or
  • I am excited to give this gift to Yahweh! or
  • I wonder why it is so important that I bring this fat and meat with my own hands?
Continue the drama.

The priest burns up the fat on the altar and gives the breast meat to Aaron, Aaron's sons, and Aaron's descendants. Then the Israelite gives the right thigh meat to the priest who made the sacrifice.

Pause the drama.

Ask the people playing the priest, Aaron, Aaron's sons, and Aaron's descendants, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people may answer things like:

  • I am so thankful that Yahweh gave us this meat to eat! or
  • Now I do not have to worry about what to feed my family; or
  • This meat is the best meat!

Ask the people playing the Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people may answer things like:

  • Yahweh is giving the priests the best meat. Yahweh must really want us to respect the priests; or
  • Yahweh must really love Yahweh's priests. Yahweh wants to give the priests the best meat.
Continue the drama.

Yahweh explains that Yahweh is giving the animal's breast meat and right thigh meat to the priests forever. Aaron and Aaron's descendants will always eat the animal's breast meat, and the specific priest who offered the sacrifice will always eat the animal's right thigh. This rule will last forever.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person may answer things like:

  • I love my priests, and I want to make sure to always take care of the priests; or
  • I want to make sure the Israelites know that the priests are important to me, so the Israelites will take care of the priests.
Continue the drama.

Either the storyteller or Yahweh explains again that this meat is the meat that the priests get to eat from the sacrifices that the Israelites give to Yahweh. Yahweh gave these instructions on the same day that the priests officially became Yahweh's priests.

Finally, the storyteller explains that Yahweh gave all of the instructions about the burnt offerings, grain offerings, purification offerings, guilt offerings, ordination offerings, and fellowship offerings to Moses when Moses was on Mount Sinai. The storyteller also explains that Yahweh gave all these instructions on the same day Yahweh told the Israelites to start bringing offerings to Yahweh.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 7:28–38 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

In this story, the storyteller always refers to God as Yahweh. Yahweh tells Moses to give instructions to the Israelites about their offerings. It is important to remember that Yahweh is God's name. For more information on Yahweh, Israelites, and the general word for offerings, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same words or phrases for Yahweh, offerings, and Israelites as you used in previous passages.

The instructions that Yahweh gives Moses are about sacrifices for the peace or fellowship offering. It is important to remember that Yahweh talked about the fellowship offering in chapter three and in the previous passage. The fellowship offering is the sacrifice the Israelites make whenever the Israelites want to give Yahweh a gift or praise Yahweh for something Yahweh has done. Use the same word or phrase for sacrifice and fellowship offering as you used in previous passages. Look up sacrifice and fellowship offering in the Master Glossary for more information.

The Israelites are supposed to bring the animal's fat to sacrifice to Yahweh. An animal's fat is the thick white substance on animal meat. Use the same word or phrase for fat as you used in previous passages. The Israelites are also supposed to bring the animal's breast meat.

Stop here and look at a picture of a cut of breast meat and a picture of an animal with the breast area circled as a group. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for the animal's breast meat. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

The Israelites are supposed to give the breast meat and the fat to Yahweh with a wave offering. A wave offering was a way for the Israelites to show that the Israelites were giving something to Yahweh without burning the item on the altar. An Israelite would probably hold the meat in the air and move it up and down and side to side to show that the meat belonged to Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for wave offering. Look up wave offering in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this phrase in another book of the Bible, use the same word or phrase that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

The breast meat of the animal belongs to Aaron and Aaron's sons. It is important to remember that Aaron and Aaron's sons were the people that Yahweh chose to be priests. Only members of Aaron's family could be priests in Israel. When Yahweh talks about Aaron and his sons here, Yahweh is also talking about all of Aaron's descendants. Use the same word or phrase for descendants as you have previously. Descendants is in the Master Glossary.

The Israelites are also supposed to give the priest who helped with the sacrifice the right thigh meat of the animal.

Stop here and look at a picture of a cut of thigh meat and a picture of an animal with the right thigh circled as a group. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for the right thigh. If you have already translated this phrase in another book of the Bible, use the same word or phrase that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

The right thigh is a gift or portion from Yahweh to Yahweh's priests. Use the same word or phrase for special portion or gift for the priests as you used in previous passages.

The story talks about the fire offerings to Yahweh. It is important to remember that these sacrifices included all the different kinds of offerings that the priests burned up on the altar. Use the same word or phrase for fire offerings as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh anointed Aaron and Aaron's sons as priests. This means that Yahweh specifically chose the priests and had Moses put oil on the priests to show that the priests would serve Yahweh. In this case, Yahweh is talking about Aaron's actual sons on the day Yahweh appointed them as priests. Use the same word or phrase for sons and anoint as you used in previous passages. For more information on sons and anoint, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh gives the Israelites a statute, or special rule, to give this portion of meat to the priests for generations. Generations are the groups of people who are living at the same time. Here, it means that the Israelites are supposed to keep giving this meat to the priests forever. Use the same words and phrases for statute and generations as you have used in previous passages, and refer to statutes and generations in the Master Glossary for more information.

The story ends with a list of six kinds of offerings. The first offering is the burnt offering. The second kind of offering is the grain offering. The third kind of offering is the sin or purification offering. The fourth kind of offering is the guilt offering. The fifth kind of offering is the ordination offering. The sixth kind of offering is the fellowship offering. Use the same words or phrases for burnt offering, grain offering, purification offering, guilt offering, and fellowship offering as you used in previous passages. For more information on these offerings, refer to the Master Glossary.

We will hear more about the ordination offering in Leviticus chapter 8. In that chapter, Yahweh will anoint Aaron and Aaron's sons as priests. Moses will fill Aaron's hands with meat, fat, and bread for a wave offering to Yahweh to show that Aaron is now a priest. The word the Israelites used for ordination offering reminds the people that Moses filled Aaron's hands with an offering to Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for ordination offering, or the offering that priests gave to Yahweh when Yahweh appointed new priests. This should be a special phrase that shows that someone is appointing someone else for a special job. Use the same word for ordination that you used in Exodus 29:22. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh gave Moses all these instructions on Mount Sinai. Use the same word or phrase for Mount Sinai as you used in previous passages.

While Yahweh gave Moses these instructions, the Israelites were camped in the Wilderness of Sinai. Use the same word or phrase for the Wilderness of Sinai as you used in previous passages. Look up wilderness in the Master Glossary for more information.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 8:1–13
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 8:1–13 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 8:1–13 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 8:1–13 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In the last story, Yahweh told Moses what meat from the sacrifices the Israelites should give to the priests to eat. Now, the storyteller tells the story about how Yahweh appoints Aaron and Aaron's sons to officially begin their work as Yahweh's priests. In the book of Exodus, chapter 29, Yahweh gave Moses specific instructions about how Moses was supposed to make Aaron and Aaron's sons into Yahweh's priests. If you have already translated Exodus 29, listen to your translation here to remember what Yahweh said.

Pause this audio here.

Yahweh told Moses to bring Aaron and Aaron's sons to the Tent of Meeting. Moses was also supposed to bring all of the other things that Moses would need to officially make Aaron and Aaron's sons Yahweh's priests. Moses needed to bring the special clothing that Aaron and Aaron's sons would wear, special oil, a bull to sacrifice for a purification offering, two male sheep, and a basket of bread without yeast. Moses would use all of these items to make Aaron and Aaron's sons Yahweh's official priests. Yahweh also told Moses to make sure that all the people of Israel gather at the Tent of Meeting to watch what was going to happen.

Stop here and discuss this question: Tell a story about a time when your community gave someone an important role or position in the community. What ceremonies or rituals did your community do to honor that person? What objects or items did you use? Who came to the ceremony? Pause this audio here.

When Moses finished bringing everything to the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting, and the special assembly of Israelites were at the tent too, Moses told the Israelites that Moses was about to do what Yahweh had told Moses to do.

Stop here and look at a picture of the Tent of Meeting and the courtyard outside of it to see where everyone stood to watch the ceremony. Pause this audio here.

First, Moses had Aaron and Aaron's sons wash themselves in water. The storyteller does not say whether Aaron and Aaron's sons washed their entire bodies or whether Aaron and Aaron's sons only washed their hands and their feet. In other parts of the Bible, we know that priests washed their hands and feet every time the priests entered the Tent of Meeting, so some people think that Aaron and Aaron's sons only washed their hands and feet here. Other people think that Aaron and Aaron's sons washed their entire bodies. On one of the most holy days of the year, the Day of Atonement, the high priest had to wash his entire body to show that the high priest was ritually clean and could offer the sacrifices to Yahweh. Since Aaron and Aaron's sons were becoming Yahweh's holy priests, Aaron and Aaron's sons might have washed their entire bodies to show that Aaron and Aaron's sons were ready to devote their whole bodies to follow Yahweh. It is important to know that Aaron and Aaron's sons were probably still wearing some sort of thin clothing if Aaron and Aaron's sons washed their entire bodies, so Aaron and Aaron's sons were not naked in front of everyone.

Stop here and discuss this question: Tell a story about a holy time or day for your community. What do different members of your community do to prepare themselves for that day? Pause this audio here.

After Aaron and Aaron's sons had washed themselves, Moses put special clothing on Aaron to show that Aaron had a special position as the most important priest out of all the priests.

Stop here and discuss this question: Think about the most important people in your community. What do those people wear? How do people in your community know that those people are the most important people? Pause this audio here.

The first piece of special clothing that Moses put on Aaron was a tunic. People wore tunics next to the body under all the other clothing. A tunic had long sleeves and sometimes had embroidery as well.

Stop here and look at a picture of a man wearing a tunic. Pause this audio here.

Next, Moses wrapped a sash around Aaron's waist. A sash is a long piece of cloth that people wrap around themselves to help keep their clothing on their bodies.

Stop here and look at a picture of a man wearing a tunic and a sash. Pause this audio here.

After the sash, Moses put a robe on Aaron. People would make a robe out of one long piece of fabric. A robe had a hole for the head and two holes for the arms. Aaron's robe covered Aaron from his neck to down below his knees.

Stop here and look at a picture of a man wearing a robe. Pause this audio here.

Once Moses put the robe on Aaron, Moses tied an ephod on Aaron. The Bible does not give detailed descriptions of an ephod, so it is hard to know exactly what an ephod was. We do know that Aaron did not put the ephod on over Aaron's head like a shirt. Moses tied the ephod onto Aaron using a special, beautiful sash. Some people think the ephod looked like a vest, and some people think it looked like an apron that Moses tied around Aaron's neck and waist. People made the ephod of high-quality materials like gold, different colors of wool fabric, and fine linen.

Stop here and look at a picture of a man wearing an ephod over the robe. Pause this audio here.

Then Moses tied a breastpiece onto Aaron's ephod. People made the breastpiece of the same high-quality materials as the ephod, and Moses used fine gold chains to attach the breastpiece to the ephod. The breastpiece had 12 precious stones as decoration. Each stone had the name of a different tribe of Israel on it.

Stop here and look at a picture of a man wearing a breastpiece over the ephod and robe. Pause this audio here.

Moses put two items, the Urim and Thummim, in special pockets in the breastpiece. The Bible does not tell us exactly what the Urim and Thummim looked like. The priests were supposed to use Urim and Thummim to understand what God wanted the priests to do, but the Bible does not tell us how God used Urim and Thummim to communicate with the Israelites.

Once Urim and Thummim were safely in the special pockets in the breastpiece, Moses placed a turban on Aaron's head. The turban could have been a long piece of fabric that Moses wound around the top of Aaron's head. Or a turban could have been a special kind of hat that Aaron could take on and off without unwinding it.

Next, Moses set a special gold decoration on Aaron's turban. On the gold decoration were the words "Holy to Yahweh," and Moses attached the decoration to the turban. The decoration might have been a rectangle shape, or it might have been a flower shape. Yahweh called the decoration a holy crown that only the high priest could wear. The crown showed that Yahweh specifically chose Aaron to be the high priest.

Stop here and look at a picture of a man wearing all the priestly clothing that Moses has put on Aaron so far, including a turban and the holy crown. Pause this audio here.

After Moses put all the special clothing on Aaron, Moses took the special oil that Moses had brought and used the oil to anoint the Tent of Meeting. The Israelites made the oil using special herbs and spices that Yahweh told the Israelites to use. When Moses poured or sprinkled the oil onto something, Moses was anointing that thing as a sign that the thing belonged to Yahweh. People had to treat the thing differently. People had to be careful not to disrespect the thing or to touch the thing when people were ritually unclean because the thing was one of Yahweh's special objects.

Moses sprinkled this special oil on the Tent of Meeting and on everything inside the Tent of Meeting to show that it all belonged to Yahweh. Moses also showed that people could only use the Tent of Meeting and all the things inside the tent to worship Yahweh. When it was time for Moses to anoint the altar, Moses sprinkled the oil on the bronze altar in the courtyard seven times. Moses also put oil on all the other things that the priests would need to use when the priests sacrificed animals on the altar. Once Moses finished sprinkling the oil on the altar and all the other tools, those items belonged to Yahweh, and the priests could use those items to worship Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time when your community wanted to give something to Yahweh or to someone important. What did you do to show that the gift belonged to that person? Pause this audio here.

Now that the Tent of Meeting and everything in it officially belonged to Yahweh, Moses poured oil on Aaron's head. This showed everyone that Yahweh had chosen Aaron to be Yahweh's priest. Aaron belonged to Yahweh now and could serve Yahweh as Yahweh's priest.

After Moses poured the oil on Aaron's head, Moses put special clothing on Aaron's sons. Moses put tunics and sashes on Aaron's sons just like Moses had put on Aaron. Then Moses put special hats on Aaron's sons' heads. These hats were different from Aaron's hat, but the Bible does not tell us exactly what these hats looked like. The hats could be skullcaps that covered the top and back of a person's head but did not have a brim. Or the hats could be tall hats that Moses tied onto Aaron's sons' heads.

Stop here and look at a picture of a man wearing a skullcap and a picture of a man wearing a tall hat.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 8:1–13 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has four scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells Moses what Moses needs to bring to make Aaron and Aaron's sons official priests.

In the second scene: Moses puts special clothing on Aaron.

In the third scene: Moses uses the special anointing oil to show that the Tent of Meeting and Aaron belong to Yahweh.

In the fourth scene: Moses puts special clothing on Aaron's sons.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Aaron
  • The assembly of the people of Israel
  • And Aaron's sons

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

In the first scene, the storyteller interrupts the long list of laws that Yahweh gives to Moses so that the Israelites can live in good relationship with Yahweh. The storyteller now tells the story about when Yahweh appoints Aaron and Aaron's sons to be priests for Yahweh. Yahweh tells Moses to bring Aaron and Aaron's sons to the Tent of Meeting. Yahweh also tells Moses to bring the other things that Moses will need for the ceremony to consecrate Aaron and Aaron's sons as Yahweh's official priests. Yahweh tells Moses to bring all the priests' clothing, the special oil, the bull for the sin or purification offering, two rams or male sheep, and a basket with bread that people made without yeast. Yahweh also tells Moses to bring all the people of Israel—the assembly—to the courtyard in front of the door of the Tent of Meeting. The assembly of people would not have been the entire population of Israelites, but it would have been a large number of people who represented the entire group of Israelites. The entrance to the Tent of Meeting probably referred to the entire courtyard around the Tent of Meeting.

Moses does everything Yahweh told Moses to. It is important to know that Yahweh did not tell Moses to bring everything by himself, so other people probably help Moses bring all the objects and animals to the Tent of Meeting. It is also important to know that the assembly of Israelites filled the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting to watch the ceremony.

In scene two, Moses tells the people that the ceremony Moses is about to do is the ceremony that Yahweh wants Moses to do. Moses is telling the people that everything Moses is going to do to make Aaron and Aaron's sons Yahweh's priests is exactly how Yahweh wants the Israelites to consecrate, or make holy, priests in the future.

Stop and discuss as a group: What is something that you do that you need to do in a specific way? Explain how to do that task to the group. What do you say to show the rest of the group how important that task is and why people have to do that task in that specific way? Pause this audio here.

Moses has Aaron and Aaron's sons step away from the rest of the Israelites and has Aaron and Aaron's sons wash themselves with water. Then Moses puts special clothing on Aaron. First, Moses puts a tunic on Aaron. Then Moses wraps a sash around Aaron's waist. Then Moses puts a robe over Aaron's head and ties the ephod onto Aaron with the special sash. After Moses ties the ephod onto Aaron, Moses attaches the breastpiece to the ephod and puts the Urim and Thummim in special pockets in the breastpiece. Finally, Moses puts the turban on Aaron's head and sets the gold plate, or the holy crown, on top.

Stop here and find different kinds of clothing and fabric that you can use to represent the different kinds of clothing that Moses put on Aaron. Choose one person to play Aaron and one person to play Moses. Have the person who is playing Moses put the different kinds of clothing on the person who is playing Aaron. Once the person playing Moses finishes, choose different people to play Moses or Aaron. Keep taking turns until everyone has a chance to be Moses and everyone has a chance to be Aaron. Pause this audio here.

When Moses puts the special clothing on Aaron, Moses does exactly what Yahweh had told Moses to do in the book of Exodus when Yahweh told Moses how to do this specific ceremony.

If you have already translated the book of Exodus, listen to Exodus 29 to remember how you translated Yahweh's instructions about the priests' clothing. Pause this audio here.

In the third scene, Moses uses the special anointing oil to anoint the Tent of Meeting, all the special tools and objects that the priests would use to worship Yahweh, and Aaron himself. Moses sprinkles the oil seven times on the altar and all the tools that the priests need when the priests sacrifice an animal on the altar. When Moses sprinkles the oil, Moses uses his fingers to flick small drops of oil onto the altar and the tools.

Stop here and find a bowl of oil. If you cannot use oil, then find a bowl of water instead. Practice sprinkling the oil or water on different objects. Choose one object to represent the altar and sprinkle the oil or water on it seven times. How do you describe this action? Pause this audio here.

Moses pours the anointing oil over Aaron's head to show that Yahweh had chosen Aaron to be Yahweh's special high priest. This also shows that Yahweh allows Aaron to touch things in the Tent of Meeting and do things to worship Yahweh that no one else could do.

Stop here and pour some of the water or oil in the bowl from the last activity onto the head of someone in the group who is willing to play Aaron. If no one in the group wants to play Aaron, find a large rock or other round object and pour the water or oil onto that instead. How would you talk about that action? Pause this audio here.

In the fourth scene, Moses puts special clothing on Aaron's sons. First, Moses puts a tunic on Aaron's sons. Then Moses ties sashes around Aaron's sons' waists. Finally, Moses puts their special hats on Aaron's sons' heads.

Stop here and find clothing or fabric that represents or is similar to the kinds of clothing that Moses puts on Aaron's sons. Choose one person to play Moses and one person to play one of Aaron's sons. Have the person who is playing Moses practice putting the clothing on the person playing Aaron's son. Take turns playing Moses and Aaron's son until everyone has had a chance to play both parts. Pause this audio here.

When Moses puts this special clothing on Aaron's sons, Moses is following Yahweh's instructions from the book of Exodus.

If you have already translated the book of Exodus, listen again, if needed, to how you translated Yahweh's instructions about the priests' clothing in Exodus 29. Pause this audio here.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 8:1–13 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has four scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Aaron
  • The assembly of the people of Israel
  • And Aaron's sons

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

At the beginning of the story, Yahweh tells Moses to bring Aaron and Aaron's sons, the special clothing Aaron and Aaron's sons will wear as priests, the bull for the purification offering, two male goats, and a basket of bread without yeast. Yahweh also tells Moses to make sure all the people of Israel come to the front of the Tent of Meeting.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • It is finally time for Aaron and Aaron's sons to become my priests. I am very excited; or
  • I want all the Israelites to see how important it is to be one of my priests; or
  • These are important instructions. I want Moses to follow my instructions very carefully.
Continue the drama.

Moses does exactly what Yahweh tells Moses to do, and all of the Israelites gather in front of the Tent of Meeting.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Moses, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • There are so many instructions! I hope I do all of the instructions correctly! or
  • This is an important day for my brother, Aaron, and for all of the people of Israel. I am so excited!

Ask the people playing the Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people might answer things like:

  • I am so curious about what is going to happen! or
  • This must be very important if we all need to be here to watch; or
  • I am so excited that Aaron and Aaron's sons are becoming our priests! Now we can offer sacrifices to Yahweh.
Continue the drama.

Moses tells everyone that the ceremony Moses is about to do is the ceremony that Yahweh said Moses needs to do. Then Moses tells Aaron and Aaron's sons to come away from the other Israelites and join Moses in front of everyone.

Pause the drama.

Ask the people playing Aaron and Aaron's sons, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people might answer things like:

  • I am so nervous. I do not know what will happen or what to expect! or
  • I am so honored that Yahweh chose me to be Yahweh's priest. I will do my best to follow Yahweh.
Continue the drama.

Moses has Aaron and Aaron's sons wash themselves, and then Moses puts all of the special clothing on Aaron. First, Moses puts the tunic over Aaron's head. Then Moses ties the sash around Aaron's waist. Then Moses puts the robe over Aaron's head and ties the ephod onto Aaron with the special waistband. Then Moses ties the breastpiece onto Aaron and places the Urim and Thummim in their special pockets on the breastpiece. Finally, Moses places the turban on Aaron's head and attaches the gold plate, or the holy crown, to the front of it.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Aaron, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person may answer things like:

  • This clothing shows that I have an important role to serve Yahweh. I need to make sure I do the right thing; or
  • This is a lot of different kinds of clothing. I will need to be careful about how I put the clothing on to make sure I follow all of Yahweh's instructions.

Ask the people playing the Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people might answer things like:

  • Yahweh wanted Aaron to wear such fancy clothing. Aaron must have a very important role; or
  • I wonder if Aaron's sons will have clothing that is just as special as Aaron's clothing.
Continue the drama.

Once Aaron is wearing all of Aaron's special clothing, Moses takes the anointing oil and sprinkles the oil on the tabernacle and all the things inside the tabernacle. Then Moes sprinkles the oil on the altar seven times and on all the other tools that the priests would use to sacrifice an animal on the altar.

Pause the drama.

and ask the person playing Moses, "What are you thinking or feeling?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am happy that this all belongs to Yahweh now, and we can use these things to worship Yahweh and follow all of Yahweh's instructions;
  • I hope all the Israelites treat these objects carefully and respectfully because these items belong to Yahweh now.

    [!end] Continue the drama.

Moses pours the oil over Aaron's head.

Pause the drama.

and ask the person playing Moses, "What are you thinking or feeling?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am so proud of my brother. I cannot believe Aaron is Yahweh's first high priest; or
  • I hope Aaron does a good job as Aaron serves Yahweh as Yahweh's high priest.

Ask the person playing Aaron, "What are you thinking or feeling?" The person might answer things like:

  • I cannot believe that I am becoming Yahweh's high priest now; or
  • I need to be even more careful to follow all of Yahweh's instructions now that I am becoming Yahweh's high priest.
Continue the drama.

Finally, Moses puts the special clothing on Aaron's sons. Moses puts a tunic over Aaron's sons' heads, ties a sash around their waists, and puts special hats on their heads.

Pause the drama.

and ask the people playing Aaron's sons, "What are you thinking or feeling?" The people might answer things like:

  • I cannot believe that I am becoming a priest of Yahweh. This is the most important moment in my life; or
  • I will do everything I can to worship and obey Yahweh and help the Israelites follow all of Yahweh's instructions.

Ask the people playing the Israelites, "What are you thinking or feeling?" The people might answer things like:

  • Aaron must be a more important priest since Aaron is wearing different clothing than Aaron's sons; or
  • Aaron's sons are wearing such special clothing. When I see that clothing, I will know that I need to listen to Aaron's sons because Aaron's sons are Yahweh's priests; or
  • I am excited to be able to make sacrifices to Yahweh now that Aaron's sons are becoming priests.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 8:1–13 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

The story starts with Yahweh giving Moses instructions. Use the same word or phrase for Yahweh that you used for previous passages. Look up Yahweh in the Master Glossary for more information.

Yahweh tells Moses to bring Aaron, Aaron's sons, and many other things to the Tent of Meeting. In this case, Aaron's sons are Aaron's male children. Use the same word for sons as you have used in previous passages, and refer to sons in the Master Glossary for more information. Use the same word or phrase for the Tent of Meeting that you used for previous passages. Look up the tabernacle in the Master Glossary for more information.

Moses must bring the bull for the sin or purification offering, two male sheep or rams, and a basket with bread that people made without yeast. Use the same words or phrases for bull, male sheep, bread without yeast, and sin or purification offering as you have used in previous passages. For more information about the purification offering, refer to the Master Glossary.

People use a basket to carry or store things, and in this case, the people carried bread in the basket. People make baskets by weaving together thin sticks, stems of plants, or reeds. A reed is a plant that grows in the water.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for a basket. Look at a picture of a basket. We do not know how big this basket was. For more information, refer to basket in the Master Glossary.

One of the things that Yahweh tells Moses to bring to the Tent of Meeting is the clothing that Aaron and Aaron's sons will wear once they become priests. This is a general word that describes any kind of clothing.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for clothing. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh also tells Moses to bring anointing oil to the Tent of Meeting. In the Bible, people would anoint other people or things by pouring, sprinkling, or smearing oil on the person or thing to show that God had chosen that person or thing for a special purpose. Use the same word or phrase for anoint that you used for previous passages. Look up anoint in the Master Glossary for more information.

Moses obeys Yahweh and gathers the assembly at the Tent of Meeting. The assembly is a general word that describes the people of Israel, and often specifically a special group of representatives from Israel. It shows that representatives, or leaders, throughout all of Israel are gathering together for a specific purpose. In this story, the specific purpose is to watch Moses do the ritual that will make Aaron and Aaron's sons into Yahweh's priests.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for assembly. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

When everyone is standing in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting, Moses puts a tunic on Aaron. A tunic is a long-sleeved piece of clothing that covers a person's torso and goes under all a person's other clothing. It is important to remember that Yahweh described all of the different kinds of clothing that Yahweh wanted the priests to wear in the book of Exodus. If you have already translated the book of Exodus, you can listen to the story about the priests' clothing there to learn more.

Stop here and, as a group, look at a picture of a man wearing a tunic. Discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for tunic. Look up tunic in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

After Moses puts the tunic on Aaron, Moses ties a sash around Aaron's waist. A sash is a long piece of cloth that people wrap around their waists to help hold their clothing on their bodies.

Stop here and, as a group, look at a picture of a man wearing a tunic and sash. Decide as a group what word or phrase you will use for sash. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Next, Moses puts a robe on Aaron. People would make a robe from a single piece of fabric, and a robe had holes for a person's head and arms. The robe covered people from their neck down to below their knees, and people wore a robe on top of other clothing, like tunics.

Stop here and, as a group, look at a picture of a man wearing a robe. Decide what word or phrase you will use for robe. Look up robe in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word here that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Moses puts an ephod on Aaron over the robe. The ephod was a kind of clothing that covered the body from the shoulders to the thighs. Moses ties the ephod onto Aaron using a special sash.

Stop here and look at a picture of a man wearing an ephod. Decide as a group what word or phrase you will use for ephod. Look up ephod in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word here that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

After the ephod, Moses puts a breastpiece on Aaron. This is a special piece of fabric that Moses tied onto Aaron's ephod. The Israelites attached 12 precious stones to the fabric and wrote the name of a different tribe of Israel on each stone. The breastpiece also had special pockets in it for the Urim and Thummim.

Stop here and look at a picture of a man wearing a breastpiece. Decide as a group what word or phrase you will use for breastpiece. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word here that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Moses places the Urim and Thummim into the special pockets in the breastpiece. The Urim and Thummim were objects that Yahweh used to tell the Israelites what Yahweh wanted the Israelites to do. The Bible never describes what the Urim and Thummim looked like or exactly what the Israelites did to use the Urim and Thummim.

Stop here and decide as a group what word or phrase you will use for Urim and Thummim. If you have already translated this phrase in another book of the bible, use the same word or words here that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Moses puts a turban on Aaron's head. A turban is a kind of hat that people wear. People make a turban out of a single long piece of fabric and wind it around their head to make a hat. Moses might have wound the fabric around Aaron's head, or people may have sewn together the fabric so that Moses could set the turban on Aaron's head like other kinds of hats.

Stop here and look at a picture of a turban as a group. Decide what word or phrase you will use to translate turban. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word or phrase that you used there. Pause this audio here.

Moses puts one more piece of clothing on Aaron. Moses puts a special golden plate on Aaron's turban. The Israelites might have made the golden plate in the shape of a flower, or the Israelites might have made the golden plate in the shape of a rectangle. Moses attached the plate to the most important priest's turban, and the Israelites carved the words "Holy to Yahweh" onto the plate.

Stop here and, as a group, look at a picture of the golden plate. Decide what word or phrase you will use to translate the golden plate. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word or phrase that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

The storyteller describes the golden plate as a holy crown. The word holy describes things that belong to Yahweh. People cannot use holy things to do ordinary tasks. Holy things belong completely to Yahweh, and people must only use these holy items to serve Yahweh. Use the same word or phrase for holy as you used in previous passages. Look up holy in the Master Glossary for more information.

Moses sprinkles some of the oil on the tabernacle and everything in the tabernacle, the bronze altar in the courtyard, the water basin or large bowl, and all the utensils that people used for work at the altar. Use the same words for sprinkle as you have used previously when priests sprinkle blood on an object with their fingers. Use the same word for altar as you have used previously. For more information about altar, refer to the Master Glossary.

The basin is a very large bowl that priests put water in. The utensils are all the forks, knives, and small bowls that priests used for work at the altar.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for tabernacle. This is the first time in Leviticus that the storyteller uses a specific word for Yahweh's living place rather than calling it a tent. For more information about tabernacle, refer to the Master Glossary. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss as a group what words or phrases you will use for basin and utensils. Use the same words for basin and utensils as you used in Exodus 35:16. Pause this audio here.

Moses pours the anointing oil on Aaron's head to consecrate Aaron. When someone consecrates someone else, the person who is doing the consecration is saying that the other person has a special job now. In other words, the priests are now holy—they belong to Yahweh. Moses consecrated Aaron, so now Aaron has the special job of being Israel's high priest.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for consecrate. Look up consecrate in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Finally, Moses puts tunics on Aaron's sons, ties sashes around their waists, and places caps on their heads. These caps were different kinds of hats from Aaron's turban. The Israelites probably made Aaron's turban by winding a long piece of fabric around Aaron's head, but the Israelites made these caps out of a smaller piece of fabric. The Israelites probably made the caps into the shape of a circle, and the caps sat on the top of Aaron's sons' heads. Another word for this kind of hat is a skullcap. Another option is that the caps were tall hats that Moses tied onto the priests' heads.

Stop here and, as a group, look at pictures of a cap and a hat. Discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for caps. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.
