title: Leviticus 8:14–21
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 8:14–21 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 8:14–21 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 8:14–21 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

Once Moses finished putting the special priestly clothing on Aaron and Aaron's sons, it was time for Moses to offer the sacrifices so that Aaron and Aaron's sons could officially start serving Yahweh as Yahweh's priests. It is important to remember that Yahweh gave Moses the specific instructions about how to make the sacrifices that would make Aaron and Aaron's sons into Yahweh's priests in the book of Exodus in chapter 29. If you have already translated Exodus 29, you can listen to your translation here to remember what Yahweh said.

Pause this audio here.

In the last story, Moses brought a bull and two male sheep to the Tent of Meeting along with the special clothing. In this story, Moses sacrificed the bull on behalf of Aaron and Aaron's sons. The bull is a sin or purification offering. It is important to remember that Yahweh gave instructions to Moses in Leviticus 4 about how to sacrifice an animal for a purification offering. When Yahweh gave those instructions, Yahweh said that the high priest needed to sacrifice a bull if the high priest ever sinned. The sacrifice would atone for the high priest. The sacrifice would pay for the high priest's sins so that the high priest did not need to die. The story does not say that Aaron and Aaron's sons have done any specific sins, but Aaron and Aaron's sons were about to become the most holy people in the community. Aaron and Aaron's sons were going to serve Yahweh in the Tent of Meeting. Aaron and Aaron's sons needed to be ritually clean from any sin so that they could offer the sacrifices that would pay for all of the Israelites' sins.

Stop here and tell a story about a ritual that a holy person in your community needs to do in order to keep serving the community in their position. Pause this audio here.

Aaron and Aaron's sons placed their hands on the bull's head, and then Moses killed the bull. Moses took some of the bull's blood and put the blood on the four horns of the altar.

Stop here and, as a group, look at a picture of the altar with the four horns circled. Pause this audio here.

Moses put the blood on the horns of the altar to purify the altar. The Israelites were going to use the altar to give sacrifices to Yahweh, so the altar needed to be ritually clean. The blood from the sin offering ritually cleaned the altar so that the priests could offer sacrifices on it.

After Moses put the blood on the horns of the altar, Moses poured the rest of the blood at the base of the altar. The words in the original language here are confusing, so scholars have two main ways to understand what this part means.

The first option is that Moses poured the blood at the base of the altar to make atonement for the altar to purify the altar from sin. Once Moses purified the altar from sin, Moses consecrated the altar and gave the altar a special purpose to serve Yahweh. Humans made the altar, so the altar might have human sin on it simply because people made the altar. When Moses poured the blood on the altar, Moses cleaned away that sin and made the altar special so people could use the altar to serve Yahweh.

The second option is that Moses made the altar special to Yahweh so that people could use the altar to make atonement for people's sins. The altar did not have any sin on it, but priests were going to use the altar to make sacrifices that would atone for the Israelites' sins. If the priests were going to use the altar to pay for the Israelites' sins, then the priests needed to consecrate the altar. Moses had to set apart the altar to serve Yahweh in a specific way. When Moses poured the blood on the altar, Moses was consecrating the altar so that the priests could use the altar to atone for Israel's sins.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time when you or someone in your community prepared a space or an object so that the community could use it to worship Yahweh, an ancestor, a spirit, or a god. Pause this audio here.

After Moses poured the blood on the altar, Moses took the bull's fat, the best part of the liver, the kidneys and all the fat that was on the kidneys, and Moses burned those pieces up on the altar.

Stop here and, as a group, look at pictures of a cow's fat, liver, kidneys, and the fat that is on the cow's kidneys. Pause this audio here.

After the bull's fat, liver, kidneys, and the fat that was on the bull's kidneys finished burning, Moses took the rest of the bull outside the camp. Moses took the bull's skin, meat, and all the other organs that were inside the bull, and Moses burned up those parts outside the camp, away from where the Israelites lived. All these things that Moses did were exactly what Yahweh had told Moses to do earlier in the book of Exodus.

Stop here and, as a group, look at pictures of a bull's skin, meat, and other organs. Pause this audio here.

After Moses finished sacrificing the bull, Moses brought one of the male sheep, which people also call rams, to Aaron and Aaron's sons. This ram was the ram that Moses was going to sacrifice as a burnt offering for Aaron and Aaron's sons. It is important to remember that a burnt offering was like a gift that the Israelites gave Yahweh. The priests burned the whole animal on the altar so that the offering would be a gift that smelled good to Yahweh.

Stop here and listen to how you translated Yahweh's instructions on how to sacrifice a burnt offering in Leviticus 1. Pause this audio here.

Aaron and Aaron's sons placed their hands on the ram's head, and then Moses killed the ram and threw the ram's blood on the sides of the altar. Moses cut the ram into pieces and burned the head, the pieces, and the fat on the altar.

Stop here and look at a picture of a ram's head, fat, and meat. Pause this audio here.

Then Moses washed the ram's internal organs and the ram's legs with water, and Moses burned the whole ram on the altar.

Stop here and look at pictures of a ram's internal organs and legs. Pause this audio here.

When Moses sacrificed the ram, Moses did everything exactly as Yahweh told Moses to do. The ram was a burnt offering that made a good smell for Yahweh to smell. It was a gift that Moses gave Yahweh with fire.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 8:14–21 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has two scenes.

In the first scene: Moses sacrifices the bull for the sin or purification offering for the priests.

In the second scene: Moses sacrifices the ram for the burnt offering for the priests.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Moses
  • Aaron
  • Aaron's sons
  • The assembly of Israelites
  • And Yahweh

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

It is important to remember that the assembly of Israelites was still watching Moses in this passage, even though the storyteller does not mention the assembly.

In the previous story, Moses brought a bull and two rams to the Tent of Meeting. The bull that Moses sacrificed in the first scene in this story is the bull that Moses brought in the previous story.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will act out that this bull is the same bull from the previous story. Pause this audio here.

The bull was a purification offering for Aaron and Aaron's sons.

First, Aaron and Aaron's sons placed their hands on the bull's head. Then Moses killed the bull and put his own finger in the blood. Moses used his finger to spread the blood on the four horns of the altar.

Stop here and find a rock or piece of wood that is similar in shape to the horn of the altar. Fill a bowl with water. Take turns dipping your finger in the water and smearing the water on the rock or piece of wood. Remember how you described this action in previous passages. Pause this audio here.

Moses poured the rest of the blood at the base of the altar. The base is the bottom of the altar where the altar touches the ground.

Stop here and look at a picture of the altar together and point to where the base of the altar is. Then find a large rock or tree. Take turns pouring water from the bowl at the base of the rock or tree. Remember how you described this action in previous passages. Pause this audio here.

After Moses finished putting the blood on the altar, Moses removed the bull's fat, the best part of the liver, the kidneys, and the fat from both kidneys, and Moses burned these pieces on the altar. Then Moses took the rest of the bull outside the camp and burned the rest of the bull there just like Yahweh had told Moses to.

Next, Moses brought one of the two rams from the last story. Moses would sacrifice this ram as the burnt offering for Aaron and Aaron's sons.

Stop here and discuss how you are going to show that the ram for this burnt offering is one of the rams that Moses brought to the tent in the last story. Pause this audio here.

Moses brought the ram to Aaron and Aaron's sons, who put their hands on the ram's head. Then Moses killed the ram and threw the ram's blood against the sides of the altar.

Stop here and fill a bowl with water. Take turns splashing the water against a rock or tree. Remember how you described this action in previous passages. Pause this audio here.

Then Moses cut the ram into pieces and burned the ram's head, meat, and fat on the altar. Next, Moses washed the ram's internal organs and legs with water and burned the rest of the ram on the altar. The ram was a burnt offering that smelled good to Yahweh, and it was a gift the priests burned with fire to give to Yahweh. The story ends when it says that Moses offered the ram to Yahweh exactly as Yahweh told Moses to.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 8:14–21 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has two scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Moses
  • Aaron
  • The assembly of Israelites
  • Aaron's sons
  • And Yahweh

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

Moses brings the bull for the sin offering to Aaron and Aaron's sons. Aaron and Aaron's sons lay their hands on the bull's head.

Pause the drama.

Ask the people playing Aaron and Aaron's sons, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people may answer things like:

  • This is a serious moment. This bull needs to die because of my sins, so that I do not have to die; or
  • I cannot believe this is actually happening. I am going to officially be one of Yahweh's priests.
Continue the drama.

Moses kills the bull and sticks his finger in the blood. Moses uses his finger to smear blood on the altar's four horns. Then Moses pours the rest of the blood at the altar's base. In this way, Moses purifies the altar and makes atonement for it.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Moses, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person may answer things like:

  • Now the altar is clean from sin, and the altar officially belongs to Yahweh; or
  • Now this altar officially belongs to Yahweh, and the priests can use the altar to make sacrifices to Yahweh to atone for all the Israelites' sins.
Continue the drama.

Then Moses takes the fat from the inside of the bull, the liver, the kidneys, and the fat that is on the bull's kidneys and burns all of these on the altar. Then Moses takes the rest of the bull outside the camp and burns the rest of the bull with fire, just as Yahweh told Moses to do it.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am very happy with Moses because Moses listened to my instructions and did exactly what I told Moses to do; or
  • I am happy that Aaron, Aaron's sons, and the altar are almost ready to serve me.
Continue the drama.

Next, Moses brings one of the rams to Aaron and Aaron's sons. Aaron and Aaron's sons lay their hands on the ram's head.

Pause the drama.

Ask the people playing Aaron and Aaron's sons, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people may answer things like:

  • This is a very serious moment. This animal is going to need to die to give this gift to Yahweh; or
  • I am excited to give this gift to Yahweh.
Continue the drama.

Moses kills the ram and throws the ram's blood on the sides of the altar. Then Moses cuts the ram into pieces, and puts the ram's head, the pieces of the meat, and the fat on the altar. Moses burns those parts of the ram. Then Moses washes the ram's legs and internal organs with water and burns all the rest of the ram's parts on the altar as a burnt offering that smells good to Yahweh. This is a fire offering to Yahweh. Moses offers this fire offering in the way that Yahweh told Moses to offer it.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am very happy with Moses because Moses listened to my instructions and did exactly what I told Moses to do; or
  • I am happy that Aaron, Aaron's sons, and the altar are almost ready to serve me.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 8:14–21 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

Moses first brings a bull to Aaron and Aaron's sons. It is important to remember that bulls are male cattle. Use the same words or phrases for bull and sons as you used in previous passages. Sons is in the Master Glossary.

Moses is going to kill the bull as a sin or purification offering. It is important to remember that Yahweh gave Moses the instructions for how to sacrifice a bull for a purification offering in Leviticus 4. Use the same words or phrases for killing an animal and for purification offering here as you used in previous passages. Look up "sin or purification offering" in the Master Glossary for more information.

After Moses kills the bull, Moses uses his finger to put some of the blood on the horns of the altar. Use the same word or phrase for the horns of the altar as you used in previous passages. Look in the Master Glossary for more information on the altar.

Moses puts the blood on the horns of the altar to purify the altar. When you purify something, you ritually clean the thing so that it can become special to Yahweh, and so people can use that thing to worship Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for purify. Look up purify in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Moses pours the rest of the bull's blood on the altar to consecrate the altar, or make it holy, so the priests can use the altar for Yahweh. It is important to remember that to consecrate an object meant that the object officially belonged to Yahweh. Priests could only use objects that the priests had consecrated to worship Yahweh. Look up consecrate in the Master Glossary for more information. Use the same word or phrase for consecrate as you used in previous passages.

The priests will use the altar to atone for the Israelites' sins. It is important to remember that atonement is what happens when a person offers the correct offerings to Yahweh so that they can have a good relationship with Yahweh again. Look up atonement in the Master Glossary for more information. Use the same word or phrase for atone as you used in previous passages.

It is important to remember that there are two main ways to understand what Moses does with the altar. The first option is that Moses atones for the altar, cleans any sin off the altar, and consecrates the altar. The second option is that Moses consecrates the altar so that the priests can use the altar to offer the sacrifices to atone for Israel's sin.

Stop here and discuss as a group which option you will use in your translation. Look at other translations in majority languages or related languages and see which option they choose. Pause this audio here.

Moses burns the bull's fat on the altar. Use the same word for fat as you used in previous passages. Moses also burns the bull's liver, kidneys, and the fat that is on the bull's kidneys. Use the same words or phrases for liver, kidneys, and the fat that is on the bull's kidneys as you used in previous passages.

Then Moses takes the bull's skin, meat, and inside organs outside the camp. Use the same words for the bull's skin, meat, and inside organs as you used in previous passages.

Moses takes all these things outside the camp to burn these things. It is important to remember that the camp is where the Israelites lived. Moses is taking the bull's skin, meat, and inside organs away from where the Israelites lived. Use the same word for camp as you used in previous passages.

Moses follows all of Yahweh's instructions exactly as Yahweh said. In this passage, the narrator calls God "Yahweh." Use the same word or phrase for Yahweh as you used in previous passages. Look up Yahweh in the Master Glossary for more information.

Then, Moses brings the ram to Aaron and Aaron's sons. It is important to remember that a ram is a male sheep. Use the same word or phrase for ram as you used in previous passages.

Moses kills the ram as a burnt offering to Yahweh and throws the ram's blood on the side of the altar. It is important to remember that Yahweh gave Moses the instructions on how to sacrifice a burnt offering in Leviticus 1. Use the same word or phrase for burnt offering and throwing the blood on the side of the altar as you used in previous passages.

After Aaron and Aaron's sons lay their hands on the ram's head, Moses kills the ram and throws the blood on the sides of the altar. Then Moses cuts the ram into pieces and burns the ram's head, pieces of the ram, and the ram's fat on the altar. Use the same words or phrases for the ram's head, pieces of the ram, and the ram's fat as you used in previous passages.

Moses washes the ram's internal organs and legs with water. Use the same words or phrases for internal organs and rams' legs as you used in previous passages.

Moses burns all that is left of the ram on the altar. The offering is a fire offering that smells good to Yahweh. Use the same word or phrase for fire offering as you used in previous passages, and refer to fire offering in the Master Glossary for more information.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 8:22–29
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 8:22–29 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 8:22–29 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 8:22–29 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In the last story, Moses sacrificed a bull and a male sheep to make the Tent of Meeting, the altar, Aaron, and Aaron's sons ritually clean and ready to serve God. In this story, Moses continues the rituals to make Aaron and Aaron's sons ready to serve Yahweh as priests. Before the ceremony started, Moses brought two male sheep to the Tent of Meeting. Now, Moses sacrifices the second male sheep, or ram. Moses calls this sheep the "ram of ordination." It is important to remember that an ordination is a ceremony that officially appoints someone to a new role in the community.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time when someone in your community gained a new role or position within the community. What did your community do to show that the person had new responsibilities now? Pause this audio here.

Moses brings the ram of ordination to Aaron and Aaron's sons, then Aaron and Aaron's sons place their hands on the ram's head. Then Moses kills the ram. Moses smears some of the ram's blood on Aaron's right earlobe, Aaron's right thumb, and the big toe on Aaron's right foot.

Stop here and look at a picture of a person with the right earlobe, hand, and foot circled. Then look at specific pictures of the right earlobe, right thumb, and the big toe on a person's right foot. Pause this audio here.

After Moses puts the blood on Aaron's right earlobe, thumb, and big toe, Moses has Aaron's sons step in front of everyone. Then Moses smears some of the ram's blood on each of Aaron's sons' right earlobe, thumb, and big toe. The story does not explain specifically why Yahweh told Moses to smear the ram's blood on Aaron and Aaron's sons. However, Yahweh probably told Moses to smear the blood on Aaron and Aaron's sons to make those men ritually clean so that Aaron and Aaron's sons could serve Yahweh as priests. The Israelites thought that the right side of a person's body was more honorable or important than the left side and that the ear, hands, and feet were the most distant parts of a person's body. When Moses put the blood on those parts of Aaron and Aaron's sons' bodies, Moses showed the Israelites that Aaron and Aaron's sons were totally and completely clean and could do honorable work as priests.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What parts of your body does your culture think are the most honorable or important parts? What do you say when you want to talk about a person's whole body? Pause this audio here.

Then Moses throws the rest of the ram's blood against the sides of the altar.

Stop here and, as a group, look at a picture of the altar. Pause this audio here.

Then Moses cuts off the ram's fatty tail, all the fat on all of the ram's internal organs, the best part of the ram's liver, both of the ram's kidneys along with their fat, and the ram's right thigh.

Stop here and look at these pictures as a group: Look at a picture of sheep fat. Look at a picture of a sheep with its fatty tail circled. Look at a picture of a sheep's internal organs covered in fat. Look at a picture of the best part of a sheep's liver. Look at a picture of a sheep's kidneys. Look at a picture of a sheep with the right thigh circled. And look at a picture of the cut of meat that is a sheep's right thigh. Pause this audio here.

After Moses cuts apart the ram, Moses takes some bread from a basket. You may remember that Moses brought a basket full of bread to the Tent of Meeting before this ceremony started. There were three different kinds of bread that the Israelites had made without any yeast in the dough. The Israelites had already dedicated the bread to Yahweh, so that the bread belonged to Yahweh. This is why some translations say that the bread was "before Yahweh."

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time when your community dedicated something to God, a spiritual being, or an ancestor. What did you call the thing you dedicated after you finished the ceremony? Pause this audio here.

The first kind of bread that Moses takes out of the basket is a thick loaf of bread.

Stop here and look at a picture of a thick loaf of bread without any yeast in it. Pause this audio here.

The second kind of bread is another thick loaf of bread, but the Israelites had used olive oil to make this second thick loaf.

Stop here and look at a picture of a thick loaf of bread without yeast that also has olive oil in it, and a picture of olive oil. Pause this audio here.

The third kind of bread is a thin loaf of bread.

Stop here and look at a picture of a thin loaf of bread without yeast. Pause this audio here.

Moses gives all the bread and all the different kinds of fat and meat that Moses had cut off the ram to Aaron and Aaron's sons. Aaron and Aaron's sons wave the bread, the fat, and the meat in the air to show Yahweh that they are giving the bread, fat, and meat to Yahweh. Then Moses takes all the bread, fat, and meat from Aaron and Aaron's sons and completely burns up the bread, fat, and meat on top of the burnt offering. The bread, fat, and meat are an ordination sacrifice. This sacrifice officially makes Aaron and Aaron's sons into Yahweh's priests. The smoke from the bread, fat, and meat burning up smells good to Yahweh. It is important to remember that when the storyteller says that something smells good to Yahweh, the storyteller is saying that Yahweh accepts and appreciates the offering that the people made.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time you gave a gift to God, a spiritual power, or an ancestor. How did you know that God, the spiritual power, or the ancestor appreciated the gift? Pause this audio here.

After the bread, fat, and meat finish burning, Moses takes the ram's breast meat and waves it before Yahweh to show that Moses is giving the meat to Yahweh.

Stop here and look at a picture of a ram's breast meat and a picture of a ram with the breast circled. Pause this audio here.

Moses keeps the ram's breast meat to eat it himself because that is what Yahweh told Moses to do.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 8:22–29 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has two scenes.

In the first scene: Moses kills the ram of ordination and smears blood on Aaron and Aaron's sons.

In the second scene: Moses places the bread, fat, and meat in the hands of Aaron and Aaron's sons, who wave the bread, fat, and meat in front of the Tent of Meeting. Then Moses burns the bread, fat, and meat on the altar.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Moses
  • Aaron
  • Aaron's sons
  • The assembly of Israelites
  • And Yahweh

The story does not specifically mention the assembly of Israelites, but the Israelites are still watching Moses prepare Aaron and Aaron's sons to be priests.

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

In the first scene, Moses is probably in the courtyard near the altar of burnt offering. Moses brings the ram of ordination close to Aaron and Aaron's sons. Remember that Moses had brought two rams to the Tent of Meeting, and this ram of ordination is the second ram. Aaron and Aaron's sons place their hands on the ram's head, and then Moses kills the ram. Moses smears some of the ram's blood on Aaron's right earlobe, the thumb on Aaron's right hand, and the big toe on Aaron's right foot. Then, Moses has Aaron's sons stand in front of everyone, and Moses smears the ram's blood on the same places on each of Aaron's sons.

Stop here and get a small bowl filled with water. Have one person pretend to be Moses and one or more people pretend to be Aaron and Aaron's sons. Have the person who is pretending to be Moses smear the water on the right earlobe, right thumb, and big toe of the right foot of the person or people pretending to be Aaron and Aaron's sons. Pause this audio here.

After Moses finishes smearing the blood on Aaron and Aaron's sons, Moses throws the rest of the blood onto the sides of the altar of burnt offering.

Stop here and find a large rock or tree to use as an altar for this activity. Take the bowl of water from the previous activity and move the bowl quickly through the air toward the rock or tree so that the water flies out of the bowl and lands on the sides of the rock or tree. Remember how you described this action in previous passages. Pause this audio here.

In the second scene, Moses cuts up the ram. Moses cuts out the ram's fat, the ram's fatty tail, the fat that was on the ram's internal organs, the long part, or best part, of the ram's liver, the ram's kidneys and their fat, and the ram's right thigh. Then Moses takes the three kinds of bread from the basket of bread that belonged to Yahweh. Moses hands all the bread, fat, and meat to Aaron and Aaron's sons. Then Aaron and Aaron's sons wave the fat, bread, and meat in the air before Yahweh. When someone does something before Yahweh, it means the person does it in the presence of Yahweh, which is at the Tent of Meeting. Moses, Aaron, and Aaron's sons may be standing near the altar of burnt offering in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting, facing the tent. We are not sure exactly how a person would wave a wave offering. It is likely that the person holds the offering, then raises and lowers their arms one or more times.

Stop here and find objects that you will use to represent the different kinds of bread, fat, and meat. If you have bread, fat, and meat that you can use for this exercise, use those instead of other objects. Have one person pretend to be Moses, and have other people pretend to be Aaron and Aaron's sons. Practice having the person playing Moses hand the objects that represent the bread, fat, and meat to Aaron and Aaron's sons, and then have the people playing Aaron and Aaron's sons wave those objects up and down in the air. Pause this audio here.

After Aaron and Aaron's sons wave the fat, bread, and meat in the air, Moses takes the bread, fat, and meat from Aaron and Aaron's sons and burns the bread, fat, and meat on the altar. The story says that the meat from the first ram that Moses killed for the burnt offering is still burning on the altar when Moses adds the bread, fat, and meat from the second ram. This means that the bread, fat, and meat burn up in the fire at the same time as the meat from the burnt offering that Moses sacrificed to Yahweh in the previous story.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will show that Moses places the bread, fat, and meat from the ordination offering on top of the meat from the burnt offering when you act out this story in the next script. Pause this audio here.

The bread, fat, and meat are an ordination offering that makes Yahweh happy with Moses, Aaron, Aaron's sons, and the Israelites. It is an offering by fire because it burns up on the altar.

After Moses puts the bread, fat, and meat on the altar, Moses takes the ram's breast meat and waves it as a wave offering while Moses faces the Tent of Meeting. Yahweh told Moses to do this because Yahweh wanted to give the ram's breast meat to Moses.

Stop here and find something to use for the ram's breast meat. Take turns practicing waving the meat up and down in the air. Pause this audio here.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 8:22–29 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has two scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Moses
  • Aaron
  • Aaron's sons
  • The assembly of Israelites
  • And Yahweh

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

Moses brings the second ram over to Aaron and Aaron's sons. Aaron and Aaron's sons place their hands on the ram's head. Then Moses kills the ram and takes some of the ram's blood. Moses smears the blood on Aaron's right earlobe, right thumb, and right big toe. Then Moses tells Aaron's sons to stand in front of everyone, and Moses smears the blood on the right earlobes, right thumbs, and right big toes of Aaron's sons.

Pause the drama.

Ask the people playing Aaron and his sons, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people might answer things like:

  • Now every part of me is ritually clean, and I can serve Yahweh as Yahweh's priest; or
  • Yahweh has honored me so much. I cannot believe I am finally able to serve Yahweh as a priest.
Continue the drama.

Then Moses throws the rest of the blood on the sides of the altar. Once Moses is done throwing the blood, Moses cuts the ram apart so that Moses has the ram's fat and fatty tail as well as the fat that was on the ram's internal organs, the best part of the ram's liver, the ram's kidneys, the fat that was on the ram's kidneys, and the ram's right thigh. Then Moses turns to the basket of bread that belongs to Yahweh. Moses takes out three kinds of bread, which have no yeast. The first kind is a thick loaf, the second kind is a thick loaf that the Israelites baked with olive oil, and the third kind is a thin loaf. Moses puts all the bread, fat, and meat into Aaron's and Aaron's sons' hands. Aaron and Aaron's sons wave the bread, fat, and meat while facing the Tent of Meeting.

Pause the drama.

Ask the people playing Aaron and Aaron's sons, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people might answer things like:

  • I am so thankful I can give this gift to Yahweh; or
  • I am so excited to be a priest!
Continue the drama.

Moses takes the bread, fat, and meat back from Aaron and Aaron's sons and puts the bread, fat, and meat in the fire on the altar where the meat from the burnt offering is. Yahweh sees the ordination offering and accepts it.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am so glad that Aaron and Aaron's sons gave this offering to me; or
  • It is almost time for Aaron and Aaron's sons to be my priests; or
  • I am glad I chose Aaron and Aaron's sons to be my priests.
Continue the drama.

Then Moses waves the ram's breast meat while Moses faces the Tent of Meeting to give the meat to Yahweh. Yahweh gives the ram's breast meat to Moses for Moses to eat.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Moses, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am so thankful to Yahweh for this meat; or
  • I am giving this meat to Yahweh as a gift, and then Yahweh is giving the meat back to me.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 8:22–29 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

Moses brought the second ram to Aaron and Aaron's sons. A ram is a male sheep. Use the same word or phrase for ram and for sons as you used in previous passages. Sons is in the Master Glossary.

The ram was a ram of ordination. It is important to remember that ordination is a ceremony that gives someone a new role or position within the community. You will remember that the original name for the ordination offering reminds the priests of the way that Moses filled Aaron's hands with the bread, fat, and meat for the wave offering. Use the same word or phrase for ordination as you used in previous passages.

Moses killed the ram and smeared the ram's blood on Aaron's right earlobe. Use the same word or phrase for killing an animal that you have used in previous passages.

Stop here and look at a picture of a person with the right earlobe, right thumb, and right big toe circled. Then look at a picture of a right earlobe. Discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for the right earlobe. If you have already translated this phrase in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Then Moses smeared the ram's blood on Aaron's right thumb.

Stop here and look at a picture of a right thumb. Discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for the right thumb. If you have already translated this phrase in another book of the Bible, use the same word or phrase that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Finally, Moses smeared the ram's blood on Aaron's right big toe.

Stop here and look at a picture of a right big toe. Discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for the right big toe. If you have already translated this phrase in another book of the Bible, use the same word or phrase that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Then Moses told Aaron's sons to stand in front of everyone, and Moses smeared the blood on Aaron's sons' right earlobes, right thumbs, and right big toes. Then Moses threw the rest of the blood around the altar. Talk about throwing the blood on the sides of the altar in the same way you have in previous passages. Use the same word or phrase for altar as you used in previous passages. For more information about altar, refer to the Master Glossary.

Then Moses cut up the ram. Moses took out the ram's fat, fatty tail, internal organs, the best part of the ram's liver, kidneys, the fat around the kidneys, and the right thigh. Use the same words or phrases for these parts of the ram as you used in previous passages.

After Moses finished cutting up the ram, Moses took the bread out of its basket. The bread in the basket belonged to Yahweh. Yahweh is God's personal name. Use the same word or phrase for Yahweh as you used in previous passages. Look up Yahweh in the Master Glossary for more information.

The Israelites made all the bread without any yeast. Use the same word or phrase to talk about bread without yeast as you used in previous passages.

Moses took three different kinds of bread out of the basket. People made all of these types of bread without yeast. The first kind of bread was a thick loaf. The second kind of bread was a thick loaf of bread that the Israelites made with olive oil. The third kind of bread was a thin loaf of bread.

Stop here and discuss what phrases you will use for these three kinds of bread. Pause this audio here.

Moses placed the kinds of bread on the fat and the meat and handed it all to Aaron and Aaron's sons. Aaron and Aaron's sons gave the bread, fat, and meat to Yahweh by waving these things in the air while Aaron and Aaron's sons faced the Tent of Meeting. This was a wave offering. Use the same word or phrase for wave offering as you have used in previous passages. For more information about wave offering, refer to the Master Glossary.

Then Moses took the bread, fat, and meat from Aaron and Aaron's sons and burned the bread, fat, and meat on the altar. The ram that was the burnt offering was still burning on the altar when Moses added the bread, fat, and meat. Use the same word or phrase for burnt offering as you used in previous passages. Look up burnt offerings in the Master Glossary for more information.

The bread, fat, and meat were ordination offerings that made a good smell for Yahweh. It was a fire offering for Yahweh. An ordination offering appointed Aaron and Aaron's sons to officially become Yahweh's priests. Use the same words or phrases for ordination offering and fire offering as you used in previous passages. Fire offering is in the Master Glossary.

Last, Moses gave the ram's breast meat to Yahweh as a wave offering. Use the same word or phrase to talk about the ram's breast meat as you used in previous passages. The ram's breast meat was Yahweh's gift, or portion, to Moses for Moses to eat. Use the same word or phrase for portion of an offering as you have used in previous passages.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 8:30–36
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 8:30–36 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 8:30–36 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 8:30–36 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In the last story, Moses killed the ram of ordination for Aaron and Aaron's sons. Now Moses starts the last steps of the ceremony that officially makes Aaron and Aaron's sons into Yahweh's priests. Moses takes some of the blood that is on the altar and some anointing oil, and sprinkles both liquids onto Aaron, Aaron's sons, and the clothing that Aaron and Aaron's sons are wearing. Moses might have sprinkled the blood and oil one at a time. Or Moses might have mixed the blood and oil together into a new mixture and then sprinkled the mixture on Aaron, Aaron's sons, and then onto Aaron's and Aaron's sons' clothing. Either way, the sprinkling ceremony shows all the Israelites that Aaron and Aaron's sons now have a special relationship with Yahweh and with the Tent of Meeting. Aaron and Aaron's sons are the only Israelites whom Yahweh allows to make sacrifices on Yahweh's altar. Aaron and Aaron's sons can only make the sacrifices when they wear their special priest clothing.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Who can use religious things or do religious rituals in your community? Tell a story about a time that person interacted with religious things or rituals. What kinds of clothing did the person need to wear? How did the community know that the person was using religious things or doing a religious ritual? Pause this audio here.

In the last story, Moses killed the ram of ordination, but Moses did not burn the entire ram on the altar. Moses only burnt the ram's fat and some of the ram's meat. Now, Moses tells Aaron and Aaron's sons to cook the rest of the meat. The word in the original language for cooking here does not tell us how people cooked the meat. Sometimes the word seems to refer to boiling food in water, but it can mean other kinds of cooking as well.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about the last time you cooked meat. How did you cook the meat? Pause this audio here.

Moses tells Aaron and Aaron's sons to cook the meat at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. This means that Aaron and Aaron's sons are not supposed to go outside the courtyard that surrounds the Tent of Meeting. Because Aaron and Aaron's sons are becoming Yahweh's priests, the ram's meat is even more holy than normal sacrifices. This means that Aaron and Aaron's sons cannot eat the meat outside of the Tent of Meeting, as the Israelites would normally eat the meat of the fellowship or peace offering.

Stop here and look at a picture of the Tent of Meeting and the area in the courtyard outside of it. Pause this audio here.

In the last story, Moses burnt some bread on the altar from a special basket as a sacrifice to Yahweh. In this story, Moses tells Aaron and Aaron's sons to eat the rest of the bread that is in the basket. Moses repeats how important this is and says that Aaron and Aaron's sons should eat this meat just as Moses says to. Then Moses tells Aaron and Aaron's sons to burn any of the meat or bread that Aaron and Aaron's sons do not eat. Aaron and Aaron's sons cannot save any of the leftover meat or bread to eat at another time.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about an important meal in your community. Where do you eat the meal? What rules do you follow about what you need to eat and when you need to eat the food? Pause this audio here.

Next, Moses tells Aaron and Aaron's sons to live in the Tent of Meeting for the next seven days. Aaron and Aaron's sons cannot go and walk around the rest of the camp with the other Israelites. Aaron and Aaron's sons need to stay close to Yahweh's Tent of Meeting until the very last day of the official ordination process. That process will take seven full days to finish. The Israelites believed that the number seven meant that something was complete or perfect, so that is why it took seven days for Aaron and Aaron's sons to complete the process to become Yahweh's priests.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time when someone in your community got married, became an adult, or became someone who could interact with spirits, ancestors, or gods. How long did the ceremonies take? Why do the rituals take that amount of time? Pause this audio here.

After Moses tells Aaron and Aaron's sons how long it will take to become Yahweh's priests, Moses says that everything Moses did from when Moses first brought everything to the Tent of Meeting to start the ceremony until now was exactly what Yahweh told Moses to do. Moses explains that Moses needed to do all these things to atone for Aaron and Aaron's sons so that Aaron and Aaron's sons could be holy and serve Yahweh. Then Moses reminds Aaron and Aaron's sons to live in the Tent of Meeting for seven days and do everything Yahweh says to do so that Yahweh does not kill Aaron and Aaron's sons. Because Aaron and Aaron's sons are Yahweh's priests, Aaron and Aaron's sons are set apart for special service to Yahweh in a way that other Israelites are not. Anything the priests do that disobeys Yahweh makes Yahweh's holy things ritually dirty, and that is a very serious problem.

Stop here and discuss this question as a community: Who are the most important people in your community? Tell a story about the kinds of rules or behaviors those people need to follow that are different from the rules that other people in the community need to follow. Pause this audio here.

Moses finishes when Moses says again that everything Moses told Aaron and Aaron's sons is what Yahweh told Moses to tell Aaron and Aaron's sons. Then Aaron and Aaron's sons obey Yahweh and do everything Moses said to do.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 8:30–36 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has two scenes.

In the first scene: Moses sprinkles anointing oil and blood on Aaron, Aaron's sons, and their clothing.

In the second scene: Moses gives Aaron and Aaron's sons instructions about what to do for the next seven days.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Moses
  • Aaron
  • Aaron's sons
  • The assembly of Israelites
  • And Yahweh

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

It is important to remember that the assembly of Israelites is still watching Moses, Aaron, and Aaron's sons, even though the storyteller does not specifically talk about the Israelites.

In the first scene, Moses takes some of the anointing oil to sprinkle on Aaron and Aaron's sons. Moses also takes some of the blood off of the altar to sprinkle on Aaron and Aaron's sons. Moses sprinkles both the oil and the blood on Aaron, Aaron's sons, and the clothing that Aaron and Aaron's sons are wearing. Moses probably mixed the blood and oil together, but Moses might have sprinkled the blood and oil on Aaron and Aaron's sons one at a time. Either way, Moses sprinkles the oil and the blood on Aaron and Aaron's clothing and on Aaron's sons and Aaron's sons' clothing to dedicate Aaron, Aaron's sons, and their clothing to serve Yahweh. We do not know exactly how Moses sprinkled the oil and blood. Moses may have used his fingers to dip in the bowl and then flick the oil and blood on the people and their clothing.

Stop here and get two bowls of water. Have one or two people pretend to be Aaron and Aaron's sons. One of the bowls of water represents the anointing oil. Practice sprinkling, or putting, the water from that bowl on the people who are pretending to be Aaron and Aaron's sons. Make sure you sprinkle the water on those people and their clothing. Then, pour one bowl of water on a smooth rock or tree trunk to represent the blood that is on the altar. Practice wiping the water off the rock and tree trunk and sprinkling it on the person or people who are pretending to be Aaron and Aaron's sons. How do you describe these actions? How will you describe these actions in your translation? Pause this audio here.

In the second scene, Moses gives Aaron and Aaron's sons more instructions. Moses repeats himself a lot in these instructions to show how important and serious the instructions are.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time when you gave very important instructions to someone else. How did you make sure that the other person knew how important those instructions were? Tell a story about a time when someone gave you very important instructions. How did you know how important those instructions were? Pause this audio here.

Moses tells Aaron and Aaron's sons to cook the meat from the ram of ordination that Moses did not burn on the altar. Aaron and Aaron's sons need to cook the meat without leaving the courtyard around the Tent of Meeting. Aaron and Aaron's sons need to eat the ram's meat as well as the bread that Moses did not sacrifice on the altar. Aaron and Aaron's sons need to eat both the meat and the bread while they are still in the Tent of Meeting courtyard. Moses explains that this is just what Moses said to do when Moses said that Aaron and Aaron's sons needed to eat the meat and the bread.

Next, Moses explains that Aaron and Aaron's sons need to stay at the Tent of Meeting for seven days. Aaron and Aaron's sons cannot leave the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting for any reason until the ordination ceremonies are completely finished. Moses explains that it will take seven full days for Aaron and Aaron's sons to finish the ordination ceremonies. Moses explains that Yahweh told Moses to do all these ceremonies to make atonement for Aaron and Aaron's sons, so that they can have a good relationship with Yahweh. Now Aaron and Aaron's sons need to stay at the Tent of Meeting all day and all night for seven days to serve Yahweh as Yahweh said to. If Aaron and Aaron's sons do not obey these instructions, then Yahweh will kill Aaron and Aaron's sons. Moses explains that Yahweh told Moses to tell Aaron and Aaron's sons all of these instructions.

The story ends when it explains that Aaron and Aaron's sons listen to Yahweh and do everything that Moses said to do.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 8:30–36 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has two scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Moses
  • Aaron
  • Aaron's sons
  • The assembly of Israelites
  • And Yahweh

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

It is important to remember that the Israelites are still watching Moses, Aaron, and Aaron's sons, even though the story does not specifically talk about the Israelites.

In the first scene, Moses takes some of the anointing oil and then takes some of the blood that Moses had thrown on the altar. Moses sprinkles both the blood and the oil on Aaron and Aaron's clothing and on Aaron's sons and their clothing.

Pause the drama.

and ask the people playing Aaron and his sons, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people might answer things like:

  • I am going to have to be very careful about how I act now since Yahweh has given me such an important role in the community; or
  • I cannot believe that I get to serve Yahweh by making sacrifices to Yahweh now; or
  • I feel so honored.
Continue the drama.

In the second scene, Moses tells Aaron and Aaron's sons to cook the meat by the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. Moses says to also take the bread that was still in the basket from the ordination offering and eat the bread with the meat there at the entrance. Moses explains that Aaron and Aaron's sons need to eat the meat and the bread just like Moses said to do when Moses first said that Aaron and Aaron's sons needed to eat the meat and bread. Then Moses warns Aaron and Aaron's sons that they must burn any meat or bread that they do not eat.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Moses, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing Moses might say things like:

  • I really want Aaron and Aaron's sons to realize how serious and important this is; or
  • I am excited that my brother is almost Yahweh's priest; or
  • I really want to make sure that Aaron and Aaron's sons obey Yahweh's instructions.
Continue the drama.

Then Moses explains that Aaron and Aaron's sons need to stay at the Tent of Meeting for seven days and cannot leave until after all the ordination ceremonies. Moses explains that it will take seven days to finish the ordination ceremonies. Moses explains that Moses did all the different rituals and sacrifices to atone for Aaron and Aaron's sons so that Aaron and Aaron's sons can serve Yahweh as Yahweh's priests. Now, Aaron and Aaron's sons need to stay at the Tent of Meeting all day and all night for seven full days and do everything that Yahweh says to do so that Yahweh does not kill Aaron and Aaron's sons. Moses ends his speech and says that Yahweh told Moses to give Aaron and Aaron's sons all of these instructions.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Moses, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing Moses might say things like:

  • I do not want Aaron and Aaron's sons to die! I want Aaron and Aaron's sons to know how important it is to follow these instructions; or
  • I want to make sure that Aaron and Aaron's sons remember all of these instructions so they know what to do; or
  • I am worried Aaron and Aaron's sons will forget, and then Yahweh will have to kill Aaron and Aaron's sons.

Ask the people playing Aaron and Aaron's sons, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people might say things like:

  • These rules must be very important and serious because Moses keeps repeating them. We need to pay attention and do everything Moses says; or
  • I do not want to die! I need to listen to what Moses is saying; or
  • Yahweh has given me so much honor by making me Yahweh's priest. I need to make sure I do not do something that would make Yahweh's holy things ritually dirty.
Continue the drama.

Aaron and Aaron's sons follow all of Yahweh's instructions and do everything that Moses said to do.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 8:30–36 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

First, Moses took some of the anointing oil to sprinkle on Aaron and Aaron's sons and the clothing these men were wearing. It is important to remember that anointing oil was oil that someone would pour onto someone else to show that God chose the person for a special task or role. Use the same words or phrases for anointing oil and sons as you used in previous passages. Look up anoint and sons in the Master Glossary for more information.

Then Moses took some of the blood from the altar to sprinkle on Aaron and Aaron's sons and their clothing. Use the same word or phrase for altar as you used in previous passages. Look up altar in the Master Glossary for more information.

Moses sprinkled the oil and blood on Aaron, Aaron's sons, and the clothing that Aaron and Aaron's sons were wearing to consecrate them. This means that Moses was showing everyone that Yahweh had chosen Aaron and Aaron's sons to be Yahweh's. Aaron and Aaron's sons were going to be Yahweh's priests and serve Yahweh in a way no one else could. Aaron and Aaron's sons were holy. Use the same word or phrase for consecrate as you used in previous passages. Look up consecrate in the Master Glossary for more information.

Then Moses told Aaron and Aaron's sons to cook the meat from the ram of ordination at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

Stop here and look at a picture of the Tent of Meeting and the entrance area. Then, as a group, discuss what word or phrase you will use for the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. Look up the tabernacle in the Master Glossary for more information. Pause this audio here.

Moses told Aaron and Aaron's sons how to eat the meat and bread from the basket for the ordination offering. Then Moses said not to leave the Tent of Meeting until the last day of their ordination. An ordination is a ceremony that gives someone a new role or responsibility within the community. Use the same words for basket, ordination, and ordination offering as you used in previous passages. Basket is in the Master Glossary.

Moses explains that Moses did everything for the ordination ceremony because Yahweh told Moses to do it that specific way. Yahweh is God's personal name. Use the same word or phrase for Yahweh as you used in previous passages. Look up Yahweh in the Master Glossary for more information. Moses did all the ceremonies to atone for Aaron and Aaron's sons. Use the same word for atone as you have used in previous passages. Look up atone in the Master Glossary for more information.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.
