Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 15:19–24 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

NOTE: This passage talks about subjects that you may want to discuss in groups of only men and only women. Stop here and discuss as a group if you will listen to this passage in groups of only men and only women. Pause this audio here.

In this part of Leviticus, Yahweh is talking about the things that make people ritually clean and unclean, or dirty. In the previous two passages, Yahweh told Moses and Aaron to tell the Israelites what men need to do if a man has pus coming out of his penis. Yahweh also explains what a man and woman need to do when the man and woman have sex with each other. In this passage, Yahweh explains what women need to do when the women are on their period, which is the time of the month when a woman bleeds from her vagina.

First, Yahweh says that when a woman has a discharge of blood that is the regular discharge from her body, the woman will be ritually unclean or dirty for seven days. While the woman is ritually dirty, anyone who touches the woman will also be ritually dirty until the evening, which means after the sun sets. The Israelites started each new day when the sun set, so Yahweh is saying that the person will be ritually dirty until the end of the day.

Then Yahweh explains what happens when the woman is ritually dirty in this way. Everything that the woman lies on while the woman is ritually dirty will also be ritually dirty. Anyone who touches the woman's bed needs to wash their clothes and bathe in water, and that person will be ritually dirty until evening. In Israelite culture, people often used a thick piece of cloth as a bed. People also sometimes used a short wooden table with a mat on top as a bed.

Stop here as a group and look at an image of a mat. Pause this audio here.

Stop here as a group and look at an image of a short table. Pause this audio here.

Also, anyone who touches anything the woman sits on needs to wash their clothes and bathe in water, and that person will be ritually dirty until evening. Then Yahweh says these rules again in a different way. Yahweh says that whether it is the bed the woman lay on or anything the woman sat on, if anyone touches those things, that person will be ritually dirty until evening. These rules are similar to the rules for if a man has pus coming out of his penis. Yahweh does not mention anything here about what people need to do if the woman who is on her period touches pottery, or if the woman spits on someone. This is probably because the woman is not sick while the woman is on her period, so the woman does not need to be as strict about what the woman touches.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what are the rules women need to follow when a woman is on her period? Pause this audio here.

Additionally, Yahweh says that if any man has sex with a woman who is on her period and the woman's impurity touches the man, the man will be ritually dirty for seven days. The woman's impurity is the blood from the woman's period. Yahweh might mean that if the woman's period starts while the man and woman are having sex, then the man is ritually dirty. Later in Leviticus, Yahweh will tell the Israelites that men are never supposed to have sex with a woman while the woman is on her period. Yahweh will say that if a man and a woman have sex while the woman is on her period, then the community will cut the man and woman off from the people of Israel. Because Yahweh will say that later, here Yahweh probably means that if a man and woman have sex before the man and woman realize that the woman is on her period, then the man is ritually dirty for seven days.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what are the rules about having sex with a woman on her period? Pause this audio here.

While the man is ritually dirty, every bed the man lies on also becomes ritually dirty. Yahweh does not say it here, but that means that anyone who touches a bed that the man lies on will be ritually dirty as well.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 15:19–24 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has two scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh explains that a woman on her period is unclean or ritually dirty for seven days. Yahweh explains what people need to do if someone touches that woman, the bed the woman has lain on, or anything the woman sat on.

In the second scene: Yahweh explains what a man needs to do if the man sleeps with a woman and gets some of the woman's period blood on him.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Aaron
  • The Israelites
  • A woman on her period
  • Anyone who touches the woman on her period
  • Anyone who touches the bed that the woman on her period lay on
  • Anyone who touches anything that the woman on her period sat on
  • And a man who had sex with a woman on her period

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

In the first scene, Yahweh talks about when a woman has a flow of blood that is the regular flow of blood from her flesh. Here, Yahweh uses the word "flesh" to refer to the woman's vagina.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what words or phrases do people use to refer to a woman's vagina in a way that is appropriate? What word or phrase would work best in this context? Pause this audio here.

The regular flow of blood is a woman's period, or menstruation.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what words or phrases do people use to refer to a period, or menstruation? What word or phrase would work best in this context? Pause this audio here.

Then Yahweh gives three different situations that might happen whenever a woman is on her period. In the first situation, Yahweh says that if someone touches the woman, then that person will be ritually dirty until the evening. In the second situation, Yahweh says that anything a woman lies on while the woman is on her period becomes ritually dirty. In the third situation, anything the woman sits on while on her period becomes ritually dirty. If anyone touches anything the woman lies on, then that person becomes ritually dirty until evening. That person needs to wash themselves and their clothes. Also, if anyone touches anything the woman sat on, then that person becomes ritually dirty until evening and needs to wash themselves and their clothes. Finally, Yahweh says again that if someone touches anything the woman on her period has lain on or sat on, then that person will be ritually dirty until evening. Yahweh is summarizing the rules for when a woman is on her period.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how does a person summarize information that a person has given to someone else? Pause this audio here.

In the second scene, Yahweh explains that if a man has sex with a woman and the woman's period blood touches the man, then the man will be ritually dirty for seven days. While the man is ritually dirty, every bed the man lies on becomes ritually dirty. Probably this means that if someone touches the bed the man was lying on, then that person also becomes ritually dirty until evening, and that person needs to wash themselves and their clothes. Yahweh probably does not say that the person needs to wash their clothes and their hands here because the Israelites already know that Yahweh wants a ritually dirty person to wash.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 15:19–24 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has two scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Aaron
  • The Israelites
  • A woman on her period
  • Anyone who touches the woman on her period
  • Anyone who touches the bed that the woman on her period lay on
  • Anyone who touches anything that the woman on her period sat on
  • And a man who had sex with a woman on her period

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

In the first scene, Yahweh says that if a woman has a flow of blood that is the regular flow of blood from the woman's flesh, then the woman is ritually dirty.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing a woman on her period, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am in a lot of pain because of this period; or
  • I am sad because I am ritually dirty for seven days; or
  • I am glad that while I am on my period, I do not have to do my normal activities because I am ritually dirty.
Continue the drama.

If someone touches a woman who is on her period, then that person will be ritually dirty until the evening. Also, anything a woman lies on while the woman is on her period becomes ritually dirty, and anything the woman sits on becomes ritually dirty. If anyone touches anything the woman lies on, then that person becomes ritually dirty until evening. That person needs to wash themselves and their clothes. If someone touches anything the woman on her period sat on, then that person will be ritually dirty until evening, and that person needs to wash themselves and their clothes.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing anyone who touches the bed that the woman on her period lay on, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am frustrated that I have to wash because I touched this woman's bed; or
  • I do not really mind being ritually dirty until evening.
Continue the drama.

In the second scene, Yahweh explains that if a man has sex with a woman and the woman's period blood touches the man, then the man will be ritually dirty for seven days. While the man is ritually dirty, every bed the man lies on becomes ritually dirty.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing a man who had sex with a woman on her period, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I did not realize the woman was on her period when I had sex with the woman; or
  • I am frustrated because I am ritually dirty for the next seven days; or
  • I am glad that Yahweh decided not to punish me when I accidentally had sex with my wife during my wife's period.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 15:19–24 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

Yahweh says that if a woman has blood flowing from her vagina, then the woman is unclean or ritually dirty. Use the same word or phrase for ritually dirty as you used in previous passages. For more information on clean and unclean, refer to the Master Glossary.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for a woman who is bleeding during her regular monthly flow of blood. Pause this audio here.

Everyone who touches the woman will be ritually dirty until evening. Use the same word or phrase for evening as you used in previous passages.

People who touch the woman or her things must bathe in water. Use the same words or phrases for bathing in fresh water as you have used in previous passages.

Anyone who touches a bed that the woman who is bleeding has lain on will be ritually dirty until evening.

Stop here and look at the pictures of a mat and a short table that people might use as a bed. Discuss what word or phrase you will use for bed.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 15:25–33
content:
Hear and Heart

NOTE: This passage talks about subjects you may want to discuss in groups of only men and only women. Stop here and discuss as a group if you will listen to this passage in groups of only men and only women. Pause this audio here.

In this step, hear Leviticus 15:25–33 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 15:25–33 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 15:25–33 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

NOTE: This passage talks about subjects you may want to discuss in groups of only men and only women. Stop here and discuss as a group if you will listen to this passage in groups of only men and only women. Pause this audio here.

In this part of Leviticus, Yahweh is talking about things that make people ritually clean and ritually dirty. In the last few passages, Yahweh has been explaining what the Israelites need to do if someone has a discharge, which means that something flows from a person's genitals. In this passage, Yahweh starts by explaining what a woman needs to do if the woman has blood coming out of her vagina when the woman is not on her period, either because the blood started coming out at a completely different time or because the blood kept flowing past the normal seven days of a period. As long as the woman has blood coming out of her vagina, the woman is ritually dirty, just like when the woman has a normal period.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what does a woman need to do if the woman starts bleeding from her vagina when it is not the woman's period? Pause this audio here.

As long as the woman has the blood flowing from her vagina, any bed the woman lies on or anything the woman sits on becomes ritually dirty, just like when the woman has a normal period. Anyone who touches the things the woman lies on or sits on becomes ritually dirty, and that person needs to wash their clothes and themselves. After that, the person will stay ritually dirty until evening, when the new day starts.

When blood stops flowing from the woman's vagina, the woman has to wait seven days. After those seven days, the woman is ritually clean. Then, on the eighth day, the woman needs to take two turtledoves or two pigeons to a priest at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, which people also call the tabernacle. Turtledoves and pigeons are two different kinds of birds that Israelites sacrificed to Yahweh. The difference between the two birds is sometimes unclear.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of doves and pigeons. Pause this audio here.

The priest will use one of the birds to make a sin or purification offering and one of the birds to make a burnt offering. That is how the priest will make atonement for the woman who had blood flowing from her vagina. That means that when the priest makes the two offerings, Yahweh will restore Yahweh's relationship with the woman. Sometimes the Israelites thought that when someone became sick, Yahweh had made that person sick because that person had sinned. It is possible that the woman had to make an offering to get atonement because the woman had sinned. The woman also might need to make a sacrifice because the woman was not able to worship God while the woman had blood coming out of her vagina. The two birds were the least expensive animal sacrifice a person could make, so it seems that Yahweh did not consider a discharge as serious as something like a skin disease.

Yahweh wants the Israelites to follow these rules about what people who have a discharge from their genitals should do. If the Israelites do follow these rules, then the Israelites will keep themselves separate from ritual dirtiness. If the Israelites do not follow these rules, the Israelites will make Yahweh's Tent of Meeting or tabernacle, which is in the middle of the Israelite camp, ritually dirty. If the Israelites make Yahweh's tabernacle ritually dirty, Yahweh will kill the Israelites. The Israelites cannot go near anything holy, like the tabernacle, when the Israelites are ritually dirty.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do people treat things that are holy or religious? What happens to a person if someone breaks the rules about things that are religiously or spiritually important? Pause this audio here.

Then Yahweh says that these are the rules for anyone who has a discharge of any kind. These rules are the rules for a man who has semen come out of his penis, which makes the man ritually dirty. These rules are also the rules for a woman who is on her period, and these are the rules for any man or woman who has an abnormal discharge from their genitals. These rules are also the rules for a man who lies with a woman who is ritually dirty because she is bleeding during her normal monthly period of bleeding.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what does someone have to do when that person has a discharge coming from their genitals? How is that similar or different from the rules Yahweh has given in this and in the last four passages?

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 15:25–33 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has three scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh explains the rules for if a woman is bleeding from her vagina outside of the normal time of the woman's period.

In the second scene: Yahweh explains the rules for when a woman stops bleeding from her vagina.

In the third scene: Yahweh says that the Israelites need to keep ritually dirty things and people away from the tabernacle. Then Yahweh says again that these are the rules for when a person has a discharge coming out of their genitals.

The characters in this passage are:

  • A woman who has blood coming out of her vagina outside of the normal time of her period
  • A person who touches something that the woman laid on or sat on
  • The priest
  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Aaron
  • The Israelites
  • A man whose semen comes out of his penis
  • A woman who has her period
  • A person who has an abnormal discharge from their genitals
  • And a man who has sex with a woman who is ritually dirty from her period

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

Yahweh has been telling Moses and Aaron what rules Yahweh has for people who have something flowing out of their genitals. Yahweh had just explained what rules Yahweh has for when a woman has a period. Now, Yahweh explains to Moses and Aaron the rules for when a woman has blood flowing out of her vagina outside of the normal time of her period. Then Yahweh finishes the entire section on what people who have a discharge need to do.

In the first scene, Yahweh says that if a woman has blood coming from her vagina for a long time, and it either goes longer than the woman's normal period or the blood starts flowing outside the woman's normal time for her period, then the woman will become ritually dirty. The woman will be ritually dirty as long as the woman has blood flowing out of her vagina.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do you talk about blood flowing from a woman's vagina outside the normal time of a woman's period? What would be the most appropriate way for you to describe the situation here? Pause this audio here.

While the woman who has blood coming out of her vagina outside of the normal time of the woman's period is ritually dirty, anything that the woman lies on or sits on becomes ritually dirty, just like when the woman has her period. Yahweh wants to show the Israelites that the rules for a woman who has blood coming out of her vagina outside of the normal time of her period are the same rules as for a woman who has a normal period. Anyone who touches the bed this woman lay on, or something this woman sat on, will become ritually dirty. That person will need to wash their clothes and themselves. Then that person will be ritually dirty until evening.

In the second scene, Yahweh says that when the woman stops bleeding from her vagina in this abnormal way, the woman needs to wait seven days, and the woman will become clean after that. On the eighth day, the woman has to take two doves or two pigeons to the priest at the entrance to the tabernacle. The entrance was in the courtyard of the tabernacle, near the altar in the courtyard. The priest will use one of the birds to make a sin or purification offering and one of the birds to make a burnt offering. That is how the priest will make atonement for the woman who had blood flowing from her vagina. These are the same rules for how a man who had pus coming out of his penis needs to make atonement after the man becomes ritually clean. In both situations, the people need to restore their relationship with Yahweh, but in both cases, it is not as serious as something like a skin disease.

In the third scene, Yahweh finishes talking about what Israelite people need to do when someone has something come out of their genitals. Yahweh says that Moses and Aaron must keep the Israelites separate from their uncleanness or ritual dirtiness. When Yahweh says that the Israelites will be separate from their ritual dirtiness, Yahweh means that when the Israelites obey these rules, then the Israelites will stop one person from making everyone ritually dirty by spreading their ritual dirtiness. Yahweh also says that these rules will stop people from dying. The people will die if people make Yahweh's tabernacle ritually dirty, which Yahweh put in the middle of the Israelites' camp. Yahweh wants the Israelites to know that the Israelites need to keep holy things like the tabernacle from becoming ritually dirty.

Finally, Yahweh ends this section of Leviticus by explaining that these are the rules for people who have something flowing from their genitals. Then Yahweh again states which situations Yahweh is talking about: men who have semen coming out of their penis, which makes the men ritually dirty, women who have a period, people who have something abnormal coming out of their genitals, and a man who has sex with a woman who is ritually dirty. These are the situations Yahweh has talked about in Leviticus chapter 15.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 15:25–33 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has three scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • A woman who has blood coming out of her vagina outside of the normal time of her period
  • A person who touches something that the woman laid on or sat on
  • The priest
  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Aaron
  • The Israelites
  • A man whose semen comes out of his penis
  • A woman who has her period
  • A person who has an abnormal discharge from their genitals
  • And a man who has sex with a woman who is ritually dirty from her period

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

In the first scene, Yahweh says that if a woman has blood come out of her vagina outside of the normal time of the woman's period, then the woman becomes ritually dirty. The woman will be ritually dirty as long as the blood is coming out of her vagina, just like when the woman has a period. So, every bed the woman lies on and everything the woman sits on becomes ritually dirty as well.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing a woman who has blood coming out of her vagina outside of the normal time of her period, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • This is a really bad thing that is happening to me; or
  • I feel sad because I am unclean, and it feels like something is wrong with me; or
  • I feel sad because I cannot worship Yahweh until I am ritually clean again.
Continue the drama.

Anyone who touches something the woman laid on or sat on becomes ritually dirty, and that person needs to wash their clothes and themselves with water. Once the new day starts in the evening, the person will become ritually clean again.

In the second scene, Yahweh says that if the blood stops flowing from the woman's vagina, then the woman needs to wait seven days. After seven days without blood flowing from her vagina, the woman is clean again. On the eighth day, the woman needs to take two turtledoves or two pigeons to the priest at the entrance to the tabernacle. The priest will use one of the birds to make a purification offering and one of the birds to make a burnt offering. That is how the priest will make atonement for the woman who had blood flowing from her vagina.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing a woman who has blood coming out of her vagina outside of the normal time of her period, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am so happy that I can be ritually clean again; or
  • I am glad that Yahweh restored my relationship with Yahweh.
Continue the drama.

In the third scene, Yahweh says that when the Israelites obey these rules, the Israelites will keep themselves separate from ritual dirtiness, and the Israelites will not die because the Israelites will not make the tabernacle ritually dirty.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • It is really important to keep ritually dirty things away from the tabernacle; or
  • I am glad that Yahweh is telling us how we can be safe and have Yahweh's presence in our camp; or
  • I am scared because I could die if I do not obey these laws, so I will make sure to do the right thing.
Continue the drama.

Yahweh finishes by saying these are the laws for anyone who has a discharge: for a man who has semen coming out of his penis, for a woman who has a period, for anyone who has an abnormal discharge, and for a man who sleeps with a woman who is having a period.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 15:25–33 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

If a woman has blood coming out of her vagina outside of the normal time of the woman's period, then the woman is unclean or ritually dirty. Use the same word or phrase for ritually dirty as you used in previous passages. For more information on clean and unclean, refer to the Master Glossary.

The bed a woman lies on becomes ritually dirty. Israelites had two different types of beds. One kind was a thick mat that people lay on. The other kind of bed was a short wooden table that a person could lie on. Sometimes people would put a soft mat on a table. Use the same word or phrase for bed as you used in previous passages.

Anyone who touches what this woman lies on or sits on is ritually dirty until evening. Evening was the time that the new day started for the Israelites. Use the same word or phrase to translate evening as you used in previous passages.

Anyone who touches things the woman has sat on or lain on needs to wash themselves and their clothes with water. Use the same phrases for washing with water as you have used previously.

On the eighth day after the woman stops having blood come out of her vagina, the woman needs to take two turtledoves or two pigeons to the priest at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. The entrance was in the courtyard of the tabernacle, near the altar in the courtyard. Use the same word or phrase for the entrance to the Tent of Meeting that you used in previous passages.

Turtledoves and pigeons are two different kinds of birds that Israelites sacrificed to Yahweh. The difference between the two birds is unclear. Use the same words or phrases for turtledoves and pigeons as you used in previous passages. For more information on doves, refer to the Master Glossary.

Stop here as a group and look again at a photo of doves as needed. Pause this audio here.

The priests were the people who helped the Israelites have a good relationship with Yahweh, and the priests did that by sacrificing, or killing, animals to make these offerings for the Israelites. Use the same word or phrase for priests as you used in previous passages. For more information on priests, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh says that he has put his tabernacle in the middle of the Israelites' camp, because the tabernacle was where the Israelites met with Yahweh. The tabernacle is another way to talk about the Tent of Meeting. Use the same word or phrase for the tabernacle as you used in previous passages. For more information on tabernacle, refer to the Master Glossary.

The priest will use one bird to make a sin or purification offering. Use the same word or phrase for purification offering as you used in previous passages. For more information on purification offering, refer to the Master Glossary.

The priest will use the other bird to make a burnt offering. When people made a burnt offering, the people were showing Yahweh that the people were completely devoted to Yahweh by completely burning an animal. Use the same word or phrase for burnt offering as you used in previous passages. For more information on burnt offering, refer to the Master Glossary.

That is how the priest will make atonement for the woman who had blood flowing from her vagina. That means that when the priest makes the two offerings, Yahweh will restore Yahweh's relationship with the woman. Use the same word or phrases for atonement as you used in previous passages. For more information on atonement, refer to the Master Glossary.

Stop here and review as a team the words and phrases you have used for ideas like discharge, menstruation, and sex. Make sure that you have used similar words and phrases throughout Leviticus 15.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 16:1–5
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 16:1–5 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:1–5 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:1–5 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

The next five sections in Leviticus focus on one of the holidays that Yahweh told the people of Israel to celebrate every year. People called this holiday the Day of Atonement, the Day of Cleansing, or Yom Kippur. In this section, Yahweh began to tell Moses how to celebrate the Day of Atonement.

Two important things happened before Yahweh told Moses about the celebration. First, Moses had chosen Moses' older brother Aaron and Aaron's four sons to be Yahweh's priests. To be Yahweh's priests meant that only Aaron and Aaron's sons could burn incense to Yahweh and offer sacrifices of grain and animals to Yahweh. The second important thing that happened was that Aaron's two oldest sons, Nadab and Abihu, burned incense the wrong way and then died. It is unclear whether Nadab and Abihu burned the wrong kind of incense or whether Nadab and Abihu went in to try to see Yahweh when they were burning the incense.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of burning incense. Pause this audio here.

Because Nadab and Abihu burned incense the wrong way, Yahweh began this section by telling Moses to warn Aaron not to come into the Most Holy Place that is behind the curtain whenever Aaron wants to. Yahweh allowed Aaron and Aaron's sons to go into the Holy Place inside the tent where the lampstand, table, and incense altar are. But Yahweh does not allow Aaron and Aaron's sons to go behind the curtain to the Most Holy Place where the ark of the covenant is.

Stop here as a group and look at a diagram of the Tent of Meeting. Notice the difference between the area behind the curtain and the main part of the tent. Pause this audio here.

The top part of the ark of the covenant was the "atonement cover," and the people of Israel thought of the cover as Yahweh's earthly throne. Yahweh had told Moses that Yahweh would talk to Moses from above the atonement cover that was on the ark of the covenant. But no one else could go into that space, the Most Holy Place where the ark of the covenant is. If someone went in to try to see Yahweh, that person would die.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of the ark of the covenant. Notice the atonement cover where Yahweh said Yahweh would talk to Moses. Pause this audio here.

But we hear later in this part of Leviticus that once a year, on the Day of Atonement, the high priest could go behind the curtain. When the high priest did this, the high priest would burn incense to create a cloud of smoke. Some people believe that the cloud was to make it so that the high priest would not accidentally see Yahweh and then die.

After Yahweh told Moses to warn Aaron not to come into the Most Holy Place behind the curtain whenever Aaron wants, Yahweh told Moses the only way that Aaron may come into that area. On the Day of Atonement, Aaron could go into the Most Holy Place behind the curtain. When Aaron did, Aaron needed to bring to the Tent of Meeting a young bull for a purification or sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of a young bull and a ram. Pause this audio here.

Aaron also needed to wear special linen clothes. These clothes included a linen tunic, linen undergarments, a linen sash around Aaron's waist, and a linen turban or hat on Aaron's head. These linen clothes were different from the usual clothes that the high priest would wear. These linen clothes were simpler and less fancy. Nobody knows exactly why these clothes were different, but the priests only wore these clothes for the Day of Atonement ritual. These linen clothes were holy to Yahweh, and so people needed to treat the clothes with extra respect.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: When people in your culture perform religious or sacred rituals, what kind of special clothing do those people need to wear? Why? Pause this audio here.

In order to prepare for this yearly ceremony, Aaron needed to wash his body with water and then put on the special linen clothes. Washing with water was an important part to be ritually clean. One of the purposes of this annual ritual was to cleanse everyone and everything from all of the ways that the people of Israel had betrayed and rebelled against Yahweh. When people betrayed Yahweh and rebelled against Yahweh, they had made the priest's family, the holy place, the bronze altar, and the people of Israel ritually and spiritually dirty. That ritual and spiritual dirtiness had built up throughout the year. The Day of Atonement was the day on which the high priest performed the ritual to cleanse everything and everyone from being ritually and spiritually dirty. Because of that, the high priest got ready for the Day of Atonement by first washing his body with water to become clean and then putting on the holy linen clothes.

After Aaron had washed and dressed in the appropriate clothing, the representatives of the people of Israel needed to give Aaron two young goats, probably male, for a purification offering, and one ram for a burnt offering.

Stop and look at a picture of a young goat.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:1–5 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has two scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells Moses to warn Aaron that Aaron cannot come into the Most Holy Place behind the curtain whenever Aaron wants.

In the second scene: Yahweh tells Moses to tell Aaron what Aaron has to do to prepare to come into the Most Holy Place behind the curtain.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Aaron
  • Aaron's two oldest sons, Nadab and Abihu
  • And the assembly, or representatives of the people of Israel

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

In this passage, Yahweh talks about things that happen at the Tent of Meeting. Pay special attention to the most holy area behind the curtain, where the ark of the covenant is.

The first scene starts by explaining the background of the Day of Atonement. Before Yahweh talked with Moses to explain the instructions for the Day of Atonement, Aaron's two oldest sons, Nadab and Abihu, had burned incense to Yahweh the wrong way and had died. Although the original story does not say exactly why Nadab and Abihu died, some translations include the information that Nadab and Abihu had burned incense in the wrong way. You may include that information if it is helpful.

Stop and discuss: Tell someone a set of rules and instructions about something important. Pretend that the person you are telling the rules to has a close family member or friend who already broke the rules, and the community has punished that family member or friend. How does the person who tells the rules explain the reason they tell the listener the rules? How does the person mention what has already happened? Pause this audio here.

Some time after Nadab and Abihu died, Yahweh tells Moses to warn Aaron not to come into the most holy area behind the curtain where the ark of the covenant is. Yahweh tells Moses, "Tell your brother Aaron that Aaron cannot come into the most holy area behind the curtain whenever Aaron wants to. If Aaron does, then Aaron will die. That is because the atonement cover is behind the curtain, and I am going to appear in a cloud above the atonement cover."

Stop and discuss: Tell someone a set of rules and instructions about something important. How does the person who tells the rules emphasize how important these rules are? Pause this audio here.

The second scene continues with Yahweh talking to Moses about what to tell Aaron. In this scene, Yahweh focuses on what Aaron needs to do when Aaron goes into the most holy area behind the curtain so that Aaron does not die. Yahweh says, "When Aaron comes into the most holy area behind the curtain, Aaron needs to bring a young bull for a purification offering, and a ram for a burnt offering." We know that Aaron does not bring the actual bull and ram into the most holy area behind the curtain. This probably means that Aaron must bring these animals for these offerings when Aaron comes to the Tent of Meeting to prepare to go into the most holy area behind the curtain.

Aaron also needs to wear the holy linen clothing. This clothing includes a linen tunic, linen undergarments, a linen sash around Aaron's waist, and a linen turban or hat on Aaron's head. Yahweh describes these events out of order because the next thing Yahweh describes Aaron doing is the first thing that Aaron needs to do in order to get ready for these offerings. The first thing Aaron needs to do is to wash Aaron's body with water, and then put on all of the holy linen clothing.

Stop and look at a picture of what the high priest might have worn during the Day of Atonement ritual. Pause this audio here.

Then, after Aaron has washed himself and dressed in the holy linen clothing, Aaron will need to get the bull and the ram for his own offerings. Aaron will also need to get three animals from the assembly, which is the group of representatives of the people of Israel. The three animals that Aaron will need are two young goats and one ram. The two young goats are for the purification offering, and the ram is for the burnt offering.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:1–5 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has two scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Aaron
  • Aaron's two oldest sons, Nadab and Abihu
  • And the assembly, or representatives of the people of Israel

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

Scene one starts by explaining the background of the Day of Atonement. Aaron's two oldest sons, Nadab and Abihu, had burned incense to Yahweh the wrong way and then died.

After Nadab and Abihu died, Yahweh tells Moses to tell Aaron, "Tell your brother Aaron that Aaron cannot come into the most holy area behind the curtain whenever Aaron wants to. If Aaron does, then Aaron will die. That is because the atonement cover is behind the curtain, and I am going to appear in a cloud above the atonement cover."

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am sad that Nadab and Abihu died, and I do not want any more people to die; or
  • I really hope Aaron and Aaron's descendants listen to me.
Continue the drama.

Scene two continues as Yahweh tells Moses to tell Aaron what Aaron has to do before Aaron can go into the most holy area behind the curtain.

Yahweh says, "When it is time for Aaron to come into the most holy area behind the curtain, Aaron first needs to bring a young bull for a purification offering, and a ram for a burnt offering. Aaron also needs to wear the holy linen clothing. This clothing includes a linen tunic, linen undergarments, a linen sash around Aaron's waist, and a linen turban or hat on Aaron's head. To get ready, Aaron first needs to wash his body with water, and then put on all of the holy linen clothing."

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Aaron, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am sad that my sons died, and I wish my sons had done the right thing; or
  • I am glad Yahweh is telling me what to do so I will not die; or
  • I feel very serious as I get ready to go into Yahweh's presence.
Continue the drama.

Yahweh says, "Then, after Aaron has washed himself and dressed in the holy linen clothing, Aaron will need to get three animals from the representatives of the people of Israel. The three animals that Aaron will need are two young goats and one ram. The two young goats are for the purification offering, and the ram is for the burnt offering."

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:1–5 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

Before, Aaron's two oldest sons burned incense as unauthorized fire to Yahweh and died. Use the same terms for unauthorized fire and for Yahweh as you used before. Yahweh is in the Master Glossary.

After Aaron's sons died, Yahweh tells Moses, "Tell your brother Aaron that Aaron cannot come into the holy area behind the curtain whenever Aaron wants to." This is where the ark of the covenant was. A curtain separated this area from the rest of the tent. Some translations call this area the "Most Holy Place" behind the curtain to show that it is different from the front room of the tabernacle.

Stop here as a group and look at a diagram of the Tent of Meeting. Notice the difference between the area behind the curtain and the main part of the tent. Discuss how best to refer to the area behind the curtain. For more information, refer to "Most Holy Place" in the Master Glossary. Pause this audio here.

Aaron cannot come behind the curtain in front of the atonement cover. The atonement cover was the lid of the ark of the covenant. The people of Israel thought of the atonement cover as Yahweh's earthly throne. Yahweh had told Moses that Yahweh would talk to Moses from above the atonement cover that was on the ark of the covenant.

Stop here and look at a picture of the ark of the covenant as a group. Notice the atonement cover where Yahweh said Yahweh would talk to Moses from. Look up the "ark of the covenant" in the Master Glossary for more information. Discuss what word or phrase you will use to talk about the atonement cover. For more information about atonement, see the Master Glossary. If you have already translated the book of Exodus, use the same term for "atonement cover" throughout this book as well. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that Aaron must not come in front of the atonement cover whenever Aaron wants to because Yahweh will appear in a cloud on top of the atonement cover. If Aaron goes into that area on the wrong day or in the wrong way, Aaron will die. This word cloud refers both to the clouds in the sky and to a cloud of smoke or incense.

Stop here and look at a picture of a cloud of incense or smoke. Discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for cloud here. If your language also uses the same word for both clouds in the sky and clouds of smoke or incense, use that word. If your language uses different words, then use the word that refers to a cloud of smoke or incense. Pause this audio here.

Then Yahweh tells Moses to tell Aaron what Aaron has to do before Aaron can go into the holy area behind the curtain on the Day of Atonement. Yahweh says, "When Aaron comes into the holy area behind the curtain, Aaron needs to bring a young bull for a sin or purification offering, and a ram for a burnt offering." Look up purification offering and burnt offering in the Master Glossary for more information. Use the same term for purification offering and burnt offering as you used before.

Aaron also needs to wear the holy linen clothing. Look up holy in the Master Glossary for more information. Use the same terms for holy and linen as you used before.

The holy linen clothing included a linen tunic, linen undergarments, a linen sash around Aaron's waist, and a linen turban or hat on Aaron's head. The tunic would have covered the top half of the priest's body and likely covered his legs all the way down to his ankles. The priest would have worn the undergarments underneath the tunic. The sash would have been a strip of cloth that went around the priest's waist. The priest would have worn the turban or hat on top of his head.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of what the priestly garments might have looked like. Discuss what words or phrases you will use for tunic, undergarments, sash, and turban or hat. See the Master Glossary for more information about tunic. If you have already translated the book of Exodus, use the same terms throughout this book as well. Pause this audio here.

To get ready, Aaron first needs to wash his body with water and then put on all of the holy linen clothing. Then, after Aaron has washed himself and dressed in the holy linen clothing, Aaron will need to get three animals from the assembly of the people of Israel. Here, the assembly, or community of Israel, refers to all of the free adult men who had the power and authority to make decisions that affected the entire nation of Israel. It did not include the women, slaves, or children.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for the assembly of the people of Israel. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, decide if it is appropriate to use the same word that you have used there. For more information about Israelites, refer to the Master Glossary. Pause this audio here.

The three animals that Aaron will need from the community of Israel are two young goats and one ram. The two young goats are for the purification offering, and the ram is for the burnt offering. Use the same words for young goats and the ram as you have used previously.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.
