title: Leviticus 16:6–14
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 16:6–14 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:6–14 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:6–14 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this passage, Yahweh gave Moses the instructions for the rest of the work that Aaron needed to do to prepare for the Day of Atonement ritual. Yahweh also gave the instructions for the first part of the Day of Atonement ritual, where Aaron would cleanse himself and Aaron's family from the ways that Aaron and Aaron's family had betrayed and rebelled against Yahweh throughout the year. Even though Yahweh talked about what Aaron needed to do in this ritual, once Aaron died, the next high priest would be the one to do the ritual. This high priest would have been one of Aaron's direct blood descendants. When you listen to what Aaron needed to do, remember that these instructions are not only for Aaron but for every high priest that ever lived.

So, to begin, Aaron must have three animals at the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting. These were a bull and two goats. You will remember from the last passage that Aaron and the community also brought two rams to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. Aaron would use those two rams at a later part of the ceremony. The first animal was a bull that Aaron would later sacrifice as a purification or sin offering that would cleanse, or atone for, Aaron and Aaron's entire household. A man's household included the man's wife and concubines, the man's sons, the man's unmarried daughters, and the man's slaves. This included the slaves the man had bought from someone else, and the slaves who were born to slaves who already belonged to the family. People did not consider visitors and hired workers to be members of the household.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, who all is a part of the person's household? Pause this audio here.

The next two animals were the two goats that Aaron had already gotten from the representatives of the people of Israel. To prepare for later in the ritual, Aaron needed to bring both goats to the entrance, or courtyard, of the Tent of Meeting. This courtyard was part of Yahweh's earthly home, which was the tent itself. That is why Aaron needed to present the two goats to Yahweh in the courtyard.

After Aaron presented the goats to Yahweh, Aaron needed to cast lots for the goats. Different people who lived around the Israelites cast lots in different ways. To cast lots, people used physical objects to determine what a god or goddess wanted the people to do. Because the people of Israel made a binding agreement, or a covenant, with Yahweh that Yahweh would be their only God, the Israelites were only supposed to cast lots to see what Yahweh wanted. And Yahweh also told the Israelites not to cast lots in most of the ways that other people did. Most of the normal ways to cast lots allowed the person who interpreted the lots to make up an answer. Yahweh did not want this to happen. Yahweh made it illegal for the people of Israel to cast lots in ways that would allow the person who interpreted the lot to say something different than what Yahweh actually said.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do people discover what a god, spirit, or ancestor wants? How are those ways similar or different from what Yahweh does not allow the Israelites to do? Pause this audio here.

Instead of casting lots the way everyone else did, the people of Israel were usually supposed to have Aaron and Aaron's descendants, who were the priests, use the Urim and the Thummim.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of what the Urim and Thummim might have looked like. Pause this audio here.

Nobody knows exactly how the Urim and Thummim worked. Some people believe that one of the stones would glow. Other people believe that the priests rolled the stones. Still other people believe that the priests put stones into a bag and then shook the bag until one of the stones came out. Even though we do not know exactly how the stones worked, we do know that Yahweh always had the option not to answer at all.

For the Day of Atonement, Aaron probably used the Urim and Thummim to cast lots for the two goats. This process was to determine which goat to give to Yahweh and which goat to release. Later in the second part of the Day of Atonement ritual, Aaron would sacrifice the goat for Yahweh as a purification offering. Then, in the third part of the Day of Atonement ritual, Aaron would present the second goat to Yahweh. This other goat had to be alive to cleanse the people. Later in the ritual, someone would send this goat into an area where nobody lived. When the goat left, the goat would carry away all of the spiritual dirtiness that had spread among the people and the community because of all the ways that the people had betrayed and rebelled against Yahweh and done wrong to other people throughout the year.

Once Aaron had prepared the bull and cast lots for the two goats, Aaron could begin the first part of the ritual of the Day of Atonement. First, Aaron would kill the bull that Aaron would use as the purification offering for himself and Aaron's entire household. This bull's blood would atone, or cleanse Aaron and Aaron's entire household from all of the ways Aaron and Aaron's household had betrayed and rebelled against Yahweh and done wrong to other people throughout the year. That cleansing meant that Yahweh would not punish Aaron and Aaron's household. Offering Yahweh the bull was also how the high priest and the high priest's household would make amends with Yahweh, which would restore their relationship with Yahweh.

After Aaron killed the bull, Aaron would take a censer full of burning coals from the bronze altar that was in the courtyard surrounding Yahweh's tent.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of what the censer might have looked like. Pause this audio here.

After Aaron filled the censer with burning coals from the bronze altar, Aaron would take a handful of the sweet-smelling, finely-ground incense. Incense is a blend of several spices that smells good when people burn it. For this particular incense, Yahweh had told Moses the recipe of the different spices that Yahweh wanted the Israelites to use for Yahweh's incense, and people could only use this particular recipe for Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: When do people burn incense or spices to smell good in your culture? Why do people burn those spices or incense? Pause this audio here.

Then Aaron would take the censer full of burning coals and the handful of incense behind the curtain and into the Most Holy Place of the Tent of Meeting, where the ark of the covenant was. Next, Aaron would take the handful of incense and put the incense on the censer full of burning coals. The burning incense would create a cloud that would surround the atonement cover that was on top of the ark of the covenant. Sometimes people called this ark the "Testimony" or the "ark of the Testimony." This is because the word in the original language that people translate here as "Testimony" was one name for the ten commands that Yahweh wrote on two tablets of stone. These commands were part of the covenant that the people of Israel promised to obey. Moses later put these stone tablets inside the ark.

The reason Aaron was supposed to cover the atonement cover is that it was where Yahweh said Yahweh would meet with Moses. Since Yahweh's presence was there, Aaron needed to cover the top with a cloud of incense so Aaron would not die. Some people believe it was so that Aaron would not see Yahweh's presence and die. Some people believe it was so that Aaron—and later priests—would remember what happened when Yahweh came down on top of Mount Sinai and made the covenant with the people of Israel.

Once there was a cloud of incense to protect Aaron, Aaron would take some of the bull's blood and use his fingers to sprinkle the blood seven times. The number seven is an important number in the Bible because Israelite people believed that the number seven represented completeness or wholeness.

Yahweh said that Aaron needed to sprinkle the bull's blood on the east side of the atonement cover and in front of the atonement cover. The east side would have been the side that faces where the sun rose in the morning. It was also the side of the atonement cover that would have faced Aaron when Aaron entered that part of the tent behind the curtain.

It is not clear whether the words "on top of the atonement cover" and "in front of the atonement cover" refer to the same place. Some people believe that it is the same place. If that is true, then Aaron would enter the tent, see the side of the atonement cover that was facing Aaron, and use his finger to sprinkle the bull's blood seven times. The blood would fall on top of the atonement cover and in front of the atonement cover.

However, some people believe that "on top of the atonement cover" and "in front of the atonement cover" do not refer to the same place. If that is true, then Aaron would enter the tent, see the side of the atonement cover that was facing Aaron, and use his finger to sprinkle the bull's blood on top of the atonement cover seven times. Then, Aaron would use his finger to sprinkle the bull's blood on top of the space in front of the atonement cover. Aaron would do this seven times also.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:6–14 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has two scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh gave Moses the instructions for the rest of the things that the high priest needed to do to prepare for the Day of Atonement ritual.

In the second scene: Yahweh gave Moses the instructions for what the high priest needed to do to cleanse the high priest and the high priest's household from the ways that the high priest and the high priest's family had betrayed and rebelled against Yahweh throughout the year.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Moses
  • Aaron the high priest
  • Aaron's household
  • And Yahweh

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

Yahweh talked about what Aaron would do at the Tent of Meeting, especially at the entrance to the courtyard, the bronze altar that is in the courtyard, and the ark of the covenant that is in the Most Holy Place behind the curtain in the tent itself. The important part of the ark of the covenant is the east side that faces where the sun rises.

In scene one, Yahweh continued to tell Moses what Aaron needed to do to prepare for the Day of Atonement ritual. Remember that these instructions for Aaron will also be for every high priest after Aaron.

Stop here and have someone tell someone instructions that apply to that person and to that person's children when the person's children grow up. How does the speaker clearly show that the instructions apply to that person right now and to that person's descendants many years later? Pause this audio here.

Aaron has already begun preparing for the ritual by washing himself and putting on the special clothes. Since Aaron finished those actions, Yahweh gave Aaron instructions on how to use three of the animals that Aaron and the people had gathered for these offerings. The first animal was a bull that Aaron would sacrifice later in the ritual as a purification offering that would cleanse, or atone for, Aaron and Aaron's entire household. The next two animals were the two goats that Aaron had already gotten from the representatives of the people of Israel. To prepare for later in the ritual, Aaron needed to bring both goats to the courtyard, or entrance, of the Tent of Meeting.

After Aaron presented the goats to Yahweh, Aaron needed to cast lots for the goats. Aaron would sacrifice one goat to Yahweh as the purification offering. Aaron would present the other goat alive to Yahweh, and then someone else would send that goat away into an area where no one lived. Even though Yahweh explained what was going to happen to both goats in this section, none of that had happened yet. Aaron would cast the lots first, and then later on, Aaron would sacrifice Yahweh's goat and have someone send the other goat away.

Stop here and have someone tell someone else instructions for how to prepare for an activity, and then instructions for how to actually do that activity. How does the speaker clearly show there is a shift between preparing to do an activity and doing the activity? Pause this audio here.

In scene two, Yahweh gave instructions for how Aaron would begin the first part of the Day of Atonement ritual. First, Aaron would kill the bull that Aaron would use as the purification offering for Aaron and Aaron's entire household. This bull's blood would atone, or cleanse, Aaron and Aaron's entire household from all of the ways Aaron and Aaron's household had betrayed and rebelled against Yahweh and done wrong to other people throughout the year.

After Aaron killed the bull, Aaron would take a censer full of burning coals from the bronze altar that was in the courtyard surrounding Yahweh's tent. Then Aaron would take a handful of the sweet-smelling, finely-ground incense.

Then Aaron would bring the censer full of burning coals in one hand and a handful of incense in the other hand behind the curtain and into the Most Holy Place of the Tent of Meeting, where the ark of the covenant was. Then Aaron would put the handful of incense on the censer full of burning coals. The burning incense would create a cloud that would surround the atonement cover that was on top of the ark of the covenant. This cloud would protect Aaron from dying.

Stop here and talk about what happens when you put certain things into a fire and it causes a lot of smoke. How do you describe what happens? Pause this audio here.

After Aaron had made a cloud of incense, Aaron would take some of the bull's blood and use his finger to sprinkle the blood seven times. Aaron needed to sprinkle the bull's blood on top of the atonement cover and in front of the atonement cover on the east side. The east side would have been the side that faced where the sun rose in the morning. It would also have been the side of the ark that was facing Aaron when Aaron went into the area behind the curtain.

It is not clear whether the words "on top of the atonement cover" and "in front of the atonement cover" refer to the same place. Some people believe that it is the same place. If that is true, then Aaron would enter the tent, see the side of the atonement cover that was facing Aaron, and use his finger to sprinkle the bull's blood seven times. The blood would fall on top of the atonement cover and in front of the atonement cover.

However, some people believe that "on top of the atonement cover" and "in front of the atonement cover" do not refer to the same place. If that is true, then Aaron would enter the tent, see the side of the atonement cover that was facing Aaron, and use his finger to sprinkle the bull's blood on top of the atonement cover seven times. Then Aaron would use his finger to sprinkle the bull's blood on top of the space in front of the atonement cover. Aaron would do this seven times also.

Stop here and act out both options. Then, discuss which option you think is most likely. Act out that option again and discuss how to explain what is happening. Pause this audio here.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:6–14 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has two scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Moses
  • Aaron the high priest
  • Aaron's household
  • And Yahweh

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

In scene one, Yahweh continued to tell Moses what Aaron needed to do to prepare for the Day of Atonement ritual. To begin, Aaron needed three animals at the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting. The first animal was a bull that Aaron would sacrifice later in the ritual as a purification or sin offering that would cleanse, or atone for, Aaron and Aaron's entire household. The next two animals were the two goats that Aaron had already gotten from the representatives of the people of Israel. To prepare for later in the ritual, Aaron needed to bring both goats to the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.

After Aaron presented the goats to Yahweh, Aaron needed to cast lots for the goats. Aaron would sacrifice one goat to Yahweh as the purification offering. Aaron would present the other goat alive to Yahweh, and then someone else would send that goat away into an area where no one lived. Both of these things would happen later in the ritual.

In scene two, Aaron would begin the first part of the Day of Atonement ritual. First, Aaron would kill the bull that Aaron would use as the purification offering for Aaron and Aaron's entire household. This bull's blood would atone, or cleanse, Aaron and Aaron's entire household from all of the ways Aaron and Aaron's household had betrayed and rebelled against Yahweh and done wrong to other people throughout the year.

After Aaron killed the bull, Aaron would take a censer full of burning coals from the bronze altar that was in the courtyard surrounding Yahweh's tent. Then Aaron would take a handful of the sweet-smelling, finely-ground incense.

Aaron would bring the censer full of burning coals in one hand and a handful of incense in the other hand behind the curtain and into the Most Holy Place of the Tent of Meeting, where the ark of the covenant was. Then Aaron would put the handful of incense on the censer full of burning coals. The burning incense would create a cloud that would surround the atonement cover that was on top of the ark of the covenant. This cloud would protect Aaron from dying.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Aaron, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am afraid to enter Yahweh's presence, but I am glad Yahweh has a way to protect me; or
  • I am happy that Yahweh wants me to live; or
  • This reminds me of when Yahweh came down on top of Mount Sinai, and there was fire and a big cloud to hide Yahweh's presence.
Continue the drama.

After Aaron had made a cloud of incense, Aaron would take some of the bull's blood and use his fingers to sprinkle the blood on the east side of the atonement cover and in front of the atonement cover. The east side would have been the side that faced where the sun rose in the morning. Aaron needed to sprinkle the bull's blood with his finger seven times.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:6–14 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

In this passage, Yahweh continued to tell Moses what Aaron needed to do to prepare for the Day of Atonement ritual. Look up Yahweh in the Master Glossary for more information. Translate Yahweh the same way you have done previously.

To begin, Aaron needed to bring three animals to the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting. The first animal was a bull that Aaron would sacrifice later in the ritual as a sin or purification offering. Look up purification offering in the Master Glossary. Use the same word or phrase for purification offering as you used in previous passages.

This purification offering would cleanse, or atone for, Aaron and Aaron's entire household. Look up atonement in the Master Glossary for more information. Use the same word or phrase for atone as you used in previous passages.

A man's household included the man's wives and concubines, the man's sons, the man's unmarried daughters, and the man's slaves. These were the slaves that the man bought from someone else as well as the slaves who were born to slaves who already belonged to the family. Visitors and hired workers were not members of the household.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for household. Look up household in the Master Glossary for more information. Pause this audio here.

The next two animals were the two goats that Aaron had already gotten from the representatives of the people of Israel.

To prepare for later in the ritual, Aaron needed to bring both goats to the entrance, or courtyard of the Tent of Meeting. Look up tabernacle in the Master Glossary for more information. Translate "Tent of Meeting" and "entrance to the Tent of Meeting" in the same way you have done previously.

After Aaron presented the goats to Yahweh, Aaron needed to cast lots for the goats. Casting lots refers to the practice where people used physical objects to determine what a god or goddess wanted the people to do. Nobody knows exactly how casting lots worked. Some people believe that one of the stones or objects would glow. Other people believe that the priests rolled the stones. Still other people believe that the priests put stones into a bag and then shook the bag until one of the stones came out. Yahweh had told the people of Israel that the Israelites must only cast lots to see what Yahweh wanted. Yahweh also told the Israelites not to cast lots the way that many of the people around the Israelites did. For this ritual, the people of Israel probably used the Urim and the Thummim, but we do not know that for certain. Use a word that focuses on the idea of using physical objects to know what Yahweh wants. Keep in mind that Yahweh had forbidden the people of Israel from casting lots in ways that would allow the person who interpreted the lot to say something different than what Yahweh actually said.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for cast lots. If you have already translated this phrase in another book of the Bible, decide if it is appropriate to use the same phrase that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

The lots would decide which goat belonged to Yahweh and which goat was the scapegoat. Nobody knows exactly what Yahweh meant by this description of this goat. Some people think it refers to a rough and challenging place, like the wilderness where the goat was sent later in the ritual. Other people think it means "a goat that someone sent away." Regardless of what the word means, Aaron would present the scapegoat alive to Yahweh, and then someone else would send that goat away into the wilderness, which was an area where no one lived.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for this kind of goat. Pause this audio here.

If you use the idea of wilderness in your word for scapegoat, look up wilderness in the Master Glossary for more information, if needed. Decide if it is appropriate to translate wilderness the same way you have done previously. Pause this audio here.

Later in the Day of Atonement ritual, Aaron would sacrifice one goat to Yahweh as the purification offering. Aaron would present the other goat alive to Yahweh, and then someone else would send that goat away into an area where no one lived.

After Aaron finished preparing for the Day of Atonement ritual, Aaron would begin the first part. First, Aaron would kill the bull for the purification offering for Aaron and Aaron's entire household. This bull's blood would atone, or cleanse, Aaron and Aaron's entire household from all of the ways that Aaron and Aaron's household had betrayed and rebelled against Yahweh and done wrong to other people throughout the year.

After Aaron killed the bull, Aaron would take a censer full of burning coals from the bronze altar that was in the courtyard surrounding Yahweh's tent.

Stop here and look at a picture of a censer as a group. Discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for censer. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, decide if it is appropriate to use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Then Aaron would take a handful of the sweet-smelling, finely-ground incense. Incense was a blend of several spices that would smell good when people burned the spices. For this particular incense, Yahweh had told Moses the recipe of the different spices that Yahweh wanted the Israelites to use for Yahweh's incense. People could only use this particular recipe for Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for incense. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, decide if it is appropriate to use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Aaron would bring the censer full of burning coals in one hand and a handful of incense in the other hand behind the curtain and into the sacred place of the Tent of Meeting. Then Aaron would put the handful of incense on the censer full of burning coals. The burning incense would create a cloud that would surround the atonement cover that was on top of the Testimony, which people also called the ark of the covenant.

Stop here and look up Testimony and ark of the covenant in the Master Glossary for more information. Decide whether or not to translate the Testimony the same way you have done previously. Pause this audio here.

This cloud would protect Aaron from dying. Use the same word for cloud as you used in previous passages.

After Aaron had made a cloud of incense, Aaron would take some of the bull's blood and use his fingers to sprinkle the blood on the east side of the atonement cover and in front of the atonement cover. The east side would have been the side that faced where the sun rose in the morning. Use the same word or phrase for sprinkle and for atonement cover as you used in previous passages.

Aaron needed to sprinkle the bull's blood with his finger seven times.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 16:15–22
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 16:15–22 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:15–22 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:15–22 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this section, Yahweh continued to tell Moses the instructions to tell Aaron about the Day of Atonement ritual. After Aaron finished atoning for Aaron and Aaron's household, Aaron needed to kill Yahweh's goat as a sin or purification offering. This would cleanse the Most Holy Place from all of the bad things that the people of Israel did throughout the year.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of a goat. Pause this audio here.

After killing the goat, Aaron needed to bring the goat's blood behind the curtain in the Tent of Meeting, where the ark of the covenant was. Then Aaron needed to do the same thing with the goat's blood that Aaron did with the bull's blood in the previous passage. This means that Aaron needed to use his fingers to sprinkle the goat's blood seven times on the east side, on top of the atonement cover and in front of the atonement cover. The east side would have been the side that faced where the sun rose in the morning. The east side was also the side of the atonement cover that would have faced Aaron when Aaron entered that part of the tent behind the curtain.

Aaron would use the goat's blood to cleanse, or atone for, the Holy Place. When Yahweh told Aaron to cleanse the Holy Place during the Day of Atonement, Yahweh probably meant the "Most Holy Place," or the part of the tent that was behind the curtain. This was where the ark of the covenant was.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of the ark of the covenant. Pause this audio here.

Stop here as a group and look at a diagram of the inside of the Tent of Meeting. Notice the area behind the curtain and where the ark of the covenant is. Pause this audio here.

After Aaron cleansed the part of the Holy Place that was behind the curtain, Aaron needed to cleanse the whole Tent of Meeting. This included the main part of the tent, where the incense altar, lampstand, and table with the bread were. The whole Tent of Meeting was holy, and so was everything inside the tent, so Aaron needed to cleanse the whole tent as well.

Nobody knows exactly how Aaron was supposed to cleanse the Tent of Meeting. Aaron probably did a similar thing to what Aaron just did to cleanse the holy area behind the curtain. This means that Aaron probably sprinkled the goat's blood on the items in the front room of the Tent of Meeting, but we do not know exactly what Aaron did.

Yahweh told Aaron to cleanse the Most Holy Place behind the curtain and the Tent of Meeting because the Israelites had made the Most Holy Place ritually dirty with all of the ways the people had rebelled against Yahweh and betrayed Yahweh throughout the year. The bad things that the Israelites did made the Israelites and the things and places around the Israelites spiritually unclean, or ritually dirty. Since Yahweh's tent was in the middle of where the Israelites were living in their tents, all of the bad things that the Israelites did made both the Israelites' own tents and Yahweh's tent ritually dirty. That was why Aaron needed to cleanse Yahweh's tent once a year during this ritual.

People in the Bible often used the same word "unclean" or ritually dirty to talk about things that were physically dirty and things that were morally or spiritually dirty. Things that were physically dirty were things like dead bodies of people and animals, genital discharge, and certain diseases. Things that were morally and spiritually dirty were things like murdering someone, stealing from someone, cheating on the person you married, worshipping false gods and goddesses, and doing other bad things to Yahweh or other people. In the laws that Yahweh gave the people through Moses, Yahweh said that both the things that made people physically dirty and the things that made people morally or spiritually dirty also made people ritually dirty. If someone was ritually dirty, that person could not go near any place or anything that was holy, which meant that person could not participate in many religious ceremonies and festivals. In order to become ritually clean, the people of Israel would need to do cleansing rituals and sometimes offer sacrifices of animals throughout the year to make themselves ritually clean from the physical dirt and the spiritual dirt. And once a year, the head priest would need to do this Day of Atonement ritual to make all of the people and the entire Holy Place clean from the ritual dirt. Once the priests, the Holy Place, and the people became ritually clean, the people could continue to worship Yahweh at the Holy Place.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: How does your culture talk about things that are both physically dirty and spiritually dirty? Do people need to do anything special to become clean from these kinds of dirt? Pause this audio here.

And while Aaron was inside the tent itself, cleansing the Most Holy Place behind the curtain and the Tent of Meeting, nobody else could go into the Tent of Meeting. Usually, Yahweh allowed the priests to go into the Tent of Meeting. However, while Aaron was doing the Day of Atonement ritual, Yahweh did not allow anyone else to go into the Tent of Meeting. The priests had to wait until after Aaron had finished cleansing the Most Holy Place behind the curtain and the Tent of Meeting, and the entire community of Israel.

After Aaron cleansed the Most Holy Place behind the curtain and the Tent of Meeting, Aaron had to go to the bronze altar that was in the courtyard and cleanse, or atone for, the altar. This was the altar in the courtyard where the priests would offer the people's offerings of animals and grain throughout the year.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of the bronze altar. Pause this audio here.

To cleanse the bronze altar, Aaron needed to use some of the bull's blood and some of the goat's blood that Aaron had used to cleanse the Holy Place. Aaron would put the blood of the bull and goat on the horns of the bronze altar. Then Aaron was supposed to use his fingers to sprinkle some of the blood on the altar seven times.

The Israelites had made the bronze altar spiritually unclean. But with the blood, Aaron would cleanse the bronze altar and rededicate the altar, to make the altar holy to Yahweh again. Once Aaron finished cleansing, or atoning for, the Most Holy Place behind the curtain, the Tent of Meeting, and the bronze altar, Aaron had to get the live goat. This was the goat that the lots had marked to go away into a place where no one lived.

Aaron was supposed to put both his hands on the head of the live goat and announce over the goat all of the bad things that the people of Israel had done throughout the year. Aaron must announce all of the evil things, or iniquities, that the people of Israel did, including all of the transgressions or rebellions and all of the people's sin or betrayal.

This word for iniquity refers to actions and behavior so evil that someone needs to severely punish the person who did that evil thing. Some of the things that people in the Bible thought were evil enough to be called iniquities were: someone killing their blood brother, a priest trying to take Yahweh's place and become a god, and the people of Israel breaking their promise to Yahweh and worshipping and serving fake gods and goddesses.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What kinds of things do people in your culture think are so evil that someone needs to severely punish that person? How would you describe that kind of evil thing? Pause this audio here.

The word for transgressions, or rebellions, refers to actions that cross a boundary line that Yahweh has put in place. For example, people might cross a physical boundary by stealing from someone else. People might cross a moral boundary by doing something especially bad like selling their blood brother into slavery. People might cross a leadership boundary line by rebelling against the leader whom Yahweh chose.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What kinds of things do people in your culture think are so rebellious against Yahweh or another person that someone needs to severely punish that person? How would you describe that kind of rebellious thing? Pause this audio here.

The word for sin, or betrayal, refers to any actions that are against another human or against Yahweh. Some of the things that people in the Bible thought were betrayals were: oppressing poor people, breaking a promise to someone, and the people of Israel breaking their promise to Yahweh and worshipping and serving false gods and goddesses.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What kinds of things do people in your culture think betray others that someone needs to severely punish that person? How would you describe when someone betrays someone else or breaks their promise to that person? Pause this audio here.

When Aaron put his hands on the goat and announced all of these bad things, Aaron would put all of the Israelites' rebellion and all of the evil things the Israelites did on the head of the goat. This meant that those bad things would not make the people of Israel ritually dirty anymore, since those bad things were on the goat now. As a result of that, the people of Israel would become ritually clean.

After Aaron put all of the people's rebellion and all of the evil things the people did on the goat, a different man would release the goat into the wilderness area where there were no farms or crops. So the goat would carry away all of the evil things the people of Israel did into an area where no one lived.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of the wilderness.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:15–22 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has three scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells Moses to tell Aaron how to do the second part of the Day of Atonement ritual. This second part focused on cleansing both the Most Holy Place behind the curtain and the rest of the Tent of Meeting.

In the second scene: Yahweh tells Moses to tell Aaron how to do the third part of the Day of Atonement ritual. This third part focused on cleansing the bronze altar.

In the third scene: Yahweh tells Moses to tell Aaron how to do the fourth and final part of the Day of Atonement ritual. This fourth and final part focused on cleansing all of the people of Israel.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Aaron, the high priest
  • The people of Israel
  • And someone else

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

Yahweh talked about what Aaron should do in the Tent of Meeting, especially the Most Holy Place behind the curtain where the ark of the covenant is. Two more important parts of the setting are the bronze altar in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting and the wilderness where no one lives.

Stop here and remember that Yahweh tells Moses to tell Aaron to sprinkle blood in a similar way throughout the Tent of Meeting area. Listen to someone give instructions for how to do something. Make sure that part of the instructions requires the listener to repeat some of the steps at a different time and to do some of the steps in a similar way. How does the storyteller make it clear that the listener should do similar things at different times? Pause this audio here.

In scene one, Yahweh told Moses to tell Aaron how to do the second part of the Day of Atonement ritual. During the second part, Aaron was supposed to atone for the Most Holy Place behind the curtain and the rest of the Tent of Meeting. Since the Day of Atonement ritual happened every year, Aaron's descendants would continue to do this after Aaron died.

For the second part, Aaron needed to kill Yahweh's goat as a purification offering. Remember that in the previous section, Aaron cast lots to determine which goat Aaron would sacrifice to Yahweh and which goat someone would send into the wilderness, which was the place where nobody farmed or grew food. Aaron needed to kill the goat that the lots determined was for Yahweh.

After Aaron killed the goat, Aaron needed to bring the goat's blood behind the curtain in the Tent of Meeting. Then Aaron needed to do the same thing with the goat's blood that Aaron did with the bull's blood in the previous passage. This means that Aaron needed to use his fingers to sprinkle the goat's blood seven times on the east side, on top of the atonement cover and in front of the atonement cover. The east side was the side of the atonement cover that would have faced Aaron when Aaron entered that part of the tent behind the curtain.

It is not clear whether the words "on top of the atonement cover" and "in front of the atonement cover" refer to the same place. Some people believe that it is the same place. If that is true, then Aaron would enter the tent, see the side of the atonement cover that was facing Aaron, and use his finger to sprinkle the bull's blood seven times. The blood would fall on top of the atonement cover and in front of the atonement cover.

However, some people believe that "on top of the atonement cover" and "in front of the atonement cover" do not refer to the same place. If that is true, then Aaron would enter the tent, see the side of the atonement cover that was facing Aaron, and use his finger to sprinkle the bull's blood on top of the atonement cover seven times. Then, Aaron would use his finger to sprinkle the bull's blood on top of the space in front of the atonement cover. Aaron would do this seven times also.

Aaron would use the goat's blood to atone for the part of the Holy Place that was behind the curtain. Yahweh told Aaron to cleanse the Most Holy Place because the Israelites had contaminated the Most Holy Place with all of the ways the Israelites had rebelled against Yahweh and betrayed Yahweh throughout the year.

After that, Aaron needed to use the goat's blood to make atonement for the rest of the Tent of Meeting. This included the part of the Tent of Meeting that was in front of the curtain. This area was also holy, and so Aaron needed to cleanse that part too from all of the ways the people of Israel had rebelled against Yahweh and all of the bad things the Israelites did throughout the year.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of the Tent of Meeting. Pay attention to the difference between the place behind the curtain and the rest of the Tent of Meeting. Pause this audio here.

And while Aaron was cleansing the Tent of Meeting, nobody could go into the Tent of Meeting until Aaron came out of the tent and had made atonement for Aaron, Aaron's household, and the entire community of Israel. This means that no one could go into the Tent of Meeting until after the fourth and final part of the ritual, where Aaron had someone else send the live goat away.

In scene two, Yahweh told Moses to tell Aaron how to do the third part of the Day of Atonement ritual. During the third part, Aaron was supposed to make atonement for the bronze altar. This was the altar in the courtyard where the priests would offer the people's sacrifices of animals and grain throughout the year.

To cleanse the bronze altar, Aaron would take some of the bull's blood that Aaron had used to cleanse Aaron and Aaron's household and some of the goat's blood that Aaron had used to cleanse both the Most Holy Place behind the curtain and the Tent of Meeting. Aaron would put the blood of the bull and the blood of the goat on the horns of the bronze altar. Then Aaron would use his fingers to sprinkle some of the blood on the altar seven times. This would cleanse the bronze altar and rededicate the altar and make the altar holy to Yahweh again because the Israelites had contaminated the bronze altar and made the altar ritually dirty.

In scene three, Yahweh told Moses to tell Aaron how to do the fourth and final part of the Day of Atonement ritual. During the fourth and final part, Aaron was supposed to atone for all of the Israelites.

To begin, Aaron would get the live goat. Remember that in the previous section, Aaron cast lots to determine which goat Aaron would sacrifice to Yahweh and which goat someone would send into the wilderness area. This is the goat that someone would send into the wilderness area.

Aaron would put his hands on the live goat and announce over the goat all of the ways that the people of Israel were guilty—the ways the Israelites had rebelled against Yahweh and done very evil things throughout the year. Remember that these actions are so evil that someone needs to severely punish the people who did those evil things.

When Aaron put his hands on the goat and announced all of these bad things, Aaron would put all of the people's rebellion and all of the evil things the people had done on the head of the goat. This meant that those bad things were not making the people of Israel ritually dirty or ceremonially unclean anymore, so the people of Israel would become spiritually and ritually clean.

After Aaron put all of the people's rebellion and all of the evil things the Israelites did on the goat, a different man would release the goat into the wilderness area. So the goat would carry away all of the evil things the people of Israel did into an area where no one lived.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:15–22 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has three scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Aaron, the high priest
  • The people of Israel
  • And someone else

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

The passage begins as Yahweh continues to tell Moses the instructions to tell Aaron about the Day of Atonement ritual.

Yahweh said, "Aaron needs to kill the goat for the purification offering." Remember that this is Yahweh's goat that Aaron had cast lots for.

Yahweh said, "Aaron needs to bring the goat's blood behind the curtain in the Tent of Meeting. Next, Aaron needs to sprinkle the goat's blood on the east side of the atonement cover and in front of the atonement cover the same way that Aaron did with the bull's blood." Remember that this means that Aaron needs to use his fingers to sprinkle the goat's blood seven times on the east side, on top of the atonement cover and in front of the atonement cover.

Yahweh said, "This is how Aaron will cleanse, or atone for, the Most Holy Place. Aaron needs to cleanse the Most Holy Place because the people of Israel have become ritually dirty and have rebelled against me and betrayed me, and done bad things to other people. These rebellions, betrayals, and bad things are ritually dirty and make the people who do these things ritually unclean.

"Next, Aaron will need to cleanse, or atone for, the rest of the Tent of Meeting. Aaron needs to cleanse the Tent of Meeting because my tent is in the middle of where the people of Israel are camping. This means that my tent is in the middle of all of the Israelites' ritual dirtiness."

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Aaron, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • This is a serious responsibility, and I want to do it right; or
  • I am glad Yahweh made a way to cleanse everything.
Continue the drama.

Yahweh said, "Nobody else can be inside the Tent of Meeting while Aaron is inside the tent. From the time that Aaron goes into the Most Holy Place to cleanse it until Aaron is finished cleansing himself and his household and everyone in Israel and then comes out, nobody else can be inside the Tent of Meeting."

Then Yahweh said, "After Aaron leaves the Tent of Meeting, Aaron needs to go to the bronze altar that is in the courtyard before me and cleanse the altar. To cleanse the altar, Aaron will need to put some of the bull's blood and some of the goat's blood on the horns of the bronze altar all around. Then Aaron will use his fingers to sprinkle some of the blood on the altar seven times. Doing this will cleanse the bronze altar and rededicate the altar and make the altar holy to me again since the Israelites made it ritually dirty.

"After Aaron has finished cleansing the Most Holy Place behind the curtain, the Tent of Meeting, and the bronze altar, Aaron will need to bring the live goat near. Then Aaron will need to put both of his hands on the head of the live goat and announce over the goat all of the ways that the people of Israel have rebelled against me and all of the evil things that the people have done throughout the year. When Aaron does this, Aaron will put all of these bad things on the goat."

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the people of Israel, "What are you feeling or thinking as you hear Aaron announce all of the bad things that you and your neighbors have done?" The person might answer things like:

  • I feel sad about the bad things we have done; or
  • I feel relieved that Yahweh told Aaron to put these bad things on the goat; or
  • I feel that it is very serious that we have done so many bad things.
Continue the drama.

Yahweh said, "After Aaron puts these bad things on the goat, a certain person will need to send this goat into the wilderness area. The goat will carry all of the evil things that the people of Israel have done into a place where nobody lives. That is why the person will need to release the goat into the desert area."

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:15–22 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

In this section, Yahweh continues to tell Moses the instructions to tell Aaron about the Day of Atonement ritual.

Yahweh says, "Aaron needs to kill the goat for the sin, or purification, offering." Use the same word for the purification offering that you used before. Look up "purification offering" in the Master Glossary for more information. Use the same word for killing an animal that you have used previously.

Aaron needs to bring the goat's blood behind the curtain in the Tent of Meeting. Use the same word or phrase for "Tent of Meeting" that you used before. Look up tabernacle in the Master Glossary for more information.

Next, Aaron needs to sprinkle the goat's blood on the east side of the atonement cover and in front of the atonement cover the same way that Aaron did with the bull's blood. Use the same words for sprinkle and for atonement cover that you used before.

Yahweh says, "This is how Aaron will atone for the Most Holy Place." Use the same word for cleanse or atone for as you used before. Look up atonement in the Master Glossary for more information.

Although your translation may say that Aaron atones for the "Holy Place," we know that the atonement cover is behind the curtain in the Most Holy Place. You may choose to make it clear that this is the Most Holy Place. Look up Most Holy Place in the Master Glossary for more information, and use the same word for Most Holy Place that you used in Leviticus 16:3.

These rebellions, betrayals, and bad things are unclean or ritually dirty and make the people who do these things ritually dirty. People in the Bible often used the same word "unclean" to talk about things that were physically dirty and things that were morally or spiritually dirty. And in the laws that Yahweh gave the people through Moses, Yahweh said that both the things that made people physically dirty and the things that made people morally or spiritually dirty also made people ritually dirty and unable to worship Yahweh in his Holy Place. In this section, when Yahweh talks about the people of Israel being "unclean," the emphasis is on the people of Israel being spiritually and morally unclean, which also made the people unable to worship Yahweh. Use the same words for unclean as you have used previously, and refer to clean and unclean in the Master Glossary for more information.

Then Yahweh tells Aaron to cleanse, or atone for, the rest of the Tent of Meeting. Yahweh also says that no one can be inside the Tent of Meeting while Aaron is in there.

After Aaron leaves the Tent of Meeting, Aaron needs to go to the bronze altar that is in the courtyard and cleanse, or atone for, the altar. Use the same word for the bronze altar as you used before. Look up altar in the Master Glossary for more information.

To cleanse the bronze altar, Aaron will need to take some of the bull's blood and some of the goat's blood, and put the mixed blood on the horns of the bronze altar all around.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of the bronze altar. Notice the horns of the altar. Remind each other as a group how you have previously translated the horns of the altar. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says, "After that, Aaron will use his fingers to sprinkle some of the blood on the altar seven times. This will clean or purify the bronze altar and consecrate, or make the altar holy to me again, since the Israelites made it ritually dirty." When someone makes something holy, the person gives it to whatever god that person worships. For the people of Israel, that means that when Aaron makes the altar holy again, Aaron will give the altar to Yahweh again. After someone gives something to Yahweh, that thing belongs to Yahweh. People need to treat anything that belongs to Yahweh with more respect and care. Use the same words or phrases for Israelites, purify, and consecrate as you have used previously. Refer to Israelites, purify, and consecrate in the Master Glossary for more information.

Yahweh says, "After Aaron has finished cleansing, or atoning for, the Most Holy Place behind the curtain, the Tent of Meeting, and the bronze altar, Aaron will need to bring the live goat near." Aaron was supposed to put both his hands on the head of the live goat and announce over it all of the bad things that the people of Israel had done throughout the year. Aaron must announce all of the evil things, or iniquities, that the people of Israel did, including all of the transgressions or rebellions and all of their sin or betrayal. Although in this case, iniquities, transgressions, and sin all refer to evil things that the Israelites do, you may choose to use three different words that have slightly different meanings, just like the original language. If you choose to use three different words, here is some information about each word.

The word for iniquity refers to actions and behavior so evil that someone needs to severely punish the person who did that evil thing.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Which word will you use for iniquities? You may choose to use the same word for iniquities that you used in Leviticus 7:18. For more information about iniquity, refer to the Master Glossary. Pause this audio here.

The word for transgressions, or rebellions, refers to actions in which people steal from someone, treat someone very badly, or rebel against a leader whom Yahweh chose.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Which word will you use for transgressions? For more information about transgression, refer to the Master Glossary. Pause this audio here.

The word for sin, or betrayal, refers to any actions that are against another human or against Yahweh. You have used the word for sin several times in the book of Leviticus, so be sure to use the same word for sin as you have used previously. Refer to the Master Glossary for more information about sin.

Yahweh says, "When Aaron puts his hands on the live goat and announces all of the bad things that the people of Israel did, Aaron will put all of these bad things on the goat. After Aaron puts these bad things on the goat, an appropriate person will need to send this goat into the wilderness area, or an area where no one lives." The people of Israel used the word "wilderness" to talk about land that nobody could farm or grow crops on. However, sometimes people would graze their animals in the wilderness.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of the wilderness area. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for wilderness area. Look up wilderness in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh said, "The goat will carry all of the iniquities that the people of Israel have done into a place where nobody lives. That is why the person will need to release the goat into the desert area."

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.
