title: Leviticus 16:23–28
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 16:23–28 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:23–28 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:23–28 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this section, Yahweh finished telling Moses the instructions that Moses needs to tell Aaron about the Day of Atonement ritual.

After Aaron had finished cleansing, or atoning for, Aaron and Aaron's household, the Most Holy Place behind the curtain and the rest of the Tent of Meeting, the bronze altar, and everyone in Israel, Aaron was supposed to go into the Tent of Meeting. There, Aaron would change out of the holy linen clothing that Aaron had been wearing while Aaron cleansed everyone and everything. After Aaron had changed out of the clothes, Aaron needed to leave the holy linen clothing inside the Tent of Meeting.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of the holy linen clothing that Aaron wore for this ritual. Pause this audio here.

Aaron needed to go somewhere to change clothes so that nobody would see Aaron naked. Aaron needed to wash himself with water and then put on the clothing Aaron was wearing before Aaron had changed into the holy linen clothing. In this part, when Yahweh talks about washing with water inside the holy place, nobody knows exactly where Aaron washed himself. Some people think that means that Aaron washed himself in the basin in the courtyard with his undergarments on and then went back into the Tent of Meeting to put his clothing back on. Other people think that there was a screened-in area near the tent where Aaron went to wash himself.

Either way, after Aaron washed and changed his clothes, Aaron was supposed to come out of the Tent of Meeting and offer two burnt offerings. The first burnt offering was for Aaron, and the second burnt offering was for all of the people of Israel. You will remember that Aaron and the people had each brought a ram earlier for their burnt offerings. Aaron offered both of these burnt offerings to cleanse, or atone for, both Aaron and the people. Even though Aaron already cleansed himself and the people, some people believe that Aaron needed to offer the burnt offerings to show how important the cleansing was that happened on this day.

Aaron also needed to offer the fat from the purification offering to Yahweh on the bronze altar. Aaron did this by burning the fat on the altar until there was nothing left. In other words, Aaron needs to burn the fat completely so that it makes smoke and a good smell for Yahweh. This fat was from the bull and goat whose blood Aaron used previously in the ritual to cleanse Aaron and Aaron's household, the whole Tent of Meeting, the bronze altar, and all of the people of Israel.

While Aaron was doing this, the person who had released the live goat into the wilderness area needed to stay outside of the area where the people of Israel were camping until the person made himself clean. In the previous section, Aaron had put all of the bad things that the people of Israel had done onto the live goat. That made the goat ritually dirty. Since the goat was ritually dirty because of all the bad things that the people of Israel had done, the person who had released the goat needed to make himself clean from the goat's ritual dirtiness. The place where the Israelites were camping was holy because Yahweh's tent was in the middle of the camp. That is why the person who had released the live goat could not go back into where people were camping until after the person became clean. In order to make himself clean, the person needed to wash his clothing and his body with water. After that, the person could come back into the area where the people of Israel were camping.

Also, a different person needed to take the bull and the goat that Aaron used for the purification offerings outside of where the people of Israel were camping. This bull and this goat were the animals whose blood Aaron had used to cleanse, or atone for, the Most Holy Place. The person who took the dead bull and dead goat outside the area where the people of Israel were camping needed to burn the hide, meat, and waste with fire. The hide refers to the animal's skin. People would often use the hide to make clothing or tents. The meat refers to the part of the animal that people would normally eat. It is not clear what the "waste" of the animals was. The waste could have been the animal's poop. The waste could have been the animal's intestines. Or the waste could have been both the animal's poop and the animal's intestines. Regardless, burning up the hide, meat, and waste meant that the person needed to burn up every part of the bull and every part of the goat. Nobody could use any part of either animal.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of a bull and a goat. Then look at pictures of a slaughtered animal's hide, meat, and waste. Pause this audio here.

After the person burned up the bull and the goat, the person needed to wash his clothes and his body with water. After that, the person could come back into the area where the people of Israel were camping.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:23–28 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has three scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells Moses what Aaron needs to do after he makes atonement for Aaron and Aaron's household, the whole Tent of Meeting, the bronze altar, and all of the people of Israel. To finish, Aaron needs to wash and change his clothes. Then Aaron must offer a burnt offering for Aaron, a burnt offering for the people of Israel, and the fat from the sin, or purification, offerings.

In the second scene: Yahweh tells Moses what the person who had released the live goat into the desert area needs to do before that person can come back into the area where everyone else is camping.

In the third scene: Yahweh tells Moses what someone needs to do with the dead bodies of the bull and the goat that Aaron used for the purification offerings.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Aaron, the high priest
  • The person who released the live goat
  • The person who burned up the dead bodies of the purification offerings
  • And the people of Israel

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

Yahweh talked about what Aaron and other priests would do inside the Tent of Meeting, at the bronze altar, and outside the area where the people of Israel were camping.

Stop here and have someone give instructions about one event. Make sure that this event requires at least two different people to do different things at the same time. How does the storyteller make it clear about who is doing what part? Pause this audio here.

In the first scene, Yahweh focused on what Aaron needed to do next.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will show that this passage comes immediately after what Aaron did in the previous passage. Pause this audio here.

After Aaron had cleansed, or made atonement for, Aaron and Aaron's household, the whole Tent of Meeting, the bronze altar, and all of the people of Israel, Aaron needed to go into the Tent of Meeting to change Aaron's clothing and wash himself. First, Aaron would take off the linen clothing that Aaron had been wearing in the Tent of Meeting. Then Aaron would wash himself in the sanctuary area, which refers to the entire area in and around the Tent of Meeting. Nobody knows exactly where Aaron washed himself in the sanctuary area. Some people think that means that Aaron washed himself in the basin in the courtyard with his undergarments on and then went back into the Tent of Meeting to put his clothing back on. Other people think that there was a screened-in area near the tent where Aaron went to wash himself. After Aaron had washed his body, Aaron needed to put back on the clothing Aaron had been wearing before Aaron had put on the linen clothing.

After Aaron changed his clothing, Aaron needed to come out and sacrifice two burnt offerings. One of the burnt offerings was to cleanse, or atone for, Aaron. The second burnt offering was to atone for all of the people of Israel. You will remember from previous passages that Aaron and the people had brought a ram each for this burnt offering.

After Aaron offered both burnt offerings, Aaron needed to burn up the fat of the purification offerings on the bronze altar.

In the second scene, Yahweh focused on what the person who had released the live goat into the wilderness area needed to do. Nobody knows who this person was or how the priests chose this person. This person was probably an adult man, but we do not know that for certain.

After this person had released the live goat into the wilderness area, the person needed to wash his clothing and his body with water. Then the person could come back into the area where everyone was camping. This person would wash himself and his clothing as soon as the person had finished releasing the goat. The person did not need to wait until after Aaron had washed and changed Aaron's clothes and offered the burnt offerings. This meant that this person might have been washing and changing his clothes while Aaron was offering the sacrifices.

In the third scene, Yahweh focused on how a person should burn up the dead bodies of the bull and goat that Aaron had used as the purification offerings. Nobody knows who this person was or how the priests chose this person. All we know is that this person would have done his or her part immediately after Aaron had burned up the fat from the purification offering on the bronze altar.

The bull and goat each had five parts: the blood, the fat, the hide, the meat, and the waste. Aaron had already used the blood during the Day of Atonement ritual to cleanse, or make atonement for, Aaron and Aaron's household, the whole Tent of Meeting, the bronze altar, and all of the people of Israel. And in the first scene of this passage, Aaron had burned all of the fat on the bronze altar.

The only parts of the animal that were left were the hide, meat, and waste. For these remaining parts, someone would take the hide, meat, and waste outside of the area where everyone was camping. Then, that person needed to burn the hide, meat, and waste with fire.

After the person burned up the hide, meat, and waste, that person needed to wash their clothing and their body with water. After the person had washed their body and clothing, the person could come back into the area where everyone else was camping and join everyone else.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:23–28 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has three scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Aaron
  • The person who released the live goat
  • The person who burned up the dead bodies of the purification offerings
  • And the people of Israel

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

In this section, Yahweh finishes telling Moses the instructions that Moses needs to tell Aaron about the Day of Atonement ritual.

Yahweh speaks to Moses first about Aaron. Yahweh says, "After that, Aaron needs to come into the Tent of Meeting and take off the linen clothing that Aaron had put on at the beginning when Aaron first went into the Most Holy Place. Aaron should leave the linen clothing inside the Tent of Meeting.

"Next, Aaron needs to wash his body with water in the holy place and put on the clothes that Aaron had been wearing earlier.

"After Aaron has washed his body and changed his clothing, Aaron needs to come out and offer a burnt offering for Aaron and a burnt offering for the people of Israel. These burnt offerings will cleanse, or atone for, Aaron and the people of Israel.

"Next, Aaron needs to burn the fat from the purification offerings of the bull and goat on the bronze altar."

Yahweh speaks to Moses next about the person who had released the live goat into the desert area where no one lived. Yahweh says, "The person who released the live goat into the area where no one lived needs to wash his clothing and his body with water. After the person has washed himself and his clothing, the person may come back into the area where everyone is camping."

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the one who had released the live goat into the desert area, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am glad Yahweh made an easy way for me to become clean after I released the goat; or
  • I am glad to wash the ritual dirtiness from the goat off of me; or
  • I want to wash quickly so I do not miss more of the ritual.
Continue the drama.

Yahweh speaks to Moses next about what needs to happen to the hide, meat, and waste of the purification offerings of the bull and goat. Yahweh says, "Someone needs to take the dead bodies of the bull and the goat that Aaron used for the purification offerings outside of the area where everyone is camping. This bull and this goat are the animals whose blood Aaron had used to cleanse the holy area.

"After this person brings the bodies of the bull and goat outside of the area where everyone is camping, that person needs to burn up what is left of both animals. This means that the person needs to burn up the animals' hide, meat, and waste.

"After the person burns up the rest of both the bull and the goat, the person needs to wash their clothing and body with water. Then the person can come into the area where everyone is camping."

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the one who burned up the rest of the purification offerings, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am happy that I have the honor to burn up the bull and goat; or
  • I want to make sure everything burns up; or
  • I am glad to be clean so I can join everyone else again.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:23–28 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

In this passage, Yahweh finishes telling Moses the instructions that Moses needs to tell Aaron about the Day of Atonement ritual.

Yahweh speaks to Moses first about Aaron. Yahweh says, "After that, Aaron needs to come into the Tent of Meeting and take off the linen clothing that Aaron had put on at the beginning when Aaron first went into the holy place. Aaron should leave the linen clothing inside the Tent of Meeting." Use the same words for Tent of Meeting and linen clothing that you used before. Look up tabernacle in the Master Glossary for more information. For this reference to "holy place," you may use a general word for holy place or sanctuary, or you may use your word for the Most Holy Place behind the curtain where the ark of the covenant is. Remember that "Most Holy Place" is in the Master Glossary.

Next, Aaron needs to wash his body with water in the sanctuary, or holy place, and put on the clothes that Aaron had been wearing earlier. It is not clear exactly where this holy place was, but it was probably either the Tent of Meeting or somewhere in the courtyard that surrounded the Tent of Meeting.

Stop here and decide how to refer to where Aaron washed himself. Make sure that whether you use the word for the Tent of Meeting or for the courtyard, you do not use the words that talk specifically about the Most Holy Place behind the curtain where the ark of the covenant is. Look up sanctuary in the Master Glossary for more information. Pause this audio here.

After Aaron has washed his body and changed his clothing, Aaron needs to come out and offer a burnt offering for Aaron and a burnt offering for the people of Israel. Use the same word for burnt offering that you used before. Look up burnt offering in the Master Glossary for more information.

These burnt offerings will atone for Aaron and the people of Israel. Use the same word for atone for that you used before. Look up atonement in the Master Glossary for more information.

Next, Aaron needs to offer the fat from the purification offering on the bronze altar as smoke. In other words, Aaron needs to burn the fat completely so that it makes a good smell for Yahweh. Use the same words for fat, purification offering, and bronze altar as you have used before. Look up purification offering and altar in the Master Glossary for more information.

Yahweh speaks to Moses next about the person who had released the live goat into the wilderness area where no one lived. Yahweh says, "The person who released the goat for the scapegoat needs to wash his clothing and his body with water." Remember that nobody knows exactly what Yahweh meant by the Hebrew word for scapegoat. Some people think it refers to a rough and challenging place, like the wilderness area where the person released the goat. Other people think it is actually two words that mean "sent away goat." Use the same word for scapegoat as you used before.

Yahweh says, "After the person has washed himself and his clothing, the person can come back into the area where everyone is camping."

Yahweh speaks to Moses next about what needs to happen to the hide, meat, and waste of the purification offerings of the bull and goat. Yahweh says, "Someone needs to take the dead bodies of the bull and the goat that Aaron used for the purification offerings outside of the area where everyone is camping. This bull and this goat are the animals whose blood Aaron had used to cleanse, or atone for, the holy area."

Stop here and discuss as a group: It is possible that the phrase "holy area" here refers only to the place behind the curtain, the Most Holy Place, but it probably refers to Yahweh's entire tent, or sanctuary. Your local translation may say "Most Holy Place," however. Decide how you will translate this: either as the "Most Holy Place" or as the more general term "sanctuary." Pause this audio here.

After this person brings the bodies of the bull and goat outside of the area where everyone is camping, the person needs to burn up what is left of both animals. This means that the person needs to burn up the animals' hide, meat, and waste. It is not clear what the "waste" of the animals was. It could have been the animal's poop. It could have been the animal's intestines. Or it could have been both the animal's dung and the animal's intestines.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of a bull and a goat. Then look at pictures of a slaughtered animal's hide, meat, and waste. Translate these things in the same way you have in Leviticus 4:11, and decide how you will talk about the animals' waste. Pause this audio here.

After the person burns up the rest of both the bull and the goat, the person needs to wash their clothing and body with water. Then the person can come into the area where everyone is camping. Use the same words and phrases for when a person washes their clothing and body with fresh water as you have used previously.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 16:29–34
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 16:29–34 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:29–34 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:29–34 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this part, Yahweh gave Moses some final commands about the details of the Day of Atonement ritual.

Yahweh told Moses that the Day of Atonement ritual would be a requirement that the people of Israel had to do for all time. This ritual was supposed to happen every year on the tenth day of the seventh month, which was harvest time for the Israelites. On the first day of the seventh month, the people of Israel were supposed to blow trumpets and celebrate a special day of rest. Then, ten days later, the people of Israel were supposed to celebrate the Day of Atonement.

On the Day of Atonement, while the high priest was doing his part of the ritual, the people of Israel were supposed to celebrate the day by doing two things. The first thing the people needed to do was humble, or "lower," their souls. In this part of the Bible, this phrase means that the people of Israel needed to fast. When the people of Israel fasted, the people did not eat or drink as a way to show how sorry the people were for what the people did and to ask Yahweh to forgive the people. It is possible that the people also did not have sexual relations with their husbands or wives on this day, so that the people would remain ritually clean on that day.

The second thing the people of Israel needed to do was rest and avoid working. These requirements about fasting and resting applied to everyone. It did not matter if the person was a descendant of the man named Israel or if the person was not a descendant of Israel but had moved to live with the Israelites. Everyone who was traveling and camping around Yahweh's tent needed to celebrate the Day of Atonement.

People needed to fast and to rest because this was the day that Yahweh chose for the high priest to atone for and cleanse all of the people from the ways the people had betrayed Yahweh. The bad things that people did would make the people ritually dirty. The Day of Atonement ritual would make people ritually clean. To be ritually clean was very important. If no one removed the bad things that people did, then those people would still be ritually dirty, and Yahweh would punish those people for the bad things those people did. Also, Yahweh was holy, and that meant that everything, every place, and every person near Yahweh needed to be physically, ritually, and spiritually clean. If people wanted to live near Yahweh, the people needed someone to remove all of the bad things that the people had done from the people so that the people could be clean. The Day of Atonement ritual was the way Yahweh made for the people to become clean. Then Yahweh would not punish the people for the bad things the people did, and the people could live near Yahweh. Yahweh wanted the Israelites to know that the Israelites did not need to be afraid or worry because Yahweh had already made a way to cleanse the Israelites from all of the bad things that the Israelites had done. This is the most important part of this passage.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Tell a story about a time when you felt relieved because someone forgave you for something wrong you did and did not punish you. Why do you think it was important for the Israelites to know that Yahweh had made a way to cleanse them from their sins? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh then repeated that the Day of Atonement was also a special day of rest for the people of Israel. In addition to resting, the people also needed to fast. These were the requirements for the people of Israel on the Day of Atonement.

The anointed priest was the one who would do the cleansing, or atoning, part of the ritual. In this ritual, the anointed priest was the high priest. At this time, the first high priest was Aaron. Earlier, Moses had used oil to anoint, or choose, and confirm Aaron as Yahweh's high priest. During the ritual to anoint Aaron as the high priest, Aaron had filled his hands with bread and meat as an offering to Yahweh. Because Aaron was the high priest, Yahweh said that Aaron would do the first Day of Atonement ritual. But Yahweh knew Aaron would eventually die. So Yahweh made a way for another priest to do the Day of Atonement ritual after Aaron died.

Yahweh decided that after Aaron died, Aaron's son would be the next high priest. The next high priest would then put on the holy linen clothing and do the Day of Atonement ritual to cleanse the Most Holy Place behind the curtain and the rest of the Tent of Meeting, the bronze altar, the priests, and all of the people of Israel. After Aaron's son died, Aaron's grandson would become the next high priest. To become the next high priest, someone would pour oil on the head of each new high priest to anoint that man for the special role of Yahweh's high priest. During the ritual to anoint the new high priest, the priest who became the new high priest would do the same thing that Aaron had done before and fill his hands with bread and meat as an offering to Yahweh. In other words, Yahweh would ordain the new high priest. Each new high priest would then do what Aaron did on the Day of Atonement. This process would continue for all time.

These requirements for the Day of Atonement ritual would also happen every year for all time in order to cleanse the people of Israel from all of the ways the people had betrayed Yahweh and done bad things to other people.

After Moses told everyone what to do, Aaron did what Yahweh had commanded Moses.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:29–34 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has three scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells Moses what the people of Israel need to do to celebrate the Day of Atonement.

In the second scene: Yahweh tells Moses that each high priest after Aaron needs to do the Day of Atonement ritual like Aaron does it.

In the third scene: The storyteller emphasizes that Aaron obeys Yahweh.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Aaron
  • Aaron's son
  • Aaron's other descendants who will be high priests
  • Aaron's other descendants who will be other priests
  • The Israelites
  • And foreigners who live with the Israelites

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

Yahweh talks about what to do at the Tent of Meeting and the place where the Israelites were camping.

Stop and have someone give another person instructions about something important. Pay attention to how the speaker emphasizes the important part. Pause the audio here.

Yahweh tells Moses the information in the first scene in a special way because Yahweh wants to emphasize what the Israelites need to do. Yahweh gives Moses two pieces of information, and then Yahweh tells Moses the most important part. After Yahweh tells Moses the most important part of Yahweh's message, Yahweh repeats the two pieces of information in a reverse way. Here is what Yahweh says to Moses.

In the first piece of information, Yahweh tells Moses that the statute, or requirement, will last for all time. Every year on the tenth day of the seventh month, the people of Israel must celebrate the Day of Atonement.

Stop and discuss how people usually talk about times of the year, especially days and months. Pause the audio here.

In the second piece of information, Yahweh tells Moses that all of the people of Israel need to humble their souls and rest on the tenth day of the seventh month. When the people humble their souls, the people deny themselves of something. In this case, the people probably fasted, or did not allow themselves to eat food. The people may have also denied themselves from having sexual relations.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will talk about how the Israelites deny themselves. If in your language you need to say what the people deny themselves, you may say that the people fast or deny themselves from eating. Pause this audio here.

The people also need to rest because this ritual is a special day of rest. Everyone must do this. All of Israel's descendants must do this, and all of the people from other people groups who live with the Israelites must do this. These people from other people groups, or foreigners, have decided to live among the Israelites permanently and follow many of the same rules and customs as the Israelites do.

Then Yahweh tells Moses the most important part. Yahweh reminds Moses that the Day of Atonement is for the people of Israel. Yahweh says that the purpose of the Day of Atonement is to atone for and clean, or purify, the Israelites from all their sins. This means that at the end of the Day of Atonement, Yahweh will restore the Israelites' relationship with Yahweh and completely cleanse the Israelites from all of the ways the Israelites had betrayed Yahweh and all of the bad things the Israelites had done to other people. When the Israelites have a relationship with Yahweh because the Israelites are ritually and spiritually clean, then the bad things the Israelites have done do not make the Israelites ritually dirty anymore. So the people of Israel do not have to worry that Yahweh will punish the Israelites. This statement helps the Israelites not worry because Yahweh makes a way to completely purify the Israelites from all of the bad things the Israelites do.

After Yahweh tells Moses the most important part, Yahweh repeats the first two pieces of information. Yahweh says that these requirements will last for all time and that everyone must fast and rest.

Stop and discuss among yourselves how best to organize the first two pieces of information and the most important part. Make sure to emphasize the most important part. Pause the audio here.

In the second scene, Yahweh tells Moses that each high priest after Aaron needs to do the Day of Atonement ritual like Aaron does. Since Aaron will die in the future, Yahweh makes a way for the ritual to continue. Someone will anoint and ordain Aaron's son as the next high priest. This next high priest will do everything that Aaron had done. The new high priest will put on the holy linen clothing and atone for the Most Holy Place behind the curtain and the Tent of Meeting, the bronze altar, all of the priests, and all of the people of Israel. In this scene, Yahweh repeats that the high priest will atone. The reason Yahweh keeps using the word "atone" is to emphasize the main purpose of the high priest's role on this day. Yahweh requires the high priests to perform the Day of Atonement ritual every year for all time.

In the third scene, the storyteller says that Aaron does exactly what Yahweh told Aaron to do.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:29–34 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has three scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Aaron
  • Aaron's son
  • Aaron's other descendants who will be high priests
  • Aaron's other descendants who will be other priests
  • The Israelites
  • And foreigners who live with the Israelites

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

Yahweh told Moses, "These are what I am requiring you all to do for all time. Every year, on the tenth day of the seventh month, you need to fast, and you must not work at all. These statutes apply to both people who are blood descendants of Israel and people from other people groups who live with you. The reason this day is so important is that it is the day that the high priest will atone for you and cleanse you from all of the ways you have betrayed me and done bad things to other people. The purpose is so that you all will be clean."

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing a foreigner, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am glad that Yahweh cares about me, even though I am not a blood descendant of Israel; or
  • I am glad that Yahweh made a way for me to become clean, too.
Continue the drama.

Yahweh said, "The Day of Atonement will be a special rest day for all of you, where you will spend the day fasting from food and water. I require you to do this every year for all time.

"Each high priest after Aaron will make atonement. This is the high priest on whose head someone poured oil to choose the man as high priest. This is the high priest who filled his hands with offerings to Yahweh to ordain himself as the high priest. Each new high priest will take over his father's position. This new high priest will put on the holy linen clothing and atone for the Most Holy Place behind the curtain and the rest of the Tent of Meeting, the bronze altar, all of the priests, and all of the people of Israel. The new high priest will be responsible for cleansing on the Day of Atonement. I require each high priest to do this ritual every year for all time in order to cleanse the Israelites from all the ways the Israelites betray Yahweh and from all the bad things the Israelites did to other people."

So Aaron did what Yahweh commanded Moses.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Aaron, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I want to do everything exactly right; or
  • I wish my two oldest sons had listened to Yahweh and had not died; or
  • I am glad Yahweh made a way to cleanse all of us so we do not die and so we can live near Yahweh.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 16:29–34 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

Yahweh told Moses, "These are what I require you to do for all time." People often translate the word for "requirement" as "statute." A statute is usually a requirement or instruction that a group of people has to do. Often, when Yahweh used this word in the law Yahweh gave the people through Moses, this word focused specifically on the religious rules about how to celebrate festivals, perform religious rituals, and offer sacrifices of animals and grain. Yahweh also used this word to talk about the rules for what the priests needed to do. Look up statute in the Master Glossary for more information, and translate statute in the same way you have previously.

Yahweh said, "Every year, on the tenth day of the seventh month, you need to deny yourself, or fast, and you must not work at all." People may have denied themselves both food and sexual relations. However, if you need to say what people denied themselves, it is best to talk about people denying themselves of food. When people fasted, people did not eat anything or drink anything. People usually fasted to show how sad those people were that something had happened or how sorry those people were for the bad thing that those people had done. Since the focus of the Day of Atonement was cleansing from the bad things people had done, the people probably denied themselves on the Day of Atonement to show how sorry the people were.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for deny yourself, or fast. Look up fasting in the Master Glossary for more information if you decide to translate this as fasting. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh said, "These requirements apply to both people who are blood descendants of Israel and foreigners who moved to live with you." This word for "foreigners" refers to people who were born in a different country and then moved from their home country to live somewhere else. These people were not related to the rest of the people of Israel, but these people had decided to permanently live with the people of Israel.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for foreigner. Look up foreigner in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, see if it is best to use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh said, "The reason this day is so important is that it is the day that the high priest will atone for you and purify you from all of the ways you have betrayed, or sinned against, me and done bad things to other people. The priest does this so that you all will be clean to Yahweh." In the original language, Yahweh does not say who performs the rituals on the Day of Atonement here, but if you need to say who does the rituals, you may say that it is the high priest. Use the same words for high priest, atone, purify, sin, clean, and Yahweh that you used before. Look up high priest, atonement, purify, sin, clean and unclean, and Yahweh, in the Master Glossary for more information.

Yahweh said, "This day will be a special, or Sabbath, rest day for all of you, where you will spend the day fasting from food and water. I require you to do this every year for all time." Some festivals encouraged people to rest but also allowed the people to do some kinds of work on those days. However, the Day of Atonement was a special rest day. This means that people could not do any kind of work at all. You will remember that the Sabbath, or rest day, was normally the seventh day of each week for the Israelites and was also a special day of rest. Here, Yahweh uses the word for Sabbath to remind the Israelites that they should rest on the Day of Atonement in the same way they rest on the weekly Sabbath day of rest.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for Sabbath, or special rest day. Refer to the Master Glossary for Sabbath. If you have already translated this idea in another book of the Bible, see if it is best to use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh said, "Each priest after Aaron will make atonement. This is the high priest whom someone anointed. In other words, someone poured oil on that man's head to choose that man as high priest. Someone ordained this high priest, or filled his hand with meat and bread to offer to Yahweh." Use the same words for anoint and ordain that you used before. Look up anoint in the Master Glossary for more information.

Yahweh said, "Each new high priest will take over his father's position. This new high priest will put on the holy linen clothing and atone for the Most Holy Place and the rest of the Tent of Meeting, the altar, all of the priests, and all of the people of Israel." Use the same words for holy, linen, Most Holy Place, Tent of Meeting, altar, and priest as you used before. Look up holy, Most Holy Place, tabernacle, altar, and priest in the Master Glossary for more information.

The high priests made atonement for all the assembly or people of Israel, along with the foreigners who lived there. Use the same word or phrase for assembly when it means all the people of Israel, as you have used earlier.

So Aaron did what Yahweh commanded Moses. Use the same words for command that you used before.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 17:1–9
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 17:1–9 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 17:1–9 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 17:1–9 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

This passage begins the next big section of Leviticus, where Yahweh teaches the Israelites more specific rules about how to live as Yahweh's people in a holy way. This way of life will show other people that the Israelites are Yahweh's special people. In this passage, Yahweh told Moses to give commands to Aaron, Aaron's sons, and all of the rest of the Israelites about where to bring their sacrifices and what not to do with the animal blood that they used in those sacrifices.

Yahweh did not allow the Israelites to kill animals for the sacrifices to Yahweh anywhere except at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. Remember that the Tent of Meeting was where Yahweh met with the Israelites, and the people thought of the tent as Yahweh's home. That is one of the reasons why people had to bring their offerings to the Tent of Meeting.

The other, and more important, reason was that Yahweh did not want the Israelites to sacrifice any part of the animal to false gods, which were demons. The people who lived around the Israelites would sometimes pour blood on the ground to sacrifice to false gods and demons because people believed these gods lived below the earth in the underworld. The underworld was where people believed that people would go after people died. Yahweh did not want the people of Israel to even think about pouring blood on the ground for these false gods and demons. So Yahweh told the people of Israel to always bring their sacrifices to the Tent of Meeting, where the priests would use the animal's blood the way that Yahweh had said to.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Do people in your culture, or in the cultures around you, use blood in any religious or magic rituals? What do people do with the blood? Why do people do that? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh said that the people of Israel must not kill any animal for sacrifice inside or outside the area where the people of Israel were camping. It did not matter whether the people were sacrificing an ox, a lamb, a goat, or any other animal. Some people think this rule is for any time a person kills an ox, lamb, or goat, even when the people just want to eat the animal. But this rule is probably for when people specifically want to sacrifice an animal for an offering to Yahweh. The people had to bring the animal to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting to offer the animal to Yahweh. The entrance to the Tent of Meeting was somewhere in the courtyard area between the entrance to the courtyard and the entrance to the tent itself. It was probably near the bronze altar.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of the Tent of Meeting, the bronze altar, and the surrounding courtyard. Pause this audio here.

Anyone who did not bring their animal to the Tent of Meeting to sacrifice the animal for Yahweh would be guilty. It is not clear what exactly the person was guilty of. The Hebrew words say that the person would be guilty of pouring out blood. This can mean one of three things. It might mean that the person was guilty of pouring blood onto the ground as a sacrifice to the underworld demons. Or it might mean that Yahweh was going to consider what the person did the same as murdering a person. Or it might be a general way to say that the person did something wrong with blood. Since life is connected to blood, and Yahweh is the owner of all life—and therefore all blood—then to do something wrong with blood was a serious offense.

If someone was guilty of killing an animal to sacrifice the animal away from the Tent of Meeting, the penalty was to "be cut off from their people." No one knows exactly what this means. It either means that someone killed that person, or that the community sent the person away from the nation of Israel. That meant that the person would have to move away from all of that person's friends and family. That person would no longer be one of Yahweh's people, so Yahweh would not protect, provide for, or take care of that person anymore.

Yahweh said that even though the Israelites had been offering Yahweh animal sacrifices in the open field before people made the Tent of Meeting, now that there was a Tent of Meeting, the Israelites had to bring their sacrifices to the Tent of Meeting. The Israelites could not continue to offer sacrifices to Yahweh in the fields. The Israelites had to bring their sacrifices to the priests at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

The entrance of the Tent of Meeting is where the Israelites would offer their fellowship, or peace, offerings. The fellowship offerings were special because those were the only sacrifices where the person who offered the sacrifice would eat part of the meat to show their friendship and connection with Yahweh. Yahweh wanted to be sure that Yahweh's people were only eating sacrifices with Yahweh and not with underworld demons.

After someone brought their sacrifice to Yahweh to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, the priest would sprinkle or throw the blood on Yahweh's bronze altar, which was near the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. The priest would also burn up the fat from the animals on the bronze altar like incense that would smell good to Yahweh.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of the bronze altar. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh said that the people of Israel must not sacrifice to the male goats anymore. Nobody knows exactly what these "male goats" refer to. People who lived back then often thought of both goats and demons as living in the wilderness, so these "goats" were probably connected to the underworld demons. But Yahweh said that the people of Israel must not pour out blood to the goats or demons.

Yahweh said that to pour out blood to these goats, or underworld demons, was the same as being unfaithful against Yahweh, like a husband or wife is unfaithful to their husband or wife. When Yahweh and the people of Israel made a covenant with each other, the people of Israel promised that Yahweh would be their only God. This covenant was similar to a wife promising to only have one husband and to be faithful to her husband. If the people of Israel worshipped other gods and goddesses, it was the same as a wife who slept with a man who was not her husband. Yahweh used this language to emphasize how serious it was to sacrifice or pour out blood to other gods and goddesses. Most of the people who lived around Israel were used to worshipping and sacrificing to many different gods and goddesses at the same time, so it was easy for the Israelites to think that the Israelites could worship many different gods and goddesses as long as the Israelites also worshiped Yahweh. But Yahweh said that worshipping other gods and goddesses was as wrong and as serious as a married woman sleeping with men who were not her husband.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Do people in your culture think it is okay to worship or sacrifice to more than one spirit, or god or goddess? Why or why not? If Yahweh were talking to the people in your culture, what language might Yahweh use to emphasize how important it is to only worship Yahweh and sacrifice to Yahweh? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh said that this rule about not pouring out blood or sacrificing animals to anyone other than Yahweh would last forever throughout every generation. This rule would never change. Yahweh also told the people that this rule applied both to the people who were blood-related descendants of Israel and to people who had a different ancestor but who had moved to live with the Israelites. Anyone who offered a burnt offering or any other kind of sacrifice had to bring the animal for the sacrifice to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. Whoever sacrificed the animal somewhere else had to "be cut off." Again, this either means that someone killed that person or that the person was no longer one of Yahweh's people.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 17:1–9 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has two scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells Moses to command all of the Israelites to bring their sacrifices of animals to Yahweh's Tent of Meeting.

In the second scene: Yahweh tells Moses that the commands about only sacrificing animals at Yahweh's Tent of Meeting apply to foreigners who live with the Israelites.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Aaron, who is the head priest
  • Aaron's sons, who are the priests
  • The people of Israel, who are sacrificing animals
  • And foreigners who live with the Israelites

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

Yahweh talks about what the Israelites should do at the entrance of Yahweh's Tent of Meeting and the bronze altar, which is in the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting. Yahweh also talks about what the Israelites should not do in an open field or anywhere that is not the courtyard of the Tent of Meeting.

These instructions from Yahweh begin a large new section in Leviticus about how to live in a holy, or clean, way.

In this whole passage, Yahweh tells the people to stop sacrificing, or killing animals for sacrifice, in the open field where the Israelites have sacrificed animals to Yahweh in the past. Yahweh also tells the Israelites not to sacrifice to the goat demons, as the Israelites have done in the past. Instead, Yahweh says the Israelites must only sacrifice to Yahweh and that the Israelites must bring all of their sacrifices to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting.

Stop here and have someone give instructions about how people need to stop doing a cultural tradition that people have been doing, and how people need to do something else instead. How does the person who gives the instructions explain the difference between what people have done traditionally and what people need to do now? How does the person emphasize how important it is for people to change their actions? Pause this audio here.

In scene one, Yahweh tells Moses to command Aaron, the head priest, Aaron's sons, who are the priests, and all of the Israelites to bring their sacrifices of animals to Yahweh's Tent of Meeting.

Yahweh says that the Israelites must not kill animals for the sacrifice anywhere except at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. It does not matter whether the people are sacrificing an ox, a lamb, a goat, or any other animal. The Israelites have to bring the animal to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting to offer the animal to Yahweh. If someone kills the animal anywhere else—whether inside the area where the people of Israel were camping or outside the area where the people of Israel were camping—then that person was guilty of doing something wrong with blood. The punishment was that either someone would kill that person or that person would no longer be one of Yahweh's people.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: How do you talk about bad things that people do that have to do with blood, such as when people offer blood to the wrong god, spirit, or ancestor, or people kill an animal the wrong way? Discuss how you want to translate the way that the person would be guilty of doing something wrong with blood. Pause this audio here.

In the past, the people of Israel had been sacrificing, or killing animals, for Yahweh in the open fields. But now Yahweh will no longer allow the Israelites to do that. Instead, the Israelites have to bring their sacrifices to Yahweh at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, to the priests. That is the only place where the people of Israel may sacrifice fellowship or peace offerings.

Once the Israelites give the animal to the priest at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, the priest will sprinkle or throw the blood around Yahweh's bronze altar. This altar was at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. Then the priest will burn the fat from the sacrifice on top of the bronze altar like incense that smells good to Yahweh.

Yahweh says that the people of Israel must not sacrifice to the goat demons anymore. These were the goat demons that the people of Israel had sacrificed to before. When the people of Israel sacrificed to the goat demons, that was as serious and as wrong as when a married woman sleeps with a man who was not her husband.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: How do you talk about the way a married woman sleeps with a man that she is not married to? Discuss how you will compare the way the Israelites sacrificed to the goat-demons to the way a married woman sleeps with a man who is not her spouse. Pause this audio here.

This statute, or rule, about not pouring out blood or sacrificing animals to anyone other than Yahweh will last forever throughout every generation. This rule will never change.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will describe the way the statue will last forever. Pause this audio here.

In scene two, Yahweh tells Moses that the commands about only sacrificing animals at Yahweh's Tent of Meeting also applied to immigrants or foreigners who moved to live with the Israelites. Anyone who offers a burnt offering or any other kind of sacrifice—whether the person is a blood-descendant of Israel or not—has to bring the animal for the sacrifice to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. If a person sacrifices an animal somewhere else, then either someone needs to kill that person, or that person is no longer one of Yahweh's people.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 17:1–9 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has two scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Aaron, who is the head priest
  • Aaron's sons, who are the priests
  • The people of Israel, who are sacrificing animals
  • And foreigners who live with the Israelites

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

Yahweh spoke to Moses and said, "Tell Aaron and his sons and all of the people of Israel what I am commanding you right now.

"If any of the people of Israel kill an animal like an ox, lamb, or goat to sacrifice inside the area where everyone is camping or outside the area where everyone is camping, and the person does not bring the animal to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting to Yahweh to sacrifice the animal there, then that person will be guilty of doing something wrong with blood. The punishment will be that the person will no longer be a part of his people.

"Even though the people of Israel have been sacrificing in the open fields, the Israelites must not do that anymore. The Israelites need to bring their sacrifices to Yahweh at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. The Israelites must give the animals to the priests to sacrifice the animals as fellowship offerings to Yahweh.

"The priest will throw the blood around Yahweh's bronze altar, which is at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. The priest will burn the fat from the animal on the bronze altar like incense that smells good to Yahweh.

"The people of Israel cannot continue to sacrifice to the goat demons. The Israelites have been acting like a married woman who sleeps with men who are not her husband, and the Israelites need to stop that."

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I need to stop sacrificing to goat demons; or
  • I did not realize it was this serious; or
  • I hope Yahweh protects me from the goat demons if I stop sacrificing to the goat demons.
Continue the drama.

Yahweh said, "This statute will last forever for the Israelites. It will apply to every generation."

Yahweh also said, "Tell the Israelites that this statute applies to Israel's blood descendants and to immigrants who have a different ancestor but who moved to live with the people of Israel. Anyone who offers a burnt offering or any other kind of sacrifice—whether the person is a blood descendant of Israel or not—and who does not bring their animal to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting to offer it to Yahweh will be punished. The punishment will be either that someone will kill that person or, more likely, that person will not belong to Yahweh anymore."

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the immigrants, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I did not realize that I would only be allowed to sacrifice to Yahweh; or
  • I am glad that Yahweh thinks of me as one of Yahweh's people; or
  • I need to make sure I only sacrifice to Yahweh.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 17:1–9 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

Yahweh spoke to Moses and said, "Tell Aaron and his sons and all of the people of Israel what I am commanding you right now." Use the same word or phrase for Yahweh and Israelites as you have used in previous passages. For more information on Yahweh and Israelites, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh talks about what happens if any of the people of Israel kill an animal like an ox, lamb, or goat to sacrifice or give these animals as an offering anywhere outside the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. Some people might not sacrifice an animal at the Tent of Meeting, but instead inside the area where everyone is camping or outside the area where everyone is camping. If a person does not kill the animal for the offering at the tabernacle, then that person will be guilty of doing something wrong with blood." Use the same word for ox, lamb, goat, Tent of Meeting, tabernacle, and offering that you used before. Use the same word or phrase for killing an animal as a sacrifice as you have used before. Look up offering, sacrifice, and tabernacle in the Master Glossary for more information. Note that Yahweh uses both the phrases for Tent of Meeting and for tabernacle in this passage.

Stop here as a group and look again at a picture of an ox, a lamb, a goat, and the Tent of Meeting as needed. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh said, "The punishment will be that someone will cut off the person who used the blood wrongly." No one knows exactly what this means. It probably means either that someone will have to kill that person to punish them or that the community will send the person away from the people of Israel. That meant that the person would have to move away from all of their friends and family. The person would no longer be one of Yahweh's people, so Yahweh would not protect, provide for, or take care of that person anymore. Use the same word or phrase for this punishment that you used before.

Yahweh said, "Even though the people of Israel have been sacrificing in the open fields, the Israelites cannot do that anymore."

Stop here and discuss what word or phrase you will use for sacrifice here. This is the word that means that someone gives a gift to Yahweh on an altar. Refer to the Master Glossary for more information about sacrifices. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and look at a picture of an open grain field as a group. Use the same word or phrase for this place that you used before. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh said, "The Israelites need to bring their sacrifices to Yahweh at the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. The Israelites must give the animals to the priests to sacrifice the animals as peace or fellowship offerings to Yahweh. The priest will throw the blood around Yahweh's altar, which is at the entrance, or courtyard, of the Tent of Meeting. The priest will burn the fat from the animal on the bronze altar so that it will smell good to Yahweh." Look up fellowship offering, priest, and altar in the Master Glossary for more information. Use the same words or phrases for fellowship offering, priest, bronze altar, fat, and "burning the fat to smell good" as you did before.

Yahweh said, "The people of Israel must not continue sacrificing to the goat demons." No one knows exactly what this word refers to. The Hebrew word literally means "male goat," but it is a different word than what Yahweh used earlier to talk about the kinds of animals that the people of Israel might sacrifice. Some of the people in other people groups believed that goats were connected with the wilderness and that the wilderness was connected with the underworld. The underworld was where people believed that people would go after people died. So these "goat demons" might have been connected to the false gods and demons that some people believed lived in the underworld. These people would often pour blood on the ground to make the underworld demons not angry anymore. Yahweh did not allow the people of Israel to pour out blood to these goat demons.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for goat demons. If you use a word for evil spirit or demon, you can look up demon in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh said, "The Israelites have been acting like a married woman who sleeps with men who are not her husband, and the Israelites need to stop that. This rule, or statute, will last forever for the Israelites. It will apply to every generation." Look up statute and generation in the Master Glossary for more information. Use the same words for statute and generation that you have used earlier.

Yahweh also said, "Tell the Israelites that this rule applies to Israel's blood descendants and to foreigners who have a different ancestor but who moved to live with the people of Israel." These foreigners were not related to the Israelites. Instead, these foreigners had a different ancestor. However, the foreigners or their ancestors had left their homeland to move to where the Israelites lived. For most of the laws in the Bible, Yahweh said that the foreigners and the Israelites had the same rules and people needed to treat both the foreigners and the Israelites the same.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for foreigner. Look up foreigner in the Master Glossary for more information. Use the same word for this kind of foreigner that you used in the previous passage. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh said, "Anyone who offers a burnt offering or any other kind of sacrifice—whether the person is a blood descendant of Israel or not—and who does not bring their animal to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting to offer it to Yahweh will be punished. The punishment will be either that someone will kill that person or that person will not belong to Yahweh anymore." Look up burnt offering in the Master Glossary for more information. Use the same word that you used earlier in this book.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.
