title: Leviticus 17:10–16
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 17:10–16 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 17:10–16 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 17:10–16 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this passage, Yahweh emphasized that Yahweh does not allow the Israelites or foreigners with the Israelites to eat blood. Yahweh continued talking to Moses and said that no one may eat blood. This rule means that no one could drink blood or eat meat that still had blood in it. Instead, the people of Israel had to fully drain the blood from an animal before the Israelites ate the meat.

Yahweh said that these rules applied to both Israelites who were blood descendants of Israel and to foreigners who were born in a different country and moved to live with the Israelites. Yahweh thought of these foreigners as part of Yahweh's people, even though the foreigners were not descendants of Israel. That was why the rules applied to the foreigners too.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do you separate out different kinds of people? Does it depend on family, tribe, social status, how long a family has lived in the area, or something else? Are the laws different for different groups of people? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh said that the punishment for a person who drank blood or ate meat with blood still in it was that Yahweh would oppose that person and "cut that person off" from Yahweh's people. This phrase probably means that Yahweh would work against that person until that person died. It might also mean that Yahweh would no longer consider that person as one of Yahweh's people.

Yahweh said that the reason for this rule was that an animal's life was in its blood. People must not eat an animal's life. Yahweh said that the only right way to use an animal's blood was to put the blood on the altar to cleanse, or atone for, people who had done something wrong. The blood would atone for the person's life. Since Yahweh created everything, including the animals, Yahweh owns everything, including the animals' blood. Yahweh said that Yahweh had given the animals' blood to the Israelites to atone for themselves, and that was why the Israelites must not use blood for any other reason.

Since people used an animal's blood to cleanse people, no one who was a member of Yahweh's people—whether a blood descendant of Israel or a foreigner—could drink blood or eat meat that still had blood in it.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what do people think of animal blood? Do people use blood to cook? Do people use blood for any magical or religious reasons? How is your culture's view of blood similar or different from how Yahweh talks about blood? Pause this audio here.

So, if an Israelite or a foreigner who lived with the Israelites went out to hunt and caught a wild animal or a bird that Yahweh allowed the Israelites to eat, that person first had to pour out the animal's or bird's blood on the ground and cover the blood with dirt. These kinds of animals included deer, gazelle, wild goats, mountain sheep, and other wild animals that Yahweh had said people could eat. These kinds of birds included quail, partridges, and other wild birds that Yahweh had said people could eat.

Stop here as a group and look at pictures of the kinds of wild animals and wild birds that the Israelites might have hunted. Pause this audio here.

Even though people could eat these animals and birds, people could not sacrifice the animals. So the blood from these animals and birds would never go on the altar. Instead, whoever caught one of these animals or birds would always have to drain the blood and bury the blood under dirt. No one knows exactly why Yahweh said to cover the blood with dirt. Some people think it was to make sure that no one could drink the blood. Some people think it was to make sure that no one used the blood to do magic or sorcery. And other people think it was to treat the animal with respect by giving the animal's blood a proper burial. But no one knows for certain.

After explaining what to do, Yahweh again emphasized that the reason people had to do this was that the life of animals, birds, and people was in the blood. The blood made it so that animals, birds, and people could live. That was why Yahweh said that no one could drink the blood of anything or eat any meat that had blood in it. The punishment for drinking blood or eating meat with blood in it was that someone would "cut off" that person. In this statement, this phrase either means that that person would die or that people would force the person to leave the community, and that person would no longer be one of Yahweh's people.

Finally, Yahweh told Moses what a person needed to do if that person ate an animal that died of natural causes or that another animal had killed. In Exodus, Yahweh said that the descendants of Israel must not eat an animal that another animal killed. Later in Deuteronomy, Yahweh will say that the descendants of Israel must not eat any animal that the Israelites find already dead, which would include animals that die of natural causes. However, Yahweh did not give those rules to the foreigners who lived with Israel's descendants. The foreigners could eat both animals that had died of natural causes and animals that had died because another animal killed them. However, the foreigners would become ritually unclean or dirty. So here, Yahweh explained what the foreigners should do if the foreigners become ritually dirty because they ate an animal the foreigners found dead. Yahweh also explains what Israel's descendants should do if one of Israel's descendants breaks Yahweh's rule, eats an animal that he or she found already dead, and becomes ritually dirty.

Anyone who ate animals that died needed to wash his or her clothing and body with water and then wait until evening. That person who ate the animal would be ritually dirty until evening. People had to wait for evening because evening began a new day. If the person had washed their body and clothing with water, then that person would become ritually clean when the new day began at evening. However, if the person did not wash their clothing and body, then that person would pay for their crime. This means that someone would punish that person. Yahweh did not say what the punishment was or who would punish the person.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 17:10–16 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has three scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh explains to Moses the only right way to use animal blood.

In the second scene: Yahweh explains to Moses what to do with an animal's blood if someone hunts that animal for food.

In the third scene: Yahweh explains to Moses how a person needs to clean themselves if that person eats an animal that dies naturally or an animal that a wild animal killed.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • An Israelite
  • And a foreigner who lives with the Israelites

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

Yahweh talked about the altar at the Tent of Meeting and places where people would hunt animals.

In the first scene, Yahweh explained to Moses the only right way to use animal blood. The most important information in this scene is in the middle. So at the beginning and the ending of this scene, Yahweh said that Yahweh does not allow the Israelites or foreigners with the Israelites to drink an animal's blood or eat meat with the blood still in it. Yahweh also explained that the punishment for drinking blood or eating meat with the blood still in it was that Yahweh would set Yahweh's face against that person. This phrase probably means that Yahweh would reject and oppose that person and make sure that that person died.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will talk about Yahweh setting his face against a person. Pause this audio here.

The middle part of this scene is the most important because here Yahweh explained why this rule was so important. Yahweh also explained the only right way to use an animal's blood. Yahweh said that an animal's life was in its blood, so people must not eat an animal's life. Yahweh said that the only right way to use an animal's blood was to put the blood on the altar to cleanse or atone for people who had done something wrong. The blood would cleanse, or atone for, the person's life. Since Yahweh created everything, including the animals, Yahweh owns everything, including the animals' blood. Yahweh said that Yahweh had given the animals' blood to the Israelites so that the Israelites could atone for themselves. That was why the Israelites must not use blood for any other reason. This blood was a gift that Yahweh had given to the Israelites to cleanse them, so the Israelites could not use animal blood for any other reason.

Stop and have someone give another person instructions about something important. Pay attention to how the speaker emphasizes the important part. Pause the audio here.

Stop and discuss among yourselves how best to organize this section in your language. Remember to emphasize the most important part. Pause the audio here.

In the second scene, Yahweh explained to Moses what to do with an animal's blood if someone hunted that animal for food. Yahweh explained what an Israelite or a foreigner who lives with the Israelites should do if the person went out hunting and caught a wild animal or a bird. That person first had to pour out the animal's or bird's blood on the ground and cover the blood with dirt.

Then Yahweh explained again the reason why the people had to do this. Yahweh said that the life of animals, birds, and people was in the blood. The blood made it so that animals, birds, and people could live. That was why Yahweh said that no one could drink the blood of anything or eat any meat that had blood in it. The punishment for drinking blood or eating meat with blood in it was that the person who drank or ate blood would be cut off. That person would either have to leave the community or die.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you have translated the idea of Yahweh cutting off someone from the Israelite community. How did you translate this idea? Pause this audio here.

In the third scene, Yahweh explained to Moses how the people of Israel need to clean themselves if someone eats an animal that dies naturally or an animal that wild animals killed. Remember that Yahweh already told Israel's descendants not to eat animals that another animal had killed. Later, Yahweh will tell Israel's descendants not to eat any animal that they find dead. But Yahweh did not give these rules to the foreigners who lived with Israel's descendants. Yahweh allowed foreigners who lived with Israel's descendants to eat animals that died naturally and animals that wild animals killed. However, anyone who ate an animal that died naturally or an animal that wild animals killed would become ritually dirty, or unclean. We are not sure exactly why Yahweh told Israel's descendants what to do if one of Israel's descendants ate an animal that Yahweh said not to eat. Perhaps Yahweh was telling the descendants of Israel what to do if they disobeyed Yahweh in this way. Either way, anyone who ate an animal that someone found dead, whether the person eating was one of Israel's descendants or a foreigner who lived with Israel's descendants, that person who ate the dead animal would become ritually dirty. That person would need to become ritually clean again.

If anyone ate an animal that died of natural causes, or an animal that another animal killed, that person needed to wash their clothing and body with water and then wait until evening, when a new day began. That person who ate the animal would be ritually dirty until the new day began at evening. If that person had washed their body and clothing with water, then that person would become ritually clean when the new day began at evening. However, if the person did not wash his or her clothing and body, then that person would pay for their iniquity, or guilt. This means that someone would punish that person. Yahweh did not say what the punishment was or who would punish the person.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 17:10–16 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has three scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • An Israelite
  • And a foreigner who lives with the Israelites

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

In the first scene, Yahweh explained to Moses the only right way to use animal blood. Yahweh said, "If anyone drinks blood or eats meat with the blood still in it, I will completely oppose that person and make sure that person dies. It does not matter which tribe or household that person belongs to. It does not matter if that person is a descendant of Israel or a foreigner who moved to live among the Israelites. I will oppose that person and make sure that person dies.

"The reason this is so important is that blood is what makes an animal, bird, or person live. I gave you the blood of animals and birds so that you could put that blood on the altar to cleanse yourselves. This blood is to cleanse your lives.

"That is why I told Israel's descendants that no one may drink blood or eat meat with the blood still in it. None of Israel's descendants and none of the foreigners who live among the Israelites may drink blood or eat meat with the blood still in it."

Pause the drama.

Ask the people playing an Israelite and a foreigner, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • Wow, Yahweh is very serious about this rule; or
  • I want to make sure that I do not ever eat meat with blood in it; or
  • I am a little scared of what might happen if I drink blood or eat meat with blood in it.
Continue the drama.

In the second scene, Yahweh explained to Moses what to do with an animal's blood if someone hunted that animal for food. Yahweh said, "If anyone goes hunting and catches any of the animals or birds that I said people could eat, that person has to pour out the blood and cover it with dirt. It does not matter if the person is one of Israel's descendants or a foreigner who lives among the Israelites. Everyone has to pour out the blood of whatever someone hunted and cover that blood with dirt.

"The reason this is so important is that everything that is alive is living because of the blood that is inside the body. This blood keeps every person, animal, and bird alive. That is why I told the Israelites not to eat meat that still has the blood in it. Because blood is what makes an animal, bird, or person live, whoever drinks blood or eats meat with blood in it will be cut off."

In the third scene, Yahweh explained to Moses how the people needed to clean themselves if someone ate an animal that died naturally or an animal that wild animals killed. Yahweh said, "Whoever eats an animal that died naturally or that another animal killed needs to wash their body and clothing in water. That person will be ritually dirty until evening, and then after that, the person will be ritually clean. These rules apply both to blood descendants of Israel and to foreigners who live among the Israelites. If anyone does not wash their body and clothing, then that person will pay for their crime."

Pause the drama.

Ask the people playing an Israelite, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I need to make sure I wash my clothing and my body if I eat an animal that died naturally; or
  • I am glad that it is easy to become ritually clean after eating an animal that died naturally.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 17:10–16 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

Yahweh began this passage by saying, "If anyone drinks blood or eats meat with the blood still in it, I will completely oppose that person and make sure that person dies. It does not matter which tribe or household in Israel that person belongs to. It does not matter if that person is a descendant of Israel or a foreigner who moved to live among the Israelites. I will oppose that person and make sure that person dies." A person is a foreigner in a country when the person is in a country that is not where that person was born. Some foreigners live with the Israelites. Even though foreigners were not descended from Israel, Yahweh thought of the foreigners as members of the community of Israel. Use the same words for Israelite and foreigner that you used previously. Look up Israelite and foreigner in the Master Glossary for more information.

Yahweh said, "The reason this is so important is that blood is what makes an animal, bird, or person live. I gave you the blood of animals and birds so that you could put that blood on the altar to cleanse yourselves. This blood is to atone for your lives." Use the same words for altar, blood, and atone that you used previously. Look up altar, blood, and atonement in the Master Glossary for more information.

Yahweh said, "That is why I told Israel's descendants that no one may drink blood or eat meat with the blood still in it. None of Israel's descendants and none of the foreigners who live among the Israelites may drink blood or eat meat with the blood still in it."

Yahweh continued and said, "If anyone goes hunting and catches any of the animals or birds that I said people could eat, that person has to pour out the blood and cover the blood with dirt." The animals that Yahweh said the people could eat refer to ritually clean animals.

Stop here as a group and look at pictures of some of the kinds of animals or birds that Yahweh said people could eat. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh said, "It does not matter if the person is one of Israel's descendants or a foreigner who lives among the Israelites. Everyone has to pour out the blood of whatever people hunted and cover that blood with dirt."

"The reason this is so important is that everything that is alive is living because of the blood that is inside the body. This blood keeps every person, animal, and bird alive. That is why I told the Israelites not to eat meat that still has the blood in it. Because blood is what makes an animal, bird, or person live, whoever drinks blood or eats meat with blood in it will be cut off." This phrase "cut off" either means that that person would die or that people would force that person to leave the community, and that person would no longer be one of Yahweh's people. Use the same word or phrase for "cut off" as you have used in previous passages.

Yahweh continued and said, "Whoever eats an animal that died naturally or that another animal killed needs to wash their body and clothing in water." An animal that died naturally was an animal that no person or animal had killed, but that had died anyway.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for died naturally. If you have already translated this phrase in another book of the Bible, decide if it is a good idea to use the same phrase that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh said, "That person will be ritually unclean or dirty until evening, and then after that, the person will be ritually clean." Use the same word for ritually dirty and for ritually clean that you used previously. Look up clean and unclean in the Master Glossary for more information.

The person who is ritually dirty must wash their clothes and bathe themselves. Use the same phrases for "wash their clothes" and "bathe themselves in water" as you have used previously.

Yahweh said, "These rules apply both to blood descendants of Israel and to foreigners who live among the Israelites. If anyone does not wash their body and clothing, then that person will pay for their crime, or iniquity." The word for iniquity here is one of the three main words that people used to talk about bad things that someone did. People often used this word when they talked about bad things that someone was going to punish that person for very soon. Use the same word for iniquity that you used previously. Look up iniquity in the Master Glossary for more information.

The word for pay for here literally means "to carry the burden." When someone did something wrong to someone else, there was an offender and a victim. The offender was the person who did the bad thing to the other person, who was the victim. People thought of the bad thing that the offender did, and the punishment for that bad thing or the consequences of doing that bad thing, as the burden. If the victim "carried the burden," that meant that the victim would forgive the offender, and no one would punish the offender. If the offender "carried the burden," that meant that someone would punish the offender for what the offender did. In this passage, Yahweh said that the offender would carry the burden of their iniquity, which means that someone would punish the person who did not wash their body and clothing after eating either an animal that died naturally or an animal that another animal had killed.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for pay for, or carry the burden of their iniquity. If you have already translated this phrase in another book of the Bible, decide if it is a good idea to use the same phrase that you have used there.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 18:1–5
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 18:1–5 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 18:1–5 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 18:1–5 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In previous passages, Yahweh has been explaining to Moses what laws the people need to follow about killing animals and eating blood. In this section of Leviticus, Yahweh will begin explaining a series of laws about who and what the people must not have sex with. Yahweh starts by telling Moses to remind the Israelites who Yahweh is and why the Israelites need to follow Yahweh's rules.

First, Yahweh tells Moses to remind the Israelites that Yahweh is the Israelites' God. Yahweh reminds the Israelites that Yahweh is the Israelites' God because Yahweh wants the Israelites to pay attention to the laws Yahweh is about to give the Israelites. Yahweh is the Israelites' God because Yahweh chose to help and take care of the Israelites.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about when someone in authority needed to use their authority to make new rules. How did the person use their authority to convince people to follow the new rules? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh tells the Israelites not to do what the Israelites did in the land of Egypt, where the Israelites came from. Before Yahweh started giving the Israelites these laws, Yahweh rescued the Israelites from Egypt, a powerful empire that had enslaved the Israelites for many years. Yahweh does not want the Israelites to do the same terrible things that the Egyptian people do, like worshipping gods other than Yahweh or enslaving and mistreating people for generations. Yahweh also does not want the Israelites to do what people in Canaan do. Canaan is the land Yahweh is bringing the Israelites to and the land Yahweh is going to give to the Israelites. Yahweh does not want the Israelites to worship the gods that the Canaanites worship or do the terrible things that the Canaanites do.

Stop here as a group and look at a map of ancient Egypt and Canaan. Pause the audio here.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What things do other nearby people groups do that people in your culture think are terrible or wrong to do? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh tells the Israelites that the Israelites must not obey the laws of those people. Instead, the Israelites need to follow Yahweh's ordinances and statutes. Yahweh reminds the Israelites again that Yahweh is the Israelites' God, and so the Israelites need to follow Yahweh's laws. Yahweh is giving the Israelites laws so that as the Israelites follow the laws, other people will see that the Israelites are different than people around the Israelites. Again, Yahweh says that the Israelites should obey Yahweh's statutes and ordinances. When the Israelites do obey, the Israelites will live. This means that when the Israelites obey Yahweh, Yahweh will take care of the Israelites and not punish the Israelites. Most people who heard these laws mostly focused on the fact that Yahweh was giving the people physical life. But it is clear that in this and similar passages, Yahweh is promising more than just physical life. Yahweh is talking about a happy life in which the Israelites will enjoy all the good things that come from Yahweh: health, children, friends, and everything people need to live well and fulfill Yahweh's purposes for the people in this life. Once again, Yahweh says he is Yahweh.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 18:1–5 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has two scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites not to do what the Egyptians or Canaanites do.

In the second scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites to follow and obey Yahweh's ordinances and statutes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Moses
  • Yahweh
  • The Israelites
  • Yahweh mentions the Egyptians
  • And Yahweh mentions the Canaanites

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

Yahweh has been telling the Israelites how to kill animals and what to do with the blood of animals. Now Yahweh will tell the Israelites different kinds of laws.

In the first scene of this passage, Yahweh talks to Moses. When the storyteller says this, the storyteller is showing that this is a new section in the book of Leviticus. Yahweh tells Moses to tell the Israelites that Yahweh is Yahweh, the Israelites' God. Yahweh says he is Yahweh their God once here and once in this second scene of this passage. At the end of this passage, Yahweh says that he is Yahweh. Yahweh repeats that he is Yahweh so much because Yahweh wants to make it clear that the Israelites are following Yahweh only, not any other god.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: How can you translate these phrases to show how Yahweh is using his authority to establish these new rules? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh tells the Israelites not to do what the people in the land of Egypt do, which is where the Israelites had lived. Then Yahweh tells the Israelites not to do what the people in the land of Canaan do, which is where Yahweh is taking the Israelites to. Yahweh ends the scene by telling the Israelites not to follow the statutes that the Canaanites or Egyptians have. Remember that the Israelites are currently at a place called Mount Sinai, far away from any other group of people. Yahweh has just rescued the Israelites from Egypt. The leaders of Egypt had made the Israelites live as slaves in Egypt for 400 years. A long time before the Egyptians had enslaved the Israelites, Yahweh had promised Abraham, who is an ancestor of the Israelites, that Yahweh would give the land of Canaan to Abraham's descendants. Now, Yahweh has repeated this promise to Abraham's descendants, the Israelites.

In the next scene, Yahweh contrasts the statutes of the Canaanites and the Egyptians, which Yahweh tells the Israelites not to follow, with Yahweh's ordinances and statutes, which Yahweh tells the Israelites to follow and obey instead. Yahweh's ordinances are the decisions that Yahweh makes about what the Israelites should do. Yahweh's statutes are the rules that Yahweh gives the Israelites about how to treat each other and how to perform religious rituals. Yahweh emphasizes that the Israelites need to follow Yahweh's ordinances and statutes when Yahweh says again that he is Yahweh, their God. Then Yahweh says again that the Israelites must follow Yahweh's statutes and decisions. Yahweh reminds the Israelites that if the Israelites obey Yahweh's statutes and ordinances, then the Israelites will live. You will remember that it is clear that in this and similar passages, Yahweh is promising more than just physical life. Yahweh is talking about a happy life in which the Israelites will enjoy all the good things that come from Yahweh: health, children, friends, and everything people need to live well and fulfill Yahweh's purposes for the people in this life.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will say that if a person obeys Yahweh's statutes and ordinances, he will live by them. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh ends this passage when Yahweh tells the Israelites again that he is Yahweh, the Israelites' God. This is the third time Yahweh has clearly stated that he is the Israelites' God. This is a very important statement.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Yahweh is emphasizing that Yahweh is Israel's only god. When you translate this, how will you show that this is an important statement? Pause this audio here.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 18:1–5 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has two scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Moses
  • Yahweh
  • The Israelites
  • Yahweh mentions the Egyptians
  • And Yahweh mentions the Canaanites

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

In the first scene of this passage, Yahweh talks to Moses. Yahweh tells Moses to tell the Israelites that Yahweh is Yahweh, the Israelites' God.

Yahweh tells the Israelites not to do what the people in the land of Egypt do, which is where the Israelites lived. Then Yahweh tells the Israelites not to do what the people in the land of Canaan do, which is where Yahweh is taking the Israelites to. Yahweh ends the scene by telling the Israelites not to follow the laws that the Canaanites or Egyptians have.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the Canaanites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • We do not want to worship Yahweh; or
  • I do not understand why the Israelites will not do what we do; or
  • I like our laws, because our laws are easier to follow.
Continue the drama.

In the next scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites to follow and obey Yahweh's statutes. Yahweh emphasizes that the Israelites need to follow Yahweh's ordinances and statutes when Yahweh says again that he is Yahweh, their God.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I really love my people, the Israelites, and I want the Israelites to do the right thing; or
  • I am worried that the Israelites are going to want to do things how the Egyptians and Canaanites do things.
Continue the drama.

Then Yahweh says again that the Israelites must follow Yahweh's statutes and ordinances. Yahweh reminds the Israelites that if the Israelites obey Yahweh's statutes and ordinances, then the Israelites will live.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am so glad Yahweh explained how I can live a good life; or
  • I need to be careful to obey all the laws and decisions Yahweh has; or
  • Yahweh is making us special people when Yahweh gives us these ordinances and statutes.
Continue the drama.

Yahweh ends this passage by telling the Israelites that he is Yahweh, the Israelites' God.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 18:1–5 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

In the beginning of this passage, Yahweh speaks to Moses. Yahweh is the personal name God gave to Moses for the Israelites to call God. Use the same word or phrase to refer to Yahweh in this passage as you used in previous passages. For more information on Yahweh, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh tells Moses that Yahweh is the Israelites' God. God is the most powerful spiritual being who created everything. Use the same word or phrase to refer to God as you used in previous passages. For more information on God, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh tells the Israelites not to follow the statutes of the people who live in Egypt or Canaan. Statutes are instructions for living in a society, especially concerning its religious practices. Use the same word or phrase to refer to statutes as you did in other passages. For more information on statute, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh also tells the Israelites to obey and follow Yahweh's ordinances. When a person in authority decides how the people need to act, that ordinance becomes a law or a rule that the people need to follow. The person in authority might make this ordinance after people ask the person in authority what the person thinks people should do in a particular situation. Or the person in authority might make the ordinance when the person decides that people need to follow a new rule.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for ordinance. Look at ordinance in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 18:6–18
content:
Hear and Heart

NOTE: This passage talks about subjects that you may want to discuss in groups of only men and only women. Stop here and discuss as a group if you will listen to this passage in groups of only men and only women. Pause this audio here.

In this step, hear Leviticus 18:6–18 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 18:6–18 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 18:6–18 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

NOTE: This passage talks about subjects that you may want to discuss in groups of only men and only women. Stop here and discuss as a group if you will listen to this passage in groups of only men and only women. Pause this audio here.

In this part of Leviticus, Yahweh gives specific rules about who Yahweh allows a person to have sex with. In the previous passage, Yahweh introduced this section on appropriate sexual relations by telling Moses to tell the Israelites not to follow the rules of the Egyptians and the Canaanites, and instead follow Yahweh's statutes and ordinances. In this passage, Yahweh begins explaining which family members Yahweh does not allow the Israelites to have sex with. Yahweh does not allow Israelites to marry people outside of the Israelite people. Israelites often wanted to marry people who were in the same clan or extended family so that people outside the extended family or clan did not inherit the land and possessions the family owned. But Yahweh tells the Israelites not to marry anyone who is too closely related.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what close relations can marry each other? What do people in your culture consider inappropriate marriages because the people are too closely related? Pause this audio here.

First, Yahweh says that no one should approach anyone who is immediate family. Immediate family is mother, father, son, daughter, brother, and sister. Yahweh says a person must not approach a family member to uncover their nakedness, or their genitals. Uncovering nakedness is one way the Israelites talk about having sex with someone that they should not have sex with.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do people talk about having sex with someone that the person should not have sex with? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that he is Yahweh. That is a way Yahweh reminds the Israelites that Yahweh has rescued the Israelites and has authority over the Israelites. Yahweh is also reminding the Israelites that as followers of Yahweh, the Israelites are different than the Egyptians and Canaanites, and the Israelites need to act differently. Yahweh is giving the Israelites rules that help the Israelites show how the Israelites are different. Then Yahweh addresses each man in Israel and starts giving specific rules for whom the men must not have sex with. Yahweh directly talks to the Israelite men. Yahweh says, "You cannot uncover your father's nakedness, or dishonor your father, which means you must not have sex with your mother."

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, why do people not allow a man to have sex with his mother? How is that different or similar to the reason Yahweh gives here? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says, "You must not have sex with your father's wife because the woman's naked body belongs to your father." When Yahweh says "your father's wife," Yahweh does not just mean a man's mother. Sometimes an Israelite man married more than one woman, so a person's father's wife might not be that person's mother. Yahweh does not allow a man to have sex with any woman who is married to the man's father.

Yahweh says, "You must not have sex with your sister, whether the sister was born to your father or just to your mother." That means the man cannot have sex with his full sister or half sister, whether the sister was born in the man's house into the man's family or born outside in another house to another family. That probably means the mother gave birth to the sister in the mother's family's house, and then the mother married the man's father.

Yahweh says, "You must not have sex with your granddaughter, whether the woman is your son's daughter or your daughter's daughter, because the family's nakedness is your nakedness." Here, Yahweh probably means that because the granddaughter is the man's descendant, if the man dishonors anyone in his family, then the man also dishonors himself.

Yahweh says, "You also must not have sex with your father's wife's daughter, or your stepsister." Yahweh says the sister was born to the father, but that probably means that the father adopted the sister when the father married the woman's mother, and that is why Yahweh says the sister is the man's sister.

Yahweh says, "You must not have sex with your aunt on your father's side or mother's side. You also must not expose the nakedness of your father's brother, or shame him, by having sex with your uncle's wife. This woman is your aunt.

"You must not have sex with your daughter-in-law who married your son, because the woman is your son's wife.

"You must not have sex with your brother's wife, because the woman's naked body belongs to your brother.

"You must not have sex with both a woman and her daughter, or a woman and her granddaughter through the woman's daughter or son." The reason a man must not have sex with both a woman and the woman's female descendants is that the descendants are flesh. This probably means that the female descendants are related to the man, but it might mean that the female descendants are related to the mother or grandmother. Yahweh says that when people do this, people are doing a wicked thing.

Finally, Yahweh says, "You must not take a rival wife to her sister," which means a man must not have sex with a sister of the man's wife while the wife is alive. Israelite men sometimes married more than one woman, but Yahweh did not want a man to marry two women who were sisters to each other.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 18:6–18 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has two scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh gives a list of family members that a man cannot have sex with.

In the second scene: Yahweh gives a list of people who a woman is related to that a man cannot have sex with.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • An Israelite man
  • The man's father
  • The man's mother
  • The man's father's wife
  • The man's sister
  • The man's half sister
  • The man's son
  • The man's son's daughter
  • The man's daughter
  • The man's daughter's daughter
  • The man's stepsister
  • The man's father's sister
  • The man's mother's sister
  • The man's father's brother
  • The man's father's brother's wife
  • The man's daughter-in-law
  • The man's brother
  • The man's brother's wife
  • A woman
  • The woman's daughter
  • The woman's daughter's daughter
  • The woman's son
  • The woman's son's daughter
  • The man's wife
  • And the man's wife's sister

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

In this part of Leviticus, Yahweh gives specific rules about who Yahweh will not allow the people to have sex with. In the previous passage, Yahweh introduced this section on appropriate sexual relations by telling Moses to tell the Israelites not to follow the rules of the Egyptians and the Canaanites, and instead follow Yahweh's statutes and ordinances. In this passage, Yahweh begins explaining which family members Yahweh does not allow the Israelites to have sex with.

In the first scene, Yahweh says that no one should approach anyone who is immediate family. Immediate family is mother, father, son, daughter, brother, and sister. Yahweh says not to approach immediate family to uncover their nakedness, or their genitals. Uncovering nakedness is a way Israelites talk about having sex with someone they should not have sex with. When someone "uncovers someone's nakedness," they also shame or dishonor that person.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What word or phrase should you use in this passage to describe sex with people you should not have sex with? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that he is Yahweh. That is a way Yahweh reminds the Israelites that Yahweh has rescued the Israelites and has authority over the Israelites. Then Yahweh addresses each man in Israel and starts to give specific rules about whom the men cannot have sex with. Yahweh directly speaks to the Israelites in this passage. In your language, you may need to specify each time that Yahweh is talking to each type of Israelite man.

When Yahweh talks about the different family relationships, Yahweh is trying to tell the Israelite men not to sleep with anyone who is too closely related to the men. Each time Yahweh mentions a brother or sister or wife, Yahweh is talking about both younger and older family members. Each time Yahweh talks about a son or a daughter, Yahweh is talking about any sons or daughters. Yahweh is talking about oldest children, second-born children, youngest children, and any other children.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what words do people use to talk about different family members? What are the differences between those words? What are the best ways to translate the words Yahweh is using to talk about the different family members? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says, "You must not shame your father, or uncover your father's nakedness, by having sex with your mother." When a man has sex with his mother, the man is not only shaming his mother, but his father as well. Then Yahweh says, "You cannot have sex with your father's wife because the woman's naked body belongs to your father."

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What is the best way to translate the family members that Yahweh is talking about here? Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss as a group: How will you translate that if a man has sex with his mother, it shames both the man's mother and the man's father? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says, "You cannot have sex with any of your sisters, older or younger, whether the sister was born to your father or just to your mother." That means the man cannot have sex with any of his full sisters or any of his half sisters, whether she has both the same father and mother as the man, just the same father as the man, or just the same mother as the man. It could happen that a man's mother gave birth to the man's sister and raised the sister in a different home than the man.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What are the best words to use for the family members that Yahweh is talking about here? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says, "You also cannot have sex with your granddaughter, whether your granddaughter is any of the daughters of any of your sons or any of the daughters of any of your daughters." Here, Yahweh probably means that the descendants are the man's descendants, so the shame or honor that comes from the descendant's body also reflects on the man.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What are the best words to use for family members that Yahweh is talking about here? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says, "You also cannot have sex with any of your father's wife's daughters, or your stepsisters." Yahweh says the sister was born to the father, but that probably means that the father adopted the girl when the father married the girl's mother, and that is why Yahweh says the girl is the man's sister.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What are the best words to use for the family members that Yahweh is talking about here? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says, "You cannot have sex with any of your aunts, whether the aunt is on your father's side or your mother's side. You also cannot shame or expose the nakedness of any of your father's brothers by having sex with any of your uncle's wives because these women are your aunts."

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What are the best words to use for the family members that Yahweh is talking about here? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says, "You cannot have sex with any of your daughters-in-law who married any of your sons, because these women are your sons' wives."

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What are the best words to use for the family members that Yahweh is talking about here? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says, "You cannot have sex with any of the wives of any of your brothers, because these women's naked bodies belong to the brother the woman is married to."

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What are the best words to use for the family members that Yahweh is talking about here? Pause this audio here.

In the second scene, Yahweh says a man cannot have sex with both a woman and any of the woman's daughters, or with both a woman and any of her granddaughters through any of her daughters or any of her sons. The reason a man cannot have sex with a woman and her female descendants is that the descendants are flesh. This probably means that the female descendants are related to the man, but it might mean that the female descendants are closely related to each other. Yahweh says this is wickedness. When Yahweh calls something wickedness, Yahweh means that if a person does this action, then the person is doing an especially bad thing.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What is the best way to translate the family members that Yahweh is talking about here? Pause this audio here.

Finally, Yahweh says, "You cannot take your wife's sister as another wife," which means a man cannot have sex with a sister of the man's wife while the man's wife is alive.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 18:6–18 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has two scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • An Israelite man
  • The man's father
  • The man's mother
  • The man's father's wife
  • The man's sister
  • The man's half-sister

  • The woman's daughter
  • The woman's daughter's daughter
  • The woman's son
  • The woman's son's daughter
  • The man's wife
  • And the man's wife's sister

As a group, retell the passage twice. You should retell the passage in your own language.

Because your translators may not want to act out the content of this passage, you may just want to have someone speak the passage, or you may want to use objects to show the different relationships of people. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and retell the passage.

The group should retell this passage a second time. At certain points, in the retelling, pause the retelling and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the retelling.

Pause this audio here and retell the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the retelling and possible responses.

In the first scene, Yahweh says that no one should approach anyone who is immediate family to have sex. Yahweh says that he is Yahweh.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I love the Israelites, and I want the Israelites to have good relationships with each other; or
  • I know that people will try to have sex in ways people should not have sex, so I really need to convince people not to do that.
Continue the drama.

Then Yahweh says, "You cannot uncover your father's nakedness, which means you cannot have sex with your mother. You cannot have sex with your father's wife because the woman's naked body belongs to your father.

"You cannot have sex with your sister, whether your sister was born to your father or just to your mother, whether your sister was born in your house into your family or born outside in another house to another family. You cannot have sex with your son's daughter, and you cannot have sex with your daughter's daughter, because their nakedness is your nakedness. You also cannot have sex with your father's wife's daughter, or your step-sister. You cannot have sex with your aunt on your father's side or your mother's side. You also cannot expose the nakedness of your father's brother by having sex with your uncle's wife because that woman is your aunt. You cannot have sex with your daughter-in-law who married your son, because that woman is your son's wife."

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing an Israelite man's son, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am glad I do not have to worry about my father having sex with my daughter or my wife; or
  • My father is important to me, so I am glad Yahweh gave clear instructions so that we can continue to have a good relationship.
Continue the drama.

In the second scene, Yahweh says, "You cannot have sex with both a woman and the woman's daughter, or a woman and her granddaughter through her daughter or her son. The reason you cannot have sex with a woman and her female descendants is that they are closely related to each other. This is wickedness. You cannot take your wife's sister as another wife, which means you cannot have sex with a sister of your wife while your wife is alive."

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the wife's sister, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am glad I do not have to fight with my own sister to get my husband's love; or
  • Even if I want to marry the man who married my sister, I know that I cannot; or
  • My sister is important to me, so I am glad Yahweh gave clear instructions so that we can continue to have a good relationship.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 18:6–18 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

Yahweh tells the Israelites not to have sex with their immediate family, then Yahweh says that he is Yahweh. Yahweh is the personal name that the Creator God gave to the Israelites to call God. Use the same word or phrase for Yahweh as you used in previous passages. For more information on Yahweh, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh says that if an Israelite man has sex with a woman and any of her female descendants, it is wickedness. When Yahweh calls something wickedness or evil, Yahweh means that if a person does that action, that person is doing an especially bad thing. Yahweh uses this word often when Yahweh is talking about sexual immorality.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for wickedness. Look up wickedness in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 18:19–23
content:
Hear and Heart

NOTE: This passage talks about subjects that you may want to discuss in groups of only men and only women. Stop here and discuss as a group if you will listen to this passage in groups of only men and only women. Pause this audio here.

In this step, hear Leviticus 18:19–23 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 18:19–23 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 18:19–23 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

NOTE: This passage talks about subjects that you may want to discuss in groups of only men and only women. Stop here and discuss as a group if you will listen to this passage in groups of only men and only women. Pause this audio here.

Remember that in this part of Leviticus, Yahweh has been telling the Israelites Yahweh's laws and decisions about sex, because Yahweh does not want the Israelites to do what the Canaanites and the Egyptians do. In the previous passage, Yahweh told the Israelites which members of a person's family Yahweh does not allow the Israelites to have sex with. In this passage, Yahweh gives more rules about things that the Egyptians and Canaanites do that Yahweh does not want the Israelites to do. Yahweh is giving these laws mostly to the men of Israel, and Yahweh expects people to be able to use these laws to understand what people need to do in similar situations.

First, Yahweh tells the Israelite men not to approach a woman to uncover her nakedness while the woman is in her time of uncleanness. Yahweh uses special language here twice. First, Yahweh says that a man cannot approach a woman to uncover her nakedness. When a man uncovers a woman's nakedness, the man has sex with the woman. Also, the time of a woman's uncleanness could refer to any time a woman is ritually dirty, but here it almost certainly means that the woman is on her period and ritually dirty because of that. So Yahweh is telling the Israelites not to have sex with a woman while the woman is on her period. You will remember that in Leviticus 15, Yahweh told the Israelite men that they would become ritually dirty if they had sex with a woman while she was on her period.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what rules do people have about having sex with a woman on her period? Pause this audio here.

Next, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to have sex with the wife of a kinsman, or another Israelite. Here, Yahweh does not use special language to talk about sex; instead, Yahweh uses very clear and specific language. Yahweh says if a man has sex with a kinsman's wife, the man will make himself ritually dirty. This does not just mean that the man will not be able to participate in religious rituals and special worship. In this case, Yahweh means the man will be spiritually dirty, which means the man will be unable to stay with the Israelites or stay in the land of Israel. Later in Leviticus, we hear that the punishment for a man who had sex with a married woman was death.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time someone had sex with their neighbor's wife. How did people treat the people who had sex with each other? Pause this audio here.

Then, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to give any of the Israelites' children to pass over to Molech. Yahweh is using special language to say that the Israelites must not use the Israelites' children as a sacrifice to Molech by killing the children. Molech was probably the name of a god that the Canaanites and other people around Israel would worship by killing their children as a sacrifice to Molech.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what terrible thing do people sometimes do to worship a god? How do other people react when someone does that? Pause this audio here.

People would think that Yahweh is a terrible and evil god if Yahweh let the Israelites kill their children as a sacrifice, so Yahweh reminds the Israelites that Yahweh is their God and he is Yahweh.

Then, Yahweh tells the Israelite men not to lie with a man as a man does with a woman. This is special language that means Yahweh does not allow the Israelite men to have sex with men. When men have sex with men, that is an abomination, or a terrible thing to do. Yahweh does not allow men to have sex with an animal either, which would make the men spiritually dirty. Yahweh does not allow the Israelite women to try to get an animal to have sex with the woman, either. If a person has sex with an animal, that person has done something perverse and terrible.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 18:19–23 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has five scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites not to have sex with a woman who is on her period.

In the second scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites not to have sex with another Israelite's wife.

In the third scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites not to sacrifice their children to Molech.

In the fourth scene: Yahweh tells the Israelite men not to have sex with men.

In the fifth scene: Yahweh tells the Israelite men and women not to have sex with animals.

The characters in this passage are:

  • The Israelite men
  • The Israelite women
  • A woman on her period
  • Another Israelite man
  • Another Israelite man's wife
  • The Israelite man's children
  • And Yahweh

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

Remember that in this part of Leviticus, Yahweh has been telling the Israelites Yahweh's laws about sex, because Yahweh does not want the Israelites to do what the Canaanites and the Egyptians do. In the previous passage, Yahweh told the Israelites which members of their family Yahweh does not allow the Israelites to have sex with. In this passage, Yahweh gives more rules about things that the Egyptians and Canaanites do that the Israelites must not do. Yahweh is giving these laws mostly to the men of Israel, and Yahweh expects people to be able to use these laws to understand what people need to do in similar situations. As Yahweh did in the last passage, Yahweh addresses each man in Israel and starts giving specific rules about whom the men cannot have sex with. Yahweh directly speaks to the Israelites in this passage. In your language, you may need to specify each time that Yahweh is talking to each type of Israelite man.

In the first scene, Yahweh tells the Israelite men not to approach a woman to uncover her nakedness while the woman is in her time of uncleanness. Yahweh uses special language here twice. First, Yahweh says not to approach a woman to uncover her nakedness. When a man uncovers a woman's nakedness, the man wrongly has sex with the woman and dishonors her.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What words or phrases would be appropriate to refer to having sex with a woman in this scene? Pause this audio here.

Also, the time of a woman's uncleanness could refer to any time a woman is ritually dirty, but here it almost certainly means that the woman is bleeding during her monthly period and ritually dirty because of that. So Yahweh is telling the Israelites not to have sex with a woman while the woman is on her period.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What words or phrases would be appropriate to refer to a woman's period in this passage? Pause this audio here.

In the second scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to have sex with the wife of a kinsman, or another Israelite. Here, Yahweh does not use special language to talk about sex; instead, Yahweh uses very clear and specific language.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What words or phrases would be appropriate to refer to having sex with a woman in this scene? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says if a man has sex with a kinsman's wife, the man will make himself ritually dirty. A kinsman most likely means a fellow Israelite. You may use a term like "fellow Israelite" or "neighbor." This is a very serious wrongdoing. This does not just mean that the man will not be able to participate in religious rituals and special worship. In this case, Yahweh means the man will be spiritually dirty, which means the man will be unable to stay with the Israelites or stay in the land of Israel.

In the third scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to give any of their children to pass over to Molech. When Yahweh tells the Israelites not to give any of their children to pass over to Molech, Yahweh is using special language to say that the Israelites must not use their children as a sacrifice to Molech by killing the children.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What words or phrases would be appropriate to translate the special language about sacrificing children? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that if the Israelites sacrifice their children to Molech, it will profane the name of their God. Here, Yahweh is using special language to mean that people will not think Yahweh is special or worth obeying if the Israelites sacrifice children to Molech. To the Israelites, a person's name was a way to talk about that person's reputation, or other people's opinion of that person.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Think about times when people in your culture have insulted or said bad things about each other. How will you talk about profaning the name of Yahweh, or causing people to think badly of Yahweh? Pause this audio here.

Then Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh. Yahweh does this when Yahweh wants to make sure the Israelites pay attention and carefully follow the rules Yahweh is giving to the Israelites. Yahweh also does this to remind the Israelites of the difference between Yahweh and the Canaanites' gods.

In the fourth scene, Yahweh tells the Israelite men not to lie with a man like a man does with a woman. This is special language that means Yahweh does not allow the Israelite men to have sex with men. When men have sex with men, that is an abomination, or a terrible thing to do. In other words, Yahweh hates it when men have sex with men.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What in your culture is an especially terrible thing to do that Yahweh hates? What are words that you use to describe actions or events like these? Pause this audio here.

In the fifth scene, Yahweh does not allow the Israelite men or women to have sex with an animal, either, which would make the person spiritually dirty. If a person has sex with an animal, the person has done something perverse that people should avoid.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 18:19–23 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has five scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • The Israelite men
  • The Israelite women
  • A woman on her period
  • Another Israelite man
  • Another Israelite man's wife
  • The Israelite man's children
  • And Yahweh

Because your translators may not want to act out the content of this passage, you may just want to have someone speak the passage, or you may want to use objects to show the different relationships of people. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and retell the passage.

The group should retell this passage a second time. At certain points, as you retell the passage, pause the retelling and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the retelling.

Pause this audio here and retell the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the retelling and possible responses.

In the first scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to have sex with a woman while the woman is on her period.

In the second scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to have sex with the wife of a kinsman, or another Israelite, because the Israelites will make themselves spiritually dirty.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the wife or the husband of the wife, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am angry that my wife is having sex with someone else; or
  • I am jealous of the man my wife is having sex with; or
  • I am unhappy with my relationship with my husband, and I want to have sex with someone else.
Continue the drama.

In the third scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to use their children as a sacrifice to Molech by killing their children.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing an Israelite man's child, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am scared of Molech because Molech wants my parents to kill me; or
  • I am so glad that Yahweh wants to keep me safe and will not let my parents sacrifice me.
Continue the drama.

People will think that Yahweh is a terrible and evil god if Yahweh lets the Israelites kill their children as a sacrifice, so Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is their God and he is Yahweh.

In the fourth scene, Yahweh tells the Israelite men not to have sex with men, because that is an abomination, or a terrible thing to do.

In the fifth scene, Yahweh does not allow the Israelite men to have sex with an animal either, which would make the men spiritually dirty. Yahweh does not allow the Israelite women to try to get an animal to have sex with the women, either. If a person has sex with an animal, that person has done something perverse and terrible.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 18:19–23 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

Yahweh tells the Israelites not to approach a woman while the woman is in the uncleanness of her monthly period. This is a reference to a woman's period. Use the same word or phrase for uncleanness or ritual dirtiness as you used in previous passages. See clean and unclean in the Master Glossary.

Yahweh then says that if an Israelite has sex with a fellow Israelite's wife, the person will defile themselves or make themselves ritually and spiritually dirty. Yahweh does not allow ritually dirty people to go to the tabernacle or do religious rituals. Here, the people are unclean because of how wrong their actions are, not just because of what the people touched. Use the same word or phrase to translate defile as you used in previous passages. For more information on defile, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh says that if someone sacrifices their children to Molech, that person will profane, or make people think less of, the name of Yahweh, or Yahweh's reputation.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for profane. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. See profane in the Master Glossary. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh tells the Israelites that he is Yahweh. Yahweh is the personal name that the one true God gave to the Israelites as the name the Israelites should call God. Yahweh uses his name, Yahweh, to show the difference between Yahweh and the Canaanite gods. Use the same words for Yahweh and for God as you used in previous passages. Refer to the Master Glossary for more information about Yahweh and God.

Yahweh tells the Israelite men not to have sex with men because it is an abomination, or a terrible thing to do. Yahweh hates this action.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for abomination. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Then Yahweh says that Yahweh does not allow the Israelite men or women to have sex with animals, because it is perversion. It is deeply wrong in a way that goes against how Yahweh organized people and animals and how people and animals should relate to each other. People should avoid doing anything that is a perversion.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for perversion.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.
