title: Leviticus 18:24–30
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 18:24–30 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 18:24–30 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 18:24–30 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

Remember that in this part of Leviticus, Yahweh has been telling his people Yahweh's rules about who and what the people cannot have sex with. In this passage, Yahweh explains why the people cannot do all these terrible things Yahweh described.

Yahweh tells the Israelites not to defile themselves, or make themselves ritually and spiritually dirty, by doing any of the things Yahweh just described. When Yahweh talks about being ritually dirty in these cases, Yahweh means that the people cannot participate in the religious rituals because the people have done wrong things against Yahweh's laws. This also means Yahweh will punish the ritually and spiritually dirty people. Yahweh explains that the nations who live in the land did these things and made themselves dirty. Yahweh is talking about the land of Canaan, which Yahweh promised to the Israelites' ancestor, Abraham. We hear in the book of Exodus how Yahweh had promised the Israelites that Yahweh would give the land to the Israelites and help the Israelites remove the different nations that are in the land now in this story.

Stop here as a group and look at a map of Canaan and the area around it. Pause this audio here.

When the people who lived in the land of Canaan made themselves ritually dirty, those people made the land ritually dirty, so Yahweh is punishing the land for the sin that happened in the land. The ancient Israelites and other people groups thought that if people were ritually dirty, those people could spread the dirtiness to the things people interacted with. Here, Yahweh is saying that if people do these terrible things Yahweh has been talking about in the last two passages, then those people become ritually dirty, and that spreads to the land the people live in, just like how other dirtiness can spread to things like people, couches, and beds.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about how people changed their opinion about a place because of what people did in that place. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says the land will vomit out the people there. This is special language that means Yahweh will remove the people from the land. Then Yahweh tells the Israelites that the Israelites need to keep Yahweh's statutes and follow Yahweh's ordinances. The Israelites must not do any of the things that Yahweh has been talking about in the last two passages. Both the descendants of Israel, or the Israelites, and any foreigner who lives among the Israelites as part of the community need to follow these rules. You will remember that some people who were not Israelites chose to live among the Israelites and also follow Yahweh. This meant that these foreigners needed to follow the same laws that the Israelites followed.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What are some examples of rules that only apply to people who are citizens of your country? What are some rules that apply to both citizens and foreigners who live there as part of the community? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh again reminds the Israelites that the reason the Israelites must not do the things Yahweh has talked about is that those things are what the people who are currently living in the land did. Those people have done those evil things and defiled the land. If the Israelites do not do what Yahweh says to do, the land will vomit the Israelites out, too. This means Yahweh will remove the Israelites just like Yahweh will remove the nations currently in the land if the Israelites make the land ritually dirty. Whoever does these evil things will be cut off from their people, which means the Israelites will not consider that person to be an Israelite anymore, and Yahweh will not consider that person to be one of Yahweh's people anymore. It is even possible that Yahweh would kill the person. You will remember that we are not exactly sure what it means to "cut off" someone from their people.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what would a person have to do for their people to stop considering that person to be part of the group? Pause this audio here.

Then Yahweh tells the Israelites to obey Yahweh's command not to do any of the terrible things that the people in the land were doing. Yahweh does not want the Israelites to become ritually dirty by doing these things. Yahweh ends this passage by reminding the Israelites that he is Yahweh, their God.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 18:24–30 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has three scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites not to do the things that caused Yahweh to reject the people who currently live in Canaan.

In the second scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites to obey Yahweh's rules so that Yahweh does not reject the Israelites from the land.

In the third scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites not to do the terrible things that Yahweh has been talking about, or Yahweh will reject the Israelites from the community of Israel.

The characters in this passage are:

  • The nations, or people groups, in the land of Canaan
  • Yahweh
  • Foreigners who live with the Israelites
  • And the Israelites

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

In this passage, Yahweh is trying to convince the Israelites not to do all the terrible things that Yahweh has described in the last two passages. Yahweh wants to show that this is very important, so Yahweh repeats himself a lot. Yahweh talks five times about people defiling themselves, or making themselves ritually dirty. Yahweh says four times that what the people do is an abomination, or a very terrible thing. Three times, Yahweh mentions that the land will vomit out or reject its people. Yahweh repeats these phrases to make sure the Israelites understand and remember how bad it is to do any of the terrible things Yahweh commanded the Israelites not to do in the last two passages.

When Yahweh tells the Israelites these rules, the Israelites are in the wilderness near Mount Sinai. Yahweh is preparing the Israelites to go to the land of Canaan. There, Yahweh will cause the Israelites to force out the nations living there and take the land for themselves. Here, Yahweh talks about what those nations have done to cause Yahweh to remove the nations from the land, but Yahweh has not actually removed the nations from the land yet. When Yahweh talks about removing the nations from the land, Yahweh is talking about something that Yahweh will do in the future.

In the first scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to defile themselves, or make themselves ritually dirty, by doing the things Yahweh has been talking about. The nations, or people groups, that live in the land Yahweh is giving the Israelites did these things and made themselves ritually dirty. When the nations made themselves ritually dirty, the nations also made the land ritually dirty. So Yahweh punished the land because of the sins that people did in the land, and the land vomited out the people who lived in it. Yahweh is using special language here. Yahweh is talking as if the land were a person that Yahweh can punish and that can vomit because of people's ritual dirtiness. In reality, Yahweh is the one who removes people from the land.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What is the best way in your language to express this special language about the land vomiting? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh is talking about the people who are in the land of Canaan before the Israelites are in the land of Canaan because Yahweh wants the Israelites to understand that Yahweh really will force the Israelites to leave the land if the Israelites make themselves ritually dirty. Yahweh is using the people in the land as an example of what Yahweh is willing to do.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time someone proved that the person was willing to do something by showing that the person had done it in the past. Pause this audio here.

In the second scene, Yahweh tells the people to obey Yahweh's ordinances and statutes, and not to do any of the terrible things Yahweh has been talking about in the last two passages. Yahweh calls these terrible things "abominations." You will remember that abominations are terrible things that Yahweh hates. Yahweh does not want the Israelites to do any of these things, and Yahweh also does not want any foreigners who will live with the Israelites to do any of these things either.

Stop here and remind each other of how you described abominations in previous passages. Pause this audio here.

Then Yahweh reminds the Israelites again that the people who are in the land of Canaan did all these terrible things, which made the land ritually dirty. If the Israelites do not obey Yahweh, the land will vomit the Israelites out because the Israelites defiled the land, just like the land vomited out the nations that were in the land before the Israelites. Yahweh is using the same special language Yahweh used earlier when Yahweh spoke as if the land could vomit.

In the third scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites that anyone who does any of the terrible things Yahweh has talked about in the last two passages will be cut off from their people. This probably means that Yahweh will no longer consider the person an Israelite and that Yahweh will expect the other Israelites not to consider the person an Israelite. Yahweh is probably strengthening Yahweh's statements about not defiling the land by telling the Israelites to disown anyone who does these things. If the Israelites remove anyone who does these terrible things Yahweh has been talking about in the previous two passages, then Yahweh will not have to remove the entire Israelite nation from the land. Yahweh once again tells the Israelites not to defile themselves by doing any of the terrible things Yahweh has talked about in the last two passages. Yahweh finishes by reminding the Israelites that he is Yahweh, the Israelites' God.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 18:24–30 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has three scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • The nations, or people, in the land of Canaan
  • Yahweh
  • Foreigners who live with the Israelites
  • And the Israelites

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

In the first scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to make themselves ritually dirty in any of the ways Yahweh has described in the last two passages, because the nations that are currently in the land made themselves ritually dirty by doing these things. When the nations made themselves ritually dirty, the nations made the land ritually dirty. Yahweh is punishing the land, and the land is vomiting out the nations in the land.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am angry because these people are doing terrible things; or
  • I will be upset if my people do what the Canaanites do; or
  • I want my people to live in the best way, not in ways that make the people ritually dirty. Then the people cannot have good relationships with me or with other people.
Continue the drama.

In the second scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites to obey Yahweh's ordinances and statutes. Yahweh does not allow the Israelites to do any of the abominations Yahweh talked about in the last two passages. Yahweh does not allow the Israelites to allow any foreigners, or non-Israelites, who are living in the land to do any of these things either. When the people who are living in the land did these abominations, those people made the land ritually dirty. If the Israelites do these abominations, then the land will vomit the Israelites out because the Israelites defiled the land, just like the land is vomiting out the nations that live in the land now.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I do not want the land to vomit me up; or
  • I am glad that Yahweh has warned me now what I need to avoid in order to stay in the land; or
  • I know that we need to remember these rules so that Yahweh does not punish us.
Continue the drama.

In the last scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites that Yahweh does not consider anyone who does these abominations to be an Israelite. Yahweh tells the Israelites again to follow Yahweh's rules and not to do any of these abominations that the people already living in the land are doing. Yahweh does not allow the Israelites to make themselves ritually dirty by doing these terrible things Yahweh has talked about in the last two passages. Yahweh ends this passage by telling the Israelites that he is Yahweh and he is their God.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I know that if the Israelites follow these rules, the Israelites will live a good life in the land I will give to the Israelites; or
  • I want the Israelites to do the right thing and take good care of the land I am giving to the Israelites; or
  • These are my people, so I need to tell my people what the right and wrong things to do are.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 18:24–30 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

At the beginning of this passage, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to defile themselves, or make themselves unclean. If a person is unclean or ritually dirty, then that person is not fit for service to God. Use the same word or phrase for defile as you used in previous passages. For more information on defile, and clean and unclean, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh says that the nations living in the land made themselves ritually dirty. A nation is a group of people who belong together and who live in the same country and who have the same ruler.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for nations. Look up nation in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh tells the Israelites that Yahweh will punish the land for the iniquity the people have done in the land. These iniquities are perverse actions that make people guilty. These are the sins that the nations in the land committed, which are causing Yahweh to punish the nations. Use the same word or phrase for iniquity as you used in previous passages. For more information, see iniquity in the Master Glossary.

Yahweh tells the Israelites to obey Yahweh's statutes. A statute is an instruction for living in a society. Use the same word or phrase for statute as you used in previous passages. For more information on statute, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh also talks about Yahweh's ordinances, or decisions. When a person in authority decides how the people they rule need to act, that ordinance becomes a law or a rule that the people need to follow. The person in authority might make this decision after people ask the person what people should do in a particular situation. Or the person in authority might make the decision when the person decides that people need to follow a new rule. Use the same word or phrase for ordinance as you used in previous passages. For more information on ordinance, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh describes the actions that the people in the land have done as abominations. An abomination is an action that is completely wicked and that Yahweh hates. Use the same word or phrase to translate abomination as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh says that these ordinances apply to everyone, including the foreigners who live with the Israelites. A foreigner is a non-Israelite who is living in the Israelites' land. Use the same word or phrase to translate foreigner as you used in previous passages. For more information on foreigners, refer to the Master Glossary.

If anyone does one of these abominations, Yahweh says the person will be cut off from the people. This means that Yahweh will not consider that person to be part of the community of Israel anymore. Use the same word or phrase to translate "cut off from the people" as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh finishes this passage by reminding the Israelites that he is Yahweh. Yahweh is the personal name that the one true God told the Israelites to call him. Use the same word or phrase for Yahweh as you used in previous passages. For more information on Yahweh, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh also says that he is the Israelites' God. That means Yahweh is the most powerful spiritual being and the God who created everything. Use the same word or phrase for God as you used in previous passages. For more information, refer to God in the Master Glossary.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 19:1–8
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 19:1–8 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:1–8 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:1–8 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In the previous passages in Leviticus, Yahweh has been telling the Israelites what rules to follow about sex. In this passage, Yahweh speaks to Moses again and tells Moses to speak to the assembly of Israelites who had gathered to hear the laws. Yahweh tells Moses to tell the Israelites that each Israelite needs to be holy because Yahweh, their God, is holy. You will remember that Yahweh wants the Israelite people to be holy, or live differently from all the other people groups, because the Israelite people know Yahweh and what is important to Yahweh. Yahweh also wants the Israelite people to show other people groups what Yahweh is like and to show other people how to worship Yahweh.

Each Israelite also needs to fear their mother and father. Yahweh says that the Israelites should fear their parents because when the Israelites fear people, the Israelites recognize that this person has authority, and so they need to listen to this person. In other words, the Israelites need to respect their parents and honor their parents.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do people treat their parents? Tell a story about someone who honors their parents. How do you know that person honors their parents? Pause this audio here.

The Israelites need to obey Yahweh's rules about the Sabbath every week. Yahweh had told the Israelites through Moses that the seventh day of every week was special. On the seventh day, the Israelites should not do any work. Instead, the Israelites were supposed to rest and let anyone they were in charge of rest as well. Yahweh called this day the Sabbath. Yahweh gave the Israelites rules to help the Israelites understand what counted as work on the Sabbath. Here, Yahweh reminds the Israelites to follow the rules Yahweh gave for this special day. When the Israelites obeyed Yahweh's instructions for the Sabbath, the Israelites acted differently from all the people around the Israelites. This let the other people around the Israelites know that the Israelites' God was special.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what days do people rest? Why do people rest on those days? Pause this audio here.

Then Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh and he is the Israelites' God. Here, like in the previous passages, Yahweh is reminding the Israelites that they are a special people, set apart for and belonging to Yahweh himself. Yahweh is holy, so the Israelites should show that they belong to Yahweh by acting in these holy ways also.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, who are the special groups of people? How do those people act to show that they belong to the special group? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh also does not allow the Israelites to stop worshipping Yahweh and start worshipping idols. Yahweh calls these idols worthless. Yahweh does not allow the Israelites to melt metal and form the metal into an image that people can worship. Yahweh does not want anyone to make an image that represents Yahweh or any other god. But Yahweh especially does not want Yahweh's special people to worship any other gods. Here, Yahweh reminds the Israelites that Yahweh expects the Israelites to totally devote themselves to Yahweh. Yahweh also reminds them again that he is Yahweh and he is the Israelites' God.

Stop here as a group and look at a metal idol. Pause this audio here.

Then Yahweh tells the Israelites some of the rules for when people offer a peace or fellowship offering. A fellowship offering was a sacrifice people made to Yahweh when people were thankful for something Yahweh had done. These offerings were special because Yahweh did not require people to give these fellowship offerings. You will remember that when the Israelites gave a fellowship offering, the people ate some of the meat from the animal that they sacrificed for the offering. When the people ate some of the food and burned some of the food on the altar, it was like the people were sharing a meal with Yahweh, and people made their relationship with Yahweh better when people did that.

The Israelites need to offer their fellowship offerings in such a way that Yahweh accepts the offering. Yahweh allows the Israelites to eat this offering on the same day that someone offers the offering or the day after, but people need to burn anything that is left on the third day. If an Israelite eats any of the fellowship offering on the third day, then the fellowship offering becomes ritually dirty meat. Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to eat ritually dirty meat, and Yahweh will not accept the offering. Also, Yahweh will punish anyone who eats the fellowship offering on the third day or later, because that person profaned that thing, or made that thing not holy. Yahweh will cut that person off, or stop considering that person an Israelite, if that person eats the fellowship offering more than two days after the person offered the fellowship offering. Yahweh expects all the Israelites to treat that person the same way.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What is an example of special food in your culture that has special rules about how and when to eat it? How do people punish a person if someone breaks those rules?

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:1–8 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has three scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells Moses to tell the Israelites to be holy because Yahweh is holy.

In the second scene: Yahweh reminds the Israelites of Yahweh's rules about honoring their parents, Yahweh's rules about the Sabbath, and Yahweh's rules about idols.

In the third scene: Yahweh reminds the Israelites of Yahweh's rules about eating food from fellowship offerings.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelites
  • The parents
  • And someone who eats meat from a fellowship offering after the second day

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

Remember that Yahweh has been telling the people Yahweh's statutes and ordinances about sex. Yahweh has told the people that if they do not follow those rules, the people will make the land Yahweh is giving to the people ritually dirty, and Yahweh will remove the people from the land. In this passage, Yahweh reminds the Israelites of other rules Yahweh has already given to the Israelites.

In the first scene, Yahweh tells Moses to talk to the assembly, or large group, of Israelites who have gathered to hear what Yahweh has to say. Each time the storyteller of Leviticus reminds us that Yahweh is talking to Moses, the storyteller tells us that Yahweh is talking about something new. Like in previous passages, Yahweh speaks to Moses as if Yahweh were speaking directly to the people.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time someone needed to explain a lot of different rules. How did that person show they were talking about a new set of rules? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh requires the Israelites to be holy, or completely devoted to Yahweh. The Israelites should show everyone that the Israelites belong to Yahweh by what the Israelites do. The reason Yahweh requires the Israelites to be holy is that Yahweh, the Israelites' God, is holy; Yahweh is completely good, pure, powerful, and majestic.

Stop here and remember how you translated the phrase in Leviticus 11:44 that the Israelites should be holy because Yahweh is holy. Pause this audio here.

In the second scene, Yahweh tells Moses to tell the Israelites to respect, or honor, their mother and father. Normally, when people mention parents, people talk about the father and then the mother. Here, Yahweh does the opposite. This is probably because Yahweh wants to focus on the mother, since mothers primarily raise the children in Israelite culture. When Yahweh tells the Israelites to respect or honor their parents, Yahweh wants the Israelites to understand that the parents have authority over their children and that people need to respect that authority.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Talk about people in your culture that you highly respect. When you talk about how you feel about those people and how you do what those people tell you to do, what words and phrases do you use? Pause this audio here.

The Israelites also need to obey the rules Yahweh has about the Sabbath. To remind the Israelites why the Israelites need to follow both these rules, Yahweh tells the Israelites that he is Yahweh and he is their God.

Next, Yahweh says that Yahweh does not allow the Israelites to abandon Yahweh to worship worthless idols. Yahweh also does not allow the Israelites to make sculptures out of metal to worship the sculptures. Yahweh reminds the Israelites again that he is Yahweh and he is their God.

In the third scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites that when someone offers a fellowship offering to Yahweh, that person needs to make sure that Yahweh accepts the offering. Yahweh reminds the Israelites that Yahweh allows the Israelites to eat the meat from the fellowship offering on the day that someone gives the offering, and the day after someone gives the offering. On the third day, the Israelites must burn the meat in a fire, because the meat becomes ritually dirty meat, or meat that Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to eat. Yahweh will punish anyone who eats the meat from a fellowship offering three days after someone offered the meat because that person profaned something holy. When people profane something holy, people make that thing common or ordinary. But Yahweh's things are holy, so Yahweh is not pleased when people profane something that is holy. If someone mistreats things that are special to Yahweh, Yahweh will cut off that person from the people. Yahweh will not consider that person to be an Israelite, and Yahweh will expect the other Israelites to treat that person the same way.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What is an appropriate way to talk about Yahweh cutting someone off from the people? Remember how you have translated this in previous passages. Pause this audio here.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:1–8 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has three scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelites
  • The parents
  • And someone who eats meat from a fellowship offering after the second day

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

In the first scene, Yahweh tells Moses to tell the Israelites who have assembled together that the Israelites need to be holy because Yahweh, the Israelites' God, is holy.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I want my people to be special and to do the right things; or
  • I love my people so much, and I want my people to do the right thing.
Continue the drama.

In the second scene, each Israelite needs to respect their mother and father.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I know that my parents have authority and power over me; or
  • I respect my parents; or
  • I need to obey my parents.
Continue the drama.

The Israelites also need to obey Yahweh's rules about the Sabbath. Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh and he is their God.

Yahweh also does not allow the Israelites to abandon Yahweh for a worthless idol. Yahweh does not allow the Israelites to make metal sculptures of gods and worship those sculptures. Yahweh reminds the Israelites again that he is Yahweh and he is their God.

In the third scene, Yahweh says that when the Israelites offer a fellowship offering, the Israelites need to offer this offering so that Yahweh accepts and is happy with the offering. The Israelites can eat the meat from the fellowship offering on the day someone offers the offering and the day after someone offers the offering. However, on the third day, the Israelites need to burn the meat in a fire. If anyone eats the meat from the fellowship offering on the third day, that person does a terrible thing, because on the third day the meat becomes ritually dirty meat, or meat that Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to eat. Yahweh will not accept the fellowship offering, and Yahweh will punish the person who eats the meat at the wrong time. A person who eats the meat from the fellowship offering on the third day after someone offers the fellowship offering is profaning that offering, which is holy, or completely devoted to Yahweh. Yahweh will cut that person off from the people of Israel.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing someone who eats meat from a fellowship offering after the second day, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am so upset because Yahweh is punishing me; or
  • I feel so lonely because I am no longer a part of my people; or
  • I regret that I did not treat the fellowship offering correctly.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:1–8 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

Yahweh talks to Moses. Yahweh is the name that the one true God gave to the Israelites to call God. Use the same word or phrase for Yahweh that you used in previous passages. For more information on Yahweh, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh is the name of the Creator God. God is the most powerful spiritual being. Use the same word or phrase for God that you used in previous passages. For more information on God, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh tells the assembly of Israelites to be holy. Use the same word or phrase for assembly, or large group of Israelites, as you have used in previous passages. People who are holy are people Yahweh has dedicated to himself. Those people must not act like the people around them. Use the same word or phrase for holy in reference to people as you used in previous passages. Yahweh also reminds the Israelites that Yahweh is holy. That means Yahweh is completely good, pure, powerful, and majestic. Use the same word or phrase for holy in reference to Yahweh that you used in previous passages. For more information on holy, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh tells the Israelites to obey Yahweh's rules about the Sabbath. The Sabbath is the seventh and final day of the week in the Jewish calendar, and it is a day that the Israelites dedicate to Yahweh. On that day, no one is allowed to work.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for Sabbath. Look up Sabbath in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh does not allow the Israelites to worship worthless idols. Idols are images of gods that represent the gods. In this passage, people made these images of god from melted metal. People would make sacrifices or worship the idol as a way to worship the god it represented.

Stop here and discuss as a group what words or phrases you will use for idol and gods. Look up idol and gods in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated these words in another book of the Bible, use the same words that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh gives the Israelites instructions about how to sacrifice a peace or fellowship offering. A fellowship offering was a sacrifice that the Israelites offered to Yahweh to thank Yahweh. The Israelites also offered a peace or fellowship offering when the Israelites had finished doing something they had made an oath to do. Use the same words or phrases for sacrifice and peace or fellowship offering as you used in previous passages. For more information on sacrifice and peace or fellowship offerings, refer to the Master Glossary.

After the second day, the meat from a peace or fellowship offering becomes unclean or ritually dirty. When food is unclean, the Israelites cannot eat the meat because the meat will make the Israelites ritually dirty. Use the same word or phrase for unclean or ritually dirty as you used in previous passages. For more information on clean and unclean, refer to the Master Glossary.

If someone eats the ritually dirty meat from the fellowship offering, that person will receive punishment for their iniquity. The person is guilty. When someone is guilty, it means that person did something wrong, and Yahweh should punish that person. Use the same word or phrase for iniquity as you used in previous passages. For more information on iniquity, refer to the Master Glossary.

If someone eats the meat from a fellowship offering in the wrong way, that person will profane the offering. When someone profanes something, that person mistreats something that is holy and instead treats that thing as if it is common. Use the same word or phrase for profane that you used in previous passages. For more information on profane, refer to the Master Glossary.

If an Israelite eats the meat from the fellowship offering in the wrong way, Yahweh will cut that person off from the Israelites. When Yahweh cuts someone off from the Israelites, Yahweh will not consider that person to be an Israelite, and Yahweh will expect the other Israelites to treat that person the same way. Use the same word or phrase for "cut them off" as you used in previous passages.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 19:9–14
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 19:9–14 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:9–14 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:9–14 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this passage, Yahweh continues to remind the Israelites of the rules that the Israelites must follow so that the Israelites can show they are holy people, or people dedicated to Yahweh.

When the Israelites harvest their crops in the land Yahweh is giving to the Israelites, Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to harvest all the way to the edge of the field where they had planted the crops. In most cultures, people would expect the farmers to harvest all the crops the farmers had planted and cared for. Normally, the farmers should pay attention to even the crops in the corners of and at the edge of the fields. However, Yahweh wants the Israelites to stop harvesting before the Israelites finish clearing out the edges and corners.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of a grain field. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh also does not allow the Israelites to gather the gleanings when the Israelites harvest. A gleaning was the crop that a person accidentally did not harvest. Perhaps the crop fell on the ground, or perhaps a person did not remove the food from the plant. In many cultures, people would go back through the field again after harvesting the crops and check for any crops they missed. Yahweh is telling the Israelites not to do that.

Stop here and look at a photo of crops that people have left in a field. Discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do people harvest crops? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh also tells the Israelites not to take off every single grape from the grapevine, and not to gather the grapes that have fallen when people harvest the vineyard. A vineyard is a special farm where people grow grapes.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of a vineyard. Pause this audio here.

Instead of completely harvesting their fields and their vineyards, Yahweh wants the Israelites to let the poor people and the foreigners gather the food the Israelites leave behind. People mainly made money by growing crops on the land they owned. The poor people were the people who could not provide food for themselves or their families. Foreigners would also have trouble providing food for themselves because the foreigners would not have land. You will remember that foreigners are people who have come from another people group, but who have chosen to live among the Israelites. Yahweh wants the Israelite farmers to help people who need food by not harvesting everything in the fields.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do people help poor people and foreigners? Why would a poor person or a foreigner in your land need your help? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh and he is their God, which is why the Israelites should do what Yahweh says to do.

Next, Yahweh reminds the Israelites that Yahweh does not allow the Israelites to steal, trick people, or lie to each other. Yahweh also does not allow the Israelites to swear falsely by Yahweh's name. Yahweh does not want people to make promises that people do not plan to keep. Sometimes a person would make a strong promise and say that Yahweh could punish that person if the person did not keep that promise. Yahweh especially commands his people to never use Yahweh's name to make a promise that they do not plan to keep. Yahweh says that if the Israelites swear falsely by Yahweh's name, then the Israelites profane Yahweh's name. This means that the Israelites will make people think that the Israelite's God is not holy. People will think that Yahweh is not completely good, pure, powerful, and majestic.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time someone used someone's name or authority to trick people or make people think that the person was going to do something that the person was not going to do. Pay attention to the words you use when that person deceives people. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh reminds the Israelites again that he is Yahweh, which is a way for Yahweh to say that he is the one true God.

Next, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to oppress their neighbors. A neighbor is someone in your community. Yahweh means that the Israelites must not oppress anyone, but Yahweh calls the people neighbors so that the Israelites would realize how bad it is to oppress people. Yahweh also tells the Israelites not to rob people and not to hold on to the wages of a worker until morning. When people would hire a person for a job, it was normal to pay that worker the day someone hired the worker, because otherwise the worker might not have money to buy food for the day.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how does a good employer need to treat their employee? When should a good employer pay their employee? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh also will not allow the Israelites to curse a deaf person, even though the deaf person cannot hear the curse. Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to put an obstacle or a tripping hazard in front of a blind person. Then, Yahweh tells the Israelites to fear their God. Yahweh probably means that Yahweh wants the Israelites to respect Yahweh. But Yahweh also means that Yahweh wants the Israelites to be afraid of what Yahweh will do if the Israelites mistreat people in the ways Yahweh is describing. Finally, Yahweh reminds the Israelites one more time that he is Yahweh.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:9–14 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has three scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh reminds the Israelites of the rules to follow about harvesting crops.

In the second scene: Yahweh reminds the Israelites of the rules Yahweh has about deceiving people.

In the third scene: Yahweh reminds the Israelites of the rules Yahweh has about treating people who do not have money, power, or family to protect themselves.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelites
  • Poor people
  • The foreigner
  • The neighbor
  • The worker
  • Deaf people
  • And blind people

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

Remember that in this part of Leviticus, Yahweh is reminding the Israelites, through Moses, how to act because Yahweh is the Israelites' God. Yahweh is giving the Israelites these rules so that the Israelites are ready to live in the land that Yahweh has promised to give to the Israelites.

In the first scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites some of the things the Israelites must not do when they harvest crops. At the time that Yahweh is giving these instructions to the Israelites, the Israelites are still traveling to the land Yahweh will give to the Israelites. The Israelites have not started planting or harvesting crops. Yahweh is talking about how the Israelites need to behave when the Israelites live on and farm the land Yahweh promised to give to the Israelites.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of Canaan and the Arabian Peninsula, where the Israelites are at the time of this passage. Pause the audio here.

Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to harvest the crops at the edge of their fields. The Israelites also must not gather the crops that the Israelites accidentally left behind when the Israelites harvested the first time. Yahweh also will not allow the Israelites to completely harvest all the grapes in their vineyards or pick up the grapes that fall to the ground. Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to do these things because Yahweh wants the Israelites to let the poor people and the foreigners take the extra crops and grapes. Yahweh also reminds the Israelites again that he is Yahweh and he is their God. The reason the Israelites need to obey Yahweh is that Yahweh became the Israelites' God when Yahweh made a covenant with the Israelites.

Stop here and discuss how you will translate the idea of having leftover crops in the field. This includes crops that people did not harvest, and crops that people did not pick up and accidentally left in the field. Pause this audio here.

In the second scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites that Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to secretly take things that do not belong to the Israelites. Yahweh also will not allow the Israelites to trick people into believing something that is not true, or to lie to each other. These are two similar ideas.

Finally, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to swear falsely by Yahweh's name. When Yahweh talks about his name, Yahweh is using special language. Yahweh's name represents Yahweh's reputation and character. Yahweh means that Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to use Yahweh's reputation to swear an oath to do something that the Israelites do not intend to do. Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to use Yahweh's reputation to swear an oath that they are telling the truth when they are not telling the truth.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will translate this special language about Yahweh's name. Pause this audio here.

In the third scene, Yahweh reminds the Israelites that Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to oppress their neighbors or rob their neighbors. When someone oppresses a weaker person, they take advantage of that person because they are stronger than the weaker person in some way. When a person robs someone else, that person takes something away from someone else that does not belong to that person.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will talk about Yahweh's rule that the Israelites not oppress or rob their neighbors. Pause this audio here.

A neighbor is someone you have a connection with. A neighbor may be someone who lives in your town, or a neighbor may be someone from your people group. A neighbor may not live very close to you! In other words, Yahweh is telling the Israelites that the Israelites should not oppress anyone or rob anyone.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Name a person you would consider a neighbor based on this description. What words do you use to describe that person? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh also will not allow an Israelite to hold on to money that the Israelite owes to a worker for working. The Israelites need to pay the worker before the next morning. Yahweh also will not allow the Israelites to curse a deaf person or place something in front of a blind person to make the blind person trip and fall. Yahweh tells the Israelites that the Israelites need to be afraid of their God so that the Israelites will not do these evil things to people. Finally, Yahweh reminds the Israelites again that he is Yahweh.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:9–14 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has three scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelites
  • Poor people
  • The foreigner
  • The neighbor
  • The worker
  • Deaf people
  • And blind people

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

In the first scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites that when the Israelites harvest their crops in the land Yahweh will give the Israelites, Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to harvest all the way to the very edge of the field. Yahweh also will not allow the Israelites to go back over an area the Israelites have harvested to get any crops they missed.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am frustrated that Yahweh will not allow me to harvest everything in my fields; or
  • I know that I need to take care of the poor people and foreigners. I am happy that Yahweh cares for these people. One day, I may need this help too!
Continue the drama.

In the Israelites' vineyards, Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to completely strip all the grapes when the Israelites harvest the grapes. Yahweh also will not allow the Israelite farmers to harvest the grapes that fall on the ground. Instead, the Israelites need to leave these extra crops for the poor and the foreigners to eat. Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh and he is the Israelites' God.

In the second scene, Yahweh does not allow the Israelites to secretly take things that do not belong to the Israelites. Yahweh also does not allow the Israelites to trick people or to lie to each other. Yahweh does not allow the Israelites to use Yahweh's name to swear an oath when the Israelites are not being honest, because that will make people think Yahweh is not holy. Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am angry at the idea that someone would use my name to lie to people; or
  • I need people to understand how holy I am so that people will do the right thing.
Continue the drama.

In the third scene, Yahweh does not allow the Israelites to oppress their neighbors or rob people. Yahweh also does not allow the Israelites to keep the money the Israelites owe a worker overnight, instead of giving the money to the worker.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the laborer, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am so grateful that I get paid every day; or
  • I know that I will get paid today for the work I did today.
Continue the drama.

Yahweh also does not allow the Israelites to curse a deaf person or place something in front of a blind person to make the person trip and fall.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the blind person, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am so glad that Yahweh is taking care of me; or
  • I know it is safe to walk around because Yahweh will not let people hurt me.
Continue the drama.

Instead, the Israelites need to be afraid of what Yahweh will do to the Israelites if the Israelites hurt people. Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:9–14 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

Yahweh tells the Israelites not to harvest all the grapes in their vineyard. A vineyard is a garden for growing grapes. Grapes are a soft, juicy fruit that grows in clusters on a vine.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for vineyard. Look up vineyard in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh tells the Israelites to leave the leftover crops for the foreigners. A foreigner is someone who is not an Israelite but lives in the land of Israel. Use the same word for foreigner as you used in previous passages. For more information on foreigner, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh and he is their God. Yahweh is the name the one true God gave to the Israelites to call God. Use the same words for Yahweh and God as you used in previous passages. For more information on Yahweh and God, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh also tells the Israelites that Yahweh will not allow them to curse deaf people, or people who cannot hear. When you curse someone, you wish that something bad will happen to that person.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for curse. Look up curse in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh also tells the Israelites that the Israelites must not use Yahweh's name to swear an oath when the Israelites do not plan to do what they promise. When someone swears an oath, that person is saying, "If I do not do what I promised to do, God will punish me." Use the same word or phrase for swear as you used in previous passages. For more information on swearing an oath, refer to oath in the Master Glossary.

Yahweh says that if the Israelites swear falsely, the Israelites will profane Yahweh's name. Use the same word for profane as you used in previous passages. For more information, see profane in the Master Glossary.

Yahweh then tells people not to oppress their neighbor. A neighbor is someone you have a connection to who lives in your community or belongs to your people group. Translate neighbor in the same way as you have in previous passages. Look up neighbor in the Master Glossary for more information.

Yahweh tells the Israelites to fear Yahweh. When someone fears Yahweh, that person has a great reverence, honor, and respect for Yahweh. That person believes that everything that Yahweh has said is true. As a result, that person obeys Yahweh because the person knows that Yahweh's commandments are good, and that Yahweh will punish that person if that person disobeys Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for fear of God. Look up "fear of God" in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this phrase in another book of the Bible, use the same phrase that you have used there.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.
