title: Leviticus 19:15–18
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 19:15–18 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:15–18 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:15–18 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this part of Leviticus, Yahweh is reminding the Israelites of the rules that Yahweh has for the Israelites so that the Israelites will be holy people, or people dedicated to Yahweh.

Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to make a legal decision that is unjust. In the Israelite culture, when two people disagreed with each other, those two people would go to a leader in the community and talk to the leader about the disagreement. Perhaps the two people disagreed about whether someone should receive a punishment or who owned a specific piece of property. The leader would decide what the people needed to do, and the people would need to obey that leader's decision. Yahweh says that Yahweh will not allow the leader to make a decision that is not right or fair to the people who have a disagreement.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time that two people had a disagreement over something, such as who should own a piece of property. How did those people decide what to do? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh will not allow the Israelite leaders to decide something that helps a poor person just because that person is poor. Yahweh also does not allow the Israelite leaders to honor a rich person by making a decision that helps the rich person if the decision is not fair or right. Instead, Yahweh always wants the Israelite leaders to do the right thing when the leaders make a decision about a disagreement between their fellow Israelites.

Next, Yahweh talks about how Yahweh wants the people in the community to act. Yahweh will not allow any Israelite to lie about other people. Most times that the Israelites had a disagreement, the Israelites would ask someone else to confirm or explain what had happened. This person would also go with the two people who had the disagreement to the leader to talk about the disagreement. However, if this other person lied about what really happened, the person could cause the Israelite leader to make a decision that was not right or fair to the people who disagreed with each other.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time that someone in the community lied about another person to make that other person look bad. What happened to the person who lied? What happened to the person they lied about? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh also will not allow the Israelites to stand on the blood of other Israelites. This is special language. Yahweh probably means that Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to lie about a person specifically if the lie would cause the Israelite leaders to decide to kill the person. Yahweh could also mean that Yahweh wants the Israelites to say something if the Israelites have information that could stop an Israelite leader from deciding to punish a specific person.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time someone lied and the lie caused someone to die. How did people feel about this person who lied? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh reminds the Israelites again that he is Yahweh.

Then, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to hate their brother in their heart. This is special language. Yahweh probably means that Yahweh does not want an Israelite to remain silent if another Israelite does something wrong to the first Israelite. Instead, Yahweh wants the Israelites to confront the person who did something wrong. Yahweh may mean that Yahweh wants the Israelites to confront the person who did something wrong directly, so the person can fix what the person did, or make it right. Yahweh may also mean that Yahweh wants the Israelites to tell an Israelite leader that the person did something wrong, so that the leader can make a decision about what needs to happen.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, when someone does something wrong to another person, how is the other person supposed to act? What is that person supposed to do about the person who did something wrong? Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a person who hurt a second person, but the second person did not say anything to the first person about it. Later, the second person hated the first person because the second person never said anything to the first person. The second person was silent about the wrongdoing. What did the second person do to the person they hated? Pause this audio here.

If the Israelites do not accuse the person who did something wrong, the Israelites will also become guilty. Yahweh may mean that the Israelites will be guilty because the Israelites did not let the Israelite leaders punish the person who did something wrong. Yahweh may also mean that the Israelites will become guilty because the Israelites will try to punish the person who did something wrong themselves, rather than letting the Israelite leaders punish that person.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time that someone tried to punish a person themselves instead of talking to the appropriate leaders. What happened to the people involved? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to punish a person who did something wrong without first going to the Israelite leaders. Yahweh also will not let the Israelites keep being angry at other Israelites. Yahweh probably means that Yahweh wants the Israelites to quickly handle any problems the Israelites have with each other instead of being angry with each other for a long time. Yahweh tells the Israelites instead to love their neighbors as much as the Israelites love themselves. Yahweh reminds the Israelites again that he is Yahweh.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:15–18 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has two scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites how to act when an Israelite leader is making a decision about a disagreement.

In the second scene: Yahweh tells an Israelite person how to act when someone does something wrong to the Israelite person.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Moses
  • The Israelite leaders
  • Poor people
  • Rich people
  • An Israelite
  • Another Israelite
  • And Yahweh

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

Remember that in this part of Leviticus, Yahweh has been reminding the Israelites, through Moses, about the rules Yahweh wants the Israelites to follow so that the Israelites will be holy, or dedicated to Yahweh. Here, Yahweh talks about how Yahweh expects people to act when people need to handle a disagreement or deal with someone who did something wrong.

In the first scene, Yahweh reminds both the Israelite leaders and the other Israelites how an Israelite leader should make a decision when people disagree, or when someone accuses someone else and says that person did something wrong. Yahweh tells the Israelite leaders not to make a decision about a disagreement that is not fair or right. Yahweh then says more about that by telling the Israelite leaders not to unfairly favor poor people or unfairly honor the great or rich people. Here, Yahweh uses special language to show that Yahweh does not want the Israelite leaders to make a decision about a disagreement based on how much money or power someone has.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Yahweh says that leaders should judge fairly. The leaders should not be more kind to the poor person because that person has no money. The leaders should not be more kind to the rich person because the rich person has more money. How will you talk about the way judges should judge people fairly? Pause this audio here.

Instead, Yahweh tells the Israelite leaders to act justly, or do the right thing, when the leaders need to make a decision about a disagreement or an accusation.

Then, Yahweh talks about how Yahweh wants people in the community to act when an Israelite leader is trying to make a decision between two people who disagree or accuse each other of doing something wrong. Yahweh tells the Israelites not to slander other Israelites, or lie about something an Israelite did, to a leader who is trying to make a right decision. Yahweh also will not allow the Israelites to stand on the blood of other Israelites. This is special language. Yahweh probably means that Yahweh will not allow an Israelite to lie about another person, specifically if the lie would cause the Israelite leaders to decide to kill the other person. Yahweh may also mean that Yahweh wants an Israelite person to say something if the Israelite has information that could stop an Israelite leader from deciding to punish the other person.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What is the best way to talk about "standing on the blood of other Israelites"? In other words, how will you translate that Yahweh does not want the Israelites to tell a lie that would cause the leaders to punish an innocent person? Or how will you translate that Yahweh does not want the Israelites to remain silent when they have information that can help an innocent person? Pause this audio here.

Stop here and do this activity as a group: Act out a situation where someone accuses someone else of doing something wrong, and a leader has to decide what the right thing to do is. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh ends this scene by reminding the Israelites that he is Yahweh. When Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh, Yahweh wants the Israelites to think about everything that Yahweh has done for the Israelites and how powerful Yahweh is. Yahweh wants the Israelites to think about all of this because it will help the Israelites understand how the Israelites need to act.

In the next scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites how to act when one Israelite has done something wrong to another Israelite. Yahweh tells the Israelites that Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to hate their brother in their heart. Yahweh uses special language twice here. When Yahweh talks about their brother, Yahweh means any Israelite, since the Israelites are all related to each other through their common ancestor Jacob, or "Israel." When Yahweh says not to "hate your brother in your heart," Yahweh probably means that Yahweh does not want an Israelite to secretly hate someone else instead of openly telling that other person what the other person has done wrong. For example, if a man does something wrong to a woman, and the woman does not say anything about it to the man, the woman may begin to hate and feel bad towards the man, who is her fellow Israelite. Yahweh does not want an Israelite to secretly hate another Israelite and not properly deal with the problem.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What is the best way to describe when someone hates a brother, or fellow community member, in that person's heart? Pause this audio here.

Instead, Yahweh tells the Israelites to confront the other Israelite who did something wrong. Yahweh calls the other Israelite their neighbor. Both brother and neighbor are words that people used to refer to people in the same nation, like Israel. If a person does not say something about the Israelite who did something wrong, either to that Israelite or to an Israelite leader, then the original person will become guilty of doing something wrong.

Yahweh also will not allow an Israelite to take revenge, which is when someone punishes someone themselves rather than let a leader decide what to do. Yahweh also will not allow an Israelite to be angry at another person for a long time. Instead of punishing someone themselves, Yahweh wants the Israelites to love their fellow Israelites as much as the Israelites love themselves. Yahweh ends this passage by reminding the Israelites that he is Yahweh.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:15–18 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has two scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Moses
  • The Israelite leaders
  • Poor people
  • Rich people
  • An Israelite
  • Another Israelite
  • And Yahweh

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

In the first scene, Yahweh will not allow the Israelite leaders to make a decision about a disagreement or an accusation that is not right or fair to the people involved. Yahweh will not allow the Israelite leaders to decide in favor of a person because of how much money that person has, whether that person is a poor person or a rich person.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the rich people, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am sad that my money will not cause the Israelite leaders to decide in my favor; or
  • I know that if I have a disagreement, the leader who decides what to do about it will treat me fairly; or
  • I am glad that the Israelite leaders will not rule against me just because I am rich.
Continue the drama.

Yahweh expects the Israelite leaders to do the right thing when the leaders decide a case.

Yahweh will not allow an Israelite to lie about a person, and Yahweh will not allow an Israelite to lie about another Israelite so that an Israelite leader decides to kill the person. Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I really care about whether the Israelites do the right thing when the Israelites have a disagreement or when someone does something wrong; or
  • I hate when people lie, especially if someone else dies because of the way that someone lied.
Continue the drama.

In the second scene, Yahweh will not allow an Israelite to secretly hate another Israelite. Instead, Yahweh tells the Israelites to confront the other Israelite if the Israelite has done something wrong, or the first Israelite will become guilty themselves.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing an Israelite, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I really hate this person because this person did something wrong; or
  • I need to tell a leader that this person did something wrong.
Continue the drama.

Yahweh will not allow an Israelite to punish a person themselves instead of talking to the Israelite leaders. Yahweh also will not allow an Israelite to be angry at another Israelite for a long time.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing another Israelite, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am glad that Yahweh will not let people punish me without talking to an Israelite leader; or
  • I am scared because an Israelite leader will decide how to punish me; or
  • I am glad that we are dealing with this situation quickly instead of taking a long time.
Continue the drama.

Instead, Yahweh tells the Israelites to love each other as much as the Israelites love themselves. Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:15–18 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

In this passage, Yahweh tells the Israelites to use justice, or do the right thing, when the Israelites judge their neighbor. Justice is when someone treats someone else fairly according to the law.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for justice. Look up justice in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Someone judges actions that people do by deciding if what that person does is right or wrong, and therefore if the person is guilty or innocent of breaking a law. A judge will punish the person if the judge decides that the person is guilty of doing wrong.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for judging if an action is right or wrong. Look up judge in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that the Israelites should not hate their fellow "brother," or "neighbor," in their heart. The Israelites talked about their heart as the place where they had feelings and thoughts. When someone hates someone else in their heart, they hate that person, but they do not tell anyone.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will talk about hating a fellow "brother," or a "neighbor," in your heart. For more information about heart, refer to heart in the Master Glossary. Pause this audio here.

A neighbor is a person in your community with whom you come into contact. Use the same word or phrase for neighbor as you used in previous passages. Use the same word or phrase for neighbor throughout this passage. For more information on neighbor, refer to the Master Glossary.

If an Israelite does not confront another Israelite when that other Israelite does something wrong, the first Israelite will be guilty of sinning. When someone has guilt, it means that the person did something wrong, and someone must punish that person. Although Yahweh does not use the word for guilt in this passage, Yahweh is saying that the person will be guilty of sinning. Use the same words or phrases for guilt and sin as you used in previous passages. For more information on guilt and sin, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh. Yahweh is the name the one true God gave to the Israelites to call God. Use the same word or phrase for Yahweh as you used in previous passages. For more information on Yahweh, refer to the Master Glossary.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 19:19–25
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 19:19–25 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:19–25 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:19–25 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this part of Leviticus, Yahweh has been telling the Israelites what the Israelites need to do to be holy. Here, Yahweh continues telling the Israelites the rules Yahweh wants the Israelites to follow so that the Israelites will be holy, or different from the other people groups.

At the beginning of this passage, Yahweh tells the Israelites that Yahweh requires the Israelites to obey Yahweh's statutes. Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to breed two different kinds of animals together. Yahweh is not talking about the same kinds of animals that look different, such as two kinds of dogs. Yahweh is talking about animals that are completely different, like how cows are completely different from goats. Yahweh will also not allow the Israelites to sow two different kinds of crops in one field. Yahweh is not talking about two kinds of the same crop that look different, such as two kinds of corn. Yahweh is talking about crops that are completely different, like how wheat is completely different from barley. Yahweh also will not allow the Israelites to put on a piece of clothing that people made from two different materials. Israelites used different materials to make clothes, such as linen from a flax plant or wool from sheep. Here, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to wear clothes made of both linen and wool, or any other two materials.

Stop here as a group and look at this picture of a wool tunic. Pause this audio here.

Stop here as a group and look at this picture of a linen tunic. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what do people make clothes out of? Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss as a group: What kinds of crops do you consider to be different kinds of the same crop? What kinds of crops do you consider to be completely different from one another? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh does not want the Israelites to mix two crops in the fields, two different animals, and two different types of materials because this represents how Israel is supposed to be pure, or completely devoted to Yahweh.

Then Yahweh gives the Israelites an example of a specific situation and explains what Yahweh expects the Israelites to do in the situation. In this situation, a man has sex with a woman who is a slave. This slave woman is engaged to marry a second man. The second man has not yet paid the price to free the slave woman and make the woman his wife. The woman's master also has not freed the woman. Yahweh probably wants the Israelites to punish the slave woman and the man who had sex with her in this situation. Yahweh also might want the people of Israel to investigate the situation to make sure all the facts are true. Either way, Yahweh does not want the Israelites to kill the people who had sex, since the woman is not a free woman. Normally, the Israelites would kill the man and woman who had sex when they were not married, but this law does not apply to slave women. Instead, the man who had sex with the slave woman needs to bring a guilt offering for himself to Yahweh. This means the man needs to take the guilt offering to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting, which people also call the tabernacle. This offering is for the sin that the man committed when the man had sex with the woman. You will remember that Israelites give the guilt offering when they have taken something of value from someone else. The man has taken away the slave woman from the second man, who is engaged to marry the woman. When the man who had sex with the woman offers the guilt offering, the priest will atone for the sin the man did.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what do people do if a man has sex with a woman the man is not married to? How do people react in different ways based on who the woman is? Pause this audio here.

Then Yahweh describes another situation for when the Israelites enter the land that Yahweh is going to give them. In this situation, the Israelites plant trees so that the Israelites can eat the fruit that the trees produce.

Stop here as a group and look at the picture of an orchard. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh explains that the Israelites need to consider the fruit that the trees produce in the first three years to be uncircumcised. When Yahweh says the fruit is uncircumcised, Yahweh is using special language to tell the Israelites that they should not eat the fruit but instead treat the fruit from the new trees as something Yahweh considers ritually dirty, just like Yahweh considers uncircumcised men to be ritually dirty. However, Yahweh commands the Israelites to circumcise their boys when the boys are eight days old, and then dedicate their boys to Yahweh. In a similar way, when the trees are more mature, in the fourth year that the tree produces fruit, the fruit will be holy, and the Israelites need to use the fruit to rejoice in Yahweh. Yahweh probably means that Yahweh wants the Israelites to use the fruit as an offering to Yahweh. That means the Israelites will give the fruit to the priests. This is a similar idea to how the first fruit in each harvest season belongs to Yahweh. Then, when the trees produce fruit in the fifth year, Yahweh will allow the Israelites to eat the fruit. If the Israelites do everything that Yahweh tells the Israelites to do about the fruit trees, then the trees will produce more fruit.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what rules do people have about fruit trees? Why might someone wait to eat the fruit from fruit trees? Pause this audio here.

Then Yahweh reminds the Israelites again that he is Yahweh and he is God.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:19–25 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has three scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites not to mix two different animals, crops in a field, or materials in a piece of clothing.

In the second scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites what to do if a man has sex with a slave woman who is engaged to marry another man.

In the third scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites what to do with fruit trees that the Israelites plant in the land Yahweh is going to give the Israelites.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelites
  • A man
  • A woman who is a slave
  • The man the slave woman is engaged to
  • The owner of the slave woman
  • And a priest

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

Remember that in this part of Leviticus, Yahweh has been telling the Israelites, through Moses, the rules the Israelites need to follow so that the Israelites can be holy to Yahweh. Also, remember that Yahweh has just led the Israelites out of the country of Egypt, and Yahweh is going to lead the Israelites into the land of Canaan. When the Israelites are in Canaan, Yahweh will give the land to the Israelites and will force out the people who live there in Canaan. Many of the laws Yahweh is giving the Israelites are about what the Israelites need to do when the Israelites live in the land of Canaan.

In the first scene, Yahweh again tells the Israelites to keep Yahweh's statutes, or laws. Yahweh repeats that the Israelites need to keep Yahweh's statutes because Yahweh wants the Israelites to understand how much Yahweh wants the Israelites to obey Yahweh's laws.

Then, Yahweh gives the Israelites three statutes about mixing different things. Yahweh tells the Israelites not to breed two different kinds of animals together. Yahweh also tells the Israelites not to sow two different kinds of crops in their fields. When the Israelites sowed seed in a field, the Israelites often pulled a heavy piece of metal across the ground in their field. This broke up the soil and caused the soil to be very loose. Then the Israelites often took a bag full of seeds, grabbed handfuls of the seeds from the bag, and threw the seeds in the field.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do people sow or plant seeds? What words or phrases can you use to describe how the Israelites sow seeds? Pause this audio here.

Finally, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to put on a piece of clothing that people made of two different materials, like linen and wool.

In the second scene, Yahweh gives the Israelites a specific situation. In this situation, a man has sex with a woman who is a slave. This woman is engaged to marry another man, but the man she is engaged to has not paid the money so that the woman can be free. The woman's master has also not given the woman her freedom. If this happens, Yahweh probably wants the Israelites to punish the woman and the man who had sex with each other. Yahweh also might want the Israelites to ask people questions to make sure that the Israelites really know what happened. Yahweh does not want the Israelites to kill the man and the woman who had sex with each other, because the woman is not a free woman. But Yahweh does tell the Israelites that Yahweh requires the man who had sex with the slave woman to bring a guilt offering for himself to Yahweh. The man needs to bring the guilt offering to the Tent of Meeting, or the tabernacle, and it needs to be a ram. Then the priest will sacrifice the guilt offering, and that will make atonement for the man. That means when the priest sacrifices the guilt offering, Yahweh will forgive the man, restore Yahweh's relationship with the man, and clean the guilt from the man. Yahweh then says this in another way when Yahweh says that Yahweh will forgive the sin the man has committed. Yahweh probably says that Yahweh will forgive the man because Yahweh wants the Israelites to really understand that in this situation, the man should not die, even though the man had sex with a woman who was engaged to marry another man.

In the third scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites the rules for when the Israelites plant fruit trees in the land of Canaan. Yahweh tells the Israelites that for the first three years that the trees produce fruit, the Israelites need to consider the fruit uncircumcised. When Yahweh says the fruit is uncircumcised, Yahweh is using special language to tell the Israelites that people should treat the fruit as ritually unclean, just like Yahweh considers uncircumcised men ritually unclean. The Israelites should not gather the fruit, eat the fruit, and or sell the fruit.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time when God or a leader told you that you should avoid eating something because it was wrong to eat it. How did you talk about the leader telling you to avoid eating that thing? What is the best way to describe the fruit as something the Israelites should avoid, like Yahweh does when Yahweh calls the fruit uncircumcised? Pause this audio here.

Then, Yahweh says that in the fourth year the tree produces fruit, the fruit the tree produces is holy, and the Israelites should use the fruit to celebrate Yahweh. This probably means the Israelites should use the fruit as an offering to Yahweh. Finally, in the fifth year the tree produces fruit, the Israelites can eat that fruit. Yahweh tells the Israelites that if the Israelites do this, the trees will produce more fruit. Yahweh means that if the Israelites obey Yahweh's laws, then Yahweh will bless the Israelites' fruit trees and make the trees produce more fruit. Then Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh and he is their God. When Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh, Yahweh is reminding the Israelites why the Israelites should follow the rules that Yahweh gives the Israelites. Yahweh is also reminding the Israelites that Yahweh has a special relationship with the Israelites and that the Israelites made a covenant, or promise, to obey Yahweh's rules.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:19–25 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has three scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelites
  • A man
  • A woman who is a slave
  • The man the slave woman is engaged to
  • The owner of the slave woman
  • And a priest

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

In the first scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites to keep Yahweh's statutes. Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to breed two different species of animals together. Yahweh also will not allow the Israelites to sow two different kinds of plants in the same field. Yahweh also will not allow the Israelites to put on a piece of clothing that someone made from two different materials.

In the second scene, Yahweh describes a situation. In this situation, a man has sex with a woman who is a slave and who is also engaged to be married to another man. No one has paid the slave woman's master to buy the slave woman's freedom, and the slave woman's master has not freed the woman. In this situation, Yahweh probably wants the Israelites to punish the man and the woman who had sex, but Yahweh does not want the Israelites to kill the man and woman, because the woman is not a free woman.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing a man, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am glad that Yahweh will not let people kill me even though I had sex with a woman who was engaged to someone else; or
  • I am sad that the Israelites are punishing me; or
  • I am sorry that I broke Yahweh's law by having sex with this slave woman.
Continue the drama.

The man needs to bring a guilt offering to Yahweh for himself. The man needs to bring a ram to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting. There, the priest will use a ram to sacrifice a guilt offering for the man who had sex with a slave woman. When the priest sacrifices the guilt offering, Yahweh will restore Yahweh's relationship with the man, forgive the man for his sin, and clean the man from the guilt that the man has.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am glad that this man wants to restore his relationship with me; or
  • I forgive this man for what the man did wrong.
Continue the drama.

In the third scene, Yahweh gives the Israelites another situation. In this situation, the Israelites plant trees in the land that Yahweh is going to give the Israelites so that the Israelites can eat the fruit the trees produce. In the first three years, when the trees produce fruit, Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to touch or eat the fruit. In the fourth year, when the trees produce fruit, the Israelites need to set that fruit aside and use the fruit to celebrate Yahweh.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am frustrated that this tree has produced fruit for four years and Yahweh has not allowed us to eat the fruit yet; or
  • I am so grateful to Yahweh because of everything Yahweh has done for us. I am glad to give this fruit to Yahweh; or
  • If I give this fruit to Yahweh, Yahweh will bless this tree to make even more fruit.
Continue the drama.

In the fifth year, when the trees produce fruit, the Israelites can eat the fruit. If the Israelites obey Yahweh's laws about the fruit trees, the trees will produce even more fruit. Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh and he is their God.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:19–25 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

Yahweh tells the Israelites to keep Yahweh's statutes. Yahweh's statutes are instructions that Yahweh has for living in society. Yahweh tells the Israelites to obey these instructions. Use the same word or phrase for statutes as you used in previous passages. For more information on statutes, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh says that the Israelites should not use two kinds of seed in the same field. Use the same word for seed as you have used previously, and refer to seed in the Master Glossary for more information.

Yahweh also talks about a man who has sex with a woman who is a slave. A slave is a person who works for someone else and does not have the freedom to leave their master.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for slave. Look up slave in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

No one has ransomed this slave woman. This means that no one has paid money to the woman's master so that the woman can go free.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for ransom. Look up ransom in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that the man who had sex with the slave woman needs to make a guilt offering to Yahweh. A person gives a guilt offering when the person did something wrong that took value from someone else, or from Yahweh. Use the same word or phrase for guilt offering as you used in previous passages. For more information on guilt offerings, refer to the Master Glossary.

The guilt offering is a ram that the person takes to Yahweh. Yahweh is the name the one true God gave to the Israelites to call God. Use the same word or phrase for Yahweh as you used in previous passages. For more information on Yahweh, refer to the Master Glossary.

The man takes the ram for the guilt offering to the entrance of the Tent or Meeting, or the tabernacle. Use the same word or phrase for Tent of Meeting and entrance to the Tent of Meeting as you used in previous passages. For more information, refer to tabernacle in the Master Glossary.

At the tabernacle, a priest will sacrifice the guilt offering. Yahweh appointed priests to be between Yahweh and the people. The priests did this by offering sacrifices on behalf of the people. Use the same word or phrase for priests as used in previous passages. For more information on priest, refer to the Master Glossary.

When the priest sacrifices the guilt offering, the priest will make atonement for the man. When people make atonement, Yahweh reconciles and restores the relationship. Use the same word or phrase for atonement as you used in previous passages. For more information on atonement, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh promises to forgive the man for the sin the man did when the man had sex with the woman. When Yahweh forgives someone who has done something bad, Yahweh stops being angry with that person. Yahweh no longer wants to punish the person. Use the same words or phrases for forgiveness and sin as you used in previous passages. For more information on forgiveness and sin, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh says that the fruit of a new fruit tree is uncircumcised. Although this means that the fruit is ritually dirty, or that Yahweh does not want them to eat it, you may choose to use terms for uncircumcised or for ritually dirty in your translation.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will say that the fruit is uncircumcised, or ritually dirty. Or will you say it a different way? For more information about circumcision and clean and unclean, refer to the Master Glossary. Pause this audio here.

Then Yahweh talks about the fruit trees that the Israelites will plant in the land Yahweh will give the Israelites. In the fourth year, when the trees produce fruit, Yahweh tells the Israelites that the fruit is holy. That means the fruit is dedicated to Yahweh. The fruit is not common or ordinary, and the Israelites must not use it for ordinary purposes. Use the same word or phrase for holy as you used in previous passages. For more information on holy, refer to the Master Glossary.

Finally, Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is their God. In the Bible, God refers to the God who created everything. Use the same word or phrase for God as you used in previous passages. For more information on God, refer to the Master Glossary.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 19:26–30
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 19:26–30 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:26–30 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:26–30 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this part of Leviticus, Yahweh has been telling the Israelites various laws that the Israelites need to follow to be holy. In this passage, Yahweh continues to give laws that Yahweh requires the Israelites to obey. Bible scholars do not fully understand what everything in this passage means.

First, Yahweh says that Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to eat over blood. This might refer to a specific ritual that other people groups in Canaan would sometimes do. Other people groups would sacrifice an animal to spirits or gods by cutting the animal's throat and letting the blood drain onto the ground. Then people would eat the sacrifice over the blood. People would do this so that spirits of dead people or gods would come and tell the people information that the people wanted to know. We know that Yahweh has also told the Israelites that the Israelites must not eat the blood of animals, so this law may be reminding the Israelites of that law. In any case, Yahweh cares about what the Israelites do with the blood of animals that the Israelites are going to eat.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what do people do to talk to gods or the spirits of dead people? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh also will not let the Israelites practice divination. When people practiced divination, people tried to understand what would happen in the future or a secret about the present. People believed that gods or spirits would leave signs of what would happen in various places, including in animal livers, the flight patterns of birds, and the patterns two liquids made when someone poured the liquids into the same cup. Yahweh also uses another term for divination, or magic. Although we do not know exactly what this second word means, we do know that Yahweh did not want his people to use magic to try to control nature or understand the future.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do people try to learn about what will happen in the future? Pause this audio here.

Then, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to cut the edges of their heads or the edges of their beards. In some cultures, people thought that a person's hair represented how powerful that person was. Some people probably cut the hair at the edges of their head or face and gave that hair to the spirits of dead people. People may have given the hair to the spirits to honor the spirits and to get the spirits to tell people secrets about what was happening at that time or in the future.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do people cut or take care of their hair? When do people cut their hair? Why would people cut their hair in a special way? Pause this audio here.

Next, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to cut themselves for the dead or tattoo any marks on themselves. In some cultures, people probably cut themselves because people believed that the spirits of dead people, mostly dead ancestors, would drink people's blood and have food in the afterlife. People also cut themselves to mourn a person who had died. People also sometimes gave themselves tattoos to honor dead people or to mourn someone who had died. People also might have cut themselves or given themselves tattoos for other reasons.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, when do people cut themselves? Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, when do people get tattoos? Why would people get tattoos in your culture? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh reminds the Israelites again that he is Yahweh.

Next, Yahweh tells the Israelites that Yahweh will not allow any Israelite to make their daughter a prostitute. Yahweh considers all the Israelites to be holy, or special to Yahweh. If an Israelite made his daughter a prostitute, then the Israelite would profane his daughter, which means the Israelite would not treat his daughter like the holy person she was. Yahweh also might mean that Yahweh does not want the Israelites to make their daughters prostitutes for religious rituals for other gods. Yahweh says that if the Israelites made their daughters prostitutes, the land would become a prostitute. When Yahweh says that the Israelites will make the land a prostitute, Yahweh is using special language to mean that the Israelites will do things in the land that Yahweh does not want the Israelites to do, like how a prostitute has sex with people in a way that Yahweh does not want people to have sex. Then wickedness, or evil actions, will fill the land. When Yahweh says that wickedness will fill the land, Yahweh is using special language to mean that people will do a lot of wicked things in the land.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what do people think about someone who is a prostitute? Pause this audio here.

Then, Yahweh tells the Israelites to keep Yahweh's Sabbaths. The Sabbath was the seventh day of every week. On a Sabbath, Yahweh expected his people not to work. Yahweh expected his people to worship Yahweh and think about Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, when do people not work? Why do people not work at those times and on those days? Pause this audio here.

Then, Yahweh tells the Israelites to fear the sanctuary, or to treat the sanctuary with respect. The sanctuary was the place that was holy, or that the people had dedicated to Yahweh. The tabernacle was the sanctuary, and then later, when King Solomon built the temple, the temple was the sanctuary. Finally, Yahweh again reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:26–30 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has two scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites the laws Yahweh has against interacting with spirits.

In the second scene: Yahweh gives instructions to avoid profaning sacred people and things.

The characters in this passage are:

  • The Israelites
  • Moses
  • Yahweh
  • And the daughters of the Israelites

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

Remember that Yahweh has been telling the Israelites, through Moses, how to behave so that the Israelites can be holy. Yahweh has just told the Israelites not to eat the fruit from a tree that the Israelites plant in the land Yahweh will give the Israelites until the fifth year that the tree produces fruit.

In this passage, Yahweh tells the Israelites rules to follow about spirits, and rules to follow about holy people and things. In this passage, though Yahweh is still speaking to Moses, Yahweh speaks as if Yahweh is speaking directly to the Israelites. Yahweh should be speaking directly to the Israelites in your translation if your language allows.

In the first scene, Yahweh says that Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to eat over blood. This probably refers to a specific ritual that other people groups in Canaan would sometimes do. Other people groups would sacrifice an animal to spirits or gods by cutting the animal's throat and letting the blood drain onto the ground. Then people would eat the sacrifice over the blood. People would do this so that spirits of dead people or gods would come and tell people information that people wanted to know. We know that Yahweh has also told the Israelites that the Israelites cannot eat the blood of animals, so this law may be reminding the Israelites of that law.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What is the best word or phrase to use to translate when Yahweh says to avoid eating over the blood? Will you say instead that Yahweh says to avoid eating meat with blood? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh also tells the Israelites not to practice divination of any kind.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Talk about the different ways that people in your culture describe using magic or things in nature to talk with spirits to determine what will happen in the future, or what a dream means. How will you say that Yahweh forbids using these forms of magic? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh tells the Israelites not to cut the hair at the edges of their head or the hair at the edges of their beard. Finally, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to cut their flesh for a dead person or tattoo themselves. When someone makes tattoos on themselves, that person makes tiny cuts in their skin and fills the cuts with color. Altogether, the tattoo makes a permanent picture on the person's skin. Then, Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh. Yahweh reminds people that he is Yahweh when Yahweh wants the people to remember why the people need to follow the laws that Yahweh gives.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will talk about the Israelites cutting the edges of hair and beards, cutting themselves to show that they are mourning dead people, or making tattoos on themselves. Pause this audio here.

In the second scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to profane, or mistreat, their daughters by making their daughters prostitutes. Yahweh has made all the Israelites holy, or dedicated to himself, so the daughters are holy. If the Israelites take something holy and make it unclean or use it for common things, then the Israelites profane that holy thing. If the Israelites make their daughters prostitutes, the Israelites will also make the land that Yahweh is going to give to the Israelites a prostitute. When Yahweh says the Israelites will make the land a prostitute, Yahweh is using special language to mean that the Israelites will do things in the land that Yahweh does not want the Israelites to do. Yahweh might also specifically mean that the Israelites will serve other gods besides Yahweh in the land, which will make the land itself like a prostitute that serves other gods at temples to false gods.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What is the best way to translate that the Israelites will make the land a prostitute? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh also says that if the Israelites make their daughters become prostitutes, then the Israelites will fill the land with wickedness, or evil actions. When Yahweh says that the Israelites will fill the land with wickedness, Yahweh is using special language to mean that people in the land will do wicked things, and that will cause the land to become ritually dirty.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What is the best way to translate that the Israelites will fill the land with wickedness? Pause this audio here.

Then Yahweh says that the Israelites need to keep Yahweh's Sabbaths and fear Yahweh's holy place, or the place Yahweh has dedicated to himself. This sanctuary, or holy place, can mean the entire tabernacle with the tent and courtyard, just the tent, and later the temple. The Israelites should respect and honor the place where they worship Yahweh.

Stop here as a group and look at this picture of the tabernacle. Pause this audio here.

When Yahweh tells the Israelites to fear Yahweh's holy place, Yahweh wants the Israelites to treat the holy place with respect and be afraid of what Yahweh will do if the Israelites do not treat the holy place with respect. Finally, Yahweh reminds the Israelites again that he is Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss as a group: How will you translate that the Israelites should fear, or respect, Yahweh's holy place? Pause this audio here.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:26–30 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has two scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • The Israelites
  • Moses
  • Yahweh
  • And the daughters of the Israelites

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

In the first scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to eat anything over blood. Yahweh also does not allow the Israelites to practice divination of any kind. Yahweh does not allow the Israelites to cut the hair at the edges of their head or to cut their hair at the edges of their beard. Yahweh does not allow the Israelites to cut themselves for dead people or tattoo any marks on their bodies. Then Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I hate when people try to interact with the spirits of dead people instead of coming to me; or
  • It is really important for the Israelites to know that they cannot use divination; or
  • I need to stop the Israelites from doing things that cause the Israelites to trust other gods or trust in magic instead of me. I know what is best for the Israelites. These other spirits will tell the Israelites lies!
Continue the drama.

In the second scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to profane their daughters by making the daughters be prostitutes, so that the Israelites will not make the land a prostitute.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the Israelites' daughters, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am so glad that Yahweh cares enough about us to stop our parents from making us prostitutes; or
  • I am honored that Yahweh considers me holy, or dedicated to Yahweh; or
  • I want to keep the land from becoming a prostitute, so I will not let myself become a prostitute.
Continue the drama.

If the Israelites make their daughters prostitutes, the Israelites will fill the land with wickedness, or behave badly. Then Yahweh tells the Israelites to obey the laws Yahweh has about the Sabbath and to fear, or respect, Yahweh's holy place. Then Yahweh reminds the Israelites again that he is Yahweh.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:26–30 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

In this passage, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to eat anything over blood. Blood symbolizes the life breath that Yahweh uses to make people and animals live. Use the same word or phrase to translate blood as you used in previous passages. For more information on blood, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh also tells the Israelites not to use divination. When people used divination, the people tried to talk to spirits or gods or learn things from spirits or gods.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for divination. Look up divination in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh. Yahweh is the name that the one true God gave to the Israelites to call God. Use the same word or phrase to translate Yahweh as you used in previous passages. For more information on Yahweh, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh tells the Israelites not to profane their daughters by making their daughters be prostitutes. When someone profanes a person or object, that person takes something that is holy, or dedicated to Yahweh, and makes it ritually dirty. This means the item cannot be holy as long as the item remains ritually dirty. Use the same word or phrase to translate profane as you used in previous passages. For more information on profane, refer to the Master Glossary.

Then, Yahweh tells the Israelites that the Israelites need to keep the rules Yahweh has about the Sabbath. The Sabbath is the seventh day of the week for Israelites. On the Sabbath, Yahweh did not allow the Israelites to work. Use the same word or phrase to translate Sabbath as you used in previous passages. For more information on Sabbath, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh also tells the Israelites to fear, or respect, Yahweh's holy place, or sanctuary. In this passage, the holy place refers to the tabernacle, because it is the place Yahweh dedicated to himself, where people can worship Yahweh. Use the same word or phrase to translate holy place, where holy place means the sanctuary, as you used in previous passages. For more information on holy place, refer to sanctuary in the Master Glossary.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.
