title: Leviticus 19:31–37
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 19:31–37 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:31–37 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:31–37 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this part of Leviticus, Yahweh has been telling the Israelites the laws Yahweh expects them to obey so that the Israelites can be holy. Here, Yahweh continues telling the Israelites the laws that the Israelites need to follow to be holy.

Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to use mediums or wizards. These are people who talk to spirits on behalf of other people. Sometimes mediums and wizards also refer to the spirits themselves that the people talk to. People in Canaan and the people around Canaan often asked mediums and wizards to help them learn secrets and other information they wanted to know from spirits and ghosts of dead people. Yahweh does not want the Israelites to ask these mediums and wizards for advice from the spirits. If the Israelites do this, the Israelites will be ritually dirty because the Israelites have disobeyed Yahweh's laws. Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh and he is their God.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what kind of people talk to spirits? What do people think about those people who talk to spirits? How do people treat those people who can talk to spirits? Pause this audio here.

Then, Yahweh tells the Israelites that the Israelites need to stand up in front of people with gray hair and honor people who are old. These two instructions mean the same thing. In Israelite culture, when people stood up in front of a person, the people showed that person respect and honored that person. Additionally, the Israelites associated gray hair with old age, so Yahweh talks about people with gray hair to talk about people with old age.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do people show respect to people who are old? Why do people show respect to people who are old? Pause this audio here.

Then, Yahweh tells the Israelites to fear their God, or to deeply respect Yahweh and do what Yahweh tells the Israelites to do. Then Yahweh tells the Israelites again that he is Yahweh.

Then, Yahweh tells the Israelites how to treat foreigners who live with the Israelites in the land Yahweh is giving the Israelites. These foreigners have chosen to be a part of the Israelite community, and these foreigners follow most of the Israelite customs and Yahweh's laws. The Israelites must not oppress, or mistreat, those foreigners. Yahweh will require the Israelites to treat any foreigner who lives with the Israelites in the land as a citizen of Israel. Yahweh means that Yahweh wants the Israelites to take care of the foreigner. Then Yahweh tells the Israelites to love a foreigner as much as the Israelites love themselves because the Israelites were foreigners in the land of Egypt. Yahweh is talking about how the ancestors of the Israelites moved to Egypt when there was a famine. After some time, the Egyptians enslaved the Israelites and oppressed the Israelites, and Yahweh had to rescue the Israelites from Egypt. Yahweh does not want the Israelites to treat foreigners in the same way the Egyptians treated the Israelites when the Israelites were foreigners. Yahweh reminds the Israelites again that he is Yahweh and he is the Israelites' God.

Then, Yahweh tells the Israelites that Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to do anything unfair or wrong when the Israelites measure something. The Israelites must fairly measure how long something is or how much that thing weighs. The Israelites must also fairly count things. Yahweh is specifically talking about when the Israelites measure things to buy or sell those things. Yahweh tells the Israelites to have righteous scales, or scales that truly show how much something weighs. A scale was a tool people used to weigh things by comparing that thing's weight to the weight of another object.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of a scale. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh also tells the Israelites to have accurate weights. The weights were small objects that people often made out of rock or metal to be a certain weight. A person would put the weights on one side of the scale. Then the person would put the object or group of objects they were weighing on the other side. Then people would add or remove weights until the two sides of the scale were level. When the two sides of the scale were level, it showed that the object or group of objects weighed the same amount as the weights. If the weights weighed more or less than the merchant said the weights did, the merchant could trick people into getting less or paying more than people thought.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of weights. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do people compare the weight of objects or groups of objects? How are your methods similar to how the Israelites weighed objects? How are your methods different from how the Israelites weighed objects? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh also wants the Israelites to have an accurate ephah. An ephah was a standard dry measurement. The Israelites would measure their grain in ephahs. Here, Yahweh is probably talking about a basket or bag that was supposed to hold exactly one ephah of grain. Yahweh might have also been talking about the idea of an ephah, instead of a specific container that measured an ephah. If a person used a container that was actually smaller than an ephah, that person could give someone less grain than the other person paid for.

Stop here and look at a picture of a basket full of grain. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh also wanted the Israelites to have a righteous hin. A hin was a standard measurement of volume that the Israelites used for liquids. Here, Yahweh is probably talking about a container that was supposed to hold exactly one hin of liquid. Yahweh also might have been talking about the idea of a hin, instead of a specific container that measured a hin. If a person who sold a liquid used a container that actually held less than a hin, the person who sold the liquid could give the person who bought the liquid less liquid than the buyer paid for.

Stop here and look at a picture of a container that holds a hin of liquid. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh then reminds the Israelites again that he is Yahweh and he is their God, and this time Yahweh reminds the Israelites that Yahweh brought the Israelites out of the land of Egypt. Yahweh tells the Israelites to obey all Yahweh's statutes and ordinances, and to do what Yahweh says. Then Yahweh reminds the Israelites again that he is Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what are some ways that people trick other people into paying more or getting less than they paid for?

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:31–37 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has four scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites not to ask for help from people who talk to the spirits of dead people.

In the second scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites to respect people who are old.

In the third scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites to treat foreigners in their land like citizens.

In the fourth scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites to be honest when the Israelites do business with someone.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Moses
  • The Israelites
  • Mediums
  • Wizards
  • Yahweh
  • People who are old
  • And foreigners who live in Israel

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

Remember that in this part of Leviticus, Yahweh has been giving the Israelites rules, through Moses, that the Israelites need to obey to be holy. Yahweh groups similar rules together and ends several of the groups of rules by reminding the Israelites that he is Yahweh.

In the first scene of this passage, Yahweh is continuing to talk to Moses. Yahweh tells the Israelites, through Moses, not to use mediums or wizards, which are people who talk to spirits on behalf of other people. Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to face mediums or wizards. Yahweh also will not allow the Israelites to look for the mediums or wizards. When Yahweh says that he will not allow the Israelites to face or look for mediums or wizards, Yahweh is using special language to mean that Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to look for the mediums or the wizards to ask for their help. Yahweh says this command in two different ways, but both mean the same thing.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What is the best way to translate when Yahweh tells the Israelites that Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to face mediums or wizards and that Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to look for mediums or wizards? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that if the Israelites use mediums or wizards, the mediums and wizards will make the Israelites unclean. Yahweh does not just mean that the Israelites will be ritually dirty. Yahweh also means that the Israelites will be spiritually dirty because the Israelites have disobeyed God's laws. Then Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh and he is their God. Yahweh calls himself the Israelites' God because Yahweh has made a covenant to take care of the Israelites as their God, and the Israelites made a covenant to worship and rely only on Yahweh. Yahweh probably also tells the Israelites that he is their God because Yahweh wants the Israelites to rely on Yahweh instead of relying on mediums or wizards.

Yahweh tells the Israelites to stand up in front of people with grey hair. To stand up in front of someone is one way that people show respect.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do people show respect? What ways can you translate when Yahweh tells the Israelites to stand up in front of people with grey hair to show that standing up is a sign of respect? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh tells the Israelites to show respect to those with grey hair. This is another way to talk about old people, as old people often have grey hair. So when Yahweh tells the Israelites to respect people who have grey hair, Yahweh means that Yahweh wants the Israelites to respect people who are old.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what words or phrases do you have that refer to old people? What word or phrase works best here to refer to old people? Pause this audio here.

Then, Yahweh tells the Israelites to fear their God, who is Yahweh. When Yahweh tells the Israelites to fear him, Yahweh means that the Israelites need to deeply respect Yahweh and know that Yahweh will punish the Israelites if the Israelites disobey Yahweh's laws. Then Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh.

In the third scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites to be kind and just to the people from other nations who choose to live in the Israelites' land and follow the Israelites' laws. Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to oppress the foreigners. Instead, Yahweh tells the Israelites to treat the foreigners like any other citizen of Israel. Yahweh tells the Israelites to love the foreigner as much as the Israelites love themselves. Yahweh tells the Israelites why the Israelites need to treat the foreigners well; Yahweh reminds the Israelites that the Israelites were once foreigners in Egypt. Then, Yahweh tells the Israelites again that he is Yahweh and he is the Israelites' God.

In the fourth scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites to be honest and fair when the Israelites do business. Yahweh tells the Israelites that Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to cheat people when the Israelites measure something. The Israelites must fairly measure how long something is or how much something weighs. The Israelites must also fairly count things. Then Yahweh tells the Israelites to use righteous balances, weights, ephahs, and hins. When Yahweh says these measurements need to be righteous, Yahweh means that the Israelites need to be honest when the Israelites use these measurements. The Israelites should not use unfair or incorrect measurements to cheat or trick people. Yahweh is telling the Israelites to be honest when the Israelites do business with people, and Yahweh uses the four examples of balances, weights, ephahs, and hins as ways that people measure things to trade.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your language, how would you describe measurements that are good and correct? Discuss how you want to translate the way Yahweh says these measurements must be "righteous." Pause this audio here.

Then Yahweh tells the Israelites that he is Yahweh, their God, who brought the Israelites out of Egypt. Yahweh tells the Israelites to obey all Yahweh's ordinances and statutes, and Yahweh tells the Israelites to do these ordinances and statutes. Finally, Yahweh tells the Israelites that he is Yahweh. Yahweh is telling the Israelites to obey Yahweh's rules again because Yahweh really wants the Israelites to remember and obey these rules. Yahweh also tells the Israelites to follow all these rules because Yahweh is ending this set of laws in Leviticus before he states another set of laws.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:31–37 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has four scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Moses
  • The Israelites
  • Mediums
  • Wizards
  • Yahweh
  • People who are old
  • And foreigners who live in Israel

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

In the first scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites, through Moses, not to use mediums or wizards. Yahweh does not want the Israelites to ask any mediums or wizards for help, because if the Israelites use mediums or wizards, then the Israelites will become ritually dirty. Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I do not want to become ritually dirty, so I will not use mediums or wizards; or
  • I know Yahweh does not want me to try to talk to dead people; or
  • I will not look for a medium or a wizard.
Continue the drama.

In the second scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites to show respect to people who are old. Yahweh also wants the Israelites to fear their God, who is Yahweh. Yahweh tells the Israelites again that he is Yahweh.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I know that if I do not obey Yahweh, then Yahweh will punish me; or
  • I respect the people who are old because those people have learned many things; or
  • I know that Yahweh expects me to respect people who are old; or
  • I respect Yahweh because of what Yahweh has done for us.
Continue the drama.

In the third scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to oppress any foreigner who lives with the Israelites. Yahweh tells the Israelites to treat any foreigner who lives with the Israelites as if that foreigner is a citizen of Israel. Yahweh tells the Israelites to love foreigners as much as the Israelites love themselves, because the Israelites were foreigners in the land of Egypt. Yahweh tells the Israelites again that he is Yahweh and he is their God.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing foreigners living in Israel, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am surprised that the people in Israel treat me so well; or
  • I am grateful that I am completely safe in Israel; or
  • I do not have to worry about the Israelites because Yahweh told the Israelites to be kind to me.
Continue the drama.

In the fourth scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to cheat when the Israelites measure the length, weight, or quantity of something. Yahweh tells the Israelites to be honest and fair when the Israelites use a scale or weights, and when the Israelites use an ephah or a hin to measure something. Yahweh tells the Israelites again that he is Yahweh and he is their God, and Yahweh reminds the Israelites that Yahweh brought the Israelites out of Egypt.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I care about the Israelites; or
  • I do not want anyone to cheat the Israelites or anyone else who is in Israel; or
  • I really want the Israelites to be fair and honest with people; or
  • I rescued the Israelites from Egypt, and now I want the Israelites to do the right thing.
Continue the drama.

Yahweh tells the Israelites to obey all Yahweh's statutes and ordinances, and Yahweh tells the Israelites to do those statutes and ordinances. Finally, Yahweh tells the Israelites that he is Yahweh.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 19:31–37 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

In this passage, Yahweh tells the Israelites not to use mediums or wizards. People believed that a medium could use divination to call the spirits of dead people from the place where dead people live.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for medium. Look up medium in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh also tells the Israelites not to use wizards. A wizard is very similar to a medium. A wizard learns information from dead people and tells it to other people.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for wizard. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh tells the Israelites that if the Israelites ask mediums or wizards for help, then the Israelites will defile themselves, or make themselves unclean. When someone is unclean or ritually dirty, that person is unfit for service to God. Use the same word or phrase for either defile or unclean as you used in previous passages. For more information on defile and clean and unclean, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh tells the Israelites that he is Yahweh. Yahweh is the personal name that the one true God gave to the Israelites for them to call God. Use the same word or phrase for Yahweh as you used in previous passages. For more information on Yahweh, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh also tells the Israelites that Yahweh is their God. In the Bible, "God" refers to God who created everything. God is the most powerful spiritual being. Use the same word or phrase for God as you used in previous passages. For more information on God, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh tells the Israelites to fear their God. When someone fears God, that person has a great reverence, honor, and respect for God. Use the same word or phrase for fear of God as you used in previous passages. For more information on "fear of God," refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh tells the Israelites not to oppress foreigners who live with the Israelites. A person is a foreigner in a country when that person lives in a nation that is not where the person was born. Use the same word or phrase for foreigner as you used in previous passages, when it refers to foreigners who have chosen to join the community of Israelites and follow the same laws as the Israelites. For more information on foreigner, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh requires the Israelites to have righteous measurements. Someone who is righteous is behaving in the right way. A righteous person is honest and in right relationship with others. In this passage, Yahweh is calling the measurements righteous to show that these measurements should be honest, or right.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will translate righteous in this passage. Discuss whether you will use the same word as your word for righteous, or if you will use a different word, like honest, or right. For more information on righteous, refer to the Master Glossary. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh requires the Israelites to have an honest ephah. An ephah was a measure of dry volume, and the Israelites probably used it because it was the volume of grain that a donkey could carry. An ephah was about 20 liters, but the amount changed throughout history. Use the same word or phrase for ephah as you used in previous passages, like in Leviticus 14:21. For more information on ephah, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh also requires the Israelites to have an honest hin. A hin was a measure of liquid volume. A hin was roughly equal to 4 liters. Use the same word or phrase for hin as you used in previous passages. For more information on hin, refer to the Master Glossary.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for "hin." Pause this audio here.

Yahweh tells the Israelites to obey all Yahweh's statutes. A statute is a law about how to live in society. Use the same word or phrase for statute as you used in previous passages. For more information on statute, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh also tells the Israelites to obey all Yahweh's ordinances, or decisions. When a person in authority decides how the people they rule need to act, that decision becomes a law or a rule that the people need to follow. Use the same word or phrase for ordinance as you used in previous passages. For more information on ordinance, refer to the Master Glossary.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 20:1–9
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 20:1–9 and put it in your hearts. It is important to note that Leviticus 20:1–9 contains difficult content.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 20:1–9 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 20:1–9 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In the last story, Yahweh told Moses many laws for the Israelites to obey because the Israelites were Yahweh's special people and Yahweh is a holy God. Now, Yahweh tells Moses how the Israelites should punish the people who break Yahweh's laws. Yahweh tells Moses that all of the Israelites need to hear these rules.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell stories about times people in your community broke the community's rules, and so the community punished those people. How does your community punish people who break the rules? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh tells Moses that Yahweh wants the Israelites to kill anyone who gives a child from their family to the false god Molech. It is important to remember that Molech was a god whom the people who lived near the Israelites worshiped. Those people believed that if people gave their children to Molech, then Molech would protect the people and do good things for the people. We do not know exactly how people gave their children to Molech. Some scholars think that people burned up the children on an altar as a sacrifice. Some scholars think that people left their children at Molech's temple, where the children would work for their whole lives. Either way, these people who gave their children to Molech were saying that Molech was the one in charge of the children's lives. These people were saying that the children belong to Molech and not to Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time when someone in your community gave a child to Yahweh, a god, spirits, or an ancestor. Pause this audio here.

Sometimes people gave their own children to Molech, and sometimes people gave their grandchildren or one of their other descendants.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about your descendants. How do you talk about the children in your family, even if those children are not your sons or daughters specifically? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh explains that the Israelites must kill anyone who gives a child to Molech—even if the person who gives the child to Molech is not an Israelite. Foreigners, strangers, refugees, or immigrants will one day live in Israelite towns. If one of those foreigners decides to sacrifice a child to Molech, then Yahweh wants the Israelites to kill the foreigner because of what that foreigner did.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time when your community punished someone who was not originally from your community. Why did the community punish the foreigner? What rules are foreigners in your community supposed to follow in the same way as people who belong to your community? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that the Israelites are supposed to kill the person who gives a child to Molech. The Israelites must throw stones at that person until the person dies. Yahweh will also punish the person. Yahweh will set Yahweh's face against the person, which means Yahweh will look at what the person is doing and punish that person himself.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time when Yahweh, a god, powerful spirits, or an ancestor punished someone in your community. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh will punish the person by cutting the person off from the community so that the person is not one of Yahweh's people anymore. Yahweh will punish the person because the person defiled Yahweh's Tent of Meeting. It is important to remember that Yahweh's Tent of Meeting was the place where Yahweh lived with Yahweh's people. It is also important to remember that to defile something means to make something that is supposed to be holy or ritually clean into something that is ritually dirty and not holy anymore. If someone defiles Yahweh's holy Tent of Meeting, then it is as if that person tries to make Yahweh ritually dirty and not holy anymore.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What is the most important or most holy thing in your community? Tell a story about how your community takes care of that thing to make sure that people always respect that thing. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh will also punish the person who gives a child to Molech because giving a child to Molech profanes Yahweh's holy name. It is important to remember that to profane something means to make something the opposite of holy. It means choosing to use something only for things that are ritually dirty or evil. It is also important to remember that the Israelites talked about their honor by talking about their names. When the Israelites wanted people to treat the Israelites with honor and respect, the Israelites would say that the Israelites wanted people to say the Israelites' names with honor and respect. When the Israelites were upset because people were disrespecting or dishonoring the Israelites, the Israelites would say that people were attacking the Israelites' names. Here, Yahweh says that when people give their children to Molech, the people who give their children to Molech make Yahweh's holy name into something that is ritually dirty and evil.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Who is the person that your community respects and honors the most? Tell a story about that person. Who is the person that your community respects and honors the least? Tell a story about that person. Pause this audio here.

Next, Yahweh explains what Yahweh will do if the Israelites do not kill the person who gives a child to Molech. In many Israelite communities, everyone in the community knew everyone else, and many people were related to each other. Sometimes, people would not punish someone in their community because the person who did the wrong thing was one of their family members or friends. People would pretend like they did not know that the person had done something wrong, even when people knew that the person had done something horrible.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What do people in your community do when one of their family members or close friends does something wrong? Tell a story about how a family in your community acted when one of their family members did something wrong. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that Yahweh will punish the community if someone gives a child to Molech and the community does not kill the person who gave the child. If the community ignores the problem and does not kill the person, then Yahweh will punish the person himself. Yahweh will cut off the person who gave the child, and Yahweh will also cut off the person's whole family and everyone who ignored the problem. The person who gave the child to Molech, that person's family, and everyone who ignored the problem will not belong to Yahweh's people anymore. Yahweh explains that giving the child to Molech or ignoring the problem when someone else gives a child to Molech is like becoming a prostitute and selling your body for sex. It is like being married to someone and then going and having sex with someone who is not your husband or wife. In Israelite culture, selling your body for sex and having sex with someone who is not your husband or wife were horrible things for people to do. People who sacrificed a child acted like people who betrayed their husband or wife, their community, and Yahweh.

Stop this audio and discuss this question as a group: What is the worst thing someone in your community could do? What is the worst thing someone in your family could do? Tell a story about a time someone betrayed you, your community, or your family. Pause this audio here.

Then, Yahweh tells Moses that Yahweh will punish anyone who goes to a medium or a spiritist. It is important to remember that mediums, spiritists, and necromancers tried to talk to dead people's spirits or to learn things that dead people knew. Yahweh will punish anyone who visits a medium, spiritist, or necromancer. Yahweh will cut off the person from Yahweh's people so that the person is not one of Yahweh's people anymore.

Stop this audio and discuss this question as a group: How do people communicate with the spirits of dead people in your community? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh tells Moses that the Israelites need to consecrate themselves, or make themselves holy. It is important to remember that consecrated people are people whom Yahweh sets apart so that those people can do something special for Yahweh. The Israelites need to live like they belong to Yahweh because Yahweh is their God. The Israelites need to obey what Yahweh says because Yahweh is God and Yahweh makes the Israelites holy.

Pause here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about something you do that shows that you are part of your family and not someone else's family. Tell a story about something you are proud of that your community does that is different from how the communities around you do things. Pause this audio here.

Finally, Yahweh says that the Israelites need to kill any person who curses that person's father or mother. It is important to remember that people believed that people could make bad things happen to someone else by saying evil words about that person and cursing that person. Yahweh says that the Israelites need to punish any person who tries to make bad things happen to their parents by saying evil things about their parents. It was very important to respect and honor your parents in Israelite culture.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time when someone in your community treated his or her parents very well. Tell a story about a time when someone in your community treated his or her parents very badly. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that the person who curses their own parents is responsible for their own death.

The person did a horrible, evil thing and deserves to die.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time when someone did something wrong and deserved for the community to punish that person.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 20:1–9 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has four scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells Moses how the Israelites need to punish someone who gives a child to Molech.

In the second scene: Yahweh tells Moses how Yahweh will punish someone who goes to a medium, spiritist, or necromancer.

In the third scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites to be holy.

In the fourth scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites to kill any person who curses that person's parents.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelites
  • A disobedient foreigner
  • And a disobedient Israelite

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

In this passage, Yahweh is telling Moses the rules Yahweh wants Moses to tell the rest of the Israelites. Even though the Israelites are not there with Moses listening to Yahweh, Yahweh wants all of the Israelites to follow these rules carefully.

In the first scene, Yahweh tells Moses that the Israelites need to kill anyone who gives one of their own descendants to Molech. If someone gives their own child to Molech, then the other Israelites need to kill that person who gave the child to Molech. It does not matter if the person is an Israelite or a foreigner. The Israelites need to kill the person. The Israelites need to throw stones at the person until the person dies.

Stop here and do this activity as a group: Find a tree stump, a large rock, or a bag full of cloth. Have everyone in the group find three to ten stones that are small enough to throw but heavy enough to hurt someone or something. Stand together as a group and throw the stones at the tree stump, rock, or bag of cloth. Make sure that no one will accidentally hit a person with one of the stones you throw. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that Yahweh will set his face against the person who gives a child to Molech. This means that Yahweh will oppose and punish that person. Yahweh also says that Yahweh will cut off that person from the community. It is important to remember that to cut someone off was a very severe punishment. It meant that the person could not be part of Yahweh's people and might even mean that Yahweh killed the person. Yahweh will punish the person because the person who gave a child to Molech defiled the Tent of Meeting where Yahweh lives and profaned Yahweh's holy name.

Stop here and tell a story about a time when a god or a leader gave your people a rule, and if anyone disobeyed the rule, then that person could no longer be a part of the community. What happened when someone disobeyed that rule? Pause this audio here.

Stop here and review the way you translated the phrases "set Yahweh's face against" and "cut the person off from their community" in Leviticus 17:10. Discuss if you want to translate those phrases in the same way here. Pause this audio here.

Then Yahweh says that Yahweh will punish anyone in the community who knows that someone gave a child to Molech but ignores what that person did and does not kill the person who gave the child. Yahweh will punish the person who gave the child, and Yahweh will also punish that person's family and everyone else in the community who ignored what happened. Yahweh says that giving the child to Molech is like if a person went to Molech and sold his or her body to Molech so that Molech could have sex with that person. This is why it is so bad for someone to give a child to Molech.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: How do you talk about someone who sells their body so that other people can have sex with that person? Discuss how you will translate this in an appropriate way in your language, but in a way that still shows how bad this action is. Pause this audio here.

In the second scene, Yahweh gives Moses different instructions to tell the Israelites. This time, Yahweh says that Yahweh will punish anyone who asks a medium or spiritist to talk to dead people's spirits to get information. Similarly to when someone gives their child to Molech, Yahweh says that when a person goes to talk to dead people's spirits, it is like when a person chooses to be a prostitute or to go sleep with someone who is not that person's husband or wife. Yahweh will punish anyone who goes to talk to a dead person's spirit by cutting that person off so that that person is not part of Yahweh's people anymore.

In the third scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites to be holy. It is important to remember that the Israelites are not there with Moses and Yahweh when Yahweh gives these instructions. Yahweh is still telling Moses to tell all these instructions to the Israelites, but Yahweh tells the instructions to Moses as if Yahweh is talking to all the Israelites at the same time.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Tell a story about a time when you told someone else to go and give instructions to a group of people. How did you tell the messenger the instructions? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that the Israelites need to consecrate themselves, or make themselves holy and act like holy people, because the Israelites belong to Yahweh. Yahweh made the Israelites holy by choosing the Israelites to be Yahweh's people. Now, the Israelites need to obey Yahweh and do what Yahweh says because the Israelites belong to Yahweh, and Yahweh is holy himself.

Stop here and discuss as a group: How will you say that Yahweh tells the Israelites to act in a holy way and to be Yahweh's holy, or special, people? Pause this audio here.

In the fourth scene, Yahweh says that the Israelites need to kill any person who curses that person's father or mother. Yahweh says that a person who cursed their father or mother should not be confused about why the Israelites need to kill that person. The person chose to curse their father or mother even though that person knew that the punishment was death. Yahweh says that person's blood is on their own head, which means that person alone is responsible for that person's own death. Sometimes in the Bible, people use the idea of blood to show guilt. No one else is responsible for what the person did.

Stop here and discuss as a group: How will you talk about how a person's blood will be on their own head, or how that person will be guilty of wrongdoing if they curse their father or mother? Pause this audio here.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 20:1–9 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has four scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelites
  • A disobedient foreigner
  • And a disobedient Israelite

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

Yahweh tells Moses to give these instructions to the Israelites. Yahweh says that the Israelites need to kill any Israelite or foreigner who gives a child to Molech.

The disobedient Israelite and the disobedient foreigner can each pretend to give a child to Molech, and then the rest of the Israelites can pretend to stone the disobedient foreigner and the disobedient Israelite.

Pause the drama.

Ask the people playing the disobedient foreigner and the disobedient Israelite, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people might answer things like:

  • I wanted Molech to give me good things, and that is why I gave Molech my child; or
  • I do not care what Yahweh says! I want Molech to be my god.

Ask the people playing the obedient Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people might answer things like:

  • That person is worshipping someone other than Yahweh! I am so angry! or
  • I want to obey Yahweh, even if it means I need to kill this person; or
  • Why would that disobedient person do something so evil? That person deserves to die.
Continue the drama.

Then the person playing Yahweh can act out how Yahweh opposes and punishes the disobedient Israelite and foreigner. Yahweh forces the disobedient Israelite and the disobedient foreigner to leave the community.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • The Israelites promised to be my people, and I am the Israelites' God. I do not want the Israelites to worship other gods; or
  • I am angry! These disobedient people hurt innocent children and made those children worship other gods instead of teaching their children to worship me; or
  • People who give their children and descendants to Molech are very evil. I do not want my people to do evil things.
Continue the drama.

Next, the disobedient Israelite and the disobedient foreigner pretend to give their children to Molech again. This time, the Israelites ignore what the disobedient people are doing and do not kill the disobedient people.

Pause the drama.

Ask the people playing the Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people might answer things like:

  • The person who disobeyed Yahweh is my friend! I do not want to kill my friend. Yahweh will not punish me; or
  • The person who disobeyed Yahweh is part of my family! I cannot kill someone who is part of my family! or
  • I do not think that what the disobedient people did is very bad. Everything will be fine.
Continue the drama.

This time, Yahweh punishes the disobedient people and all the rest of the community who ignored what the disobedient people did. Yahweh makes all those people leave the community.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • This whole community is so evil! These people are not listening to me and are worshipping other gods! or
  • What these people did is so bad. It is like these people went and sold their bodies to Molech instead of living with me as the people promised! or
  • These people did not kill the person who disobeyed me, so these people are acting like the disobedient person did a good thing. These people care more about the disobedient person than me, their God!
Continue the drama.

Next, the disobedient Israelite pretends to visit a medium or a spiritist. Yahweh makes the disobedient Israelite leave the community.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the disobedient Israelite, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I wanted to know what to do, so I went to the medium so I could talk to my dead ancestor; or
  • I wanted spiritual power, so I went to the medium and the spiritist so that I could do what I wanted.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am here! The Israelites are supposed to talk to me when the Israelites do not know what to do or when the Israelites need help! I am so sad and angry that this person went to dead people's spirits instead; or
  • What this person did is so bad. It is like this person went and sold their body to someone else instead of living with me as the person promised!
Continue the drama.

Yahweh tells the people to follow Yahweh's laws, because the people belong to Yahweh. Yahweh says that he is Yahweh, the Israelites' God. Yahweh tells the Israelites to obey Yahweh's instructions and do what Yahweh says. Yahweh explains that the Israelites are holy because Yahweh made the Israelites holy.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • The Israelites are my people! The Israelites are special to me because I chose the Israelites. I love the Israelites; or
  • I want the Israelites to live like the Israelites belong to me. I made the Israelites different from all the other nations because I chose the Israelites to be my people.
Continue the drama.

Finally, the disobedient Israelite pretends to curse his father or mother. The rest of the Israelites pretend to kill the disobedient Israelite.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the disobedient Israelite, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am so angry at my parents! I want bad things to happen to my parents; or
  • I do not care what Yahweh said! I am going to try to hurt my parents anyway.

Ask the people playing the obedient Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • This person deserves to die! No one made this person say such evil things about his parents! or
  • Yahweh clearly said that people who curse their parents deserve to die! This person knew what would happen and still decided to curse his parents!

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 20:1–9 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

The story starts with Yahweh telling Moses what to say to the Israelites. Yahweh is God's personal name. Use the same word or phrase for Yahweh that you have in previous passages. For more information on Yahweh, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh explains that the Israelites need to punish both Israelites and foreigners who give children to Molech. Foreigners are people who live in a country that is not where those people were born. These foreigners have chosen to live among the Israelites and to follow the same laws as the Israelites do. Use the same word for Israelites and foreigners as you used in previous passages. For more information on Israelites and foreigners, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh says that the Israelites need to kill any Israelite or foreigner who gives a child to Molech. The phrase here could mean that the person burned up the child as a sacrifice or that the person gave the child to Molech's priests so that the child grew up doing whatever Molech's priests told the child to do. The child could be the Israelite's or the foreigner's son or daughter, or the child could be any of the Israelite's or the foreigner's descendants.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use to talk about giving a child to Molech. If you have already translated this phrase in another book of the Bible, use the same word or phrase that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Molech was the false god whom people would give their children to. Use the same word or phrase for Molech as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh says that the community needs to stone anyone who gives a child to Molech. The Israelites stoned people by throwing rocks at that person until that person died.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use to talk about stoning. If you have already translated this phrase in another book of the Bible, use the same word or phrase that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that Yahweh will set his face against the person who gives a child to Molech. This means that Yahweh will oppose and punish the person. Yahweh also says Yahweh will cut the person off from the people because of what that person did. Use the same phrases for "set Yahweh's face against" and "cut the person off from the people" as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh says that Yahweh will punish the person who gives a child to Molech because the person has defiled Yahweh's sanctuary, or makes the sanctuary unclean or ritually dirty. Use the same word or phrase for defiled as you used in previous passages. Look up defile and clean and unclean in the Master Glossary for more information.

The sanctuary is the place where people worship Yahweh and where Yahweh lives with Yahweh's people. In this story, the sanctuary is the Tent of Meeting and the surrounding courtyard area. Use the same word or phrase for sanctuary as you used in previous passages. Look up sanctuary in the Master Glossary for more information.

The person who gives a child to Molech also profanes Yahweh's holy name. To profane something is to shame it and use it to do evil things. Use the same words or phrases for profane and holy as you used in previous passages. Look up profane and holy in the Master Glossary for more information.

If the members of the community do not punish the person who gives a child to Molech, then Yahweh will set Yahweh's face against the person who gives the child to Molech. Yahweh will also set Yahweh's face against the person's family or clan. The word for family here talks about all the person's relatives and not just the person's parents, husband or wife, and children. It talks about the bigger family that the person belongs to, which includes the person's aunts, uncles, cousins, grandparents, and their families. Sometimes translations use the word clan here to show the difference between a person's parents, children, and husband or wife and the rest of the person's larger family.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for clan, or large family group. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that Yahweh will punish anyone who gives a child to Molech and anyone who ignores the person who gives a child to Molech because those people are prostituting themselves to Molech. It is important to remember that the Israelites did not actually have sex with Molech. Yahweh is saying that what the Israelites are doing is just as bad as if the Israelites were selling their bodies for sex all the time or having sex with someone who was not their husband or wife. Use the same word or phrase for prostituting as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh also says Yahweh will set Yahweh's face against anyone who goes to a medium. It is important to remember that a medium is someone who speaks to dead people's spirits. Use the same word or phrase for medium as you used in previous passages. Look up medium in the Master Glossary for more information.

Yahweh will also punish anyone who goes to a necromancer or a spiritist. This is a person who tries to learn important information from dead people's spirits. A spiritist is very similar to a medium. Use the same word for necromancer or spiritist as you used in previous passages.

Then, Yahweh tells the Israelites to consecrate themselves. It is important to remember that Yahweh consecrates someone by giving the person a special job serving Yahweh. Here, Yahweh is telling the Israelites to focus on doing what Yahweh told the Israelites to do and living the holy way Yahweh told the Israelites to live. Use the same word or phrase for consecrate as you used in previous passages. Look up consecrate in the Master Glossary for more information.

Yahweh tells the Israelites to obey his statutes, or laws, for how to live in society and how to do important things in the tabernacle. Use the same word or phrase for statute as you have previously, and refer to statute in the Master Glossary for more information.

Finally, Yahweh tells the Israelites to kill anyone who curses their father or mother. It is important to remember that the Israelites believed that people could make evil things happen to someone by saying evil things about the person. That is what Yahweh is talking about in this story. Use the same word or phrase for curse as you used in previous passages. Look up curse in the Master Glossary for more information.

If a person curses his father or mother, then the person's "blood is on his own head." This means that the person deserves to be killed and that the person cannot say that what that person did was someone else's fault.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for blood is on his own head. If you have already translated this word or phrase in another book of the Bible, use the same word or phrase that you have used there. For more information, you can refer to blood in the Master Glossary.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.
