title: Leviticus 20:10–16
content:
Hear and Heart

NOTE: This passage talks about subjects that you may want to discuss in groups of only men and only women. Stop here and discuss as a group if you will listen to this passage in groups of only men and only women. Pause this audio here.

In this step, hear Leviticus 20:10–16 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 20:10–16 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 20:10–16 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

NOTE: This passage talks about subjects that you may want to discuss in groups of only men and only women. Stop here and discuss as a group if you will listen to this passage in groups of only men and only women. Pause this audio here.

In the last story, Yahweh started telling Moses how to punish people who broke Yahweh's laws, especially people who had sex with someone they should not have had sex with. You will remember that Yahweh gave Moses these laws in Leviticus chapter 18. In this story, Yahweh tells Moses how to punish people who break these laws. All of the laws in this story are about what the Israelites should do if someone has sex with someone that the person should not have sex with. In all of these rules, Yahweh assumes that both of the people wanted to have sex with each other. In a different story, Yahweh gives Moses different rules for what the Israelites should do if one person forces another person to have sex.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time someone in your community had sex with someone that the person should not have had sex with. What did your community do? Pause this audio here.

First, Yahweh tells Moses what the Israelites need to do if a man has sex with another man's wife. Adultery is when a married person has sex with someone who is not their husband or wife. Yahweh says that a man should not have sex with another man's wife. If a man has sex with another man's wife, then the man is having sex with his neighbor's wife. A neighbor is someone the man is supposed to be loyal to and take care of. If the man has sex with his neighbor's wife, then the man is betraying someone the man is supposed to be loyal to. Yahweh says that the Israelites need to punish the man who had sex with another man's wife. Yahweh says that the Israelites are also supposed to punish the woman that the man had sex with. The Israelites need to kill both the man and the woman because of what the man and the woman did. It is important to know that the Israelites only killed the man and the woman together when the married woman wanted to have sex with the man. If the man forced the married woman to have sex with the man, then the Israelites would only punish the man.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What does your community do when a married person has sex with someone who is not their husband or wife? Pause this audio here.

Second, Yahweh tells Moses what the Israelites need to do if a man has sex with the man's father's wife. This could mean that the man had sex with the man's mother, or it could mean that the man had sex with a different woman who was married to the man's father. Either way, the man is shaming his father in one of the worst possible ways.

Yahweh says that if an Israelite man has sex with any of his father's wives, then the Israelites need to kill the man and the woman who had sex with the man. The man and woman knew what they were doing was wrong and still did it anyway.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time someone in your community shamed someone else in a horrible way. Pause this audio here.

Third, Yahweh tells Moses what the Israelites need to do if a man has sex with the man's son's wife. Yahweh says that the Israelites need to kill the man and the woman who had sex with the man. Yahweh says that the man and the son's wife have done something very evil, and it is not the way Yahweh wants his creation to behave.

Yahweh says that the Israelites need to kill the man who had sex with the son's wife, and the Israelites also need to kill the son's wife. Yahweh says that the man and the woman are guilty, or their blood is on their heads, because the man and the son's wife should have known that what they were doing was wrong, but did it anyway.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time someone did something truly evil and wrong. Pause this audio here.

Fourth, Yahweh tells Moses what the Israelites need to do if a man has sex with another man. Yahweh says that men who have sex with each other are doing something ritually dirty and wrong. Yahweh says that the Israelites need to kill both of the men because these men knew what they were doing was wrong, but did it anyway.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time when a man had sex with another man in your culture. What does your culture think about men who have sex with other men? Pause this audio here.

Fifth, Yahweh tells Moses what the Israelites need to do if a man marries a woman and the woman's mother. Yahweh says that this man does something wicked—or something very wrong—if the man marries both a woman and the woman's mother. Yahweh says that the Israelites need to burn the man and both the woman and the woman's mother because of what they did. It is not clear here if the Israelites were supposed to kill the man and both of the women first and then burn their dead bodies, or if the Israelites were supposed to burn the man and both the women until they all were dead. Either way, the Israelites thought that burning someone was one of the worst punishments. The Israelites believed that burning a person completely removed the person from the community because the person did not even have any bones left in the community. It was like the person never existed. Yahweh says that the Israelites need to burn the man and both of the women because it totally removes the evil from the community.

Stop here and discuss this question as a community: What are some of the ways your community takes care of people's dead bodies? What are the most honorable ways you take care of a person's dead body? What are the most shameful things to do to a person's dead body? Pause this audio here.

Sixth, Yahweh tells Moses what to do if a man has sex with an animal. Yahweh says that the Israelites need to kill the man and the animal that the man had sex with.

Then Yahweh tells Moses what to do if a woman goes to a male animal so that the woman can have sex with the animal. Yahweh says that the Israelites need to kill the woman and the animal because the woman and the animal are completely responsible and guilty for this action, and no one else is responsible.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What rules does your community have about whether or not people should have sex with animals?

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 20:10–16 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has six scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells Moses what to do if a man has sex with another man's wife.

In the second scene: Yahweh tells Moses what to do if a man has sex with the man's father's wife.

In the third scene: Yahweh tells Moses what to do if a man has sex with the man's son's wife.

In the fourth scene: Yahweh tells Moses what to do if two men have sex with each other.

In the fifth scene: Yahweh tells Moses what to do if a man marries a woman and the woman's mother.

In the sixth scene: Yahweh tells Moses what to do if a person has sex with an animal.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Disobedient Israelites
  • And obedient Israelites

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

It is important to remember that Yahweh is telling these instructions to Moses. Later, Moses will tell all these instructions to the Israelites.

In this story, Yahweh tells Moses how to punish people who break certain of Yahweh's laws. These are the laws that Yahweh has already given Moses, and now we hear that all of the laws have very serious consequences and strong punishments when someone disobeys the laws. All of the laws are about what the Israelites need to do when someone in the community has sex with someone the person is not supposed to have sex with.

Stop here and, as a group, discuss your community's laws about who can have sex with whom, and the consequences when someone disobeys those laws. What do you notice about these laws? How do people show how important these laws are? Pause this audio here.

In the first scene, Yahweh says that the Israelites need to kill any man who has sex with another man's wife. Yahweh calls this other man the first man's neighbor. A neighbor is a member of your community. Yahweh says that a man who has sex with another man's wife is betraying someone that the man is supposed to be loyal to. The Israelites need to kill the man and the woman who had sex with each other.

Stop here and discuss how you talk about people in your community whom you should be loyal to. What do you call those people? Since you will not be able to act out what these characters do, discuss how you will remember or talk about this law in an appropriate way. Pause this audio here.

In the second scene, Yahweh tells Moses what to do if a man has sex with one of the man's father's wives. Yahweh says that the man is "uncovering his father's nakedness." This means that the man is shaming his father in one of the worst ways. So the Israelites need to kill the man who had sex with his father's wife and the woman who had sex with the man. Yahweh says that their blood is on their own heads because the man and woman knew what they were doing was wrong and still did it. The man and woman are completely responsible for what they did. Remember that Yahweh used the phrase "their blood will be on their own head" in the last passage.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Since you will not be able to act out what these characters do, discuss how you will remember or talk about this law in an appropriate way. Pause this audio here.

In the third scene, Yahweh tells Moses what to do if a man has sex with the wife of the man's son. Yahweh says that the Israelites need to kill both the man and the woman who had sex with the man. Yahweh says that what the man and woman did is a "perverse" act. The word "perverse" talks about something that is opposite to the way Yahweh made the world to work. If someone does a perverse thing, then the person does something so wrong that it breaks the most important rules of the world. Yahweh says that the man and woman's blood is on their own heads because the man and woman knew what they were doing was wrong and still did it.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Remember the story you told in the last step about someone who did something truly evil and wrong. What words or phrases would you use to describe the way that person acted? Discuss if you can translate perverse in the same way that you did in Leviticus 18:23. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Since you will not be able to act out what these characters do, discuss how you will remember or talk about this law in an appropriate way. Pause this audio here.

In the fourth scene, Yahweh tells Moses what to do if a man has sex with another man, just like how a man has sex with a woman. Yahweh says that the men did something detestable. The word "detestable" means something that is evil and wrong, and something that Yahweh hates. Some translations call this "an abomination." So the Israelites need to kill both men. The men's blood is on their own heads because the men knew what they were doing was wrong and still did it.

Stop here and discuss how you translated abomination or something that is detestable in Leviticus 18:30. Discuss whether you can translate it in the same way here. Since you will not be able to act out what these characters do, discuss how you will remember or talk about this law in an appropriate way. Pause this audio here.

In the fifth scene, Yahweh tells Moses what to do if a man marries a woman and the woman's mother. Yahweh says that a man who marries a woman and the woman's mother has done something very wrong. The Israelites need to kill the man and both the women. The Israelites might kill the man and both the women by burning them with fire, or the Israelites might kill the man and both the women in a different way and then burn their bodies with fire. Yahweh says that burning the man and both the women with fire cleans the land by destroying all the evil that the man and the women brought into the community when the man married these two women.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Since you will not be able to act out what these characters do, discuss how you will remember or talk about this law in an appropriate way. Pause this audio here.

In the sixth scene, Yahweh tells Moses what to do if a man has sex with an animal. Yahweh says that the Israelites need to kill the man and the animal that the man had sex with. Then Yahweh tells Moses what to do if a woman goes to a male animal and has sex with the male animal. Yahweh says that the Israelites need to kill the woman and the animal. Yahweh says the blood is on the woman and the animal's heads, so the woman and the animal are guilty. No one else is responsible for what the woman and the animal did.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Since you will not be able to act out what these characters do, discuss how you will remember or talk about this law in an appropriate way. Pause this audio here.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 20:10–16 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has six scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Disobedient Israelites
  • And obedient Israelites

It is important to remember that Yahweh is telling these instructions to Moses. Later, Moses will tell all these instructions to the Israelites.

As a group, retell the passage twice. You should retell the passage in your own language.

Because your translators may not want to act out the content of this passage, you may just want to have someone speak the passage, or you may want to use objects to show the different relationships of people. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and retell the passage.

The group should retell this passage a second time. At certain points in the retelling, pause the retelling and discuss what you think the characters would be feeling and thinking. Then continue the retelling.

Pause this audio here and retell the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the retelling and possible responses.

Yahweh tells Moses Yahweh's instructions.

Yahweh tells Moses that the Israelites need to kill anyone who commits adultery. If a man and a woman who is married to someone else have sex together, then the other Israelites must kill that man and woman.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you thinking or feeling?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am upset and angry. Those disobedient Israelites promised to respect my rules about marriage, but then the Israelites had sex with each other instead! or
  • I am sad and angry. The disobedient Israelite betrayed the woman's husband.

Ask the people playing the obedient Israelites, "What are you thinking or feeling?" The people might answer things like:

  • I cannot believe this man and this woman betrayed Yahweh! I am so angry! or
  • This woman betrayed her husband, and this man betrayed someone the man was supposed to be loyal to. What the man and woman did was so wrong! or
  • I am sad that we have to kill two people from our community. What the man and the woman did is very wrong, and I am upset about this whole situation.
Continue the drama.

Then Yahweh tells Moses what the Israelites need to do if a man has sex with the man's father's wife. The other Israelites need to kill the man and the woman who had sex with the man.

Pause the drama.

Ask the people playing the disobedient Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people might answer things like:

  • I know what we did was wrong, but I wanted to do it anyway; or
  • I do not care what Yahweh says! I want to do what I want to do.

Ask the people playing the obedient Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people might answer things like:

  • These disobedient Israelites knew what they were doing was wrong, but did it anyway! These two people deserve to die; or
  • That disobedient Israelite man shamed his father in such a horrible way! I cannot believe that man would do something that terrible to his own father!
Continue the drama.

Yahweh tells Moses what the Israelites need to do if a man has sex with the man's son's wife. The other Israelites need to kill that man and woman because what that man and woman did is very evil.

Pause the drama.

Ask the people playing the disobedient Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people might answer things like:

  • I know what we did was wrong, but I wanted to do it anyway; or
  • I do not care what Yahweh says! I want to do what I want to do.

Ask the people playing the obedient Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people might answer things like:

  • These disobedient Israelites knew what they were doing was wrong, but these people did it anyway! These people deserve to die; or
  • These disobedient Israelites did something perverse and bad! What these people did broke the rules that Yahweh made when Yahweh made everything. These people deserve to die.
Continue the drama.

Then Yahweh tells Moses what the Israelites need to do if a man has sex with another man. The other Israelites need to kill those two men because what those men did is something that Yahweh hates.

Pause the drama.

Ask the people playing the disobedient Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people might answer things like:

  • I know what we did was wrong, but I wanted to do it anyway; or
  • I do not care what Yahweh says! I want to do what I want to do.

Ask the people playing the obedient Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people might answer things like:

  • These disobedient Israelites knew what they were doing was wrong, but these people did it anyway! These people deserve to die; or
  • These disobedient Israelites made themselves so ritually dirty that these two people need to die to make the community ritually clean again.
Continue the drama.

Next, Yahweh tells Moses what the Israelites need to do if a man marries both a woman and the woman's mother. The other Israelites need to kill that man and the two women and burn their bodies, to get rid of any wickedness.

Pause the drama.

Ask the people playing the obedient Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people might answer things like:

  • These disobedient Israelites did such a horrible thing! We do not even want these people's bones to be in our land anymore; or
  • We need to make sure our community stays ritually clean. We need to completely destroy these people so that these people do not make our land ritually dirty even after these people are dead.
Continue the drama.

Next, Yahweh tells Moses what the Israelites need to do if a man has sex with an animal or if a woman goes to a male animal and has sex with it. The other Israelites need to kill that man or woman and the animal.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the disobedient Israelite woman, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I know what we did was wrong, but I wanted to do it anyway; or
  • I do not care what Yahweh says! I want to do what I want to do.

Ask the people playing the obedient Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people might answer things like:

  • This disobedient Israelite knew what she was doing was wrong, but she did it anyway! This disobedient Israelite deserves to die; or
  • Yahweh says that people are only supposed to have sex with the person they are married to! I am sad and angry that these disobedient Israelites did not obey Yahweh's instructions.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 20:10–16 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

Yahweh says that the Israelites need to kill anyone who commits adultery. A person commits adultery if the person has sex with someone who is married to someone else or has sex with someone who is not the person's husband or wife.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for adultery, and for both the man and the woman who commit adultery. Look up adultery in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that a man who has sex with another man's wife is having sex with his neighbor's wife. Use the same word or phrase for neighbor as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh says that the Israelites need to kill anyone who has sex with his father's wife. This might mean that the man had sex with the man's own mother, or it might mean that the man had sex with a different woman who was also the man's father's wife. Use the same word or phrase for "father's wife" as you used in Leviticus 18.

Yahweh says that anyone who has sex with his father's wife has uncovered his father's nakedness. It is important to remember that uncovering your father's nakedness means shaming your father in a horrible way. Use the same word or phrase for "uncovered his father's nakedness" as you used in Leviticus 18.

If a man has sex with his father's wife, Yahweh says that the Israelites need to kill that man and the woman who had sex with the man. The Israelites do not need to feel guilty. Yahweh says that the man and woman who had sex with each other have their own blood on their heads. It is important to remember that this phrase means that the man and the woman deserve their punishment because the man and the woman knew what they were doing was wrong and still did it anyway. Use the same word or phrase for "their blood is on their heads" as you used in previous passages and throughout this passage.

Yahweh says that the Israelites need to kill a man who has sex with the man's son's wife. Use the same word or phrase for "son's wife" as you used in Leviticus 18.

Yahweh says that the Israelites need to kill the man who had sex with his son's wife and also the woman that the man had sex with because what the man and woman did was a perversion. It is important to remember that a perversion is something that breaks Yahweh's rules for how the world is supposed to work. Use the same word or phrase for perversion as you used in Leviticus 18:23.

Then Yahweh says that the Israelites need to kill any man who has sex with another man in the same way that a man has sex with a woman. Use the same word or phrase to talk about a man having sex with another man as you did in previous passages.

Yahweh says that a man who has sex with another man does something detestable or that it is an abomination. It is important to remember that something detestable is something that is even worse than making something ritually dirty. It is something that no one should ever do because Yahweh hates it. Use the same word or phrase for detestable or abomination as you used in previous passages.

Next, Yahweh says that the Israelites need to kill anyone who marries both a woman and the woman's mother.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will say this so that it is clear that the man is marrying the woman and the woman's mother. Pause this audio here.

The Israelites need to kill the man and both of the women the man married because what the man did was wicked. It is important to remember that the word wicked shows how evil the action is. It is like saying, "This is something truly bad that no one should ever do." Use the same word or phrase for wicked or depraved as you used in previous passages. Look in the Master Glossary for more information about wickedness.

When the Israelites kill the man and both of the women, the Israelites need to burn the man and the women with fire. This either means that the Israelites burned the man and the women with fire until the man and women died, or the Israelites killed the man and the women and then burned their dead bodies with fire until there was nothing left. The Israelites need to burn the man and both the women he married with fire so that none of their wickedness stays in the Israelite community.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for burned in the fire. Pause this audio here.

Finally, Yahweh says that the Israelites need to kill anyone who has sex with an animal. If a man has sex with an animal, then the Israelites need to kill the man and the animal. If a woman goes to a male animal and has sex with the male animal, then the Israelites need to kill the woman and the animal.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 20:17–21
content:
Hear and Heart

NOTE: This passage talks about subjects that you may want to discuss in groups of only men and only women. Stop here and discuss as a group if you will listen to this passage in groups of only men and only women. Pause this audio here.

In this step, hear Leviticus 20:17–21 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 20:17–21 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 20:17–21 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

NOTE: This passage talks about subjects that you may want to discuss in groups of only men and only women. Stop here and discuss as a group if you will listen to this passage in groups of only men and only women. Pause this audio here.

In this story, Yahweh gives Moses more instructions about how to punish people who break Yahweh's laws. All five of the laws in this story are about what the Israelites should do if someone has sex with someone that the person should not have sex with. You will remember that Yahweh has already given similar laws to Moses in Leviticus chapter 18, but here Yahweh tells the Israelites how to punish people who disobey these laws. In all of these rules, Yahweh assumes that both of the people wanted to have sex with each other. In a different story, Yahweh gives Moses different rules for what the Israelites should do if one person forces another person to have sex.

First, Yahweh tells the Israelites what to do if a man and the man's sister agree to get married and then get married. Yahweh says that the law applies to any man who marries his sister. The Israelites allowed a man to have more than one wife, so sometimes people would have a brother or a sister who had the same mother or a brother and a sister who had the same father but not the same mother. Yahweh says that a man may never marry his sister, even if the sister has a different father or a different mother.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Describe a normal family in your community. How many husbands or wives can a person have? Tell a story about your own family. How do you talk about your brothers or sisters? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh explains that if a man marries the man's sister, then the man sees his sister's naked body and the sister sees her brother's naked body. Yahweh says that this is a shameful thing and the opposite of what a loyal and honorable brother should do. The Israelites need to exile the man and his sister. When the Israelites exile the man and his sister, the Israelites are publicly shaming the man and the man's sister for what these two people did.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Tell a story about a time when your whole community publicly punished someone for what the person did. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that the man who married his sister is even more guilty than his sister is. The Israelites believed that a brother's job was to protect his sister's honor and reputation. Instead of protecting his sister, the man who married his sister destroyed the sister's reputation and honor. The man is even more guilty than the sister is because the man was supposed to protect his sister, and the man did not.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Tell a story about a time when a man in your community did the right thing as a brother for his sister. Tell a story about a time when a man in your community did the wrong thing and failed to be a good brother to his sister. Pause this audio here.

In the second rule, Yahweh tells Moses what the Israelites need to do if a man in the community has sex with a woman who is currently on her period, or time of menstruation. Menstruation is when a woman has her monthly bleeding. The Israelites believed that a woman who was having her monthly bleeding was ritually dirty and needed to rest in a special way until the woman's bleeding stopped. Yahweh says that it is wrong for a man to have sex with a woman while the woman is having her monthly bleeding because it means that the man looks at the woman's bleeding and the woman shows the man her bleeding. If a man and a woman have sex during the woman's monthly bleeding, then the Israelites need to cut off or exile both the man and the woman.

Pause here and discuss this question as a group: What are things that women in your community can do while those women are having their monthly bleeding? What are things that those women cannot do? If it is appropriate, politely ask an appropriate woman in your community to tell the story of what that woman does during her monthly bleeding. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh's third rule is that a man should not have sex with a sister of the man's parents. The man should not have sex with his mother's sister or with his father's sister.

Pause here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about your father's sister. Tell a story about your mother's sister. Stop this audio here.

A man who has sex with his mother's sister or his father's sister is having sex with a woman who is related to the man by blood. Yahweh does not want the Israelites to marry people who are too closely related. Yahweh says that the man and woman who had sex will bear their guilt. Yahweh will punish the man and woman for having sex with each other when the man and woman are closely related.

Pause here and discuss this question as a group: Who are people in your community allowed to marry? Tell a story about someone who chose the right person to marry. Tell a story about someone who chose the wrong person to marry. What makes someone the right person to marry in your community? Stop this audio here.

Yahweh's fourth rule is that a man should not have sex with the woman his father's brother marries. It is not clear in this rule whether the man's uncle has died or is still alive. Either way, a man should not have sex with his uncle's wife. Yahweh says that if a man has sex with his uncle's wife, then the man is shaming his uncle in one of the worst possible ways.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about your father's brother. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that Yahweh will punish the man and the man's uncle's wife for having sex with each other. Yahweh will punish the man and woman by making it so that the man and woman never have children and have no descendants. The Israelites believed that it was very important for a family to continue to exist for generations. It was a very shameful and horrible thing for someone's family line to die out because the person did not have any descendants.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Tell a story about a family in your community that did not have any children. What does your community think of people who do not have children? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh's fifth rule is that a man should not marry his brother's wife. In other parts of the Bible, Yahweh tells a man that a man needs to marry his brother's wife if his brother dies without having any children. In that situation, the man who marries his brother's wife is honoring his brother and making sure that his brother's family can continue. The community treats any children that the brother's wife has as the dead brother's children, even if the brother is already dead. Here, Yahweh is not talking about that specific situation. Yahweh's rule is about what will happen if a man marries his brother's wife while his brother is still alive, or marries his brother's wife after his brother dies, if his brother already has children. Yahweh says that doing this makes the man and woman ritually dirty—it is a very bad thing, and Yahweh hates it! A man who marries his brother's wife in the wrong way shames his brother in the worst possible way. Yahweh says that Yahweh will punish the man and the woman by not letting the man and woman have children. The man and woman will have no descendants because of the horrible thing that the man and woman did.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Has there ever been a time in your community where someone married his brother's wife? What happened in that situation, and what did your community do in response?

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 20:17–21 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has five scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells Moses what to do if a man marries his sister.

In the second scene: Yahweh tells Moses what to do if a man has sex with a woman who is having her monthly bleeding.

In the third scene: Yahweh tells Moses what will happen if a man has sex with his father's or mother's sister.

In the fourth scene: Yahweh tells Moses what will happen if a man has sex with his father's brother's wife.

In the fifth scene: Yahweh tells Moses what will happen if a man marries his brother's wife in the wrong way.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Obedient Israelites
  • And disobedient Israelites

It is important to remember that Yahweh is telling Moses these instructions so that Moses can tell the instructions to the rest of the Israelites. The Israelites are not listening to Yahweh talk in this specific story.

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

In this story, Yahweh gives Moses a list of rules and instructions. These are the laws that the Israelites need to follow, and all of the laws have very serious consequences and strong punishments. All of the laws are about what the Israelites need to do when someone in the community has sex with someone the person is not supposed to have sex with. In this story, Yahweh tells Moses how Moses should punish people who do not obey the five rules Yahweh reminds Moses of in this story.

Stop here and discuss how you can talk about the action of sex in a way that is appropriate to talk about when both men and women are present. How did you translate this appropriately in Leviticus 18? Pause this audio here.

First, Yahweh tells Moses what to do when a man marries his sister. This rule applies to anyone who marries his father's daughter or anyone who marries his mother's daughter. The man who marries his sister sees his sister naked, and his sister sees her brother naked. Yahweh says that what the man and his sister have done is the opposite of the kind of loyalty a family should have for family. Yahweh says that the "sons of their people," who are the Israelites, need to exile the man and his sister because of what the man and his sister have done. The phrase "sons of their people" means that the punishment is very public so everyone will know what the man and his sister have done. The Israelites will work together to exile the man and woman so that the man and woman can never be part of the community again. This was a deeply shameful punishment. Yahweh says that the man who married his sister "bears his guilt." This means that the man is even more guilty than his sister.

Stop here and tell a story about someone who dishonored someone else. How do you talk about the way that someone dishonors someone else? Pause this audio here.

Stop here and tell a story about someone who did something so bad that the community sent that person away so that person could never return. What do people think about the person who could never come back? How did the community send that person away? Discuss how you will make it clear in your translation that the Israelites will publicly exile the man and the woman here. Pause this audio here.

Second, Yahweh tells Moses what to do if a man has sex with a woman who is menstruating, or having her monthly bleeding. Yahweh says that the man who has sex with a woman who is having her monthly bleeding has seen her bleeding, and that the woman has shown the man her bleeding when the woman was not supposed to. Yahweh says that the community must cut off or exile both the man and the woman from the people. You will remember that it is possible that when someone cuts off others from the community, Yahweh wants the community to kill the man and woman, but it is more likely that Yahweh just wants them to send the man and woman away from the community.

Stop here and discuss how you talk about menstruation in an appropriate way in your language. Discuss how you have talked about menstruation in earlier passages. Pause this audio here.

Third, Yahweh tells Moses what will happen if a man has sex with the sister of the man's father or mother. Yahweh says that a man who has sex with his aunt has had sex with someone who is close family. Yahweh will punish the man and the woman who had sex with each other because of the horrible thing those people did. The man and woman will carry their iniquity, which means the man and woman are guilty for what they have done.

Stop here and discuss how you will talk about the way that someone bears their own iniquity, or is guilty for what that person has done. Pause this audio here.

Fourth, Yahweh tells Moses what to do if a man has sex with his father's brother's wife. Yahweh says that a man who has sex with his father's brother's wife is "uncovering his uncle's nakedness." This means that the man has shamed his father's brother—his uncle. Both the man and the woman are guilty, and Yahweh will punish the man and the woman who had sex.

Stop here and review how you have translated the way that someone uncovers another person's nakedness, or deeply shames someone. Pause this audio here.

Fifth, Yahweh tells Moses what to do if a man marries his brother's wife when the man is not supposed to. Yahweh says that it is detestable for a man to marry his brother's wife in those situations. The word for "detestable" here talks about something that makes someone very, very ritually dirty. Some translations call what the man and woman did "an abomination," or something that Yahweh hates. Yahweh says that the man who marries his brother's wife when the man is not supposed to has shamed his brother by "uncovering his brother's nakedness." The man and the woman will die without having any children or any descendants. The man and woman's family will not exist anymore.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group. In two of these situations, the first and last, Yahweh talks about people who get married, or live together in the same way as husband and wife do. In the other situations, Yahweh talks just about having sexual relations, without getting officially married. Discuss how you will show the difference between the two kinds of situations Yahweh talks about in this passage. Pause this audio here.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 20:17–21 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has five scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Obedient Israelites
  • And disobedient Israelites

As a group, retell the passage twice. You should retell the passage in your own language.

Because your translators may not want to act out the content of this passage, you may just want to have someone speak the passage, or you may want to use objects to show the different relationships of people. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and retell the passage.

The group should retell this passage a second time. At certain points in the retelling, pause the retelling and discuss what you think the characters would be feeling and thinking. Then continue the retelling.

Pause this audio here and retell the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the retelling and possible responses.

Yahweh tells Moses what to do if a man marries the man's sister. It does not matter if the sister is the daughter of the man's mother or of the man's father and another woman who is not the man's mother. The Israelites must publicly send this man and his sister away. The man has dishonored his sister and is very guilty.

Pause the drama.

Ask the people playing the obedient Israelites, "What are you thinking or feeling?" The people might answer things like:

  • I am so angry and horrified! I cannot believe this man destroyed his sister's honor when the man was supposed to protect his sister; or
  • The disobedient Israelites are not part of our community anymore. It is like those people are dead. I do not ever want to see those people again; or
  • Yahweh said that we needed to punish people who do such horrible things. I want to follow Yahweh.

Ask the person playing the disobedient Israelite man, "What are you thinking or feeling?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am even more guilty than my sister is because I was supposed to honor and protect my sister, but I married my sister instead; or
  • I feel so horrible about what I did. I should have listened to Yahweh.
Continue the drama.

Then Yahweh tells Moses what to do if a man has sex with a woman who is having her monthly bleeding. The Israelites must force this man and woman to leave the community.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the obedient Israelites, "What are you thinking or feeling?" The people might answer things like:

  • I feel disgusted. Why would the disobedient Israelites have sex when it would make them so ritually dirty? or
  • The woman was supposed to rest in a special way. I cannot believe the woman had sex with that man instead! That man and woman disobeyed Yahweh, and so the man and woman need to leave the community now; or
  • I am upset and sad that members of our community act in this way.
Continue the drama.

Next, Yahweh tells Moses what to do if a man has sex with his mother's sister or with his father's sister. This man dishonors a close relative. Both the man and woman will be guilty, so Yahweh will punish the man and woman.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you thinking or feeling?" The person might answer things like:

  • I feel disgusted. This man had sex with a woman who was closely related to the man. That is not what I want people to do; or
  • This man and these women deserve a punishment for breaking my rules; or
  • I am sad that people do not follow my good rules for sex and marriage.

Ask the person playing the disobedient Israelites, "What are you thinking or feeling?" The people might answer things like:

  • Yahweh himself is punishing us for what we did! We should not have had sex with each other! or
  • I feel so guilty and horrible because of what I did!
Continue the drama.

Then Yahweh tells Moses what will happen if a man has sex with his uncle's wife. This man dishonors his uncle. Yahweh will punish the man and woman for what they did, so the man and woman will not have any children or any descendants.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the uncle, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am so ashamed. My nephew and my wife did such a horrible thing! or
  • I am angry! I cannot believe my nephew and my wife would do such a shameful thing to me!

Ask the people playing the man and his uncle's wife, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people might answer things like:

  • Yahweh did not let us have any children! Our family will die out, and it will be like we never existed in the community! We should have listened to Yahweh; or
  • This is such a horrible punishment! We will not have any descendants. What will we do?
Continue the drama.

Finally, Yahweh tells Moses what will happen if a man marries his brother's wife in the wrong way. This is a very shameful way to treat a brother. Yahweh will cause the man and the brother's wife to not have any children.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the brother, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I cannot believe my brother would do such a horrible thing and shame me so much! or
  • I am angry! I cannot believe my brother and my wife would do such a shameful thing to me! or
  • I am disgusted. My brother and my wife did something so evil and ritually dirty and impure.

Ask the people playing the disobedient Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The people might answer things like:

  • Yahweh did not let us have any children! Our family will die out, and it will be like we never existed in the community! We should have listened to Yahweh; or
  • This is such a horrible punishment! We will not have any descendants. What will we do?

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 20:17–21 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

First, Yahweh says what will happen if a man marries his father's daughter or his mother's daughter. These are two different ways to talk about someone's sister. A woman might be a man's sister because they have the same mother, or the woman might be the man's sister because they have the same father but a different mother. Use the same word or phrase for "father's daughter" or "mother's daughter" as you have used in Leviticus chapter 18.

Yahweh says that a man who marries his sister sees his sister's naked body, and the sister sees the man's naked body. Yahweh says that this is a disgrace. The word for disgrace here is a word that normally means loyalty and love. Here, it means that the man is doing the opposite of what a loyal and loving brother should do.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for disgrace. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

The Israelites need to cut off the man and the woman from the community. This probably means that the Israelites exiled the man and the woman. Use the same word or phrase here as you used in previous passages. Use the same word or phrase throughout.

The Israelites needed to cut off the man and the woman "in the sight of the sons of their people." This phrase means that the Israelites needed to punish the man and the woman publicly so everyone knew what a shameful thing the man and the woman had done.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for in the sight of the sons of their people. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that the man has uncovered his sister's nakedness. The phrase uncovered his or her nakedness is one way the Israelites talked about having sex with someone else when they should not. You will remember that this phrase also means that the man has made his sister ashamed. Use the same word or phrase for "uncovered her nakedness" as you used in previous passages. Use the same word or phrase throughout.

Then Yahweh says the man who marries his sister will pay for, or carry the burden of, his iniquity. It is not entirely clear how the man will carry his iniquity, but it does mean that the man will be guilty and that Yahweh will punish the man for what the man did. Use the same phrase for carrying the burden of his iniquity as you did in Leviticus 17:16.

Next, Yahweh tells Moses what to do if a man has sex with a woman who is menstruating. Menstruation is when a woman has her monthly bleeding. Use the same word or phrase for menstruation as you used in Leviticus chapter 18.

Then, Yahweh says that a man should not have sex with his father's sister or his mother's sister. Use the same word or phrase for "father's sister" or "mother's sister" as you used in Leviticus chapter 18.

Yahweh says that a man should not have sex with his father's sister or his mother's sister because the woman is a close blood relative or a close relative. Use the same word or phrase for "blood relative" or "close relative" as you used in Leviticus chapter 18.

Next, Yahweh says that a man should not have sex with his father's brother's wife. Use the same word or phrase for "father's brother's wife" as you used in Leviticus chapter 18.

Yahweh says that the man and woman who have sex will die childless. This means that the man and woman will not have any descendants who live after them. The man and woman will not have their own children or any descendants.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for childless. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word or phrase that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Finally, Yahweh talks about what will happen if a man marries his brother's wife. Use the same word or phrase for "brother's wife" as you used in Leviticus chapter 18.

Yahweh says that what the man and his brother's wife have done is detestable or is an abomination. This means that what the man and the brother's wife have done is very ritually dirty and impure, and Yahweh hates it. Use the same word or phrase for detestable as you have used in previous passages, especially when it means something that is ritually dirty.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.
