title: Leviticus 20:22–27
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 20:22–27 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 20:22–27 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 20:22–27 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this story, Yahweh keeps telling Moses the rules and instructions Yahweh wants the Israelites to obey. Later, Moses will tell the Israelites all of these instructions so that the Israelites will know how to live as Yahweh's people.

Yahweh says that the Israelites need to keep all of Yahweh's statutes and ordinances and do what Yahweh says. Yahweh says the Israelites need to do all these things so that the Israelites can live peacefully in the land that Yahweh is leading the Israelites to. It is important to remember that the Israelites were traveling from the country of Egypt, where the Israelites had been slaves, to Canaan. Yahweh had promised to give the Israelites the land of Canaan, but the Israelites had not arrived there yet.

Stop here as a group and look at a map of the Israelites' travel from Egypt to Canaan. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh had promised to give the land of Canaan to the Israelites as their new home. However, Yahweh warns Moses that the Israelites need to obey Yahweh's rules. If the Israelites do not obey Yahweh, Yahweh will send the Israelites out of the land.

Yahweh warns the Israelites to be careful about how the Israelites live when the Israelites finally arrive in Canaan. The Israelites must not live the same way that the Canaanites live. Yahweh says that Yahweh is giving the land of Canaan to the Israelites because the people who live in the land of Canaan, the Canaanites, did evil, horrible things that made Yahweh angry. Yahweh is punishing the Canaanites by giving their land to the Israelites instead. This is why Yahweh does not want the Israelites to live the same way that the Canaanites live. If the Israelites live the same way that the Canaanites live, then Yahweh will need to punish the Israelites the same way Yahweh is punishing the Canaanites.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time when you needed to take away something from someone because that person was not taking good care of that thing or doing what that person was supposed to do. Pause this audio here.

Then Yahweh reminds Moses that Yahweh promised the Israelites that Yahweh would give the Israelites the Canaanites' land as the Israelites' new homeland. The land is a gift from Yahweh. Yahweh says that the land is a beautiful place that flows with milk and honey. This means that the land is perfect for the Israelites' animals to live on so that the animals can produce a lot of milk and other good food. It also means that the land can grow delicious food for the people. The word "honey" here refers to something sweet and delicious. It can be talking about sweet syrup that people made using fruit, like the date fruit, or it can be talking about the sweet syrup that bees make. Either way, when Yahweh talks about a land flowing with milk and honey, Yahweh is saying that the land has plenty of good food to eat and plenty of water to drink.

Stop here as a group and look at pictures of milk, dates, and honey. Then, as a group, describe the best land you have ever seen. What made the land such a good place to be? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh will give the beautiful land of Canaan to the Israelites because he is Yahweh, the Israelites' God, who chose the Israelites to be different from all the other people in the world. So Yahweh says that the Israelites need to make sure to live in a different way from the other nations. If the Israelites do not, it is like the Israelites are shaming Yahweh since the Israelites are Yahweh's representatives to the other nations.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time when you needed to act differently because you were representing someone else. What did you need to do differently? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that the Israelites need to separate the ritually clean animals and birds from the ritually dirty animals and birds. Yahweh warns the Israelites not to eat any of the ritually dirty animals, birds, or other animals that crawl all over the land because eating those animals makes the Israelites ritually dirty as well. Then Yahweh reminds the Israelites that Yahweh told the Israelites clearly which animals are ritually dirty so that the Israelites know exactly what the Israelites can or cannot eat. Yahweh reminds the Israelites to be holy because Yahweh is holy and Yahweh chose the Israelites to be Yahweh's people out of all the people in the world.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time when someone ate a ritually dirty animal that the person should not have eaten. What happened? Pause this audio here.

Finally, Yahweh tells Moses what to do if one of the Israelites ever acts as a medium or tries to talk to the spirits of dead people. If the Israelites see any man or woman acting as a medium, spiritist, or necromancer, then the Israelites need to kill that person by throwing stones at the person until that person dies. This is because the medium tried to learn spiritual information without talking to Yahweh. Yahweh says that the person is guilty because the person knew that they should talk to Yahweh to learn that information and chose to talk to dead people's spirits instead.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time when someone in your community tried to gain spiritual information the wrong way. What did your community do?

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 20:22–27 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has three scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh warns Moses and the Israelites not to live like the Canaanites so that the Israelites can stay in the land that Yahweh will give to the Israelites.

In the second scene: Yahweh reminds the Israelites to only eat ritually clean animals.

In the third scene: Yahweh tells Moses how the Israelites need to punish mediums or spiritists.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Canaanites
  • Obedient Israelites
  • And disobedient Israelites

It is important to remember that Yahweh is still telling these instructions to Moses so Moses can tell the Israelites. Later, Moses will tell these instructions to the Israelites.

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

In the previous stories, Yahweh told Moses how to punish people who disobeyed Yahweh's laws. Now, in scene one, Yahweh tells Moses why it is so important for the Israelites to obey all of Yahweh's laws. Instead of telling Moses how to punish individual people for breaking Yahweh's laws, Yahweh tells Moses how Yahweh will punish all of the Israelites if the Israelites disobey Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time when someone in your community warned the entire community about something. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh tells Moses that the Israelites need to obey all of Yahweh's statutes and ordinances. If the Israelites do obey what Yahweh says, then the land that Yahweh is bringing the Israelites to will not vomit the Israelites out. A person vomits when a person gets so sick that the things in the person's stomach come back out the person's mouth. Yahweh says that when the Israelites disobey Yahweh and become ritually dirty, the dirtiness is so bad that it is as if the land itself becomes sick. Then the land vomits the Israelites out and forces the Israelites to leave. It is important to know that Yahweh is the one who would actually make the Israelites leave. Yahweh is using this special language of the land getting sick and vomiting to show the Israelites how important it is for the Israelites to continue to obey Yahweh when the Israelites arrive at the new, beautiful land.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Tell a story about a time when you were extremely sick. What happened, and how did you get better? How do you talk about the way that a person vomits food out of their stomach? How will you talk about the way Yahweh says the land will vomit the Israelites out if the Israelites disobey Yahweh? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh tells the Israelites that the people who currently live in the land of Canaan do shameful things, and that is why Yahweh is making the Canaanites leave the land. Yahweh says that the Canaanites did all these things. The phrase "all these things" here refers to shameful things that are evil and that people should be ashamed to do. Yahweh warns the Israelites not to follow the customs of the Canaanites, or to live in the same way that the Canaanites do. If the Israelites do, Yahweh says Yahweh will force the Israelites to leave the land as well.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What are some ways that other people groups act that are different than how your people group acts? How do you talk about this different way of life, or different customs? How do you talk about someone who lives in the same way as a different people group does? Pause this audio here.

Then Yahweh reminds the Israelites that Yahweh promised to give the Israelites the land of Canaan. Yahweh quotes a promise that Yahweh made earlier in the Bible. Yahweh said that the Israelites would own the Canaanite land because Yahweh would give that land to the Israelites. Yahweh also said that the land of Canaan is a "land flowing with milk and honey," or a land with plenty of good food and water.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will translate the way that Yahweh says that the land of Canaan is a land flowing with milk and honey. Pause this audio here.

Then Yahweh reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh their God who made the Israelites different from all the other people by making the Israelites Yahweh's people. It is important to see that Yahweh wants the Israelites to be careful about how the Israelites live because the Israelites are Yahweh's people.

Stop here and discuss as a group how to talk about special groups of people or nations that someone has set aside for a special purpose. How will you talk about the way that Yahweh has set the Israelites apart to be Yahweh's people? Pause this audio here.

In scene two, Yahweh tells Moses to tell the Israelites to be careful about what the Israelites eat. Yahweh says that because the Israelites are Yahweh's people, the Israelites need to be careful to separate ritually clean birds and animals from ritually dirty birds and animals. When the Israelites eat meat, the Israelites must only eat ritually clean birds or animals. The Israelites must not eat any ritually dirty animal, bird, or any other creature. If the Israelites eat anything that is ritually dirty, then the Israelites defile themselves and become ritually dirty as well. The Israelites cannot serve Yahweh until the Israelites are ritually clean again. The Israelites cannot eat anything that is ritually dirty because Yahweh told the Israelites that those animals, birds, and other creatures were ritually dirty. Yahweh says that the Israelites need to be careful about what the Israelites eat because Yahweh chose the Israelites. Just like Yahweh made the priests holy by choosing the priests to be different from the other Israelites and serve Yahweh, Yahweh also made all of the Israelites holy by choosing the Israelites from all of the other nations in the world to be Yahweh's people. Yahweh is a holy God, so the Israelites need to live holy lives as Yahweh's people. Again, Yahweh says his name and that Yahweh has separated the Israelites from the nations for Yahweh.

In scene three, Yahweh gives Moses more instructions about what the Israelites need to do if one of the Israelites disobeys one of Yahweh's laws or regulations. Yahweh says that the Israelites need to punish anyone who acts as a medium for spiritual forces or who acts as a spiritist or necromancer, whether that person is a man or a woman. If a man or woman acts as a medium or spiritist, then the Israelites need to kill that person. The Israelites must throw rocks at that person until the person dies. Yahweh says that the person's blood is on that person's own head. Yahweh means that the person is completely responsible and guilty because that person knew Yahweh's law and chose to be a medium or spiritist anyway.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will transition from the general instructions and warnings that Yahweh told Moses to tell the Israelites to this specific law about what to do with Israelites who become mediums or spiritists. Pause this audio here.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 20:22–27 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has three scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Canaanites
  • Obedient Israelites
  • And disobedient Israelites

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

Yahweh warns Moses about what the Israelites need to do. As Yahweh speaks, the people playing the obedient and disobedient Israelites can act out what Yahweh is saying.

First, Yahweh tells Moses that the Israelites need to obey all of Yahweh's statutes and laws by doing what Yahweh says. If the Israelites disobey Yahweh, then the land that Yahweh is giving to the Israelites as their new home will vomit the Israelites out. While Yahweh is talking, the people playing the disobedient Israelites should pretend to disobey Yahweh. Then show how Yahweh makes the people leave the land, just like food leaves a person's stomach when a person vomits.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you thinking and feeling?" The person may say things like,

  • I do not want the Israelites to do such horrible things! The Israelites deserve a punishment; or
    • I warned the Israelites not to do that. I am sad that the Israelites disobeyed me, and now I have to punish the Israelites.

    Ask the people playing the disobedient Israelites, "What are you thinking and feeling?" The people may say things like:

    • I did not think that Yahweh would actually punish me for disobeying Yahweh! I wish I had obeyed Yahweh; or
    • I am sad because Yahweh warned us that Yahweh would punish us if we disobeyed Yahweh, and now we cannot live in the good land anymore; or
    • I am angry that I have to leave the land even though I disobeyed Yahweh! [!end] Continue the drama.

Yahweh warns Moses that the Israelites should not live the same way that the Canaanites live. Yahweh says that the Canaanites did shameful, horrible things. That is why Yahweh is taking the land away from the Canaanites and giving the land to the Israelites instead. While Yahweh is talking, Yahweh acts out how Yahweh forces the Canaanites to leave the land and gives the land to the Israelites instead.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • The Canaanites did horrible, shameful things. I do not want my special people to live like that! or
  • I hate what the Canaanites are doing. The Canaanites are hurting themselves and others; or
  • I do not want the Israelites to live the way the Canaanites are living. If the Israelites do, I need to punish the Israelites, and I do not want to punish the Israelites.
Continue the drama.

Yahweh says that Yahweh made a promise to Israel. That promise was that the Israelites would own the Canaanites' land because Yahweh would give the land to the Israelites. Yahweh also promised that the land of Canaan would be a good land that flows with milk and honey. Then Yahweh says that he is Yahweh, the Israelites' God, and that Yahweh made the Israelites different from all the other people.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I love the Israelites! I am so excited to give the Israelites this beautiful land! or
  • I chose the Israelites to be my people, and I want the Israelites to have this special land.
Continue the drama.

Then Yahweh tells Moses that the Israelites need to be careful to separate the ritually clean animals and birds from the ritually dirty animals and birds. Yahweh says that the Israelites need to do this because Yahweh chose the Israelites to be Yahweh's people. Yahweh says that the Israelites cannot eat any bird, animal, or other creature that Yahweh says is ritually dirty because then the Israelites will be ritually dirty as well. The Israelites need to become holy people because Yahweh is a holy God. Yahweh chose the Israelites to be Yahweh's very own people and separated the Israelites from all the other nations.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person may say things like:

  • It is so important for the Israelites to carefully choose what the Israelites eat because I carefully chose the Israelites to be my people out of all the people in the world; or
  • I love the Israelites, and I want the Israelites to live holy lives. The Israelites are special to me. I want the Israelites to live in a special way so that the Israelites remember that the Israelites are special to me and so that everyone else in the world knows that the Israelites are special to me.
Continue the drama.

Finally, Yahweh tells Moses that the Israelites need to kill men and women who act as mediums or who talk to dead people's spirits. Yahweh says that the people who do those things have their own blood on their heads because these people know what Yahweh said to do, but chose to be mediums anyway.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person may say things like:

  • I feel hurt and betrayed because the person who was a medium was one of my people. This person should have talked to me to learn things. Instead, the person talked to dead people's spirits; or
  • The Israelites promised that I would be their God and the Israelites would be my people. However, this person tried to make the Israelites stop trusting me and trust dead people's spirits instead! or
  • I am angry that this person disobeyed my rules and treated dead people's spirits as more powerful and important than I am.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 20:22–27 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

Yahweh tells Moses that the Israelites need to keep Yahweh's statutes. It is important to remember that statutes are laws or rules about how to live in a society. Use the same word or phrase for statute as you used in previous passages. Look up statute in the Master Glossary for more information.

Yahweh also says that the Israelites need to be careful to obey all of Yahweh's ordinances. It is important to remember that ordinances are rules that people have to keep. Use the same word or phrase for ordinances as you used in previous passages. Look up ordinances in the Master Glossary for more information.

Yahweh says that the Israelites need to keep Yahweh's statutes and laws because otherwise the land that Yahweh is bringing the Israelites to will vomit the Israelites out instead of being their new home. While Yahweh does not say the name of the land here, we know that this land is the land of Canaan.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of the land of Canaan on a map. Use the same word or phrase to talk about the land Yahweh gave the Israelites as you used in previous passages. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that the land will vomit the Israelites out if the people do not listen. Use the same word or phrase for the land vomiting out the Israelites as you used in previous passages.

Then Yahweh says that when the Israelites get to the land, the Israelites need to live differently than the people who already live there.

Yahweh says that Yahweh detests the Canaanites because of all the things that the Canaanites have done. The word detest here means to strongly dislike or to hate someone or something. Yahweh is saying that the Canaanites have done so many horrible things that Yahweh does not want a relationship with the Canaanites anymore.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for detest. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Then Yahweh says that Yahweh has promised that Yahweh will give the land to the Israelites as their possession or for the Israelites to possess. A possession is something that belongs to you. Yahweh is saying that Yahweh wants the Israelites to live in the land and own the land instead of the people that currently live in the land.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for possess or possession. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that the land is flowing with milk and honey. It is important to remember that the land did not have milk and honey flowing across it. Instead, this phrase means that the land had enough grass and other plants for cows and goats to make a lot of milk, and it had good ground so that fruits and other sweet foods could grow. It might also mean that the land had many bees that made sweet food for the Israelites to eat. The phrase "flowing with milk and honey" is an expression that describes a very good land where people have plenty to eat and can grow many good things.

Stop here and look at the pictures of milk, dates, and honey again as a group. Discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for flowing with milk and honey. If you have already translated this phrase in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that he is Yahweh, the Israelites' God, who set the Israelites apart from other people. In this story, God refers to himself with his personal name, Yahweh. Use the same words or phrases for Yahweh and God that you have in previous passages. For more information on Yahweh and God, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh says that Yahweh set the Israelites apart or made the Israelites different from other people. Yahweh is saying that Yahweh made the Israelites different from all the other people groups in the world because Yahweh chose the Israelites to be Yahweh's special people. Use the same phrase for "set apart" or "made them different from other people" as you used in previous passages and throughout this story.

Yahweh says that the Israelites need to make a difference between ritually clean and ritually dirty animals and birds. Use the same word or phrase for ritually clean and ritually dirty as you used in previous passages. For more information about "clean and unclean," refer to the Master Glossary.

Then Yahweh explains that the Israelites must not defile themselves by eating anything ritually dirty. It is important to remember that a person who defiled himself or herself was ritually dirty and could not serve Yahweh anymore until that person was ritually clean again. Use the same word or phrase for defile as you used in previous passages. For more information about defile, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh says that the Israelites need to avoid ritually dirty animals, birds, and creatures that swarm, or move around, on the ground. It is important to remember that the Israelites used the phrase "animals, birds, and creatures that move around on the ground" to talk about every kind of animal. Here, Yahweh is saying that the Israelites cannot eat anything that is ritually dirty, no matter what. Use the same word or phrase for "animals, birds, and creatures that move around on the ground" as you used in previous passages.

After Yahweh explains that the Israelites cannot eat anything ritually dirty, Yahweh says that the Israelites need to be holy. The word holy means that something belongs to Yahweh or that Yahweh is God. Use the same word or phrase for holy as you used in previous passages. For more information on holy, refer to the Master Glossary.

Finally, Yahweh tells Moses how the Israelites need to punish men or women who become mediums. It is important to remember that mediums were people who would try to talk with or become possessed by dead people's spirits. Yahweh also tells Moses how the Israelites need to punish men or women who become spiritists or necromancers. Spiritists and necromancers were people who tried to learn information by talking to dead people's spirits. These are two very similar kinds of people. Use the same words or phrases for medium and spiritist or necromancer as you used in previous passages. Look at "medium" in the Master Glossary for more information.

Yahweh tells Moses that the Israelites need to punish mediums and spiritists by stoning these people. This meant that the Israelites would throw rocks at the person until the person died. Use the same word or phrase for "stone to death" as you used in previous passages.

Finally, Yahweh says that the person who is a medium or spiritist is guilty, or that their blood is on their head. It is important to remember that the phrase "his blood is on his head" means that the person earned their punishment because the person knew Yahweh's laws but chose to disobey anyway. Use the same word or phrase for "his blood is on his head" as you used in previous passages. For more information, see blood in the Master Glossary.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 21:1–9
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 21:1–9 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 21:1–9 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 21:1–9 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In previous passages of Leviticus, Yahweh has told Moses what the Israelites need to do to be holy and how the Israelites need to punish people who do not obey Yahweh's laws. In this passage, Yahweh begins to give Moses laws for the priests to obey so that the priests can be holy.

First, Yahweh tells Moses to talk to the priests. Yahweh also calls the priests the sons of Aaron because Yahweh said that all of Aaron's descendants will be the priests. Yahweh wants Moses to tell the priests several things.

First, Yahweh will not allow a priest to defile himself when one of the priest's relatives dies. Normally, when a person died, that person's relatives would help prepare and bury the body together, and the relatives would mourn the person together. When a person touched the dead body or went to the place where people buried the dead body, that person would become ritually dirty. Normally, Yahweh allowed people to bury and mourn the body and become ritually dirty, but here Yahweh explains that Yahweh will not allow priests to become ritually dirty for one of their relatives. However, Yahweh does allow a priest to defile himself, or make himself ritually dirty, for a relative if the relative is one of the priest's closest family members. Yahweh explains that the closest family members are a mother, a father, a son, a daughter, and a brother. Yahweh also says that a sister who is not married yet and is close to the priest, because the sister does not have a husband, is one of the priest's closest family members. Yahweh will allow the priest to defile himself for this sister and all the rest of these closest family members.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do people expect a man to care for and treat the members of his family? How do people expect a man to treat his unmarried sisters? Pause this audio here.

However, Yahweh will not allow the priests to defile themselves in other situations. Yahweh probably does not want the priest to defile himself for any of the priest's wife's family members. Yahweh might also mean that Yahweh does not want the priest to defile himself in normal situations because the priest is a leader of the Israelites. In either situation, if the priest makes himself ritually dirty, the priest will defile himself or bring shame to himself when the priest is holy.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, which people are special, or dedicated to a spirit or god? What rules do those people have to obey that no one else obeys? Pause this audio here.

Second, Yahweh will not allow the priests to make a bald spot on their heads, shave the edges of their beards, or cut themselves. Each of these different actions is what the people around Israel did when people mourned a dead person. Yahweh does not want the priests to mourn in these ways. Earlier in Leviticus, Yahweh also told all the rest of the Israelites that Yahweh does not want the Israelites to cut themselves or shave the edges of their beards to mourn a person who was dead.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do people mourn someone who has died? When do people not allow someone to mourn a person who has died? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that the priests need to be holy, or dedicated, to their God. Yahweh says the priests must not profane, or mistreat, their God's holy name. When Yahweh says Yahweh will not allow the priests to profane Yahweh's name, Yahweh is using special language to mean that the priests must not shame or dishonor Yahweh. Because the priests burn the sacrifices people give to Yahweh, the priests need to be holy. Yahweh calls these sacrifices Yahweh's food. People bring offerings of food, or fire offerings, to present to Yahweh, so that food belongs to Yahweh.

Third, Yahweh will not allow the priests to marry a prostitute or a woman who has defiled herself. When Yahweh talks about a woman who has defiled herself, Yahweh probably means a woman who has sex with people at a temple as part of special rituals. Yahweh also will not allow a priest to marry a woman whose husband has divorced that woman. The priests cannot marry any of these women because the priests are holy to their God. Yahweh tells the Israelites to treat the priests like the priests are holy people, or people who are dedicated to God, because the priests offer food to their God, which people call fire offerings. Remember that even though the priests offer the food to Yahweh, Yahweh does not eat the food. Yahweh tells the people to consider the priests holy, because Yahweh, who makes people holy, is holy.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, who can priests marry? What do people think about women who are prostitutes and women whose husbands have divorced them, or women who have divorced their husbands? What do people think about the men who marry prostitutes and the men who marry women who have had a divorce? Pause this audio here.

Finally, Yahweh tells Moses that when a daughter of a priest becomes a prostitute, she profanes or makes herself ritually dirty and dishonors or shames her father. If the daughter of a priest becomes a prostitute, Yahweh tells the Israelites to burn the daughter. Yahweh probably means that after the Israelites stone the daughter to death, the Israelites need to burn the daughter's body. People would often burn a person's dead body because the people wanted to insult that person even after that person was dead. Yahweh tells the Israelites to burn the daughter's body to show how serious the crime the daughter committed was.

Stop here and ask this question as a group: In your culture, what do people think about a leader when the leader's children act in a bad way? What do people expect a leader to do when their children act in a bad way?

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 21:1–9 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has four scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells Moses to tell Aaron and the other priests that the priests must not defile themselves for anyone but the priests' closest family.

In the second scene: Yahweh tells the priests not to make a bald spot on their head, shave the edges of their beard, or cut themselves, because the priests are holy.

In the third scene: Yahweh tells the priests to avoid marrying women who have a bad reputation.

In the fourth scene: Yahweh tells the priests to burn any of their daughters who become prostitutes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Aaron
  • The priests
  • A priest's relatives
  • A priest's mother
  • A priest's father
  • A priest's son
  • A priest's daughter
  • A priest's brother
  • A priest's unmarried sister
  • The Israelites
  • A prostitute
  • A woman who has sex at a temple
  • And a divorced woman

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

Remember that in previous passages, Yahweh has been telling Moses the laws the Israelites must obey so the Israelites can be holy. Yahweh has also been telling Moses how the Israelites need to punish people who do not follow those laws. In this passage, Yahweh begins to talk about the special rules that priests need to follow because the priests are holy, or set apart, for special service to Yahweh in a way that other Israelites are not.

In the first scene, Yahweh tells Moses to talk to the priests. Yahweh also calls the priests the sons of Aaron, because Aaron's male descendants will be the priests. Yahweh says the priests must not become ritually dirty because of a dead body. When a person died, their dead body made everyone near the body ritually dirty. The dead person's relatives would still get near the dead body and prepare the person's body so the relatives could bury the body. That would make the relatives ritually dirty for a short time. Yahweh does not want the priests to do things that would make the priests ritually dirty, except for the priests' closest family members. Yahweh lists the closest family members of a priest: the priest's mother, father, sons, any daughters, any brothers, and any sisters who have not married a man yet. You may notice that Yahweh does not mention a priest's wife. Many people think that because the wife is married to the priest, everyone would know that the wife is a close family member. Everyone would already know that a priest could mourn and become ritually dirty for the priest's wife. So perhaps that is why Yahweh does not mention a priest's wife here.

A priest may also defile himself for his sister who has not married a man. If the priest's sister is married, her husband would be responsible to bury the sister. If the sister is not married, her brother, who is the priest, may need to help bury the sister. When Yahweh mentions a priest's sons and daughters, Yahweh is including all of the children that a priest would have, from the first child through the last child. When Yahweh mentions a priest's brothers and sisters, Yahweh means brothers and sisters who are older and younger and the same age as the priest. These brothers and sisters would be children of the priest's father or mother.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What is the best way to talk about all the family members Yahweh is talking about in this passage? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh will not allow any priest to defile himself as a husband among the priest's people. Yahweh probably does not want the priest to defile himself for any of his wife's family members. Yahweh might also mean that Yahweh does not want the priest to defile himself in normal situations because the priest is a leader of the Israelites. If the priest defiles himself as a husband among his people, the priest will profane himself. The priest is holy, or special to Yahweh. So Yahweh does not want the priest to profane himself, or make himself common or unholy.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: How have you heard this part of the passage before in your area? What is the best way to translate that a priest cannot defile himself as a husband among his people? Pause this audio here.

In the second scene, Yahweh will not allow a priest to make bald spots on the priest's head. Yahweh also will not allow a priest to cut the edges of the priest's beard. Yahweh also will not allow any priest to cut himself. These three actions are things that people did when people wanted to mourn someone who had died. Yahweh is probably saying that Yahweh will not allow the priests to do any of these things to show how sad the priests are that someone died. Yahweh says that the priests will be holy, or special, to the God that the priests serve, who is Yahweh. Yahweh will not allow the priests to profane Yahweh's name, or Yahweh's reputation, because the priests offer the sacrifices the Israelites make to Yahweh by burning the sacrifices. Yahweh calls these sacrifices the food of their God, because people gave food as offerings to God. Remember that Yahweh does not eat this food. Because the people have dedicated this food to God and the food belongs to God, the people must treat the food the way God tells the people to.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: How will you translate this in such a way to make it clear that Yahweh does not say Yahweh will eat this food? Pause this audio here.

In the third scene, Yahweh shows how a priest's wife must have a good reputation, because a wife's reputation affects the husband's reputation. Yahweh will not allow any priest to marry a prostitute or a woman who has sex at a temple. Sometimes, women who worshiped other false gods would work at those gods' temples. These women would have sex with men who came to worship at the temple as part of a ritual. Yahweh calls these women defiled, and Yahweh will not allow priests to marry these women. Yahweh will also not allow any priest to marry a woman whose husband has divorced her. Often, when a man divorced his wife, it was because the woman was not faithful to her husband, so divorce was shameful to a woman. Yahweh did not want the priests to marry any woman who did not have a good reputation.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: How will you talk about a prostitute or someone who has sex with multiple people who they are not married to? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that the priests cannot marry any of these women because the priests are holy to Yahweh, who is the God the priests serve. Then, Yahweh says, "You must treat the priests as holy." Remember, Yahweh is talking to Moses at this part of the story. Since Moses will repeat these instructions to the Israelites, we can tell that Yahweh is actually saying to Moses that Moses and all the Israelites should treat the priests as holy. The priests are holy, or special, since the priests offer the food to the God the Israelites serve. Yahweh is talking again about the fire offerings that the priests offer for the Israelites, which are food that belongs to Yahweh. Yahweh says that the Israelites will treat the priests as holy because Yahweh, who made the Israelites holy, is holy himself. Yahweh is the one who makes the priests holy.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What is the best way to translate that the Israelites need to consider the priests holy because Yahweh, who made the Israelites holy, is holy himself? Pause this audio here.

In the fourth scene, Yahweh says that when a priest's daughter profanes herself by becoming a prostitute, the daughter profanes her father. All priests are holy to Yahweh. If the priest's daughter becomes a prostitute, the daughter brings shame or dishonor to her family's reputation and to her father's status as holy. Just like the priest's wife could affect the priest's reputation, the priest's daughter can also affect the priest's reputation. Yahweh tells the Israelites to burn any daughter of a priest who becomes a prostitute.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 21:1–9 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has four scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Aaron
  • The priests
  • A priest's relatives
  • A priest's mother
  • A priest's father
  • A priest's son
  • A priest's daughter
  • A priest's brother
  • A priest's unmarried sister
  • The Israelites
  • A prostitute
  • A woman who has sex at a temple
  • And a divorced woman

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

In the first scene, Yahweh tells Moses to talk to the priests. Yahweh also calls the priests the sons of Aaron, because Aaron's male descendants will be the priests. Yahweh will not allow any priest to make himself unclean in order to bury and mourn a dead person the priest is related to, except the priest's closest family members. Yahweh lists the closest family members of a priest: the priest's mother, father, any sons, any daughters, any brothers, and any sisters who have not married a man yet. A priest may defile himself for his sister who has not married a man yet because the sister depends on her brother, the priest, since the sister has no husband.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the priest, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am sad that I cannot mourn like other people do when any of my grandparents or cousins die; or
  • I am glad that Yahweh will let me deeply mourn when my closest family members die; or
  • I know that I am really special, and I cannot let myself become ritually dirty unless the reason is really important; or
  • This law will be very hard to obey, especially when a friend of mine dies and I cannot mourn as other people mourn. I trust that Yahweh has a good reason for this law, though.
Continue the drama.

But a priest must not profane himself and make himself ritually dirty for someone who is related to the priest only by marriage

In the second scene, Yahweh will not allow a priest to make bald spots on the priest's head. Yahweh also will not allow a priest to cut the edges of the priest's beard. Yahweh also will not allow any priest to cut himself. Yahweh says that the priests will be holy, or special, to the God that the priests serve, who is Yahweh. Yahweh will not allow the priests to profane Yahweh's name, or Yahweh's reputation, because the priests offer the fire offerings the Israelites make to Yahweh by burning the sacrifices. Yahweh calls these fire offerings the food that belongs to the Israelites' God.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • The priests are really special to me, so people will see how the priests act and learn more about who I am and the respect I deserve; or
  • I need people to realize how good and powerful I am; or
  • I want the priests to act differently from everyone else so people will know I am different than everyone else.
Continue the drama.

In the third scene, Yahweh will not allow any priest to marry a prostitute or a woman who has sex at a temple. Yahweh will also not allow any priest to marry a woman whose husband has divorced her. Yahweh says that the priests cannot marry any of these women because the priests are holy to Yahweh, who is the God the priests serve. Then, Yahweh says the Israelites need to treat the priests like the priests are holy, or special, since the priests offer the food to the God the Israelites serve. Yahweh says that the Israelites will consider the priests holy because Yahweh, who made the Israelites holy, is holy himself.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am amazed that the priests have to follow all these rules! These rules are very different than the rules that other gods' priests must follow; or
  • I know that the priests are different because of how the priests act; or
  • Yahweh's priests are really special, so Yahweh must be really special.
Continue the drama.

In the fourth scene, Yahweh says that when a priest's daughter profanes herself by becoming a prostitute, the daughter profanes her father. Yahweh tells the Israelites to burn any daughter of a priest who becomes a prostitute.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing a priest, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I would be so deeply sad if my daughter acted like this! I will be very careful to teach my daughters that they must not do this; or
  • I would be very angry if my daughter acted like that! My daughters would know who Yahweh is because I serve Yahweh. My daughters would know how wrong it is to be a prostitute! or
  • This is a very strong punishment! This shows me how terrible it is to sin against our God!

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 21:1–9 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

In this passage, Yahweh speaks to Moses. Yahweh is the personal name that the one true God gave to the Israelites to call God. Use the same word or phrase for Yahweh as you used in previous passages. For more information on Yahweh, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh tells Moses to speak to the priests. The priests are the people Yahweh chose to offer sacrifices to Yahweh for the Israelites. The priests also take care of the Tent of Meeting and teach the people how to worship Yahweh. Use the same word or phrase for priests as you used in previous passages. For more information on priests, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh will not allow the priests to defile themselves, or make themselves unclean for a dead person. When someone is unclean or ritually dirty, that person cannot participate in ritual worship to Yahweh. Use the same word or phrase for defile as you used in previous passages. For more information on defile, and clean and unclean, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh will allow the priests to become ritually dirty for a close relative. This includes the priest's mother, father, sons, daughters, brothers, and unmarried sisters.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will talk about close relatives here. Pause this audio here.

If a priest defiles himself for one of his wife's relatives, the priest will profane himself. When someone profanes something, that person takes something that is holy and mistreats that thing. That person makes the holy thing common or unholy. Use the same word or phrase for profane as you used in previous passages. For more information on profane, refer to the Master Glossary.

The priests need to be holy, or special, to Yahweh. Any person, place, or object that someone dedicates or devotes to God is holy. Use the same word or phrase for holy as you used in previous passages. For more information on holy, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh is the God the priests serve. In the Bible, "God" refers to the God who created everything. God is the most powerful spiritual being. Use the same word or phrase for God as you used in previous passages. For more information on God, refer to the Master Glossary.

The priests approach the altar to offer fire offerings to Yahweh. Use the same phrase for approaching the altar as you used in previous passages.

The fire offerings are food that belongs to Yahweh. An offering is a gift or a sacrifice that people give in a ritual to Yahweh. Use the same word or phrase for fire offering as you used in previous passages. For more information on "fire offering," refer to the Master Glossary.

A priest cannot marry a woman whose husband divorced her. Divorce is a permanent and legal separation between a husband and a wife.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for divorce. Look at "divorce" in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, discuss if you can use the same word or phrase here.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 21:10–16
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 21:10–15 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 21:10–15 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 21:10–15 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In previous passages, Yahweh told Moses rules that priests needed to follow because the priests were holy. In this passage, Yahweh tells Moses the rules that the high priest needs to follow about when the high priest mourns dead relatives and when the high priest marries. The high priest is the most important priest because the high priest is the only person whom Yahweh allows to go into the Most Holy Place. This was the place where Yahweh himself lived, where the ark of the covenant was. At that time, Aaron was the high priest. After Aaron died, one of Aaron's sons became the high priest, and that tradition continued for hundreds of years.

Yahweh describes the high priest in three ways. First, Yahweh says that the high priest is more important than the high priest's brothers. The high priest's brothers are all the other priests, or other descendants of Aaron. The high priest is more important because Yahweh gives the high priest more responsibility to help the Israelites than Yahweh gives the other priests. Second, Yahweh says that someone poured anointing oil on the high priest's head. Anointing oil was a special oil, probably olive oil, that people would pour onto someone's head in a ritual that gave the person a special job or role. In this case, before someone became a high priest, someone else needed to pour anointing oil on the new high priest's head. We do not know who poured the oil on the high priest's head. Third, Yahweh says that Yahweh chose the high priest to wear the clothes. Yahweh is talking about the special clothes that Yahweh told Moses to make for the high priest when Yahweh gave Moses all the instructions for how people should build the tabernacle. The high priest needs to wear these clothes every time the high priest does a ritual for God.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of the high priest's clothes. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Think about a very important religious or political leader in your culture. Describe this person to each other, and pay attention to the things about this person that you feel are important to say. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh will not allow the high priest to make the high priest's hair messy. Yahweh also might mean that Yahweh will not allow the high priest's hair to be loose. People in Israel and other people groups probably liked to keep their hair clean and neat, and might have also used string or other materials to hold the hair together. When people wanted to mourn someone who had died, people would make their hair not neat, but instead messy. Yahweh does not want the high priest to do this to his hair, even when the high priest wants to mourn someone who died.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what do people do with their hair? What special situations cause people to do something different with their hair? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh also will not allow the priest to tear the high priest's clothes. When people in Israel wanted to express a strong emotion like grief, people would often tear their clothes. Yahweh does not want the high priest to tear the high priest's clothes like other Israelites do.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time someone mourned a person who died who had been a close friend or family member. What did the person do to show that they were mourning the dead person? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh will not allow the high priest to go where there is a dead body, because if the high priest goes near a dead body, the high priest will become unclean or ritually dirty. Yahweh will not even allow the high priest to become ritually dirty if the high priest's father or mother died. Yahweh will not allow the high priest to leave the holy place, or the tabernacle, to mourn a person who has died. If the high priest leaves the sanctuary to mourn a person who has died, the high priest is mistreating Yahweh's sanctuary and is making the sanctuary less holy. The high priest mistreats the sanctuary because someone anointed the high priest with oil to be in the sanctuary for Yahweh. Yahweh tells the Israelites that he is Yahweh.

Then Yahweh tells Moses that Yahweh will only allow the high priest to marry a woman who is a virgin, or who has not had sex with a man. Yahweh will not allow a high priest to marry a widow, a divorced woman, a woman who has sex at a temple, or a prostitute. Sometimes, women who worshiped other gods besides Yahweh would work at a temple that was not Yahweh's. Men would go to the temple, and the women would have sex with the men as part of a ritual to worship the god. Yahweh calls these women defiled. Yahweh requires the high priest to marry a virgin who is one of the high priest's own people. Yahweh might mean that the high priest needs to marry a priest's daughter, but Yahweh probably means that the high priest needs to marry an Israelite. If the high priest does not marry one of the high priest's own people, the high priest will profane his children. In other words, the high priest will make the high priest's children be not holy. Yahweh will not allow the high priest to do this because of who Yahweh is and how Yahweh made the high priest holy.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 21:10–15 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has two scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh says that Yahweh will not allow the high priest to mourn people who have died.

In the second scene: Yahweh says that Yahweh will only allow a high priest to marry a woman who is both a virgin and an Israelite.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • The high priest
  • The priests
  • The high priest's parents
  • A woman whose husband has died
  • A woman whose husband divorced her
  • A woman who has sex at a temple
  • A prostitute
  • And a virgin woman who is an Israelite

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

Remember that in the previous passage, Yahweh has been telling Moses to tell the priests the rules priests must obey when they mourn or marry. In this passage, Yahweh talks about the rules a high priest specifically has to follow.

In the first scene, Yahweh describes the high priest in three ways. Yahweh is about to give very difficult rules for the high priest to follow, so Yahweh wants the priests to realize why the high priest needs to follow these rules. First, the high priest is more important than his "brothers," or the other priests. Second, someone poured anointing oil on the high priest's head. Third, Yahweh chose the high priest to wear the special clothes that a high priest has to wear.

Then Yahweh says that Yahweh will not allow the high priest to make his hair messy or tear his clothes. Yahweh also will not allow the high priest to get near a dead body, even if the dead body is the high priest's mother or father. If the high priest gets near a dead body, the high priest will become ritually dirty. The high priest will not be able to serve Yahweh while the high priest is ritually dirty. Yahweh will not allow the high priest to leave the holy place, or the tabernacle, to mourn someone who has died. This does not mean the high priest can never leave, but only that the high priest cannot leave to go mourn somewhere. If the high priest leaves the holy place to mourn someone who has died, the high priest will mistreat the holy place. The high priest will make the holy place less holy, because when someone poured the anointing oil on the high priest, then the high priest became holy. Yahweh tells the priests Yahweh's name. Yahweh's name reminds people of who Yahweh is, so Yahweh often states his name to remind people that Yahweh is holy.

In the second scene, Yahweh tells the priests that Yahweh will only allow the high priest to marry a woman who is a virgin. Then, Yahweh gives a list of women who are not virgins: widows, divorced women, women who have sex at temples, and prostitutes. Sometimes, women would work at false gods' temples and have sex with men who came to worship at the temple as part of a ritual. Yahweh calls these women defiled, and Yahweh will not allow the high priest to marry any of these women. Yahweh also tells the high priest that the virgin the high priest marries needs to be an Israelite, or the high priest's children will not be holy like the other priests' children. Yahweh will not allow the high priest to marry in the wrong way because Yahweh is Yahweh and Yahweh makes the high priest holy.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What kinds of women can the high priest marry? What kinds of women can the high priest not marry? How do you describe the kind of woman that the high priest can marry in your culture? Pause this audio here.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 21:10–15 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has two scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • The high priest
  • The priests
  • The high priest's parents
  • A woman whose husband has died
  • A woman whose husband divorced her
  • A woman who has sex at a temple
  • A prostitute
  • And a virgin woman who is an Israelite

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

In the first scene, Yahweh describes the high priest in three ways. First, the high priest is more important than the other priests. Second, someone poured anointing oil on the high priest's head. Third, Yahweh chose the high priest to wear the special clothes that a high priest has to wear.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the high priest, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am so happy that Yahweh has chosen me to be so special; or
  • I know that I need to do the right thing because of how important I am.
Continue the drama.

Then, Yahweh says that Yahweh will not allow the high priest to make the high priest's hair messy or tear his clothes. Yahweh also will not allow the high priest to get near a dead body, even if the dead body is the high priest's mother or father. If the high priest gets near a dead body, then the high priest will become ritually dirty, and the high priest will not be able to serve Yahweh while the high priest is ritually dirty. Yahweh will not allow the high priest to leave the holy place, or the tabernacle, to mourn someone who has died.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the high priest, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am sad that I cannot mourn even my parents; or
  • I know I need to keep doing my job for Yahweh even though someone close to me died.
Continue the drama.

If the high priest leaves the holy place to mourn someone who has died, the high priest will mistreat the holy place and will make it less holy, because when someone poured the anointing oil on the high priest, then the high priest became holy. Yahweh tells the priests that Yahweh is Yahweh.

In the second scene, Yahweh tells the priests that Yahweh will only allow the high priest to marry a woman who is a virgin. So Yahweh will not allow the high priest to marry a widow, a divorced woman, a woman who has sex at temples, or a prostitute. These are two different scenarios where women have sex, one which involves rituals to honor other gods, and one where women have sex for money. Yahweh calls both kinds of these women defiled. Yahweh also tells the high priest that the virgin the high priest marries needs to be an Israelite, or the high priest's children will not be holy like the other priests' children. Yahweh will not allow the high priest to do that because Yahweh is Yahweh and Yahweh made the high priest holy.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I want the high priest to be completely holy because the high priest is so important to me and to the Israelites; or
  • I love my people and want their high priest to be careful who he marries.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 21:10–15 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

In this passage, Yahweh talks about the high priest. Priests are people who are responsible for offering sacrifices to God on behalf of the Israelites. The high priest was the most important priest. Use the same words or phrases for priests and high priest as you used in previous passages. For more information on high priest, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh talks about the anointing oil. In the Old Testament, before God gave someone a special task, God would instruct someone else to pour oil over that person's head. Use the same word or phrase for anoint as you used in previous passages. For more information on anoint, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh says that Yahweh will not allow the high priest to make himself unclean or ritually dirty. When someone is unclean, that person cannot participate in worship to Yahweh. Use the same word or phrase for unclean as you used in previous passages. For more information on clean and unclean, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh will not allow the high priest to leave the sanctuary, or tabernacle, to mourn someone who died. Use the same word or phrase for sanctuary, or holy place, as you used in previous passages. For more information on sanctuary, refer to the Master Glossary.

If the high priest leaves the sanctuary, the high priest will profane the sanctuary. When someone profanes something, that person mistreats something that is holy and makes it common or unholy. Use the same word or phrase for profane as you used in previous passages. For more information on profane, refer to the Master Glossary.

When someone poured the anointing oil on the high priest's head, that person consecrated the high priest, or made him holy. Use the same word or phrase for consecrate as you have used previously, and refer to consecrate in the Master Glossary for more information.

Yahweh says that if the high priest leaves the sanctuary, the high priest will profane the sanctuary of God. Use the same word for God as you used in previous passages. For more information on God, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh emphasizes that he is Yahweh. Yahweh says this to remind the people that Yahweh and Yahweh's people are special. Use the same word for Yahweh as you used in previous passages. For more information on Yahweh, refer to the Master Glossary.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.
