title: Leviticus 21:17–25
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 21:16–24 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 21:16–24 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 21:16–24 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In the previous passages, Yahweh told Moses to tell the priests the rules to follow when a priest mourned someone or married someone. In this passage, Yahweh tells Moses to tell Aaron, the high priest and the ancestor of all Israel's priests, who Yahweh will allow to offer food offerings to Yahweh. Yahweh will not allow any of Aaron's descendants who have a physical problem or defect to go to Yahweh and offer Yahweh food. When Yahweh talks about offering food, Yahweh is talking about the sacrifices that the priests made to Yahweh on behalf of themselves and the Israelites.

Yahweh will not allow any of Aaron's descendants who have a long-term physical problem of some kind to go offer food to Yahweh at the tabernacle. Yahweh will not allow a priest who is blind or unable to walk to offer food to Yahweh. Yahweh also will not allow a priest whose face is deformed in any way or whose limbs are too long to offer food to Yahweh. Yahweh also will not let a priest whose hand or foot is broken in some way offer food to Yahweh. Yahweh also will not let someone with a hunchback or someone who is unusually small offer food to Yahweh. When someone has a hunchback, their back curves forward a lot. It makes that person walk differently and can cause that person pain.

Stop here and look at this picture of a person with a hunchback. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh also will not allow a priest with something wrong with his eyes, skin, or testicles to offer food to Yahweh. Then, Yahweh says again that Yahweh will not allow any of Aaron's descendants who have something physically wrong with them to offer the offerings to Yahweh by fire. When Yahweh talks about offering the food by fire, Yahweh is talking about the way the priests offer food to Yahweh. The priests burn offerings on the altar in the courtyard of the tabernacle.

Stop here and look at a picture of the altar in the courtyard at the tabernacle. Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do people treat people who have something physically wrong with them? What does the community not allow people to do when those people have something physically wrong with them? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh will allow the priest who has something physically wrong with him to eat Yahweh's food. When Yahweh talks about Yahweh's food here, Yahweh is talking about the food that the Israelites give to Yahweh when the Israelites tithe or when the Israelites make sacrifices. Yahweh then gives most of that food to the priests to eat. Yahweh expects the priests to eat that food to survive rather than doing other work to get food. Yahweh also wants the priests who have something physically wrong with them to eat from that same food to survive. Yahweh allows the priests who have something wrong with them to eat the most holy food and the holy food. The most holy food probably refers to the food that people gave the priests when the Israelites made a sacrifice. The holy food probably refers to the food the Israelites gave the priests when the Israelites tithed, when the Israelites offered the firstborn animals, and when the Israelites offered the first crops of a harvest. Yahweh does not stop the priests who have something physically wrong with them from eating any of the food Yahweh allows a normal priest to eat.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do people take care of people who have something physically wrong with them? Pause this audio here.

However, Yahweh will not allow the priests with something physically wrong to go near the curtain that separates the Most Holy Place from the Holy Place inside the tabernacle. Yahweh probably will not allow the priests who have something physically wrong with them to enter the Holy Place in the tabernacle at all.

Stop here as a group and look at this diagram of the tabernacle. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh also will not allow the priests who have something physically wrong with them to go close to the altar where the priests burn the sacrifices to Yahweh. If a priest who has something physically wrong with him does go near the curtain or the altar, that priest will profane, or mistreat, the holy places in the tabernacle, and make those places not holy. Yahweh tells the priests to obey these rules because he is Yahweh and Yahweh made the priests and the holy places in the tabernacle holy.

Then Moses tells Aaron and Aaron's sons and all the Israelites everything that Yahweh told Moses to say.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 21:16–24 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has three scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells Moses to tell Aaron what physical deformities will prevent a priest from offering food to Yahweh.

In the second scene: Yahweh tells Moses to tell Aaron that Yahweh will allow the priests who have something physically wrong with them to eat the holy food. However, Yahweh will not allow those priests with something physically wrong with them to be in the holy places.

In the third scene: Moses repeats Yahweh's words to Aaron and the Israelites.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Aaron
  • The priests
  • The priests who have something physically wrong with them
  • And the Israelites

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

Remember that in previous passages, Yahweh told Moses to tell the priests the rules to obey when the priests mourned people who had died and when the priests married women. In this passage, Yahweh is still giving rules for the priests to obey. Here, Yahweh is giving the rules the priests must obey when a priest has something physically wrong with them.

In the first scene, Yahweh tells Moses to talk to Aaron. The storyteller of Leviticus reminds us that Yahweh is talking to Moses because Yahweh is now changing to a different subject. Now Yahweh tells Moses to tell Aaron that Yahweh will not allow any of Aaron's descendants who have something physically wrong with them to come to Yahweh and offer food to Yahweh.

Stop the audio here and discuss this question: Describe a person in your culture who has something physically wrong with that person. What words do you use to describe that person's condition? What words will you use to translate this idea? Pause this audio here.

When Yahweh talks about offering food to Yahweh, Yahweh is also referring to the entire work that the priests do. Yahweh will not allow a priest who has something physically wrong with him to do the jobs that Yahweh gave to the priests to do.

In this passage, though Yahweh is speaking to Moses, Yahweh speaks as if Yahweh is speaking directly to Aaron and the Israelites. You should also translate the parts where Yahweh is speaking as if Yahweh is speaking directly to Aaron and the Israelites, if possible.

Then Yahweh lists the different types of physical problems a priest can have. Yahweh will not allow any priest who is blind or unable to walk, or who has a deformity on their face, to come near Yahweh in the tabernacle. Yahweh also will not allow any priest who has a limb that is too long, who has a broken foot or a broken hand, who has a hunchback, or who is unusually short to come near Yahweh in the tabernacle. Someone who has a hunchback cannot walk or stand upright because that person's spine is curved. Yahweh also will not allow someone who has something wrong with their eyes, skin, or testicles to come near to Yahweh in the tabernacle.

Stop this audio here and discuss as a group: What words do you use for these kinds of physical problems? How will you translate this part of the passage into your language? Pause this audio here.

Then Yahweh says again that Yahweh will not allow any of Aaron's descendants to get close to Yahweh to give the offerings with fire. Yahweh calls Aaron "the priest" here to remind the Israelites that Aaron is the first priest and the ancestor of all the priests. Then Yahweh says again that if a priest has something physically wrong with him, Yahweh will not allow that priest to go close to Yahweh to offer food to Yahweh.

In the second scene, Yahweh says that Yahweh will allow a priest who has something wrong with him to eat food that the Israelites offer to Yahweh. Yahweh allows the priest to eat the most holy food and the food that is holy. The holy food is probably the food that people give to Yahweh as a tithe, and the most holy food is probably the food that the people offer as a sacrifice to Yahweh. But Yahweh will not allow a priest who has something physically wrong with him to go near the curtain to the holiest place or the altar because there is something physically wrong with that priest. If the priest with something physically wrong with him does go near the curtain or the altar, that priest will profane, or mistreat, the holy places in the tabernacle and make those places common, or not holy. Yahweh will not allow a priest who has something physically wrong with him to profane the sanctuary, or holy places, in the tabernacle because Yahweh is Yahweh and Yahweh makes the holy places and the priests holy.

Then, in the third scene, Moses tells Aaron and Aaron's sons and all the people of Israel what Yahweh told Moses about all the rules for the priests. This includes information from previous passages regarding rules for the priests.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 21:16–24 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has three scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Aaron
  • The priests
  • The priests who have something physically wrong with them
  • And the Israelites

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

In the first scene, Yahweh tells Moses to talk to Aaron. Yahweh tells Moses to tell Aaron that Yahweh will not allow any of Aaron's descendants who have something physically wrong with them to come to Yahweh and offer food to Yahweh.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the priests, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am sad that I will not be able to offer food to Yahweh if I have something physically wrong with me; or
  • Yahweh is really special and holy if the priests cannot have any physical problems to serve Yahweh; or
  • I am glad Yahweh is telling us exactly what Yahweh wants us to do when we have something physically wrong with us.
Continue the drama.

Yahweh will not allow any priest who is blind, who is unable to walk, or who has a deformity on their face to come near Yahweh in the tabernacle. Yahweh also will not allow any priest who has a limb that is too long, who has a broken foot or a broken hand, who has a hunchback, or who is unusually short to come near Yahweh in the tabernacle. Yahweh also will not allow someone who has something wrong with their eyes, skin, or testicles to come near to Yahweh in the tabernacle. Then Yahweh says again that Yahweh will not allow any of Aaron's descendants who have a defect to come close to Yahweh to offer the offerings with fire. Then Yahweh says again that if the priest has something physically wrong with him, Yahweh will not allow that priest to come close to Yahweh to offer food or fire offerings to Yahweh.

In the second scene, Yahweh allows a priest who has something wrong with him to eat food that the Israelites offer to Yahweh. Yahweh allows the priest to eat the holiest food and the food that is just holy.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I love these priests who have something physically wrong with them, so I am going to make sure the Israelites take care of these priests; or
  • I really want everyone in Israel to have enough food to eat, even if those people cannot work as other people do; or
  • Even though these priests have something physically wrong with them, the priests are holy, so I will take care of those priests.
Continue the drama.

But Yahweh will not allow a priest who has something physically wrong with him to go near the curtain to the holiest place or the altar because there is something physically wrong with that priest. If the priest with something physically wrong with him does go near the curtain or the altar, that priest will profane, or mistreat, the sanctuary, or holy places in the tabernacle and will make those places less holy. Yahweh will not allow a priest who has something physically wrong with him to mistreat the holy places in the tabernacle because Yahweh is Yahweh and Yahweh made the holy places and the priests holy. Then, Moses tells Aaron and Aaron's sons and all the people of Israel what Yahweh told Moses.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 21:16–24 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

In this passage, Yahweh speaks to Moses. Yahweh is the personal name that the one true God gave the Israelites to call God. Use the same word or phrase for Yahweh as you used in previous passages. For more information on Yahweh, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh also describes himself as God in this passage. Use the same word or phrase for God as you used in previous passages. For more information on God, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh talks about Aaron's descendants. A person's descendants are his children, grandchildren, and all future generations from the same family line. Use the same words or phrases for descendants and generations as you used in previous passages. For more information on descendants and generations, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh calls Aaron a priest. Priests are people who are responsible for offering sacrifices to God on behalf of the Israelites. Use the same word or phrase for priest as you used in previous passages. For more information on priests, refer to the Master Glossary.

In this passage, Yahweh talks about the priests who have a physical problem. These physical problems may include someone who is blind, unable to walk, whose face is deformed in any way, or whose limbs are too long, whose hand or foot is broken, or who has a hunchback. They may also include anyone with open sores or anyone with damaged testicles.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will talk about the physical problems that keep a priest from offering fire offerings to Yahweh. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh allows priests who have something physically wrong with them to eat the most holy and the holy food. Any place, person, or object that is dedicated to God is holy. That means that God sets apart the object or person for God's special purposes. That person and object are no longer "common" or "ordinary," and people can no longer use those things for common or ordinary purposes. Use the same word or phrase for holy as you used in previous passages. For more information on holy, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh will not allow a person who has something physically wrong with them to go near the altar to offer fire offerings to Yahweh. You will remember that the fire offerings are the animals that the Israelites burned on the altar as food for Yahweh. The altar is a large bronze platform that the Israelites used to make sacrifices to Yahweh. Use the same words or phrases for altar and fire offerings as you used in previous passages. For more information on altar and fire offerings, refer to the Master Glossary.

If a priest who has something physically wrong with him does go near the altar, that priest will profane Yahweh's sanctuary. The word sanctuary means a holy place, so it is another name for Yahweh's tabernacle or Tent of Meeting. When someone profanes something, that person mistreats the item and makes that item unholy. Use the same words or phrases for profane and sanctuary as you used in previous passages. For more information on profane and sanctuary, refer to the Master Glossary.

Moses said these things to Aaron, Aaron's sons, and to all the Israelites. Use the same word or phrase for Israelites as you have used previously, and refer to Israelites in the Master Glossary for more information.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 22:1–9
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 22:1–9 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 22:1–9 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 22:1–9 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In previous passages, Yahweh has been telling Moses how the priests need to act when the priests mourn someone, when the priests marry someone, and when the priests have a long-term physical defect. In this passage, Yahweh starts to tell Moses who can eat the sacred food Yahweh gives to the priests.

Yahweh tells Moses to talk to Aaron and Aaron's sons, who are the priests. Yahweh probably says that Yahweh wants Moses to tell Aaron and the priests when to stay away from holy food, or food that is dedicated to Yahweh. Yahweh might be saying that Yahweh wants Moses to tell Aaron and the priests to treat the holy food with respect. The holy food is the food that the Israelites consecrate, or dedicate, to Yahweh. The priests receive this holy food from the Israelites, and Yahweh gives some of this food to the priests to eat. The priests need to treat the food in the right way.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what food do people consider special? What rules do people have to follow about that food? Pause this audio here.

If the priests do not stay away from the holy food when Yahweh says to, the priests will profane Yahweh's holy name. The priests will dishonor Yahweh by making other people think that Yahweh is not completely good and powerful. Yahweh reminds the Israelites that Yahweh is Yahweh.

Then Yahweh tells Moses to tell the priests that if a priest comes close to the sacred donations while the priest is unclean or ritually dirty, Yahweh will not allow that priest to go to the holy place and serve Yahweh as a priest anymore. Yahweh is not just talking about the priests who are alive while Moses is talking to the priests. Yahweh is talking about all his priests, including those who will serve Yahweh in the future. Yahweh reminds the priests again that he is Yahweh.

Then, Yahweh says that none of Aaron's descendants, who are the priests, can eat the holy donations of food if those descendants have a serious skin disease or if something abnormal is coming out of their penis. Those descendants need to wait until the descendants are ritually clean before they can eat the holy food. Yahweh says that the descendants cannot eat the holy food while ritually dirty. A priest can become ritually dirty if the priest touches something a dead body touched, if the priest has semen come out of his penis, or if the priest touches a ritually dirty small animal or insect. A priest can also become ritually dirty if a priest touches a person who will make other people ritually dirty, no matter why that person is ritually dirty. If a priest does any of these things, then the priest will be ritually dirty until evening, and Yahweh will not allow the priest to eat the holy food. The priest who becomes ritually dirty for any of these reasons needs to wash his body in water before the priest can eat the holy food again. After the priest has washed his body in water, and after the sun has set, then the priest will be able to eat the holy food again.

Yahweh will not allow the priests to eat an animal that died on its own or because another animal killed it. The priests can only eat animals that a person kills. If the priest eats an animal that died when a human did not kill that animal, then the priest will become ritually dirty. Yahweh reminds the priests that he is Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what kind of dead animals will you eat? What kind will you not eat? How do people treat animals that died when a human did not kill the animals? What do people do with those animals? Pause this audio here.

Then Yahweh tells Moses that the priests need to do the things Yahweh tells the priests to do. If the priests do not do the things Yahweh tells the priests to do, then the priests will become guilty because they have sinned. The priests will die because the priests profaned something holy to Yahweh. Yahweh is probably talking about how the priests profane the holy food. Yahweh might be talking about how the priests profane the things Yahweh told the priests to do. Then Yahweh reminds the priests that he is Yahweh, and Yahweh makes the priests holy.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 22:1–9 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has four scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells Moses to tell the priests not to eat the holy food while the priests are ritually dirty.

In the second scene: Yahweh talks about different things that could make a priest ritually dirty and explains when the priests can become clean and eat the food again.

In the third scene: Yahweh tells the priests not to eat food from animals that humans did not kill.

In the fourth scene: Yahweh reminds the priests that they should do what Yahweh tells the priests to do because Yahweh is the one who is holy, and Yahweh is the one who makes the priests holy.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Aaron
  • The priests
  • Israelites
  • And a person who is ritually dirty

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

Remember that in this section of Leviticus, Yahweh is telling Moses the rules the priests must obey. In the previous passages, Yahweh told Moses the rules for the priests when the priests marry someone or mourn someone, and the rules Yahweh has for priests who have something physically wrong with them.

In this passage, Yahweh begins to tell Moses that Yahweh will not allow the priests to eat the holy food when the priests are unclean or ritually dirty.

In the first scene, Yahweh tells Moses to talk to Aaron and Aaron's sons, the priests. Yahweh does not use the term for priests in this passage, but we know that Aaron's sons refer to Aaron's male descendants, who are the priests in Israel. You may need to use your term for priests in this passage to be clear about who Yahweh is talking about. Aaron and Aaron's sons need to sometimes stay away from the holy food that the Israelites dedicate to Yahweh. Yahweh is talking about the times when the priests need to avoid eating the holy food that the Israelites give to Yahweh, and then when Yahweh allows the priests to eat. If the priests eat the holy food when Yahweh does not want the priests to, then the priests will profane, or mistreat, Yahweh's name. When Yahweh says the priests will mistreat Yahweh's name, Yahweh is using special language to mean that the priests profane, or dishonor, Yahweh by making other people think that Yahweh is not completely good and powerful.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What is the best way for you to translate when Yahweh tells the priests to stay away from the holy food? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh tells the priests that he is Yahweh. When Yahweh says that he is Yahweh, Yahweh is giving the reason why the Israelites should follow Yahweh's rules.

Then Yahweh tells Moses to tell Aaron and the priests that if any of the priests or their descendants are ritually dirty, those people cannot go close to the holy food that the Israelites dedicated to Yahweh. If a priest does go close to the holy food when ritually dirty, then Yahweh will cut that priest off from Yahweh's presence. Yahweh says that the priests must follow this rule for all generations, which means that any priests in the future must also follow this rule. When Yahweh says Yahweh will cut that priest off from Yahweh's presence, Yahweh is using special language to mean that Yahweh will not allow the priests to do the jobs that a priest should do, like offering sacrifices to Yahweh. Then Yahweh says again that he is Yahweh. Yahweh is reminding the Israelites that Yahweh is their holy God.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time when someone did their work in a wrong way so that people did not allow that person to work that job ever again. How would you describe how other people stopped that person from doing that job? What is the best way for you to translate the way that Yahweh says Yahweh will cut the priests off from Yahweh's presence? Pause this audio here.

In the second scene, Yahweh gives several examples of situations where a priest would be ritually dirty. The first two situations would make a priest ritually dirty for a long time, and the next four situations would make a priest ritually dirty until evening. In the first two situations, Yahweh will not allow any of Aaron's descendants, who are the priests, who have a serious skin disease or who have something abnormal coming out of their penis, to eat the holy food until the priests are ritually clean. There are four more situations that make a priest ritually dirty, but in these cases, the priest will just be ritually dirty until evening. This is when a priest touches something that a corpse has made ritually dirty, and when a priest has semen come out of his penis. This also includes when a priest touches a ritually dirty animal or insect, and when a priest touches a ritually dirty person. Any of Aaron's descendants who do any of those things will be ritually dirty until evening. Yahweh will not allow any ritually dirty priest to eat the holy food until the priest washes his body in water. Yahweh wants Aaron's descendants to eat the holy food because that is their food. Yahweh is telling the Israelites this because even though Yahweh does not want the priests to eat food when the priests are ritually dirty, Yahweh does want the priests to eat the food that Yahweh gives the priests.

In the third scene, Yahweh will not allow the priests to eat animals that died without a human killing the animal, or that other animals killed. If the priests eat those animals, the priests will become ritually dirty.

In the fourth scene, Yahweh says again that he is Yahweh. Yahweh tells Moses that the priests need to do what Yahweh tells the priests to do. If the priests do not do what Yahweh tells the priests to do, the priests will carry their sin. This means that the priests will become guilty because the priests profaned the holy food and the priests will die. Yahweh says again that he is Yahweh and that Yahweh makes the priests holy.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: How will you translate when Yahweh says that the priest will carry their sin? Pause this audio here.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 22:1–9 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has four scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • Aaron
  • The priests
  • Israelites
  • And a person who is ritually dirty

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

In the first scene, Yahweh tells Moses to talk to Aaron and Aaron's sons. Yahweh promised that Aaron and Aaron's sons would be the priests who would make sacrifices to Yahweh for the Israelites. Aaron and Aaron's sons need to sometimes stay away from the holy food that the Israelites dedicate to Yahweh. If the priests eat the holy food when Yahweh does not want the priests to, then the priests will mistreat Yahweh's name. Yahweh tells the priests that he is Yahweh.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I want people to know that I am completely good and powerful; or
  • The priests need to be really careful when the priests eat the holy food.
Continue the drama.

Then Yahweh tells Moses to tell Aaron and the priests that if any of the priests or their descendants are ritually dirty, those people cannot come close to the holy food that the Israelites dedicated to Yahweh. If a priest does come close to the holy food when the priest is ritually dirty, then Yahweh will not allow that priest to serve Yahweh as a priest anymore. Then Yahweh says again that he is Yahweh.

In the second scene, Yahweh explains when Yahweh will not allow a priest, one of Aaron's descendants, to eat the holy food until that priest is clean. Yahweh will not let a priest eat the holy food when the priest has a serious skin disease or if the priest has something abnormal coming out of his penis. Then, Yahweh talks about anyone who touches something that a corpse made ritually dirty, anyone who has semen come out of his penis, anyone who touches a small animal or bug that makes someone ritually dirty, and anyone who touches a person who can make people ritually dirty. Yahweh says that any of Aaron's descendants who do any of those things will be ritually dirty until evening. Yahweh will not allow the person to eat the holy food until that person washes their body in water. Then Yahweh says again that when the sun sets, the person will be ritually clean and that person can eat the holy food. Yahweh wants Aaron's descendants to eat the holy food because that is their food.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the priests, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am sad that I have to wait until sunset before I can eat the holy food because I am ritually dirty; or
  • I am so glad that Yahweh is letting me eat the holy food people are giving to Yahweh; or
  • I know how important it is for me to be clean when I eat the holy food.
Continue the drama.

In the third scene, Yahweh will not allow the priests to eat animals that people did not kill or that other animals killed. If the priests eat those animals, the priests will become ritually dirty. Yahweh says again that he is Yahweh.

In the fourth scene, Yahweh tells Moses that the priests need to do what Yahweh told the priests to do. If the priests do not do what Yahweh has told the priests to do, the priests will become guilty because the priests profaned the holy food, and the priests will die. Yahweh says again that he is Yahweh and that Yahweh makes the priests holy.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 22:1–9 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

In this passage, Yahweh talks to Moses. Yahweh is the personal name that the one true God gave to the Israelites to call God. Use the same word or phrase for Yahweh as you used in previous passages. For more information on Yahweh, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh talks about the holy food, or offerings. When something is holy, someone has dedicated it to Yahweh. Use the same word or phrase for holy as you used in previous passages. For more information on holy, refer to the Master Glossary.

Someone has consecrated the holy food to Yahweh. When someone consecrates something, someone has set that thing apart for a special purpose. Use the same word or phrase for consecrate as you used in the previous passages. For more information on consecrate, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh does not want the Israelites to profane Yahweh's name. When a person profanes something, that person takes something holy and mistreats it and makes it not holy. Use the same word or phrase for profane as you used in previous passages. For more information on profane, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh tells the priests that these rules are for the priests and their descendants. Yahweh does not use the term for priests in this passage, but Aaron's male descendants are the priests. You may need to use your term for priests in this passage to be clear. A person's children, grandchildren, and all future children from the same family line are that person's descendants. Use the same words for priests and descendants as you used in previous passages. For more information on priests and descendants, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh says these rules are for all future generations. A generation refers to a group of people who are living at the same time and belong to about the same age group. When Yahweh says these rules are for all future generations, Yahweh means that the Israelites should follow these rules forever. For more on generations, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh does not want the priests to eat the holy food while the priests are unclean or ritually dirty. When someone is unclean, that person is unable to do things for Yahweh. Use the same word or phrase for unclean as you used in previous passages. For more information on clean and unclean, refer to the Master Glossary.

One of the things that could make a priest ritually dirty is if the priest has a serious skin disease. Sometimes people call this disease leprosy, although you will remember that this is not the same disease that we call leprosy today. Use the same word or phrase for this kind of skin disease as you used in previous passages. For more information, refer to leprosy in the Master Glossary.

Yahweh says that a person who does this will carry their sin. This means that the person is guilty for what the person has done. Use the same word or phrase for carrying sin as you used in previous passages. For more on sin and guilt, refer to the Master Glossary.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 22:10–16
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 22:10–16 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 22:10–16 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 22:10–16 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In the previous passage, Yahweh told the priests who are ritually dirty not to eat the holy food that Yahweh gave to the priests to eat from the sacred food the Israelites offered. In this passage, Yahweh says that Yahweh will not allow people who are not in a priest's family to eat the holy food. Here, Yahweh is providing for the priest and those in the priest's household, who have no other way to get food. We can see from the rules Yahweh gives that the people Yahweh includes in a priest's household are those people who do not have anyone else to help them.

First, Yahweh says that only the priest's family can eat the holy food. Yahweh also says that Yahweh will not allow any person who is staying with a priest while the person is traveling to eat the holy food. When the Israelites traveled, the Israelites would rest or spend the night in other people's houses. People would often share food with travelers and help travelers.

.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how often do people travel? Where do people stay when people travel? How do you take care of travelers or guests in your house? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh also will not allow a worker that a priest has hired to eat the holy food. Sometimes, when an Israelite hired someone to do some work, the worker would live with the person they worked for. Yahweh does not want those workers to eat the holy food, even though those workers might live with the priest.

Yahweh will allow a slave that a priest bought to eat the holy food. Sometimes people had a lot of debt and had to sell themselves as slaves to pay off their debt. Other people became slaves when someone captured those people during a war. A priest's slaves were part of the priest's household. In other words, the priest was responsible for the slaves, and so Yahweh will allow a priest's slaves to eat the holy food.

Yahweh also will allow anyone born in a priest's household to eat the holy food. When Yahweh says a priest's household, Yahweh is using special language to talk about a priest's family and slaves. So Yahweh will allow the priest's children to eat the holy food, and Yahweh will allow the children of the slaves of the priest to eat the holy food.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, who is part of a person's household, or family? Pause this audio here.

If a priest's daughter marries a person who is not a priest, then Yahweh will not allow the daughter to eat the holy food, because the daughter is now part of her husband's family, not her father's family. Yahweh will allow a priest's daughter whose husband dies, or whose husband divorces the daughter, to eat the holy food. Yahweh will only allow this if the priest's daughter does not have any children. If the daughter has children, Yahweh expects the children to take care of their mother. If the priest's daughter does not have any children, she needs to move back to her father's house, where the daughter lived when she was young, and then Yahweh will allow the daughter to eat the holy food.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, when a woman marries a man, where does the woman live? Whose family is the woman now a part of? Who takes care of the woman? What happens to a wife when a husband dies? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says again that Yahweh will not allow anyone besides these people to eat the holy food.

Then Yahweh says that if an outsider eats the holy food without meaning to eat the holy food, then that person needs to give the priest something that is equal to the value of the food that the person ate. That person also needs to give the priest something that is worth an extra one-fifth, or 20 percent, of the food the person ate. Yahweh does not say if the person needs to pay with money or with food. Yahweh will probably allow a person to pay with money or food.

Then Yahweh says that Yahweh will not allow anyone to profane the holy food of the Israelites. When someone profanes the holy food, that person mistreats the food and makes the food not holy. The Israelites give this holy food to Yahweh. If the priests, or anyone, profane the holy food by allowing someone who is ritually dirty or not authorized to eat the holy food, then the person who eats the food will become guilty and will probably need to offer a guilt or reparation offering. We are not sure who eats the holy food—this may be the priests who eat it when they are ritually dirty, or this may be other people who eat the food that only the priests should eat.

Yahweh says that he is Yahweh, and Yahweh makes the food holy. Because Yahweh makes the food holy, the Israelites need to be careful not to profane the food.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 22:10–16 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has three scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells the priests that no one outside the priest's household can eat the holy food.

In the second scene: Yahweh tells the priests when the priests' daughters can eat the holy food.

In the third scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites what to do if someone accidentally eats the holy food.

The characters in this passage are:

  • People who can eat the holy food, who are
  • A priest
  • Members of the priest's household, which includes
  • Slaves
  • A priest's daughter
  • People who cannot eat the holy food, such as
  • A person who is not a priest or part of the priest's family
  • A traveler staying with a priest
  • A worker whom a priest has hired
  • Yahweh
  • And Moses—although the storyteller does not mention Moses in this passage, we know that Yahweh is giving these rules to Moses

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

Remember that in the last passage, Yahweh told the priests that Yahweh will not allow the priests to eat the holy food when the priests are ritually dirty. Now, in this passage, Yahweh explains who Yahweh will and will not allow to eat the holy food.

In the first scene, Yahweh will not allow a person who is an outsider, or is not in the priest's family, to eat the holy food. Guests and hired workers cannot eat the holy food, even though guests and hired workers might stay in the same house as the priest. But slaves and people born into a priest's house may eat the holy food. When Yahweh talks about a priest's house, Yahweh is using special language to talk about the people who would live in a priest's house because those people are part of a priest's closest family. This includes a priest's children, wife, slaves, and the slaves' children.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: How do you talk about the people who live together in a household? Discuss how you want to translate the way Yahweh talks about people who are born in a priest's household. Pause this audio here.

In the second scene, Yahweh talks about a priest's daughter. If a priest's daughter marries someone who is not a priest, then Yahweh will not allow the daughter to eat the holy food. But if a priest's daughter becomes a divorced woman or a widow, and the daughter has no children who can take care of her, then the daughter can go back to her father and eat the holy food again. Then Yahweh says again that Yahweh will not allow any outsider to eat the holy food. Yahweh says this again because Yahweh wants the Israelites to remember this rule. The rest of the rules that Yahweh gives in this passage are just to help the Israelites understand how to obey this rule.

Stop here and discuss this as a group: Tell a story about a time someone gave one rule and then explained what people needed to do to follow that rule. Pay special attention to how the person emphasized how important this rule was. Pay attention also to how the person showed that everything the person said was about the original rule. Pause this audio here.

In the third scene, Yahweh gives an example of a person who eats the holy food but does not know it is holy food. In this situation, Yahweh tells the Israelites that the person needs to give the priest something that is as valuable as the holy food the person ate, plus one-fifth, or 20 percent, of the value of the food. This is a guilt offering, or a way to pay back for the wrong thing that person has done.

Stop here and discuss this as a group: In Leviticus 5:14–16, Yahweh talked about a guilt or reparation offering. In step three for that passage, you did an activity to see what 20 percent looks like. You had 10 items. Twenty percent of 10 items is 2, so you added those 2 items to the 10 to show what the whole value, plus 20 percent, looked like. If needed, review how you discussed and translated 20 percent in that passage and discuss how you will translate it in this passage. Pause this audio here.

In this final section, there is difficult wording that can make the passage difficult to understand. Yahweh probably is saying that Yahweh will not allow anyone to profane the holy food that the Israelites give to Yahweh. If someone does profane the holy food by eating the food when Yahweh does not want that person to, then that person will become guilty. That person will need to offer a guilt offering. Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to profane the holy food, or make it unholy, because he is Yahweh and Yahweh makes the food holy. Yahweh is saying that because Yahweh makes the food holy, when the Israelites profane the food, the Israelites disrespect Yahweh.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 22:10–16 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has three scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • People who can eat the holy food, who are
  • A priest
  • Members of the priest's household, which includes
  • Slaves
  • A priest's daughter
  • People who cannot eat the holy food, such as
  • A person who is not a priest or part of the priest's family
  • A traveler staying with a priest
  • A worker whom a priest has hired
  • Yahweh
  • And Moses—although the storyteller does not mention Moses in this passage, we know that Yahweh is giving these rules to Moses

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

In the first scene, Yahweh will not allow anyone who is not a part of a priest's family to eat the holy food. Yahweh will not allow any person who is staying with a priest while the person is traveling or any worker whom a priest has hired to eat the holy food. But if the priest buys someone as a slave, then Yahweh will allow that slave to eat the holy food. Also, if someone in the priest's family or household gives birth to someone, Yahweh will allow that new person to eat the holy food.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing a traveler and the person playing a hired worker, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am surprised that the priest does not share food with me; or
  • I can see that the priests are set apart because even their food is holy.

Ask the person playing a person the priest has bought, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am glad that Yahweh will allow me to eat the holy food; or
  • I am relieved that I and my children can have food; or
  • I am a part of the priest's house, so I can eat what the priest's family eats; or
  • Even my children can eat the holy food.
Continue the drama.

In the second scene, Yahweh will not allow a priest's daughter to eat the holy food if the daughter is married to someone who is not a priest. But if the priest's daughter's husband dies or divorces the daughter and the daughter has no children, then the daughter can go back to her father's house. Yahweh will then allow the daughter to eat the holy food that people give to her father.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing a priest's daughter, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • When I am married, I am no longer part of my father's family; or
  • I am so glad that Yahweh will let me eat the holy food when I am at my father's house; or
  • Yahweh is always making sure that someone takes care of me.
Continue the drama.

Yahweh says again that Yahweh will not allow a person who is not in the priest's family to eat the holy food.

In the third scene, Yahweh talks about a person who eats the holy food when the person does not mean to eat the holy food. The person who does that needs to give the priest something that is as valuable as the food. The person also has to give the priest an additional amount that is as valuable as one-fifth, or 20 percent, of the holy food that the person ate.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing a person who is not a priest, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • While I was staying at the priest's house, I ate some food on the table. I did not realize it was the holy food, not the food I could eat; or
  • I am so sorry that I ate the holy food accidentally; or
  • I am glad that Yahweh will let me make up for my mistake.
Continue the drama.

Then, Yahweh says that Yahweh will not allow anyone to profane the holy food that the Israelites give to Yahweh. If someone does profane the holy food by eating the holy food when Yahweh does not want that person to, then that person will become guilty. Yahweh tells that person to offer a guilt offering because he is Yahweh and Yahweh makes the food holy.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I want the Israelites to know how special this holy food is; or
  • I want to give this food to the priests because the priests work for me; or
  • I do not want people to think that I am not good and powerful because people do not respect my holy food.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 22:10–16 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

In this passage, Yahweh talks about the holy food, or offering to Yahweh. When something is holy, someone has dedicated that thing to Yahweh and it is special. Use the same word or phrase for holy as you used in previous passages. For more information on holy, refer to the Master Glossary.

Only the priests and their families are supposed to eat the holy food. A priest is a person who works in the tabernacle and helps the Israelites worship Yahweh. Use the same word or phrase for priest as you used in previous passages. For more information on priest, refer to the Master Glossary.

A priest's hired workers may not eat the holy food. Hired workers are people the priest pays to work for him.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will translate the idea of hired workers. If you have translated this idea in another passage, translate it the same way here. Pause this audio here.

A priest's slaves may eat the holy food. A slave is a person who does work for someone else without payment, and who cannot leave when that person wants. Use the same word or phrase for slave as you used in previous passages. For more information on slaves, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh allows anyone in a priest's household to eat the holy food. A household means all the people living together in one house. Use the same word or phrase for household as you used in previous passages. For more information on household, refer to the Master Glossary.

If a priest's daughter is divorced and goes back to live in her father's house, the daughter can eat the holy food. Divorce is a permanent and legal separation between husband and wife. Use the same word or phrase for divorce as you used in previous passages. For more information on divorce, refer to the Master Glossary.

If someone else eats the holy food, that person needs to offer a guilt offering. People made a guilt offering when people did something wrong that took value from Yahweh or someone else. Use the same word or phrase for guilt offering as you used in previous passages. For more information on guilt offering, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh does not want people to profane the holy food. When a person profanes something, that person mistreats something holy and makes that thing not holy. Use the same word or phrase for profane as you used in previous passages. For more information on profane, refer to the Master Glossary.

When someone profanes the holy food, Yahweh punishes that person because that person is guilty. Use the same word or phrase for guilt as you have used previously, and refer to guilt in the Master Glossary for more information.

The holy food is the food that belongs to Yahweh. Yahweh is the personal name that the one true God gave to the Israelites to call God. Use the same word or phrase for Yahweh as you used in previous passages. For more information on Yahweh, refer to the Master Glossary.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.
