title: Leviticus 23:9–14
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 23:9–14 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 23:9–14 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 23:9–14 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

At this time, the Israelite people are still camping near Mount Sinai. The Israelites have recently completed building the Tent of Meeting. Yahweh is giving Moses many instructions on how the Israelite people should live in a holy way. In this passage, Yahweh gives Moses instructions about the festivals that the Israelite people should celebrate. Yahweh tells Moses to give these instructions to the Israelite people. Yahweh is preparing the Israelites for what Yahweh expects from the Israelites when the Israelites enter Canaan.

Yahweh gives Moses instructions about how the Israelite people should offer the harvest offering. When the people start to live in the land of Canaan, the people will begin to grow their own crops, including grain. When the grain is ready, the Israelite people will cut down the grain to harvest it. Then the people will gather the grain, put the grain into bundles, and tie up each bundle into a sheaf. A sheaf is a bundle of something. So Yahweh calls these bundles "sheaves of grain."

Stop here as a group and look at pictures of barley and sheaves of barley. Pause this audio here.

Usually, the first grain that is ready for harvest is barley. The barley harvest happens right around the same time as Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread. Because of this, Yahweh instructs the Israelite people to bring the firstfruits offering or harvest offering at about the same time as these festivals. It is possible that the offerings that Yahweh talks about in this passage are the ones that Yahweh instructed the people to give in the last passage. In that passage, Yahweh told the Israelite people to offer fire offerings to Yahweh every day during the Festival of Unleavened Bread.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what is the most important harvest? How do people celebrate that harvest? Pause this audio here.

For the harvest offering, an Israelite must get a sheaf of grain. Again, this grain was probably barley, but the important thing is that it is the first grain crop that the person harvests. The Israelite brings the sheaf of grain to a priest near the Tent of Meeting. The priest then takes the sheaf of grain and moves the sheaf in a special way in front of the altar. We do not know exactly how the priest moves the sheaf, but we know the priest moves it in a special, ceremonial way. The priest may hold the sheaf in his hands, then raise and lower his arms a few times. In this way, the priest offers the sheaf to Yahweh. This is an example of a wave offering, which you heard about in previous passages.

Yahweh instructs the Israelites to bring the sheaf of grain for the offering on the day after the Sabbath. We are not sure which Sabbath Yahweh means here, since it can mean two different things. First, it can mean the day after the regular Sabbath. This would mean that once the Festival of Unleavened Bread begins, the first Sabbath would mark what day this is. Whenever that first Sabbath happened, the next day would be the day when the Israelite people brought the harvest offering. The second option is that this Sabbath refers to the special Sabbath which marks the first day of the Festival of Unleavened Bread. In that case, the people would bring the harvest offering on the second day of the Festival of Unleavened Bread. If possible, it is best to translate this in a way that it could mean either Sabbath.

When the Israelite brings the harvest offering, the Israelite also must bring a burnt offering. For this offering, a person brings a young male sheep.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of a young male sheep. Pause this audio here.

The Israelite person also needs to bring a grain or food offering to Yahweh. The Israelite must bring two-tenths of an ephah of flour for the grain offering. This is probably about 3 kilograms. This is twice the amount that Yahweh normally required for a grain offering. This flour was supposed to be the "finest" flour. This means that when a person grinds the grain, this is the grain that takes the longest time to grind. The Israelite people also consider the finest flour to be the best quality flour. To make the grain or food offering, the person mixes this flour with olive oil.

Stop here and discuss as a group: In your culture and language, what do you call something that is the best of its kind? Discuss what makes something high quality. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh also says that the grain offering is a pleasing aroma. Remember, we heard in an earlier passage that the priest takes a handful of the grain offering and burns it on the altar, so the "pleasing aroma" probably refers to the nice smell of the smoke when the priest burns the flour on the altar.

The Israelite person who offers the harvest offering, the burnt offering, and the grain offering must also give a drink offering. For the drink offering, the person offers one-quarter of a hin of wine. A hin may equal about 4 liters, so one-quarter of a hin is 1 liter.

This is an important offering for the Israelites, because the Israelites could not eat any of their new harvest that year until they had brought this offering to Yahweh. Yahweh reminds the Israelites that this is a statute that the Israelites should follow for all the generations in the future.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 23:9–14 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has two scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells Moses instructions about how the Israelite people should offer the harvest offering. The people must offer a bundle of grain as a wave offering, a young male sheep as a burnt offering, flour and olive oil mixed together as a grain offering, and wine as a drink offering.

In the second scene: Yahweh instructs that the people should give these offerings every harvest before the people eat any of their own harvest.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelite people
  • And a priest

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

The Israelite people are still camping in the wilderness near Mount Sinai. The Israelites have recently finished building the Tent of Meeting as Yahweh instructed. Yahweh is giving Moses instructions, which Moses then writes down and tells the Israelite people.

In the first scene, Yahweh gives Moses instructions about how the Israelite people should offer the harvest offering. Yahweh is preparing the Israelites for how the Israelites should live and honor Yahweh when the Israelites arrive in Canaan, the land Yahweh will give to the Israelites. Yahweh tells Moses to give these instructions about the harvest offering to the Israelite people. Usually, the first grain that is ready for harvest is barley. When the grain is ready, the Israelite people cut it down and gather it into bundles and tie it up into a sheaf. A sheaf is a bundle of something. So Yahweh calls these bundles of grain sheaves. Yahweh instructs the Israelite people to offer a sheaf of barley as a wave offering.

Stop here as a group and look at pictures of barley and sheaves of barley again as needed. Discuss what words you will use for "barley" and "sheaf." Pause this audio here.

The barley harvest happens around the same time as Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread. Because of this, the Israelite people must offer the firstfruits offering or harvest offering at or around the same time as these festivals. Some translations use the word "firstfruits" to talk about this offering, because the Israelite people offer the first and best of the crop to Yahweh for this offering. We will call this the harvest offering here, as a reminder that this is the offering that the Israelite people give at the beginning of harvest.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your language, what will you call this kind of offering? Pause this audio here.

For the harvest offering, an Israelite person gets a sheaf of grain and brings the sheaf to a priest near the Tent of Meeting. The priest takes the sheaf of grain and moves the sheaf in a special way in front of the altar. In this way, the priest offers the sheaf as a wave offering before Yahweh. "Before Yahweh" means "in the presence of Yahweh." The priest offers the sheaf "on behalf" of the Israelite person who brings the offering. This means that the priest offers the sacrifice, but Yahweh knows the offering is from the person who brought it.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your language, how have you translated the phrase for "wave offering"? Does the name for this offering describe what kind of ceremonial movement the priest makes? How are you going to describe the movement that the priest makes in this passage? How will you make it clear that the priest waves the offering in the presence of Yahweh? Pause this audio here.

The Israelite people bring the sheaf of grain for the wave offering on the day after the Sabbath. When an Israelite person brings the harvest offering, the Israelite must also bring a burnt offering. For this offering, a person brings a young male sheep. This sheep must be a year-old lamb that is physically perfect.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of a young male sheep, which people also call a lamb. Pause this audio here.

The Israelite person must also bring a grain offering, which is two-tenths of an ephah of flour. This is probably about 3 kilograms. This flour must be the "finest" flour. This means that when a person grinds the grain, this is the grain that takes the longest to grind. The Israelite people also consider the finest flour to be the best quality flour. The person mixes this flour with olive oil. In this passage, Yahweh refers to this grain offering as a food offering or fire offering for Yahweh. Many of the other people groups who did not worship Yahweh believed that their gods and goddesses actually ate the food that people offered to their gods. However, Yahweh does not actually eat the food. These offerings of food were just a way to honor Yahweh. Some translations call this kind of offering "an offering by fire" because the priest will take a handful of the grain offering and burn it on the altar. This makes a nice smell, so Yahweh says this grain offering is a pleasing aroma.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Why do you think Yahweh calls the grain offering an offering by fire? How have you heard this part of the passage before? Pause this audio here.

The Israelite person who offers the harvest offering and the burnt offering and the grain offering must also give a drink offering. For the drink offering, the person offers one-quarter of a hin of wine. A quarter of a hin would be about a liter of wine. So in all, the Israelite person would bring the harvest wave offering, the burnt offering, the grain offering, and the drink offering.

In the second scene, Yahweh instructs Moses that the people should not eat any of the new harvest until the people make the harvest offering. Yahweh says this is a statute for all future generations, which means it is a rule that will always be there.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 23:9–14 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has two scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelite people
  • And a priest

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

Yahweh tells Moses instructions on how the Israelite people should offer the harvest offering. The Israelites must bring four offerings. The people must offer a bundle of grain as a wave offering and a young male sheep as a burnt offering. The Israelites must mix flour and olive oil together and give the mixture to Yahweh as a grain offering. The Israelites must also give wine as a drink offering. Yahweh instructs that the people should do this every harvest before the people eat any of their own harvest.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the Israelite people, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I feel excited when I hear Yahweh speak about the harvest we will one day have. Yahweh does everything Yahweh says he will do, so we will surely have good land where we can grow a good harvest! or
  • It is strange to hear instructions about what to do when we have crops. We move from place to place and do not have time to grow crops. I will be so glad to live in one place and grow crops one day! I think it will be hard to give the first crops to Yahweh, because those first crops will be very special to me! or
  • I am thankful for the way Yahweh provides food for us as we travel. I will also be thankful when Yahweh causes our crops to grow in the future!

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am happy when the people remember to thank me for what I have given the Israelites; or
  • When the people obey me, I know that the people trust me. I want the Israelites to give these offerings to honor me and to remember that I provide for the Israelites; or
  • I hope that the people will not forget these instructions.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 23:9–14 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

In this passage, Yahweh gives Moses instructions about offering the harvest offering, which people also call the firstfruits offering. The Israelites will give this offering each year when the Israelites enter the land that Yahweh will give to the Israelites. Use the same words for Yahweh, Israelites, and firstfruits offering as you used in previous passages. For more information on Yahweh, Israelites, and "firstfruits offering," refer to the Master Glossary.

The Israelites would bring a sheaf of grain for the harvest offering. A sheaf is a bundle of something.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of sheaves of barley again as needed. Discuss how you will talk about a sheaf here. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh instructs the priest on how to offer the Israelites' harvest offering. The priest will wave the offering in Yahweh's presence. This is an example of a wave offering. Use the same word for priest as you used in previous passages. For more information on priest and wave offering, refer to the Master Glossary.

Stop here and discuss how you will translate the way that the priests wave the offering here. You look back to Leviticus 7, where you chose a phrase for "wave offering." You can either just describe the action here or give the name of the offering here. Pause this audio here.

The priest will wave this offering on the Sabbath. Every seventh day is a day of rest for the Israelite people. This is the Sabbath, the last day of the week. Use the same word for Sabbath as you used in previous passages. For more information on Sabbath, refer to the Master Glossary.

When the Israelite offers the harvest offering, the Israelite also needs to offer a burnt offering of a young male sheep. Use the same phrases for burnt offering and young male sheep as you used in previous passages. For more information on burnt offering, refer to the Master Glossary.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of a young male sheep again as needed. Pause this audio here.

The Israelite also needs to offer a grain offering with the harvest offering. Use the same phrase for grain offering as you used in previous passages. For more information on grain offering, refer to the Master Glossary.

The Israelite must bring two-tenths of an ephah of flour for the grain offering. An ephah is a unit of measurement. Two-tenths of an ephah may have been about 3 kilograms. Use the same word for ephah as you used in previous passages. For more information on ephah, refer to the Master Glossary.

In this passage, Yahweh calls the grain offering a food offering or an offering by fire. You will remember that these offerings of food were not food for Yahweh to eat, but rather a way to honor Yahweh. Some translations call this kind of offering "an offering by fire" because the priest burns part of the offering on the altar. The Israelite also offers a drink offering of wine. Use the same phrase for fire offering as you used in previous passages.

The Israelite must bring one-quarter of a hin of wine for the drink offering. A hin may equal about 4 liters, so one-quarter of a hin is 1 liter. Use the same word for hin as you used in previous passages, and refer to hin in the Master Glossary for more information.

For a drink offering, people brought a gift of wine, and the priest would pour the wine out over the altar to symbolically give it to Yahweh as an act of worship.

Stop here and discuss what word or phrase you will use for drink offering. For more information on drink offering, refer to the Master Glossary. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says this is a statute for all future generations. A statute is a rule that focuses specifically on the religious rules about how to celebrate festivals, perform religious rituals, and offer sacrifices of animals and grain. A generation is a group of people who are living at the same time and belong to about the same age group. Use the same words for statute and generations that you have used in previous passages. For more information on statute and generation, refer to the Master Glossary.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 23:15–22
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 23:15–22 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 23:15–22 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 23:15–22 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

At this time, the Israelite people are still camped near Mount Sinai. The Israelites had recently completed building the Tent of Meeting. Yahweh was giving Moses many instructions on how the Israelite people should live in a holy way. In this passage, Yahweh tells Moses about how the Israelite people should celebrate the harvest festival. In later years, the Israelite people will call this festival Pentecost. Pentecost will one day become an important day, not just for the Israelite people, but also for believers, as the day when the Holy Spirit first visited the people who followed Jesus.

For the first harvest offering in the last passage, Yahweh instructed each Israelite family to offer a sheaf of barley as a wave offering. In this passage, Yahweh tells the people what to do 50 days later. After 50 days, Yahweh wants the people to celebrate the harvest festival and to bring loaves of bread that the people made from the grain the Israelites had just harvested.

Stop here and look at a calendar that shows the day the Israelites would offer the sheaf of barley and, 50 days later, when the Israelites would celebrate the harvest festival. Pause this audio here.

Since this is the time of the wheat harvest, it is likely that most people bringing this offering would bring wheat for the end-of-harvest offering. The Israelite people are supposed to use two-tenths of an ephah of flour to make this bread. This is probably about 3 kilograms of flour. The people are supposed to make these loaves of bread with yeast. This is the only time of year when Yahweh commands the Israelite people to bring bread with yeast as an offering. The priest will take this grain offering and move it in a special way in front of the altar. In this way, the priest would offer the bread as a wave offering before Yahweh.

Stop here as a group and look at pictures of wheat and of bread that people made with yeast. Discuss: In your culture, what is the main food you eat every day? How is this main food similar or different from the Israelites' bread? Pause this audio here.

The Israelite people also must sacrifice 10 animals for burnt offerings, along with grain and drink offerings; a sin or purification offering; and a fellowship offering. You will notice that Yahweh requires a lot of sacrifices for this festival! Since it was the time of harvest, it was the time of year when the people had a lot of food. The harvest festival was a time for the Israelite people to thank Yahweh for providing the Israelites with enough food and to trust Yahweh to provide for the Israelites in the future.

Stop here and discuss: In your culture, how do people celebrate the harvest? What do people look forward to with the harvest? Pause this audio here.

In this passage, Yahweh instructs the people to sacrifice seven young male sheep, one young male bull, and two adult male sheep as burnt offerings.

Stop here as a group and look at pictures of young male sheep, a young male bull, and an adult male sheep. Pause this audio here.

The Israelites also need to present grain offerings and drink offerings along with the burnt offerings. We know from the last passage that the Israelite person who offers these offerings is also supposed to give a drink offering. For the drink offering, the person is to offer one-quarter of a hin of wine. It is possible that this would be about 1 liter of wine.

The priests also must offer the offerings that the Israelites bring. These offerings are a young male goat as a sin or purification offering and two more young sheep as a fellowship offering.

Stop here as a group and look at pictures of a young male goat and a young male sheep. Pause this audio here.

The priests must also offer the two young sheep that the Israelites bring for the fellowship offering as a wave offering for Yahweh. The priests are to do the wave offering of these two young male sheep along with the wave offering of the bread with yeast that the people had made for the end-of-harvest offering.

The Israelite people should not work on the day of the harvest festival. Instead, the Israelites should come together for a religious celebration. Yahweh calls this harvest festival a holy assembly.

Yahweh repeats instructions on how the Israelites should harvest. When the Israelite people harvest their crops, Yahweh wants the Israelites to leave some of the crops behind. The Israelites must not pick every single plant or take every single fruit or vegetable, but leave some, especially around the edges of the fields. Yahweh instructs the Israelites to do this so that the poor Israelite people and foreigners can have food to eat. Foreigners among the Israelites were any people who were not descendants of Israel.

Stop here and discuss: In your culture, how do people take care of and accept people from other languages and cultures, or people who look different?

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 23:15–22 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has three scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells Moses when the Israelites must celebrate the next festival. This festival is the harvest festival, which the Israelite people will, in later years, call Pentecost. For the harvest festival, the Israelite people need to bring grain that the Israelites had just harvested to offer to Yahweh.

In the second scene: Yahweh gives details of what offerings each Israelites family should bring for the harvest festival. The Israelite people should not work on the day of the harvest festival. Instead, the Israelites should come together for a religious celebration.

In the third scene: Yahweh repeats instructions on how to harvest. When the Israelite people harvest their crops, Yahweh says to leave some of the crops behind, so that poor people and people who are not Israelites can have food to eat.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelite people
  • An Israelite priest
  • A poor person
  • And a foreign person

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

Remember that Yahweh is giving Moses instructions that Moses then writes down and tells to the Israelite people. Remember that even though the storyteller does not mention Moses in this passage, we know from this chapter that Yahweh is telling Moses these instructions.

In the first scene, Yahweh tells Moses how to count days to see when the next festival will be. Yahweh tells Moses to count seven weeks or 50 days after the first harvest offering.

Stop here and look at a calendar that shows the day the Israelites would offer the sheaf of barley and, 50 days later, when the Israelites would celebrate the harvest festival. How do you count days and weeks? As an activity, count the days and weeks until one of your holidays. Then discuss how you want to translate the way that Yahweh tells Moses to count the days until the harvest festival. Pause this audio here.

For the first harvest offering, in the last passage, the Israelite people were supposed to bring a sheaf of grain to the Tent of Meeting. When the grain was ready, the Israelite people would cut down the grain, gather the grain into bundles, and tie up the bundles. A sheaf is a bundle of something that a person ties up. In the previous passage, Yahweh instructed the Israelite people to offer a sheaf of barley as a wave offering. Now, for this harvest festival, the Israelite people need to bring grain that the Israelites had just harvested to offer to Yahweh. This harvest festival happened at the end of the wheat harvest, so it is likely that most people who bring this offering would bring wheat for the end-of-harvest offering.

Stop here as a group and look at pictures of wheat and sheaves of grain. Discuss what you will call "wheat" and "sheaf." Pause this audio here.

Yahweh mentions the first harvest offering at the beginning of the passage. Be careful not to confuse the first harvest offering with the end-of-harvest festival, which people also called Pentecost.

Stop here and discuss: In your language, what will you call the harvest festival? How will you show the difference between the first harvest offering and the end-of-harvest offering? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh tells Moses to count seven weeks, or 50 days, after the first harvest offering to mark the day for the harvest festival. The Israelite people will one day call this festival "Pentecost."

In the second scene, Yahweh gives details of what offerings the Israelite people should bring for the end-of-harvest offering. For the harvest festival, Yahweh instructs Moses that the people should make two loaves of bread. The people are supposed to make these loaves of bread with yeast.

Stop here as a group and look at pictures of bread that people made with yeast. Discuss what you will call "bread with yeast" in your language. If possible, discuss the process people would use to make this kind of bread in your language. Pause this audio here.

The Israelite people must use two-tenths of an ephah of flour to make this bread. This is probably about 3 kilograms. The people make this bread from the grain the people had just harvested. The flour for this bread must be the "finest" flour. This means that when a person grinds the grain, this is the grain that takes the longest to grind. The Israelite people also considered the finest flour to be the best quality flour.

The priest takes this grain offering of the two loaves of bread and moves the offering in a special way in front of the altar. In this way, the priest would offer the bread as a wave offering before Yahweh.

The Israelite people also must kill ten animals for burnt offerings: seven young male sheep, one young male bull, and two adult male sheep.

Stop here and look at pictures of these animals. If necessary, go back and review the process of offering the burnt offering in Leviticus chapter 1 as a reminder of how the priest would offer these sacrifices. Pause this audio here.

The priests must offer the grain offerings and drink offerings that the Israelites bring at the same time as they offer the animals. Yahweh calls this an offering by fire. Yahweh also calls the offerings a pleasing aroma. This means that the offerings smell good to Yahweh. Remember, the priest takes a handful of the grain offering and burns it on the altar, so Yahweh also probably refers to the nice smell of the smoke when the priest burns the flour and the animals on the altar.

Stop here and, if necessary, go back to Leviticus chapter 2 and review the process for giving the grain offerings as a reminder of how the priest would offer these offerings. Pause this audio here.

The priests must offer the young male goat that the Israelites bring as a sin or purification offering and two more young sheep that the Israelites bring as a fellowship offering. The priests offer the two young sheep for the fellowship offering as a wave offering for Yahweh. The priests are to do the wave offering of the young male sheep along with the wave offering of the bread with yeast for the end-of-harvest offering. The priests will burn part of the fellowship offerings, then the priests may have some of the offering to eat.

Stop here and, if necessary, go back to Leviticus chapters 3 and 4 and review the process for giving the fellowship and purification offerings as a reminder of how the priest would offer these sacrifices. Pause this audio here.

The Israelite people should not work on the day of the harvest festival. Instead, the Israelites should come together for a religious celebration. Yahweh calls this harvest festival a holy assembly. The word for assembly means a request to meet together. Yahweh wants the Israelite people to come together as an entire nation to celebrate and worship Yahweh together. Just like Yahweh said for the harvest offering, Yahweh says this is a lasting statute, which means a rule that will never stop or go away, for every generation of Israelite people.

In the third scene, Yahweh repeats instructions from earlier about how to harvest. When the Israelite people harvest their crops, Yahweh commands the Israelites to leave some of the crops behind. The Israelite people must not pick every single plant or take every single fruit or vegetable. Instead, the Israelites need to leave some food and plants, especially around the edges of the fields. Yahweh instructs the Israelites to do this so that poor Israelite people and foreigners can have food to eat. A foreigner is any person who is not an Israelite, but lives among the Israelites.

Stop here and discuss: In your language, what do you call a person from another culture, language, or tribe? Discuss how you will translate this word as it refers to people who are not Israelite. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh finishes this instruction by repeating something Yahweh has said before. Yahweh often says in Leviticus, "I am Yahweh, your God." Yahweh wants the Israelite people to treat poor people and foreign people well because the way the Israelite people treat other people directly shows people who Yahweh is.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 23:15–22 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has three scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelite people
  • An Israelite priest
  • A poor person
  • And a foreign person

Note that even though the narrator does not mention Moses in this passage, we know from this chapter that Yahweh was telling Moses these instructions.

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

In the first scene, Yahweh tells Moses how to count the days until the next festival. Yahweh tells Moses to count seven weeks or 50 days after the first harvest offering. This festival is the harvest festival, which the Israelite people will one day call Pentecost. For the harvest festival, the Israelite people need to bring grain that the Israelites just harvested to offer to Yahweh.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Moses, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am happy that we will celebrate harvest; or
  • The Israelite people will learn to thank Yahweh at the beginning and the end of harvest. The Israelites will learn to see that every harvest is a gift from Yahweh; or
  • I wonder how we will offer all of these offerings in a bad year.
Continue the drama.

In the second scene, Yahweh gives details of what offerings the Israelite people should bring for the harvest festival. The Israelites are to bring two loaves of bread that have yeast. The Israelites also must kill ten animals for burnt offerings: seven young male sheep, one young male bull, and two adult male sheep. The priests must offer grain offerings and drink offerings at the same time as the animals. The priests also must sacrifice a young male goat as a purification offering and two more young sheep as a fellowship offering. For this ceremony, the priests also offer wave offerings of some of these sacrifices. The Israelite people should not work on the day of the harvest festival. Instead, the Israelites should come together for a religious celebration.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person or people playing the Israelite people, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person or people might answer things like:

  • We are excited for a break from work; or
  • I am thankful that Yahweh provided for us this year; or
  • For the harvest festival, we must sacrifice a lot of animals; or
  • Our religious ceremonies remind us of who Yahweh is and who we are.
Continue the drama.

In the third scene, Yahweh repeats instructions on how to harvest. When the Israelite people harvest their crops, Yahweh wants the Israelites to leave some of the crops behind, so that poor people and foreigners will have food to eat.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the poor person and the foreigner, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am thankful Yahweh remembered me; or
  • I am amazed that Yahweh provides even for people like me; or
  • I was hungry, but now I have plenty to eat.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 23:15–22 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

Yahweh instructs Moses how to count the days until the next festival, the harvest feast of Pentecost, will happen. To calculate it, Moses must count seven weeks from the day after the Sabbath, which was the day the Israelite people gave the first harvest offering. Use the same word for Sabbath as you used in previous passages. For more information on Sabbath, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh talks about many kinds of offerings in this passage. The priest is to give the harvest offering and the fellowship offering as a wave offering. Use the same phrase for wave offering as you used in previous passages. For more information on wave offering, refer to the Master Glossary.

For the Festival of Weeks, the priest offers another offering of new grain. Use the same phrase for offering as you used in previous passages. For more information on offering, refer to the Master Glossary.

The Israelites should bring two loaves of bread that someone made with two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour. Use the same word or phrase for ephah as you have used previously, and refer to ephah in the Master Glossary for more information.

The two loaves of bread will be a wave offering of firstfruits to Yahweh. Use the same word or phrase for firstfruits as you have used earlier, and refer to firstfruits in the Master Glossary for more information.

The priests must also offer many burnt offerings. Use the same phrase for burnt offering as you used in previous passages. For more information on burnt offering, refer to the Master Glossary.

The priest must also give a grain offering and drink offering, which together Yahweh calls a food offering, or a fire offering. Use the same phrases for grain offering, drink offering, and fire offering as you used in previous passages. For more information on grain offering, drink offering, and fire offering, refer to the Master Glossary.

Then the priest must offer a sin or purification offering and a fellowship offering. Use the same phrase for purification offering and fellowship offering as you used in previous passages. For more information on purification offering and fellowship offering, refer to the Master Glossary.

Use the same word or phrase for Yahweh as you used in previous passages. For more information on Yahweh, refer to the Master Glossary.

In this passage, the priest must sacrifice seven young male sheep for a burnt offering and two young sheep for a fellowship offering. Use the same word for young sheep as you used in previous passages.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of a young male sheep. Pause this audio here.

The priest must also sacrifice one young male bull as part of the burnt offering. Use the same word for young male bull as you used in previous passages.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of a young male bull. Pause this audio here.

For the burnt offering, the priest also must offer two adult male sheep. Use the same word for adult male sheep as you used in previous passages.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of an adult male sheep. Pause this audio here.

In this passage, the priest must also offer a young male goat as a purification offering. Use the same word for young male goat as you used in previous passages.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of a young male goat. Pause this audio here.

These offerings are holy to Yahweh. Use the same word for holy as you used in previous passages. For more information on holy, refer to the Master Glossary.

Use the same word for priest as you used in previous passages. For more information on priest, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh calls this harvest festival a sacred or holy assembly. Use the same phrase for holy assembly as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh says this is a statute for all future generations. A statute is an instruction or rule, especially about the place of worship. A generation is a group of people who are living at the same time and belong to about the same age group. Use the same words for statute and generations that you have used in previous passages. For more information on statute and generation, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh says to leave some of the crops in the fields for the poor people and for the foreigners who live with the Israelites. Use the same word for foreigner as you used in previous passages. For more information on foreigner, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh says, "I am Yahweh, your God." Use the same word for God as you used in previous passages. For more information on God, refer to the Master Glossary.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 23:23–32
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 23:23–32 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 23:23–32 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 23:23–32 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this passage, Yahweh continues to tell Moses the instructions for the yearly holidays and festivals. This passage focuses specifically on two festivals that happened during the last part of the harvest season for grapes and olives.

So Yahweh told Moses what to tell the people of Israel about how to celebrate the festival of loud noises. People today often call this festival the "Festival of Trumpets," which means the New Year.

Yahweh said that the celebration would happen on the first day of the seventh month. This would have happened around a harvest season. This usually happens during September or October. On that day, the people of Israel needed to rest and not do their normal work. This probably meant that the Israelites could do some kinds of work, but not do their normal jobs of farming, cleaning, or other kinds of hard work.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What kinds of normal work do people do everyday? How do people describe that kind of work? Pause this audio here.

The festival of loud noises, or Festival of Trumpets, was a day to remember, either what Yahweh has done, or to ask Yahweh to continue to remember and help the Israelites. Yahweh also says that the Israelites should gather together with loud noises. Most people translate the words "loud noises" as "the loud sound of trumpet music." If it was a trumpet, no one knows what kind of trumpet. It was most likely a trumpet that people made from a ram's horn. This kind of trumpet is a ram's horn trumpet. It could also have been a silver trumpet.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of a ram's horn trumpet and a silver trumpet. Pause this audio here.

So these words could mean that people were supposed to blow one of those two kinds of trumpets. However, these words could also mean that people were supposed to shout really loud. Elsewhere in the Bible, people use the words "loud noises" to talk about shouting to celebrate or to get people ready to go to war. Since this day was a holiday and a festival, it was some kind of loud noise that people made by shouting or blowing trumpets in order to celebrate the holiday.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What kinds of loud noises do you make to celebrate your holidays? Why do you make these noises? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh also said that this day, when people gather together, was "holy." This means that the day was special to Yahweh and that the people needed to treat the day with respect. Yahweh did not allow the people to do any of their normal kinds of work. Instead, the people were supposed to offer different kinds of sacrifices as a fire offering. You will remember that the fire offerings are often the offerings that the priests burn with fire to smell good to Yahweh. Another book of the Bible explains that the types of fire offerings the people were supposed to offer included burnt offerings, grain offerings to celebrate Yahweh as king, purification offerings, and drink offerings.

After Yahweh explained what the people needed to do during the festival of loud noises, Yahweh told Moses to tell the people of Israel what to do on the Day of Atonement. You will remember that atonement is the way to restore someone's relationship with God. The people needed to celebrate the Day of Atonement nine days after the people celebrated the festival of loud noises. So the people celebrated the Day of Atonement on the tenth day of the seventh month during the harvest season.

Yahweh said that this day was also a holy day for people to gather together. Once again, Yahweh called this day holy to show that it was special to Yahweh and that the people needed to treat the day with respect. The people needed to respect the Day of Atonement by not eating and drinking and by offering a variety of sacrifices as a gift of fire to smell good to Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: When are some times in your culture when you would choose not to eat or drink? Why do you do this? What are some other ways that you show that a holiday is very important? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh said that anyone who ate or drank on that day would be "cut off" from their people. No one knows exactly what these words "cut off" mean. It either meant that someone needed to kill the person who ate or drank something, or that that person who ate or drank something would not be one of Yahweh's people anymore.

The other way that people needed to respect the Day of Atonement was by not doing any work at all. This was because Yahweh chose the Day of Atonement to cleanse the people, the holy place, the bronze altar, and the priests from all the bad things that the people and priests did throughout the year. This day of cleansing also repaired the people's relationship with Yahweh, their God. The people needed to focus on Yahweh on this day, not on the work that the people needed to do.

Yahweh said that Yahweh would destroy anyone who worked on the Day of Atonement. This was a rule or statute that would last forever in each generation, no matter where the people of Israel lived. The Day of Atonement was a special day of rest when the people were supposed to deny themselves eating, drinking, and perhaps other things that were pleasurable.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 23:23–32 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has two scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh gave Moses instructions about what the people of Israel need to do for the festival of loud noises, or Festival of Trumpets.

In the second scene: Yahweh gave Moses further instructions about what the people of Israel need to do for the Day of Atonement.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • And the people of Israel

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

In the first scene, Yahweh talked to Moses and told Moses what to tell the people of Israel about how to celebrate the festival of loud noises. Yahweh did not actually call this festival "the festival of loud noises," or "the Festival of trumpets." Yahweh said it was a holy assembly, and a day of rest, that people remember because the people make a loud noise, or possibly trumpet blasts! This celebration would happen on the first day of the seventh month. This would have happened around one of the harvest seasons.

Stop here and discuss how people talk about times of the year. How do people talk about yearly festivals or holidays? How do people explain when those festivals or holidays are supposed to happen? Pause this audio here.

On that day, the people of Israel must rest and not do their normal work, just like the people do on the Sabbath rest days. This day was a day to remember. It is not clear what this "day to remember" is supposed to mean. Some people believe it was a day for the people of Israel to ask Yahweh to pay attention to the Israelites and continue to take care of the Israelites. However, it could also mean that the Israelites were supposed to pay attention to Yahweh and think about how Yahweh had been taking care of the Israelites.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What do you call a holiday where you remember something important? How will you translate "day of remembrance" here? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh also said that this "day to remember" is a day to remember with loud noises. Most people translate the words "loud noises" as "trumpets."

Yahweh also said that this day of people gathering together is a "holy assembly," where people gather together to worship Yahweh. This day was special to Yahweh, and the people needed to treat the day with respect. People must not do any of their normal work. Instead, the people were supposed to give an offering as a gift of fire to Yahweh. You will remember that the fire offerings, or food offerings, are often the offerings that the priests burn with fire to smell good to Yahweh. This kind of offering includes both burnt offerings and fellowship offerings. The people would have given these offerings at Yahweh's Tent of Meeting.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of the Tent of Meeting. Pause this audio here.

In the second scene, Yahweh told Moses to tell the people of Israel what to do on the Day of Atonement. You will remember that Yahweh had already talked about this festival, but this time Yahweh talked about two new pieces of information: the date and the punishments for people who disobey Yahweh. Yahweh repeated several times that the Israelites must not work on this festival day.

First, Yahweh explained when the people need to celebrate the Day of Atonement. Yahweh said the people must celebrate the Day of Atonement nine days after the people celebrate the festival of loud noises. So the people celebrated the Day of Atonement on the tenth day of the seventh month during the harvest season. For the people of Israel, the day began in the evening. So after the sun went down, it was a new day. That is why the Day of Atonement began in the evening when the ninth day ended, and it lasted until the next evening when the tenth day ended.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what marks the end of the old day and the beginning of the new day? How do you talk about something lasting a whole day? Pause this audio here.

Then Yahweh explained that the people need to deny themselves. Yahweh probably meant that the people must not eat or drink as a way to treat that day with respect. Some people think that this may mean that the people must not do anything that causes pleasure or makes people feel happy. Yahweh also said that the Israelites need to offer a variety of sacrifices as a fire offering to Yahweh.

Then Yahweh explained that the people must not do any work at all on the Day of Atonement since Yahweh chose the Day of Atonement to cleanse the people, the holy place, the bronze altar, and the priests from all the bad things that the people and priests did throughout the year. This day of cleansing also repaired the people's relationship with Yahweh, their God.

In the most important piece of information, Yahweh emphasized how serious the rules were by repeating the instructions three times not to work and to deny themselves. Yahweh also showed how serious these instructions were by explaining the punishment for people who do not do what Yahweh said. If a person ate or drank on that day, then the community would "cut off" that person from their people. These words "cut off" either meant that someone needed to kill that person or that that person would no longer be one of Yahweh's people anymore.

If someone worked on the Day of Atonement, then Yahweh would destroy the person who worked on that day because this was a day of Sabbath rest. This was a statute that would last forever in each generation, no matter where the people of Israel lived.

Stop and discuss among yourselves how best to show the way that Yahweh emphasizes these instructions for the Day of Atonement in your language. Pause this audio here.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 23:23–32 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has two scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • And the people of Israel

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

In the first scene, Yahweh talked to Moses and told Moses what to tell the people of Israel about how to celebrate the Festival of Trumpets. Yahweh said, "This festival will be on the first day of the seventh month. On that day, the people of Israel need to rest and not do their normal work. It is a day for you to remember. It is a day for you to make loud noises. It is a day when you gather together in a holy gathering to worship me, so people need to treat this day with respect. Do not do any normal work. Instead, give a food offering, or a gift of fire to me."

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the people of Israel, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am glad to take a break from work to celebrate; or
  • I am worried about taking a break during harvest time.
Continue the drama.

In the second scene, Yahweh told Moses to tell the people of Israel what to do on the Day of Atonement. Yahweh said, "The Day of Atonement will be on the tenth day of the seventh month. It is a day when you gather together in a holy gathering to worship me, and so people need to treat this day with respect. Do not eat or drink anything. Instead, give a food offering, or a gift of fire to me. And do not do any work at all on this day, because this is the day to make atonement for everyone and restore your relationship with me, Yahweh, your God."

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I want the people to understand how serious this atonement day is; or
  • I want my people to focus on me, not on everything else; or
  • I look forward to my people spending time with me.
Continue the drama.

Yahweh said, "If you eat or drink on that day, then you will no longer be one of my people anymore. If you work on this day, I will destroy you."

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the people of Israel, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I need to make sure I obey the rules for this day; or
  • I am afraid that I will do something wrong and die.
Continue the drama.

Yahweh said, "Do not do any kind of work at all on this day. This is an ongoing statute that will last in each generation, no matter where you live. This is a special day of rest for you, where you are not supposed to eat or drink.

"This day will begin in the evening when the sun goes down on the ninth day. It will last until the evening when the sun goes down on the tenth day. This is the special time to rest."

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 23:23–32 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

Yahweh gives instructions for the people of Israel about a festival that the Israelites will later call the Festival of Trumpets. Look up Yahweh, Festival of Trumpets, and Israelites in the Master Glossary. Use the same words or phrases for Yahweh and Israelites as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh said, "This festival will be on the first day of the seventh month. On that day, the people of Israel need to have a day of rest or a Sabbath and not do their normal work." Look up Sabbath in the Master Glossary. Use the same word or phrase for Sabbath as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh said, "This day is a day to remember." It is not clear what this "day to remember" is supposed to mean. Some people believe it was a day for the people of Israel to ask Yahweh to pay attention to the Israelites and continue to take care of the Israelites. However, it could also mean that the Israelites were supposed to pay attention to Yahweh and reflect on how Yahweh had been taking care of the Israelites.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for "day to remember." If you have already translated this phrase in another book of the Bible, decide if it is appropriate to use the same phrase that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh said this is a day of loud noises. The people would celebrate this festival with loud noises, which the people probably made with trumpets. So many people call this the "Festival of Trumpets." It is possible that the people also shouted.

Stop here as a group and look again at a picture of a shofar trumpet and a silver trumpet as needed. Discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for loud noises. Discuss also how you will talk about the name of this festival. If you have already translated this phrase in another book of the Bible, decide if it is appropriate to use the same phrase that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh said to have a holy assembly, or a special gathering where people worship Yahweh, so people need to treat this gathering with respect. Look up holy in the Master Glossary. Use the same word or phrase for holy assembly as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh said, "Do not do any normal work. Instead, you all need to offer me gifts that the priest will burn in the fire." Remember that this is a way to talk about all the different kinds of offerings that the Israelites can give to Yahweh. When the people burn these offerings, the aroma is pleasing to Yahweh, so sometimes people call these "food or fire offerings." Use the same word or phrase for fire or food offering as you used in previous passages.

Then Yahweh told Moses to tell the people of Israel what to do on the Day of Atonement. Yahweh said, "The Day of Atonement will be on the tenth day of the seventh month. Have a holy assembly and gather together to worship me." Look up Day of Atonement in the Master Glossary. Use the same word or phrase for "Day of Atonement" as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh said, "You need to fast and offer a gift of fire to smell good to me." To fast means not to eat or drink. Some translations say "deny or afflict yourselves." Look up fast in the Master Glossary. Use the same word or phrase for fast as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh said, "And do not do any work at all on this day, because the purpose of the Day of Atonement is to cleanse, or atone for, you all in the presence of me, Yahweh your God." Look up atonement and God in the Master Glossary. Use the same words or phrases for atone and God as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh said, "If you eat or drink on that day, then the community will cut you off from your people." This could either mean that someone would need to kill the person, or that the person would no longer be one of Yahweh's people, and the community would send this person away. Use the same word or phrase for cut off as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh said, "If you work on this day, I will destroy you." In this passage, this word "destroy" probably means that Yahweh would either kill that person or make it so that the person no longer belonged to Yahweh's people. Either way, it was a very serious punishment. The difference between this punishment and the punishment for eating or drinking is that Yahweh says Yahweh will personally punish the person who works on the Day of Atonement.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for destroy. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, decide if it is appropriate to use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh said, "Do not do any kind of work at all on this day. This is an ongoing statute that will last forever in each generation, no matter where you live." Look up statute and generation in the Master Glossary. Use the same words or phrases for statute and generation as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh said, "It is a special Sabbath, or day of rest for you, where you must not eat or drink. This day will begin in the evening when the sun goes down on the ninth day. It will last until the evening when the sun goes down on the tenth day. This is the special day of rest." Look up Sabbath in the Master Glossary. Use the same word or phrase for Sabbath as you used in previous passages.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.
