title: Leviticus 26:6–13
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 26:6–13 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:6–13 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:6–13 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In the last few sections of Leviticus, Yahweh gave Moses instructions for all the Israelites about how to live life the way Yahweh wanted. In the passage just before this, Yahweh told Moses a summary of Yahweh's instructions for how the Israelite people should live. Then Yahweh started to tell Moses what would happen to the Israelites if the Israelites obeyed Yahweh's instructions. If the Israelites follow Yahweh's instructions, then the Israelites will have healthy crops and all the food the Israelites need.

In this passage, Yahweh continues to tell Moses what will happen to the Israelite people if the Israelites follow Yahweh's instructions. It is important to notice that even though Yahweh does not mention in this passage that these good things will only happen if the Israelites obey Yahweh's instructions, this passage and the previous passage are closely related. In the previous passage, Yahweh said that if the Israelites obey Yahweh's commands, then Yahweh will cause good things to happen to the Israelites. In this passage, Yahweh talks about more of the good things that will happen to the Israelites if the Israelites obey Yahweh's commands.

So Yahweh will give the Israelites peace in the land only if the Israelites follow Yahweh's instructions. The word from the original language for peace means a lot more than just not having war in your land. It also means that people will live in harmony with others, with nature, and with God, and that the people will have what people need to be truly well.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What are some things that people in your culture need to experience for your community to be truly well and peaceful? Pause this audio here.

The Israelite people will experience this good and peaceful life in the land of Canaan that God is leading the Israelites to. The Israelites will settle in Canaan after Moses dies, and the Israelites will call the land Israel. As part of this peaceful life in Canaan, Yahweh says that the Israelite people will lie down and nothing will make the people afraid. Yahweh means that the Israelites will be able to lie down and go to sleep easily because the Israelites will not need to be afraid of anything. Yahweh also tells Moses that Yahweh will remove wild animals from the land. Yahweh is not talking about harmless animals that are not on farms or that do not belong to people. Instead, Yahweh is talking about dangerous wild animals that might harm people. Yahweh also says that the sword will not go through the land. The sword represents war in general. Enemies will not attack and fight wars with the Israelites in the Israelites' land if the Israelites obey Yahweh's instructions.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What kinds of dangerous animals are in your area? Pause this audio here.

But Yahweh says the Israelites will be successful when the Israelites go to war and attack their enemies. The Israelites will chase their enemies, which means that the Israelites will win battles and then chase away their enemies. When the Israelites do this, their enemies will die by the sword in front of the Israelites. This is just a way to say that the Israelites will use swords and likely other weapons to kill their enemies in war. Swords were the main weapon in the Israelites' culture, and swords often represent weapons in general. Sometimes, only the Israelite leaders would have swords, but since swords represent all kinds of weapons, Yahweh is just saying that Israelite warriors will kill their enemies. The Israelites will be successful against armies that are much bigger than the Israelites' army. Yahweh says that 5 Israelites will chase 100 enemy soldiers, and 100 Israelites will chase 10,000 enemy soldiers, so clearly the Israelites will be much stronger than their enemies. And then Yahweh says again that the Israelites will kill their enemies.

If the Israelites obey Yahweh's instructions, Yahweh next says that Yahweh will turn towards the Israelites. This is special language that means that Yahweh will pay attention to the Israelites and be kind to the Israelites. Then Yahweh gives the Israelites the same blessing that Yahweh gave all humans after Yahweh created people. Yahweh will make the Israelites fruitful and multiply the Israelites, which means that the Israelites will have children, so there will be more and more Israelite people. Yahweh then says that Yahweh will fulfill Yahweh's covenant with the Israelites. Yahweh will do what Yahweh agreed to do in the covenant or binding agreement Yahweh made with the Israelites. Now, Yahweh is still in the process of making a binding agreement with the people of Israel at Mount Sinai, so Yahweh is probably not talking about that covenant. Instead, Yahweh is probably talking about the covenant Yahweh made with the Israelites' ancestor Abraham. Yahweh promised Abraham in Genesis 17 that Abraham would have many descendants and that Yahweh would keep confirming this agreement with Abraham's descendants, the Israelites.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Think of three situations where people in your culture might make a covenant, a binding agreement, or a special promise with each other. When would someone renew or confirm a covenant, binding agreement, or special promise that the person made in the past? Pause this audio here.

Next, Yahweh promises that if the Israelites obey Yahweh's instructions, the Israelites will be able to grow so much food that the Israelites will be able to live on that food for a long time. In fact, the Israelites will have to get rid of some of the food from last year's harvest so that the people can make room for all the food from this year's harvest! This does not mean that the Israelites will waste a lot of food. It just means that the Israelites will never have to go without food because the Israelites will always have enough.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: How would you or other people in your culture talk about a peaceful land where everything is good? What kinds of things would happen there? What kinds of things would not happen there? Pause this audio here.

Next, Yahweh makes the most important promise of all to the Israelites. If the Israelites obey Yahweh's instructions, Yahweh will live with the Israelites in Yahweh's tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting, and Yahweh will not reject the Israelites. Yahweh says that Yahweh will walk with the Israelite people. Now, Yahweh does not mean that Yahweh will literally walk with the Israelites as a physical person. Yahweh is using special language to say that Yahweh will live with and be present with the Israelite people. Yahweh says that Yahweh will be with the Israelites in multiple ways to emphasize that Yahweh will always accept the Israelites and be with the Israelites. Yahweh then tells the Israelites that Yahweh will be their God and the Israelites will be Yahweh's people.

To reassure the Israelites that Yahweh will certainly do all of these wonderful things, Yahweh reminds the Israelites who Yahweh is and what Yahweh has done before. Yahweh says that he is Yahweh, their God, and that Yahweh rescued the Israelites from Egypt so that the Israelites would not be slaves anymore. Next, Yahweh says that Yahweh broke the bars of the Israelites' yoke so that the Israelites could stand up straight. A yoke is a wooden bar or beam that you put across the backs of two farm animals so that the animals can pull the same load together. People could attach the yoke to a cart to carry things or to several kinds of farm tools.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of animals wearing a yoke. Now look at a picture of a person wearing a yoke. Pause this audio here.

In the culture of the people who wrote the Bible, people sometimes put a yoke on people who were slaves to humiliate the slaves. Because slaves sometimes used yokes to carry heavy objects, people sometimes talk about yokes to represent slavery. Yahweh also talks about the way that people without heavy loads can stand up straight to represent the Israelites being free people. When Yahweh freed the Israelite people from slavery so the Israelites could live as free people, it was like Yahweh took a heavy load off the Israelites' backs so the Israelites could stand up straight again.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:6–13 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has three scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh continues to tell Moses what will happen to the Israelites if the people obey Yahweh. The Israelites will have peace in their land and be successful in war.

In the second scene: Yahweh says that Yahweh will also bless the Israelites with children and with the food that the Israelites need.

In the third scene: Yahweh says that Yahweh himself will also come live with the Israelites and be their God.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelite people
  • And enemy soldiers

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

Yahweh is still talking to Moses from Mount Sinai and giving Moses instructions about how the Israelite people should live. In the passage before this, Yahweh explained that if the Israelites obey Yahweh's instructions, then all the good things that Yahweh says in this passage will happen to the Israelites.

Stop here and discuss this as a group: Imagine that you tell your child to do something, and you explain all the things that will happen if your child obeys your instructions. How do you let your child know that all of these things will only happen if your child obeys your instructions, but these things will not happen if your child disobeys your instructions? Pause this audio here.

In this passage, Yahweh continues to talk about the good things that will happen if the Israelites obey Yahweh's instructions. In the first scene, Yahweh tells Moses that the Israelites will experience peace and wellness in the land Yahweh is leading the Israelites to. The Israelites will not fear anybody or anything. Yahweh says that the Israelites will lie down to sleep because the Israelites will not be afraid.

Stop here and discuss this as a group: What are some ways you can describe someone who is not afraid? How does that person feel? What does that person do? Pause this audio here.

The Israelites will not have dangerous animals or war in their land. And when the Israelites go to war, the Israelites will be very successful even when their enemies have much bigger armies. Just a few Israelite soldiers will be able to chase off many enemy soldiers, and the Israelites will be able to kill the enemy soldiers. Yahweh uses special language to talk about this. Yahweh says that the sword will not pass through the Israelites' land, and later, Yahweh says that the enemy soldiers will fall by the sword. Swords represent weapons and war in general, so Yahweh is saying that there will not be war in the Israelites' land and that the Israelites will kill their enemies with weapons.

Stop here and discuss this as a group: How do you want to translate the special language about swords? As you think through this, consider these questions: How do people in your community talk about war in general? How do people in your community talk about weapons in general? Pause this audio here.

In the second scene, Yahweh promises that Yahweh will pay attention to the Israelite people and be kind to the Israelites. Yahweh promises to make the Israelites fruitful and cause the Israelites to multiply. This is the same blessing that Yahweh gave after Yahweh created people, and it is special language that means that the Israelites will be able to have children so that their community will grow larger.

Stop here and do this exercise as a group: If you have translated Genesis 1:28, then listen to your translation of this blessing. If you have not translated Genesis 1:28, listen to the blessing in the easiest-to-understand translation. Now decide how you will translate this blessing in this passage. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh will make the Israelites' crops so successful that the Israelites will be able to store food to eat for a long time, but the Israelites will not have to use all the food because there will be so much food in the new harvest.

In the third scene, Yahweh tells Moses about the most important good things that will happen if the Israelite people obey Yahweh's instructions. Yahweh will live with the Israelites in the Tent of Meeting, which people also called the tabernacle. Yahweh will accept the Israelites and care for the Israelites. Yahweh will walk with the Israelites, meaning that Yahweh will be present with the Israelites. Yahweh and the Israelite people will belong to each other. Yahweh will be the Israelites' God, and the Israelites will be Yahweh's people.

Stop here and discuss this as a group: How would people in your community talk about the way a god is present with people? Yahweh says that Yahweh will be with the Israelites just like you would be with someone who walks with you. Discuss how you want to translate the way Yahweh says this. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh reminds the Israelite people of how Yahweh rescued the Israelites to show that Yahweh actually can do all the good things Yahweh promises. Yahweh also wants to remind the Israelites that Yahweh has already chosen the Israelites to be Yahweh's special people. Earlier, Yahweh rescued the Israelites from being slaves in Egypt. When Yahweh freed the Israelites from slavery, it was like Yahweh took a heavy wooden beam off the Israelites' backs so the Israelites could stand up straight.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: How do people in your community talk about slavery? What kinds of words do people use to represent slavery? How do people describe someone who is free and not a slave? Discuss how you want to translate how Yahweh talks about the Israelites being slaves and then free people. Pause this audio here.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:6–13 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has three scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelite people
  • And enemy soldiers

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

For the first scene, have the person playing Yahweh tell the person playing Moses that things will happen to the Israelites if the Israelites obey Yahweh's instructions.

Say that the Israelites will experience peace and wellness in the land that Yahweh is leading the Israelites to. The Israelites will not have to be afraid of anybody or anything. The Israelites will not have dangerous animals or war in their land. And when the Israelites go to war, the Israelites will be very successful, even when their enemies have much bigger armies. Just a few Israelite soldiers will be able to chase off many enemy soldiers, and the Israelites will be able to kill those enemy soldiers.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the Israelite people, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am feeling relieved that nothing and no one will attack us when we get to our new land; or
  • I am excited that we will be able to fight our enemies and win; or
  • I am impressed that we will not have to deal with dangerous animals in our land.
Continue the drama.

In the second scene, have the person playing Yahweh tell the person playing Moses that Yahweh promises to pay attention to the Israelite people and be kind to the Israelites. Yahweh will make the Israelites able to have children so that their community will grow larger. Yahweh will make their crops so successful that the Israelites will be able to store food to eat for a long time. However, the Israelites will not have to use that food because there will be so much food in the new harvest.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Moses, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am so glad that Yahweh is going to take care of the people I have been leading; or
  • I am amazed that Yahweh will give us so much when we get to the land Yahweh is taking us to; or
  • I wonder if the people will actually follow Yahweh's instructions. The people have complained a lot so far.
Continue the drama.

In the third scene, have the person playing Yahweh tell the person playing Moses about the most important good things that will happen if the Israelite people obey Yahweh's instructions. Yahweh will live with the Israelites in the Tent of Meeting, which people call the tabernacle, and Yahweh will accept the Israelites and care for the Israelites. Yahweh will walk with the Israelites, meaning that Yahweh will be present with the Israelites. Yahweh and the Israelite people will belong to each other. Yahweh will be the Israelites' God, and the Israelites will be Yahweh's people.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am happy to be close to my people because I love my people; or
  • I love my people so much that I am willing to live with them even though the people sin sometimes; or
  • I want my people to follow my instructions so that our relationship can be good.
Continue the drama.

Then have the person playing Yahweh remind Moses and the Israelite people of what Yahweh did for the Israelites before. Have the person playing Yahweh say that Yahweh rescued the Israelites from being slaves in Egypt. When Yahweh freed the Israelites from slavery to be free people, it was like Yahweh took a heavy wooden beam off the Israelites' backs so they could stand up straight.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the Israelite people, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am feeling confident that Yahweh will do these good things for us because Yahweh took care of us before; or
  • I am feeling relieved because I remember how it felt when Yahweh rescued us from being slaves; or
  • I can trust Yahweh because Yahweh took care of us before.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:6–13 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

In the previous passage and in this passage, Yahweh tells Moses what will happen to the Israelite people if the Israelites follow Yahweh's instructions. For more information on Yahweh and Israelite, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same words or phrases for Yahweh and Israelite as you used in previous passages.

If the Israelite people follow Yahweh's instructions, Yahweh will give the Israelites peace in their land.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for peace. Look up peace in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that the people of Israel will kill their enemies with swords. A sword is a weapon that people make with metal. A sword is long and sharp, and people hold onto a sword using a handle. Use the same word or phrase for swords as you have used in previous books of the Bible.

Stop here and look at a picture of a sword. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh next says that Yahweh will pay attention to the Israelite people and be kind to the Israelites. Yahweh will make the Israelites able to have children, so there will be more Israelite people. Yahweh will fulfill his covenant or binding agreement with the Israelites. This covenant is probably talking about the Israelites being able to have many children and become more numerous, since that was the covenant Yahweh made with their ancestor Abraham in the story of Genesis. For more information on covenant, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same word or phrase for covenant as you used in previous passages.

The Israelites will be able to grow so much food that the Israelites will be able to live on that food for a long time. The Israelites will have to get rid of some of the food from last year's harvest to make room for all the food from this year's harvest. Yahweh will live with the people in his tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting. Yahweh says that Yahweh will put the place that Yahweh lives in the middle of the Israelites. This emphasizes that Yahweh is choosing to live among the Israelites. The place where Yahweh lives is the tabernacle, the Tent of Meeting. For more information on tabernacle, refer to the Master Glossary. You may use your word or phrase for tabernacle here, or you may simply say "the place where Yahweh lives." If you use your word for tabernacle, use the same word or phrase for tabernacle as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh will walk with the people. Yahweh will be the Israelites' God, and the Israelites will be Yahweh's people. They will belong to each other. For more information on God, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same word or phrase for God as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh also says that he is Yahweh their God and that Yahweh rescued the Israelites from Egypt so that the Israelites would not be slaves anymore. For more information on slave, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same word or phrase for slave as you used in previous passages.

Next, Yahweh says that he broke the bars of the Israelites' yoke so that the Israelites could stand up straight. Remember that what Yahweh says about the yoke is special language. The yoke symbolizes slavery, and standing up straight symbolizes freedom. When Yahweh freed the Israelite people from slavery so the Israelites could live as free people, it was like Yahweh took a heavy beam off their backs so the Israelites could stand up straight again.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for yoke. Look up yoke in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 26:10–46
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 26:40–46 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:40–46 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:40–46 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

Over the last few passages, Yahweh has explained what will happen to the Israelites if the Israelites disobey Yahweh and do not return to obeying Yahweh after Yahweh punishes the Israelites. Now, Yahweh gives the Israelite people hope. Even after all these horrible punishments, Yahweh will still accept the Israelites back if the Israelites turn back to Yahweh.

Yahweh will remember the covenant Yahweh made with the Israelites' ancestors if the Israelites admit their iniquity and their ancestors' iniquities, or sins through the years. The Israelites must admit how the Israelites and their ancestors disobeyed Yahweh. When the Israelites betrayed and opposed Yahweh, it caused Yahweh to oppose the Israelites and send the Israelites to live in their enemies' land. But if the Israelites admit that the Israelites betrayed and opposed Yahweh, Yahweh will remember his covenant with the Israelites' ancestors.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Tell a story about a time when your community agreed together and admitted that they or their ancestors acted in a bad way. How did the community do this? How did the community show the people were sorry? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that Yahweh will remember Yahweh's covenant with the Israelites' ancestors when the Israelites humble their uncircumcised hearts. Now, no one can actually circumcise a heart, since circumcision is when someone cuts the foreskin off a penis. The Israelites circumcised their boys and men as a way to obey Yahweh and show that the Israelites were Yahweh's people. People started to call things "uncircumcised" as a way to talk about things or people that did not specially belong to Yahweh. Uncircumcised things were things that were wrong or ritually dirty. In this case, when Yahweh says that the Israelites' hearts are uncircumcised, Yahweh means that the Israelite people are stubbornly opposed to Yahweh instead of dedicating themselves to Yahweh. So if the Israelites stop stubbornly opposing Yahweh and humble themselves, Yahweh will remember his covenant with the Israelites' ancestors. Yahweh also says that Yahweh will remember his covenant with the Israelites' ancestors when the Israelites pay for their iniquity, when Yahweh punishes the Israelites.

And when the Israelites do all these things to turn back to Yahweh, Yahweh will remember his covenants with Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham. Yahweh will never forget the agreement Yahweh made with those men. In the story of Genesis, Yahweh promised Abraham that Abraham would have many descendants and Yahweh would give those descendants the land that would become Israel. Then, Yahweh made the same promise to Abraham's son, Isaac, and Isaac's son, Jacob. So when the Israelite people turn back to Yahweh, Yahweh will continue to keep Yahweh's covenant with the Israelites' ancestors and give the Israelites their land.

Yahweh also says that Yahweh will not forget the land. When Yahweh punishes the Israelites, the Israelites will leave the land so the land can rest and experience the Sabbath years of rest Yahweh planned for the land.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how long can agreements last? What kinds of covenants or agreements can people make with one another that they will still keep with their children or their other descendants? Pause this audio here.

The Israelites will have to make amends for rejecting and hating Yahweh's instructions and commandments. Even though the Israelites have rejected and hated Yahweh, Yahweh promises that Yahweh will not completely reject or hate the Israelites. Even though the Israelites will have to go to their enemies' land, Yahweh will not completely destroy the Israelites or break his covenant with the people. Yahweh reminds the Israelites that Yahweh is the Israelites' God, so the Israelites and Yahweh belong to each other.

Yahweh ends by saying that Yahweh will not forget the covenant Yahweh made with the Israelites' ancestors. This time, Yahweh is not just talking about Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, though. Yahweh says that Yahweh will not forget the covenant Yahweh has made with the Israelites whom Yahweh rescued from slavery in Egypt. People from other nations saw what Yahweh did, and Yahweh rescued the Israelites so that Yahweh would be the Israelites' God and the Israelites would belong to Yahweh. While Yahweh is currently talking to the Israelites whom Yahweh rescued from Egypt, Yahweh's instructions will also be for the Israelites' descendants. If, in the future, the Israelites' descendants admit their sin and guilt, Yahweh will keep the agreement that Yahweh made with those descendants' ancestors. The ancestors are the Israelites that Yahweh is talking to now. Yahweh then reminds the Israelites that he is Yahweh, which is the name Yahweh used to introduce himself to Moses when Moses chose to obey Yahweh as Yahweh rescued the Israelites.

Finally, the storyteller of Leviticus says that these are the statutes, ordinances, and laws that Yahweh included in the agreement between himself and the Israelite people. Some people think that the storyteller is talking about everything that has happened in the whole story of Leviticus up until now. However, it is more likely that the storyteller is talking about all the instructions that Yahweh told the Israelites, starting in Leviticus chapter 17 and ending in Leviticus chapter 25. Yahweh gives these instructions to Moses on Mount Sinai. Then, Moses will tell these instructions to the Israelites.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:40–46 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has four scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh explains that if the Israelites admit their iniquity, Yahweh will keep his covenant with the Israelites' ancestors.

In the second scene: Yahweh explains why the Israelites will not stay in their land, even though Yahweh promised the land to the Israelites' ancestors.

In the third scene: Yahweh explains that Yahweh will not forget his agreement with the Israelite people.

In the fourth scene: This is the end of the large section of Leviticus where Yahweh is telling the Israelite people how to live a holy life and obey Yahweh.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses, who is probably the storyteller of Leviticus
  • The Israelite people
  • The Israelites' ancestors, including Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
  • And people from other nations

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

Yahweh is still talking to Moses on Mount Sinai, and Yahweh has been telling Moses what will happen to the Israelites when Yahweh finally punishes the Israelites severely. Part of this is that Yahweh will force the Israelites out of their land to live as exiles in their enemies' lands. The Israelites will have horrible lives in the enemies' lands.

Now, in the first scene of this passage, Yahweh explains how Yahweh will react if the Israelites confess their sin and finish paying the price for their sin by experiencing punishment from Yahweh. First, the Israelites must admit that they and their ancestors sinned. The Israelites must admit that the Israelites and their ancestors betrayed Yahweh and walked in opposition to Yahweh. When Yahweh says that the Israelites walked in opposition to Yahweh, Yahweh uses special language that means that the Israelites lived their lives in such a way that the Israelites opposed Yahweh.

Stop here and remember as a group how, in previous passages, you translated the idea of "walking" as a way to talk about how people obeyed or followed Yahweh. Pause this audio here.

Because the Israelites opposed Yahweh, Yahweh opposed the Israelites and removed the Israelites from their land. Yahweh sent the Israelites to live in their enemies' land. The Israelites must be humble and dedicate themselves to Yahweh again. Yahweh says that the Israelites must humble their uncircumcised hearts. People circumcised Israelite boys and men to show that those boys and men obeyed Yahweh. When people talked about uncircumcised things, people meant that those things were wrong or ritually dirty. The heart represents a person's thoughts and emotions. If the heart is ritually dirty, it means that the person no longer wants to follow Yahweh. Here, Yahweh says that the Israelites' hearts are ritually dirty, so the Israelites need to dedicate themselves to Yahweh again.

Stop here and discuss this as a group: How will you translate the idea of uncircumcised hearts? Pause this audio here.

The Israelites must pay for not obeying Yahweh's instructions, which made the Israelites guilty. Yahweh must punish the Israelites so that the Israelites pay the price for what the Israelites did to become guilty.

Stop here and discuss this as a group: How will you translate the idea of paying for iniquity? In this context, iniquity refers to the wrong things people did that made the people guilty. When the Israelites pay for their guilty actions, the Israelites have to submit to Yahweh's punishment. How can you talk about this in your language? Pause this audio here.

If the Israelites pay for the wrong things the Israelites have done, then Yahweh will fulfill his covenant or keep his agreement that Yahweh made with the Israelites' ancestors, including Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Yahweh talks about the covenant with Abraham, the covenant with Isaac, and the covenant with Jacob, but Yahweh does not mean there are three covenants. Yahweh made one covenant with Abraham, and Yahweh kept the same agreement with Isaac and Jacob. In the original language, when Yahweh says that Yahweh will remember his covenant, Yahweh does not mean that Yahweh ever forgot the covenant. Yahweh just wants to emphasize that Yahweh will never forget it. So Yahweh will never forget the agreement Yahweh made with the Israelites' ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

Yahweh will also remember his agreement with the Israelites' ancestors about the land. Much earlier, Yahweh had promised the Israelites' ancestors that they would have many descendants and that those descendants would live in the land of Israel. So Yahweh probably means that Yahweh will then bring the Israelites back to their land and cause the Israelites to have many descendants again.

In the second scene, Yahweh then explains why the Israelites would not stay in their land as Yahweh had promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Yahweh would cause the Israelites to leave because the land needs rest, and the Israelites need to pay for their guilt. The Israelites will spend many years in the land of their enemies. While the Israelites are there, the Israelites will pay for the way the Israelites rejected and hated Yahweh's instructions and commandments. At the same time, while the Israelites are in other countries, the land of Israel will be empty. The land will finally experience the Sabbath years of rest that the Israelites did not give the land. You will remember that Yahweh says the land will enjoy its rest at this time.

Stop here and discuss this as a group: How will you talk about the land enjoying rest in your translation? How can you talk about land doing something that normally only a person would do? If you cannot do this in your language, how can you talk about Yahweh giving the land time to rest? Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss this as a group: Start telling a story about your family, with you as the main character. At some point, pause the story and explain something that your parents or grandparents did that affects your story. Pay attention to how you talk about things that happened before the story. Pause this audio here.

In the third scene, Yahweh emphasizes that although Yahweh will punish the Israelites because of their sin, Yahweh will not break his covenant. Even while the Israelites are in enemy lands because the Israelites hated and rejected Yahweh, Yahweh will not hate the Israelites or reject the Israelites so completely that Yahweh destroys all the Israelites. Yahweh does not want to break Yahweh's agreement with the Israelites. Yahweh is still the Israelites' God, even when the Israelites have rejected Yahweh and Yahweh is punishing the Israelites. Because Yahweh cares about the Israelites, Yahweh will remember the covenant that Yahweh is currently making with the Israelite people who are with Moses at Mount Sinai. These are the people that Yahweh rescued from slavery in Egypt. Yahweh rescued the Israelites so that Yahweh could be the Israelites' God, and Yahweh rescued the Israelites to show the other nations how powerful Yahweh is.

Stop here and discuss this as a group: Imagine you are telling a story from your life about something that happened to you while you were away from home. At the same time, something happened to your family at home. How would you talk about what happened to you? How would you talk about what happened to your family? Pay attention to how you talk about things that happen at different places at the same time. Pause this audio here.

The fourth scene is what the storyteller of Leviticus says at the end of a long section. Since chapter 17 of Leviticus, Yahweh has been telling Moses what the Israelites should do to obey Yahweh and live holy lives. Now, the storyteller lets us listeners know that this section is over. The storyteller says that all these passages that have come before this are the statutes and ordinances and instructions or laws that Yahweh gave Moses when Yahweh met with Moses on Mount Sinai to make a covenant or agreement with the people of Israel.

Stop here and discuss this as a group: When you explain something like an agreement or some long instructions to a group of people, how do you show that you have finished? How would you remind the people of the main point of everything you have said? Pause this audio here.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:40–46 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has four scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses, who is probably the storyteller of Leviticus
  • The Israelite people
  • Their ancestors, including Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
  • And people from other nations

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

Before this passage, Yahweh made a covenant with the Israelites' ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Yahweh has punished the Israelite people by forcing the Israelites to leave their land.

Then, in the first scene of this passage, have the person playing Yahweh explain to the person playing Moses how Yahweh will react if the Israelites confess their sins. First, Yahweh says the Israelites should admit that the Israelites and their ancestors have sinned, betrayed Yahweh, and opposed Yahweh, so have the person playing the Israelites do that. Then Yahweh explains that because the Israelites disobeyed Yahweh, Yahweh opposed the Israelites and removed the Israelites from their land to send the Israelites to live in their enemies' land. Yahweh also explains that the Israelites must be humble and dedicate themselves to Yahweh again, and the Israelites must pay for not obeying Yahweh's instructions, which made the Israelites guilty. Then Yahweh says that when the Israelites do these things, Yahweh will respond and remember Yahweh's covenant or keep his agreement that Yahweh made with the Israelites' ancestors, including Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Have the person playing Yahweh act out bringing the person playing the Israelites back to their land.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am so sorry that we disobeyed Yahweh! or
  • Wow, Yahweh is very good! We do not deserve for Yahweh to still keep his covenant with us, but Yahweh will still do it! or
  • I just want to go back to my land. I am sorry for everything that I and my ancestors did that caused us to have to leave our land.
Continue the drama.

For the second scene of this passage, have the person playing Yahweh tell the person playing Moses that Yahweh will not forget the land. While the Israelites are outside the land of Israel, the land will be empty and will experience the Sabbath years of rest that the Israelites did not give the land. At the same time the Israelites will have to make amends for the wrong things the Israelites did because the Israelites rejected and hated Yahweh's instructions and commandments.

For the third scene, have the person playing Yahweh explain the following things to the person playing Moses. Yahweh says that even though the Israelites will be living in their enemies' land, and even though the Israelites have rejected and hated Yahweh's commands, Yahweh will not hate the Israelites or reject the Israelites so completely that Yahweh destroys all of the Israelites or breaks his agreement with the Israelites. Yahweh says that Yahweh is still the Israelites' God and Yahweh will remember the covenant that Yahweh made with the Israelites' ancestors.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am sad that my people rejected and hated my commands. I only want what is best for my people! or
  • I love my people so much that I will not reject them even though my people rejected me; or
  • I remember the covenant that I made with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and I am committed to keeping this covenant even when it is hard.
Continue the drama.

Because this happens in the future, the ancestors that Yahweh talks about are the people of Israel that are with Moses at Mount Sinai. Have the person playing Moses remind the person playing the Israelite people that Yahweh rescued the Israelites from slavery in Egypt. Have the person playing Moses remind the Israelites that people from all the other nations saw what Yahweh did. Yahweh rescued the Israelites so that Yahweh could be the Israelites' God and the Israelites could be Yahweh's people.

The fourth scene is how the storyteller summarizes this section of Leviticus. Have the person playing the storyteller say that all these things in the previous passages of Leviticus are Yahweh's statutes and ordinances and instructions or laws. Yahweh gave all these instructions to Moses when Yahweh met with Moses on Mount Sinai. At that time, Yahweh made a covenant or agreement with the people of Israel.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am glad that Yahweh made a covenant with us. That is a great honor; or
  • I am nervous about these instructions. These instructions are very important, and it seems hard to obey all the instructions; or
  • I am so glad that Yahweh gives us clear instructions so we do not have to wonder what Yahweh wants.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:40–46 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

Before this passage, Yahweh explained many things that will happen to the Israelite people if the Israelites disobey Yahweh and do not return to obeying Yahweh after Yahweh punishes the Israelites. For more information on Yahweh and Israelites, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same words or phrases for Yahweh and Israelites as you used in previous passages.

Now Yahweh says that if the Israelite people admit their iniquities and their ancestors' iniquities, Yahweh will fulfill his covenant or binding agreement with their ancestors. You will remember that iniquity is the wrong things someone does over time that makes that person guilty. For more information on iniquity and covenant, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same words or phrases for iniquity and covenant as you used in previous passages.

But if the Israelite people admit that they betrayed and opposed Yahweh, which caused Yahweh to oppose the Israelites and send the Israelites to live in their enemies' land, Yahweh will fulfill his covenant with the Israelites' ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. For more information about Abraham, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same name for Abraham as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh says that Yahweh will remember his covenant with the Israelites' ancestors when the Israelites humble their uncircumcised hearts. In this passage, uncircumcised is a symbolic word that means that the people have not dedicated themselves to Yahweh. No one has actually circumcised the people's hearts. In the original language, the words for circumcised and uncircumcised are different words, but the ideas are similar. The circumcision Yahweh is talking about here is symbolic, and when Yahweh talks about the Israelites' hearts, Yahweh means the parts of the Israelites where the people make decisions. When Yahweh talks about uncircumcised hearts, Yahweh means that the Israelite people have not dedicated themselves to Yahweh, so the Israelites need to humble themselves and return to Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss as a group what words you will use for circumcision and heart. For more information on circumcision and heart, refer to the Master Glossary. Consider whether you should use a similar word or phrase for circumcision as you used in previous passages. Consider whether you should use the same word or phrase for heart as you used in previous passages. Pause this audio here.

When the Israelites do these things to turn back to Yahweh, Yahweh will remember or fulfill his covenant with Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham. Remember that in the original language, to say that Yahweh will remember his covenant does not mean that Yahweh at one time forgot the covenant. It means that Yahweh will fulfill the covenant and never forget it. Yahweh also says that Yahweh will remember the land. When Yahweh punishes the Israelites, the Israelites will leave the land so it can rest and experience the Sabbath years of rest Yahweh planned for the land. Remember that this is not just talking about the weekly Sabbath day of rest, but about the Sabbath year of rest that happened every seven years. For more information on Sabbath, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same word or phrase as you used for the Sabbath year of rest in previous passages.

Yahweh promises that even when the Israelite people are in their enemies' land, Yahweh will not reject the Israelites so much that Yahweh completely destroys the Israelites or that Yahweh breaks his covenant with the Israelites. Yahweh reminds the Israelites that Yahweh is the Israelites' God. For more information on God, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same word or phrase for God as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh ends by saying that Yahweh will not forget the covenant Yahweh made with the Israelites' ancestors. Yahweh does this so that people from other nations would see Yahweh rescue the Israelites. For more information on nations, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same word or phrase for nation as you used in previous passages.

At the end of the passage, the storyteller says that everything that came before was the statutes and ordinances and instructions or laws that Yahweh included in the agreement between Yahweh and the Israelite people. For more information about statute, ordinance, or law, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same words or phrases for statute, ordinance, and law as you used in previous passages. However, notice that these are not talking about three separate things. This is a way to talk about all of the things Yahweh has told the people of Israel to do to obey Yahweh. If having three different words for this in your language communicates that these are separate things, consider translating these ideas as one more general word or phrase that would include things like instructions, ordinances, and statutes. Yahweh told all these instructions to Moses on Mount Sinai.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 26:14–20
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 26:14–20 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:14–20 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:14–20 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

You remember in the previous passage how Yahweh said that if the Israelites follow Yahweh's instructions, Yahweh promised to give the Israelites rain and food. Yahweh promised to keep the Israelites safe from war and from wild animals. Yahweh promised to give the Israelites lots of children and victory over their enemies. And Yahweh promised that Yahweh himself would live with the Israelites. This passage talks about what will happen to the Israelites if the Israelites do not follow Yahweh's instructions.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Talk about a time that your parents punished you for not following their instructions. If you are a parent, talk about what happens when your child does not listen to what you tell your child to do. What do you do? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh tells the Israelites in this passage that if the Israelites do not listen to Yahweh's instructions and do the things Yahweh told the Israelites to do, then the Israelites are breaking Yahweh's covenant or special promise with the Israelites. This means that the Israelites are breaking their promise to Yahweh. Yahweh tells the Israelites that Yahweh will send the Israelites severe sickness and diseases that lead to death if the Israelites do not listen. Yahweh also says that the Israelites' enemies will eat the Israelites' crops and food before the Israelites get a chance to harvest. Yahweh will also send enemies to conquer the Israelites' land and rule the Israelites, and the Israelites will be afraid.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Talk about what happens in your culture when someone breaks a legal agreement or covenant with an important person. Think about a time when someone has broken a promise to you. How did you feel? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh continues his warning to the Israelites and tells the Israelites that if the Israelites still do not listen to Yahweh after Yahweh sends disease and war, then Yahweh will allow certain things to happen or give certain punishments so that the Israelites will obey. Yahweh does this much like a parent gives their children consequences when their children do not obey the parents. In fact, Yahweh says Yahweh will continue to discipline the Israelites over and over again as much as the Israelites need! The original language uses the special phrase "seven times" to describe this.

Stop here and discuss as a group: What did your parents do when you disobeyed your parents as a child? When your parents did those things, did you obey them? Why did your parents do this? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh tells the Israelites that Yahweh will set his face against the Israelites. In the cultures around the Israelites, when a god turned his face towards people, it meant the god was giving people blessings. The god would help the people. However, if a god turned his face away from the people, it meant the god was acting against those people. That god did not help the people and would also oppose or curse the people.

Stop here and discuss this as a group: What happens in your culture when someone important turns their face away from someone, or rejects and curses that person? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says Yahweh will help the Israelites become humble and weak by making the sky like iron and the earth like bronze. Iron and bronze are hard metals. Iron and bronze are impossible to break. This means Yahweh will stop the rain from coming and the ground from growing food.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of iron and bronze. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says the Israelites feel proud of their ability to take care of themselves by growing their own food. Yahweh says Yahweh will stop the ground's ability to grow food. This will make the Israelites remember the Israelites are not the ones who make the food grow. The Israelites will work in vain, or work and get no use out of it. Yahweh's purpose in doing this is to cause the Israelites to listen to Yahweh again and remember that Yahweh is the one who really makes the food grow for the Israelites.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:14–20 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has two scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites what will happen if the Israelites do not follow Yahweh's instructions. Yahweh says Yahweh will send diseases and war.

In the second scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites what will happen if the Israelites still do not follow Yahweh's instructions even after the deadly diseases and war. Yahweh says Yahweh will stop the sky from raining and the ground from growing food. Yahweh says he will give the Israelites as many punishments as the Israelites need to help the Israelites obey Yahweh again.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelites
  • And the enemies of the Israelites

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

In scene one, Yahweh uses special words to show that Yahweh is giving the Israelites a warning. Yahweh is still speaking to Moses, and Yahweh expects that Moses will give Yahweh's instructions to the Israelites. Yahweh tells Moses that if the Israelites do not listen to Yahweh's instructions and if the Israelites do not do all the things Yahweh told the Israelites to do, then Yahweh will send the Israelites deadly diseases and war. Yahweh makes a direct contrast in this passage with the good things that Yahweh has just told the Israelites that Yahweh will do for them. But if the Israelites do not obey Yahweh, then the opposite things will happen to the Israelites.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Think about how a parent might warn a child about what will happen if the child does not obey the parent. What words or tones of voice does the parent use? Have one participant act as a parent and another participant act as a child. Have the participant who acts as the parent give a warning to the child. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh uses similar words to say the same thing three times. Yahweh says, "If you do not listen and obey my commands, I will punish you." And Yahweh says, "If you reject my statutes, I will punish you." Yahweh then says, "If your soul hates my ordinances, or instructions, so much that you do not do what I said and break this covenant with me, I will punish you." In this culture, people often repeat ideas to show that something is important. Yahweh wants the Israelites to know how important this information is. Yahweh wants the Israelites to know how important it is that the Israelites should not disobey Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss as a group: What ways do people in your language say something is really important? Imagine that you want someone to know a piece of information really well. How would you say that information to that person? Pause this audio here.

When Yahweh is warning the Israelites, Yahweh uses the phrase "if your soul hates my ordinances." In the original language, this is a way to use emotional language to communicate the strength of the warning. "Soul" is a part of a person, but here soul refers to the whole person, just with more emphasis. The soul is the innermost part of a person. Yahweh uses the word "hate" to show that someone very strongly dislikes something. Hate is the opposite of love. In this culture, "hate" is both a strong negative emotion and what someone does when that person rejects something.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you can show the emotional strength of the original language here. What parts of the body do you use in your language to talk about the deepest part of a human? What words do you use in your language to talk about rejection and strong negative emotions? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says Yahweh will punish the Israelites if the Israelites do not follow Yahweh's instructions. Yahweh will send horrible diseases and fever that will kill the people. In the original language, Yahweh talks about the fever that wastes eyes and drains away life. The Israelites used eyes to talk about the whole person. Some people think this phrase is talking about physical and emotional suffering. Other people think that this sickness causes death. Either way, it is a horrible fever that causes a lot of suffering.

Stop here and discuss as a group what phrase you will use for the fever that puts an end to eyes and drains away life. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says the Israelites will plant seeds in the ground, but the Israelites' enemies will eat the food that grows from the Israelites' work. Yahweh tells the Israelites that Yahweh will set his face against the Israelites. In the cultures around the Israelites, when a god turned his face towards people, it meant the god was giving people blessings. The god would help the people. However, if a god turned his face away from the people, it meant the god was acting against the people. The god was not helping the people, and the god was opposing or cursing the people. Yahweh also says that the Israelites' enemies, those who hate the Israelites, will take over and rule the Israelites' land and people. Yahweh says the Israelites will be so scared that the Israelites will run away even when nobody is coming after the Israelites. Yahweh will give the Israelites all of these punishments if the Israelites do not listen to Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will talk about Yahweh setting his face against his people. Remember that Yahweh is rejecting and cursing the people when Yahweh turns his face away from the people. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh is saying that Yahweh will punish the Israelites if the Israelites do not listen to Yahweh. However, in scene two, Yahweh gives the Israelites a chance to change how the Israelites are acting and to listen to Yahweh again. Yahweh makes it clear that the whole purpose of the punishment is to help Yahweh's people begin to follow Yahweh again.

Stop here and discuss this as a group: How would you translate in your language the idea that Yahweh is punishing the people so that the people will want to obey Yahweh again? Pause the audio here.

Scene two begins with Yahweh hoping the people will obey Yahweh again. But if the people choose not to obey Yahweh after these punishments, Yahweh will continue to correct the people with more punishments. Yahweh says that Yahweh will discipline the Israelites as much as Yahweh needs to because the people have rejected Yahweh and not followed Yahweh's instructions. The original language uses the number seven to refer to this. Seven is the number of completeness. Yahweh will completely correct the Israelites.

Stop here and discuss this as a group: What numbers have special meaning in your language? What does the number seven represent? How will you translate the idea that Yahweh will punish the Israelites seven times more, which means to completely punish or correct the Israelites? Pause the audio here.

Yahweh then continues and says Yahweh will break the Israelites' pride. This is special language that means Yahweh will humble the Israelites in a forceful way. The Israelites were proud when the Israelites thought they could grow all of their own food and not need Yahweh's help. Yahweh will remind the Israelites that Yahweh is the one who grows the people's food.

Stop here and discuss this as a group: What kinds of things are people in your culture proud of? How do people in your culture think about or talk about growing food? Have you ever been proud to grow your own food? Pause the audio here.

When Yahweh says that Yahweh will break the pride of the Israelites' strength, Yahweh is using a harsh way to say how this humbling will happen. When someone breaks a dish, the edges are all jagged, and the dish does not work as a dish anymore. The original language uses the phrase "break the pride of their strength" to talk about Yahweh humbling Yahweh's people. It is also communicating the harsh way Yahweh will humble Yahweh's people.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for "break the pride of their strength." It is most likely that you will need to use different words than the original language has. Try to think of ways you could say both what Yahweh is doing and how Yahweh is doing it. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says Yahweh will make the sky like iron and the land like bronze. Iron and bronze are hard metals. Nothing can break these metals. This is special language that means that Yahweh is going to stop the rain from coming down from the sky and stop the ground from growing food. Yahweh says this is how Yahweh is going to break the Israelite's pride, or humble the Israelites. Yahweh will cause no fruit to grow on trees or vegetables to grow in the ground. Then the Israelites cannot say they are proud of growing food.

Stop here and discuss this as a group: What hard things in your culture do people talk about as the most hard thing? Pause this audio here.

Stop here and discuss as a group what special language you can use to talk about the sky being like iron and land being like bronze. Pause this audio here.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:14–20 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has two scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelites
  • And the enemies of the Israelites

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

Have the person playing Yahweh tell Moses these things: "This is very important. Remember this. In the future, if you decide to not follow the instructions I have given you, I will punish you with deadly diseases. In the future, if you choose to not follow these instructions, I will punish you with war. In the future, if your soul hates what I have told you to do, I will correct you with famine. You break our covenant when you do not follow these instructions."

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Moses, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am feeling so much care in my heart for the Israelites; or
  • I am feeling concerned for the future of the Israelites; or
  • I love the Israelites.
Continue the drama.

Have the person playing Yahweh continue to talk to Moses. Have the people playing the Israelites act out the different punishments. Yahweh says, "In the future, if you do not obey my instructions, I will send you horrible diseases that will kill you. I will punish you. I will let your enemies win wars against you. I will let the people who hate you rule your land and you. I will let you plant food, but not eat it. In fact, I will give your food to your enemies, and your enemies will eat the food. I will make you so scared in your land that you will run away even when nobody is running after you."

Pause the drama.

Ask the people playing the Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking when you hear Yahweh tell you this?" The people might answer things like:

  • We are feeling scared of what will happen to us if we do not obey Yahweh; or
  • We are feeling strong feelings of agreement with Yahweh; or
  • We are feeling like it is so important to listen to Yahweh.
Continue the drama.

Yahweh continues to say, "In the future, if all of those things happen, you can choose to obey me again, and I will stop the punishment. But if you keep disobeying my instructions, even after I sent you all those horrible punishments, I will keep correcting you. I will correct you as much as I need to until you listen to me. I will humble you. I will take your pride and break it. You are so proud of growing your own food. I will stop food from growing and rain from falling from the sky. I will make the sky as hard as iron and the ground as hard as bronze. You will not be able to grow food anymore."

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Moses, "What are you feeling or thinking when you say this to the Israelites?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am feeling sad that I have to say this; or
  • I am feeling concerned for my people; or
  • I love the Israelites so much and hope the Israelites will listen to Yahweh's warning.
Continue the drama.

Have the people playing the Israelites act like they feel humble.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:14–20 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

Yahweh says that if the Israelites will not obey Yahweh's commands, statutes, or ordinances, then Yahweh will punish the Israelites. In this passage, Yahweh wants the Israelites to know how serious and important this is. Yahweh uses three similar words that Yahweh repeats one after the other to create this importance. These words are commands, statutes, and ordinances. All of these words are referring to Yahweh's instructions that Yahweh gave the Israelites in previous passages.

Stop here and discuss as a group what words or phrases you will use for commands, statutes, and ordinances, and remember that these are similar words. Your language may not have three different words for these three similar types of instructions. Look up commandments, statutes, and ordinances in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated these words in this book, you may use the same words here. If your language creates emphasis through repetition, it may also be impactful in this passage to use the same word three times in a row here. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh warns the Israelites about what will happen if "your soul hates my ordinances." In the original language, this is a way to use emotional language to show how strongly Yahweh warns the Israelites. "Soul" is a part of a person, but here it refers to the whole person, just in a more emphasized way. The soul is the innermost, deepest part of a person. The word "hate" shows strong negative emotion. Hate is the opposite of love. In the original language, "hate" means both a strong negative emotion and shows when someone rejects someone or something else.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you can show the emotional strength of the original language here. Look up soul in the Master Glossary for more information. It might not be the best option here to use the same words you normally use to translate these terms. You could also say something like "you choose to reject my instructions." Discuss and decide if you need to pick different words or a different phrase. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh tells the Israelites that if the Israelites do not listen and obey Yahweh's instructions, then the Israelites are breaking Yahweh's covenant with the Israelites. A covenant is a promise or agreement between two people or groups of people. This covenant is legally binding, and both groups have to keep their promises. If one group breaks the covenant, there are serious consequences. For more information on the covenant, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same word or phrase for covenant as you used in previous passages.

When Yahweh tells the Israelites what will happen in the future if the Israelites do not obey, Yahweh says that Yahweh will send the wasting disease. This is a disease that makes a person so sick that the person either dies or their body becomes very weak.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for wasting disease. If you have already translated this phrase in Deuteronomy 28:22, use the same wording here. Pause this audio here.

When Yahweh tells the Israelites what will happen in the future if the Israelites do not obey, Yahweh says Yahweh will send the "fever that wastes eyes and drains away life." The Israelites used eyes to talk about the whole person. Some people think this phrase is talking about physical and emotional suffering. Other people think that this sickness causes death. Either way, it is a horrible fever that causes a lot of suffering.

Stop here and discuss as a group what phrase you will use for the fever that puts an end to eyes and drains away life. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that the Israelites will plant seeds, but the seeds will not grow plants. Use the same word for seeds that you have used previously, and refer to seed in the Master Glossary for more information.

When Yahweh continues to tell the Israelites what will happen in the future if the Israelites do not obey, even if Yahweh sends war and famine and disease, Yahweh says Yahweh will discipline or punish the Israelites seven times for their sin. The Hebrew word for discipline here means correction or teaching. People use this word in other parts of the Bible to describe how a parent punishes a child. The goal of this punishment is instruction or teaching. This word for sin is also the word that people used to describe when someone purposefully hurts someone else that person is close to.

Stop here and discuss as a group what words or phrases you will use for discipline and sin. Look up sin in the Master Glossary for more information. If you have already translated sin in this book, use the same word here. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that Yahweh will break the pride of their strength. The words "their strength" refer to the following sentences, where Yahweh explains that the Israelites take pride in their ability to grow their own food. When Yahweh uses the word "strength" to refer to the Israelites' ability to grow food, Yahweh shows two things at once. First, Yahweh shows that the Israelites believed that they could grow food on their own without help. And second, Yahweh shows that the Israelites put their trust in their own abilities rather than in Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss as a group how you will say that Yahweh will break the pride of the Israelites' strength. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says he will make the Israelite's "sky like iron" and "land like bronze." Yahweh is comparing the sky to iron and the land to bronze. Both bronze and iron are very strong metals that people cannot break. Yahweh is saying he will make the sky not produce rain and make the ground not produce food. Yahweh uses iron and bronze as symbols of what Yahweh means. This helps the Israelites understand through special language what Yahweh is going to do.

Stop here and discuss as a group what special language you can use for the sky like iron and land like bronze. Look at pictures of iron and bronze again as a group as needed. Look up bronze in the Master Glossary for more information.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.
