title: Leviticus 26:21–26
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 26:21–26 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:21–26 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:21–26 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

You remember in the previous section how Yahweh told the Israelites two things that would happen if the Israelites did not obey Yahweh's instructions. Yahweh said he would send war and disease first. Then the Israelites would have a chance to turn back to Yahweh and follow Yahweh's instructions. But if the Israelites did not, Yahweh told the Israelites that the second thing Yahweh would do to the Israelites was to punish the Israelites as much as was needed until Yahweh humbled the Israelites. Yahweh would even make the sky like iron and the ground like bronze, so that the Israelites could not grow food and be proud of their own strength. This passage continues with the third and fourth things Yahweh says he will do to the Israelites if the Israelites keep disobeying Yahweh even after Yahweh punishes the Israelites the first two times.

Yahweh tells the Israelites that if the Israelites still do not listen to Yahweh's instructions even after Yahweh punishes the Israelites the first two times, then the Israelites are actively opposing Yahweh. Yahweh says that Yahweh will give the Israelites even more punishments. Yahweh will continue to send punishments, or terrible things. Yahweh says Yahweh will send the Israelites wild animals to kill all of the Israelites' children and farm animals. This will make the Israelites' roads empty, so there will be no people on the roads. This is the third punishment.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Tell a story about a time when wild animals caused people to die. Pause this audio here.

Then Yahweh will give the Israelites another chance to change how the Israelites are living their lives and obey Yahweh's instructions. However, Yahweh says that if the Israelites do not accept Yahweh's discipline and change how they are acting, Yahweh will give the Israelites a fourth punishment. Yahweh says if the Israelites are still acting this way after the first three punishments, then the Israelites are actively fighting Yahweh. And Yahweh says that he himself will actively fight against the Israelites.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Tell a story about a group of people who are actively fighting against another group of people. What happens? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says Yahweh will fight the Israelites himself. Yahweh says he will strike the Israelites as many times as necessary because the Israelites have broken their agreement with Yahweh. The Israelites have betrayed Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Tell a story about a time a person close to you betrayed you. Tell another story about a time when someone broke a strong agreement. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says he will get revenge on the Israelites when Yahweh sends a plague and enemy armies against the Israelites. Yahweh says that because of this war, food will be so small that 10 women will bake bread in 1 oven. Normally, each family would have an oven to cook all their food in and would use the oven throughout the day. But during this time, 10 women will be able to share 1 oven, because the people will have so little food to cook. This means that 10 people will have to share 1 person's food. Everyone will always be hungry.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:21–26 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has two scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites the third thing that will happen if the Israelites continue to disobey Yahweh's instructions. Yahweh will send wild animals to kill the Israelites' children and animals.

In the second scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites the fourth thing that will happen to the Israelites if the Israelites continue to disobey Yahweh even after the first three punishments. Yahweh himself will fight the Israelites and send enemies of war who will take over the Israelites' land.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • And the Israelites

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

In this passage, Yahweh is still telling Moses how Yahweh will punish the Israelites if the Israelites do not follow Yahweh's instructions. Remember that these things have not happened yet to the Israelites.

In scene one, Yahweh says that after the first two punishments, if the Israelites continue to disobey Yahweh, then the Israelites are "walking in hostility with" or actively opposing Yahweh. "Walk in hostility with" is special language Yahweh uses to talk about a relationship. This is important. Yahweh created people to walk with Yahweh. Yahweh wants to walk with people. In other words, Yahweh wants to have a close relationship with people. Yahweh wants to live with people. Yahweh has made a special agreement with the Israelites, so Yahweh can walk with the Israelites. But in this warning, Yahweh says if the Israelites walk in hostility with Yahweh, then Yahweh will punish the Israelites like a parent punishes a child so the Israelites might change their minds and walk with Yahweh again.

Stop here and discuss as a group: What ways do people talk about close relationships in your language? Tell a story about a close relationship with one person who chose to hurt the other person. Pay attention to the language you use to talk about the close relationship before one person betrays the other person. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says if the Israelites actively oppose Yahweh after the first two punishments, Yahweh will punish the Israelites seven times for their sins and their betrayal. Yahweh will punish the Israelites by sending a plague, which in this passage means that Yahweh will judge or punish the Israelites with suffering that causes death and pain. The word "plague" means a judgment or punishment that causes death and pain.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Tell a story about a god that gives people punishments that cause death and pain. Pause this audio here.

People in the original language use the number "seven" to represent completeness or perfection. Yahweh will send a plague up to seven times. This means the plague will be the most horrible it can be.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Discuss how you might translate the ideas of plagues or punishments and the number seven that shows completeness in this passage. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh will send the Israelites a plague as the third punishment. Yahweh says this plague will cause death and pain. Yahweh will send wild animals to the Israelites. The wild animals will kill the Israelites' children. Yahweh says that Yahweh will make the people "childless," and the parents will feel pain because the parents have lost their children.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Imagine a parent loses their children. How might that parent feel? How would you talk about that feeling? Pause this audio here.

The wild animals will kill the children. The wild animals will also kill the farm animals. This plague will result in fewer people. Yahweh says that the roads will be empty. This is special language that shows that the wild animals will kill many people.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Imagine a village or town in your area that is full of people. Now imagine this same village or town with no people at all. How would you talk about this? Pause this audio here.

The second scene begins similarly to the first scene. Yahweh tells the Israelites that if the Israelites do not accept correction from Yahweh from the first three punishments, then Yahweh himself will fight against the Israelites with hostility or opposition.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Tell a story about a child who does not accept when their parents continue to discipline the child. Pay attention to the language you use to talk about the children who do not accept correction and the parents who keep disciplining the children. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh himself will strike the Israelites with a sword seven times because of the Israelites' sins. Seven times is special language that means as much as necessary. When Yahweh says he will strike with a sword, Yahweh means that Yahweh will send other people to kill the Israelites in war.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Discuss how your language might translate "seven times" in this passage. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says he will strike the Israelites as much as is necessary. Yahweh says Yahweh will bring with him a sword. In the original language, Yahweh describes this sword as a sword that "wants revenge for the covenant." You remember in the earlier passages that the Israelites made a covenant, or special promise, with Yahweh. In this passage, Yahweh is saying that Yahweh is going to fight the Israelites if the Israelites keep breaking this covenant. Yahweh will fight the Israelites with this sword that Yahweh calls "a sword that wants revenge for their betrayal." The sword is special language. People use swords to kill people. In this passage, Yahweh sends other people to start a war against the Israelites because the Israelites betrayed Yahweh. Yahweh will use a sword that will get revenge for the way the Israelites betrayed Yahweh. Yahweh will not literally use a sword, but will send other people with swords and weapons to attack the Israelites, because of how the Israelites broke Yahweh's covenant.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Discuss how you might translate the phrase "sword that wants revenge for the covenant" in this passage. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh says that this war will cause the Israelites to all be together in the cities, or towns. Yahweh will then send a plague in the middle of the Israelites. Many people think this plague is a terrible sickness that will weaken the Israelites to the point that the enemy can come in and capture the Israelites. Yahweh will use the war to cut off the food supply for the Israelites. The original language uses the word "bread" to talk about food in general. After the war makes it hard for people to get bread to eat, 10 women will bake bread in 1 oven because the women will not have much grain to make into bread, and it will not be enough food for everyone. The Israelites will eat but will still be hungry.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Tell a story about a time when war was happening, and the people did not have enough food. Pause this audio here.

The women will pass out the bread "by weight." In other words, the Israelites will have so little food that the Israelites will have to carefully split up the food and weigh it on a scale to give each person the same amount.

Stop here and discuss as a group: Imagine having so little food that you have to carefully split the food up, weigh it on a scale, and pass it out. Discuss how you might translate the phrase "pass out your bread by weight" in this passage. Pause this audio here.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:21–26 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has two scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • And the Israelites

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

Have the person playing Yahweh turn to the person playing Moses. Have the person playing Moses turn to the people playing the Israelites and say these things: "If you keep walking with me in hostility or opposition even after the first two punishments, I will send you a plague that will be as bad as it can be. If you continue to ignore me, if you do not want to listen to me, I will send you this plague. This plague is for your sins. This plague will be wild animals. I will send you wild animals. The wild animals will kill your children. The wild animals will kill your animals. The wild animals will make you have fewer people and will make your roads empty.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am feeling so sad in my heart for the Israelites; or
  • I am feeling frustrated that the Israelites are not coming back to me; or
  • I wish the Israelites would listen to me.
Continue the drama.

Have the people playing the Israelites act out grieving because they lost children.

Pause the drama.

Ask the people playing the Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am feeling so sad that my children and farm animals died; or
  • I am feeling angry at Yahweh for punishing us.
Continue the drama.

The person playing Yahweh says to Moses, "Continue to say these things to the Israelites:

'And after that, if you still do not listen to me, if you do not accept my correction from the first three punishments, then I will oppose you. I, Yahweh, will fight against you. I will strike you as much as is necessary for your sins. I will bring with me a sword that represents revenge for you breaking my covenant. This means I will send you war. I will send you war that will make you gather in your cities and towns. I will send a plague in the middle of you. I will send your enemies to fight you, and they will win. I will use the war to cut off your food. Then, after I cut off your food, it will be so bad that you will have 10 women baking bread in 1 oven. And when the women are dividing up the food, the women will split the food up by weighing it on a scale. People will pass the food out, but it will not be enough. You, the Israelites, will eat the food, and you will not be full. You will still be hungry.'"

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking when you say this?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am feeling sad that I have to say this; or
  • I am feeling concerned for my people; or
  • I love the Israelites so much and hope the people will listen to my warning.
Continue the drama.

Have the people playing the Israelites fall down to represent being hungry and dying from war.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking when you hear this?" The person might answer things like:

  • I imagine that this would feel horrible; or
  • I do not want to disobey Yahweh; or
  • I do not want this to happen.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:21–26 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

Yahweh says that if the Israelites keep disobeying Yahweh's instructions and refuse to obey Yahweh even after Yahweh has sent two punishments, then the Israelites are walking with Yahweh in hostility. Hostility is when a person is actively working against or fighting another person.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for hostility. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh will send a plague on the Israelites. A plague is something really bad that causes pain and death.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for plague. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh will send a plague because the Israelites have sinned, or betrayed Yahweh. For more information on sin, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same word or phrase for sin as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh will bring a sword that wants revenge for Yahweh's covenant with the Israelites. When you get revenge, you hurt a person because that person hurt you.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for revenge. Pause this audio here.

A covenant is a promise or agreement between two people or groups of people. This agreement or covenant is legally binding, and the people must not break it. If one group breaks the covenant, that person will experience serious consequences. For more information on the covenant, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same word or phrase for covenant as you used in previous passages.

The war Yahweh sends to the Israelites will make it so that the Israelites have no food to eat. Moses says 10 women will bake bread in 1 oven. Bread is a food that people make from grain. People sometimes use the word bread to represent food. An oven is the hot place people use to cook bread. Use the same word for bread and oven as you have used in previous passages.

Stop here as a group and together look at a picture of bread and ovens as needed.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 26:27–33
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 26:27–33 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:27–33 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:27–33 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In the last few passages, Yahweh has explained what will happen to the Israelite people if the Israelites obey Yahweh's commands and instructions and what will happen to the Israelite people if the Israelites do not obey Yahweh's commands and instructions.

In the previous two passages, Yahweh has talked about many things Yahweh will do to punish the people of Israel if the Israelites continue to disobey Yahweh's instructions. When Yahweh punishes the Israelites, the Israelites are supposed to turn back to Yahweh and start following Yahweh's instructions again. But if the Israelites do not obey Yahweh, Yahweh will keep punishing the Israelites. Each time Yahweh gives the Israelites another chance to obey Yahweh and the Israelites still refuse to turn back to Yahweh, Yahweh will give a worse punishment. Yahweh has described four punishments that Yahweh will give the Israelite people if the Israelites ignore Yahweh and continue to sin. Now, in this passage, Yahweh gives a fifth warning. In the future, if the Israelites do not pay attention to Yahweh's first four punishments, then Yahweh will punish the Israelites again.

Yahweh says that if the Israelites keep disobeying and opposing Yahweh even after the earlier punishments, Yahweh will be angry with the Israelites, and Yahweh will oppose the Israelites. Yahweh also says that at that time, Yahweh will punish the Israelites seven times worse than Yahweh has before that time. Since the number seven represents things that are finished and complete to the people of Israel, this means that Yahweh will punish the Israelites completely. It shows that the punishment will be very serious.

One of the punishments is that the people will be so hungry that the Israelites will eat the flesh of their children. Israelite people did not even eat animal blood, so the Israelites considered eating any human to be a horrible thing to do. But if the Israelites keep opposing Yahweh, the Israelites will be so hungry that the Israelites will do terrible things that the people never thought they would do.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Can you think of a true story from your culture or another culture you have heard of where people ate other people? What happened to cause the people to do that? How is that similar to or different from what will happen to the Israelite people? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh also says that Yahweh will destroy the high places where the people worship false gods. These high places were usually on top of hills, but not always. The high places would have altars and some kind of statue or object that people used to worship other gods.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What kinds of places can people go to in your culture to worship a god or spirit? Where do people in your culture make these places of worship? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh will destroy the altars where the Israelites offered incense to other gods. Yahweh will stack up the people's dead bodies on the dead bodies of the people's idols. This probably does not mean that Yahweh will literally stack bodies on top of the bodies of dead false gods. Instead, it means that Yahweh will kill so many Israelite people who worshiped false idols that someone could pile up their dead bodies. It is also a way for Yahweh to remind the Israelite people that these idols that people worship instead of Yahweh are not even alive, so the idols are no different from a dead body. Yahweh also says that Yahweh will hate the Israelite people and the Israelites will disgust Yahweh. This means Yahweh will no longer help or protect the Israelites like Yahweh did before. Yahweh will not be happy with the Israelites anymore.

Yahweh will also destroy the Israelites' cities and sanctuaries, or holy places. The holy places probably include the places where the Israelites worship false gods as well as the temple where the Israelites worship Yahweh. Yahweh will not accept the Israelites' offerings anymore either. Before, the smell of the offerings that the Israelite people sacrificed to Yahweh would make Yahweh happy, but now these offerings will not please Yahweh. Yahweh will ruin the Israelite people's land, and Yahweh will destroy the land completely. The enemies who take the Israelites' land over and move into the land will see what Yahweh did to the Israelites and their land, and it will surprise the enemies.

Finally, Yahweh says that Yahweh will scatter the Israelites among other nations. This means that Yahweh will cause the Israelites' enemies to force the Israelites to go far away from the Israelites' land. The Israelites will have to live in other countries. Yahweh will cause the Israelites' enemies to chase and attack the Israelites, so the Israelites will live in fear. Yahweh will destroy the Israelites' land and their cities.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:27–33 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has two scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells Moses that if the Israelites still do not obey Yahweh after all the ways Yahweh has punished the Israelites, then Yahweh will punish the Israelites even more strongly than before.

In the second scene: Yahweh tells Moses what will happen to the Israelite people when Yahweh punishes the Israelites.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelite people
  • And enemies of the Israelites

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

In this passage, Yahweh continues to give Moses instructions from Mount Sinai. Yahweh has told Moses what will happen to the Israelite people if the Israelites obey Yahweh. Yahweh has also just told Moses several things that will happen to the Israelites if the Israelites do not obey Yahweh. Yahweh has previously talked about four types of bad things that will happen to the Israelites if the Israelites keep disobeying Yahweh. Now, Yahweh talks about a fifth type of bad things that will happen to the Israelites if the Israelites do not turn back to Yahweh after the other four punishments. Remember that these things have not happened yet to the Israelites.

In the first scene of this passage, Yahweh describes the things that must happen before Yahweh punishes the Israelites the fifth time. The Israelites must first experience the first four punishments that Yahweh just told Moses about. The Israelites also must continue to not listen to Yahweh. The Israelites also must continue to oppose Yahweh. Yahweh will only punish the Israelites if the Israelites continue to oppose Yahweh, just as in the previous two passages. Each time, Yahweh says that Yahweh will only punish the Israelites again if the Israelites do not learn from the previous punishment. But if the Israelites still do not obey and still oppose Yahweh after Yahweh punishes the Israelites four times, then Yahweh will be very angry. Yahweh will punish the Israelites with an even more serious punishment than Yahweh did before.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: When you have asked someone to do something, and that person still has not done what you asked, even though a long time has passed, how do you say that the person still has not obeyed? How do you say that the person has not obeyed if you have reminded the person many times what you asked that person to do? Pause this audio here.

In the second scene of this passage, Yahweh explains to Moses what those punishments will be. Yahweh will cause the Israelite people to be so hungry that the Israelites will eat their own children to try to survive. Yahweh will destroy the altars and everything else on the high places where people worship false gods. Yahweh will kill many Israelite people who worship these false gods who are not even alive. When Yahweh talks about killing the Israelite people who worship false gods, Yahweh says that he will pile the dead bodies of the Israelites on top of the dead bodies of the people's idols. Yahweh compares the bodies of the people Yahweh will kill to the idols, which were never alive.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do you talk about dead bodies? How do you talk about things that were never alive? Discuss how you want to translate Yahweh's words. Can you use the same word or phrase to talk about people's dead bodies and idols that are not alive? Will it be clearer to use different words or phrases to talk about people's dead bodies and idols' bodies? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh even says he will hate the Israelite people. Yahweh then says Yahweh will destroy the Israelites' cities and sanctuaries or holy places, and that Yahweh will not accept the Israelite people's sacrifices anymore. Yahweh talks about this by saying that Yahweh will not smell the Israelites' pleasing aromas anymore. When the Israelites make sacrifices and give offerings to Yahweh, the smell from the sacrifices and offerings makes Yahweh happy. But now Yahweh says that Yahweh will not smell these things anymore. The sacrifices and offerings will not make Yahweh happy, because the Israelite people do not obey Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss this as a group: Decide how you will talk about how Yahweh will not accept the Israelites' sacrifices and offerings anymore in your translation. How will you talk about the pleasing aromas? Do you also need to explain that the aromas are from the sacrifices and offerings? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh will destroy the land by causing the land to be empty and without people. This will greatly surprise the enemies who take over the Israelites' land. When Yahweh says this, Yahweh emphasizes that Yahweh is the one who will do this.

Stop here and discuss this as a group: Think about something you have done recently. If you want to emphasize that you were the one who did that thing, and nobody else was the one who did it, how do you talk about that? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh then says that Yahweh will force the Israelite people away from their land to go live in many other countries, and that Yahweh will cause the Israelites to experience war. When Yahweh talks about this, Yahweh uses special language. Yahweh says that Yahweh will take out his sword and chase the Israelites. Swords represent war in general, so Yahweh will cause war, which will harm the Israelites.

Stop here and discuss this as a group: How will you translate this special language? How do people in your culture talk about war in general? How would people talk about God causing war? Pause this audio here.

Finally, Yahweh reminds the Israelites that Yahweh will destroy the Israelites' land and cities, so that their cities are just ruins or piles of rubble where people cannot live.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:27–33 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has two scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelite people
  • And enemies of the Israelites

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

This passage talks about some very horrible punishments that Yahweh may punish the Israelites with in the future. As you act out this passage, remember that in the story of Leviticus, these punishments have not happened yet. You may not be able to fully act out everything that happens in this passage without doing something offensive, so make sure that everyone in your group is comfortable with how you act out this passage. You may need to talk about how you would act out certain actions instead of actually acting them out.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

For the first scene, have the person playing Yahweh talk to the person playing Moses. Have Yahweh say that Yahweh wants the Israelites to listen to Yahweh and to stop opposing Yahweh. Yahweh wants the Israelites to obey Yahweh after Yahweh punishes the Israelites with all the punishments Yahweh talked about in the previous two passages. If the Israelites do not obey Yahweh after all these punishments, Yahweh will be angry with the Israelites. And this time, Yahweh will punish the Israelites very seriously, with a very complete set of punishments.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Moses, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am afraid of the punishments Yahweh says he will do to the Israelite people; or
  • I have been frustrated that the Israelite people have disobeyed Yahweh so much in the past. I know the Israelites will disobey Yahweh again, because the Israelites do not trust Yahweh as they should; or
  • I am sad that the Israelite people may someday suffer like this because the Israelites disobey Yahweh.
Continue the drama.

For the second scene, have the people playing Yahweh, the Israelite people, and the enemies of the Israelites act out or discuss what Yahweh says Yahweh will do to the Israelite people when Yahweh punishes the Israelites. When Yahweh punishes the Israelites, the Israelite people will starve so badly that the Israelites will eat their own children. Yahweh will destroy the altars and everything else the Israelites use to worship false gods on the places of worship on hilltops. Yahweh will kill many Israelite people who worship these false gods because these false gods are not even alive. Yahweh will hate the Israelite people.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the Israelite people, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I hope that we will turn back to Yahweh before Yahweh punishes us in this way; or
  • I wonder if Yahweh will really punish us as badly as Yahweh says; or
  • These punishments sound so bad! We really need to obey Yahweh so this does not happen!
Continue the drama.

Yahweh will destroy Israelite cities and sanctuaries or holy places. When Israelite people try to make sacrifices to Yahweh, Yahweh will not accept those sacrifices. Yahweh will destroy the Israelite people's land so completely that it will horrify the enemies who come and take over the Israelites' land.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the enemies of the Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • What the Israelites are going through is so awful that even I am sad for the Israelites, even though we are enemies; or
  • I am happy to see the Israelites suffer, but I am surprised how badly the Israelites are suffering; or
  • I am afraid of the Israelite's God, who is making the Israelites suffer so much.
Continue the drama.

Lastly, Yahweh will force the Israelite people to leave their land to go live in many other countries, and Yahweh will cause the Israelites to be at war with their enemies. Through this, Yahweh will totally destroy the Israelite people's land and cities.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:27–33 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

In the previous two passages, Yahweh has talked about four ways Yahweh will punish the Israelite people if the Israelites continue to disobey Yahweh's instructions. For more information on Yahweh and Israelite, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same words or phrases for Yahweh and Israelite as you used in previous passages.

If the Israelite people still do not turn back to Yahweh, Yahweh will keep punishing the Israelites. In this passage, Yahweh talks about the fifth group of things Yahweh will do to punish the people of Israel if the Israelites continue to disobey Yahweh.

Yahweh says that if the Israelite people keep sinning and opposing Yahweh even after the previous punishments, Yahweh will be angry with the Israelites, and Yahweh will oppose the Israelites with great anger. For more information on sin, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same word or phrase for sin as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh will punish the Israelites very seriously and completely. Yahweh will make the Israelite people so hungry that the Israelites will eat their own children to try and survive. Yahweh will destroy the high places on the mountains and hills where people worship false gods. High places were shrines that the people made, often on hills and mountains. People would usually put something like a sacred stone, pillar, tree, or a statue that people made to represent a false god. People would also put an altar there and use it to offer sacrifices to false gods.

Stop here and discuss as a group what word or phrase you will use for high place. If you have already translated this word in another book of the Bible, use the same word that you have used there. Pause this audio here.

Yahweh will destroy the altars where the Israelite people offer incense to false gods. For more information about altars, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same word or phrase for altar as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh will also kill so many people for worshiping other gods that it is like Yahweh will stack people's dead bodies on the dead bodies of their idols, the objects people use to worship false gods. For more information about idol, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same word or phrase for idol as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh will take out his sword to chase the Israelites. Use the same word or phrase for sword as you used in previous passages.

Yahweh also will hate the Israelite people, which means that Yahweh will no longer help or protect the Israelites like Yahweh did before. Yahweh will destroy the Israelites' cities and their sanctuaries or holy places. You will remember that this word for cities means any larger settlement that people put walls around to protect it. Use the same word for city and sanctuary as you used in previous passages. For more information about sanctuary, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh will not accept the Israelites' offerings anymore. Yahweh will ruin the Israelite people's land and destroy it so completely that it will horrify the enemies who take over and move into the land. Finally, Yahweh will force the Israelite people out of their land to go live in other nations, and Yahweh will make the Israelites experience war as Yahweh destroys the Israelites'land and cities. For more information about nations, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same word or phrase for nations as you used in previous passages.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 26:34–39
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 26:34–39 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:34–39 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:34–39 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In the previous few passages, Yahweh has explained what Yahweh will do to the Israelites if the Israelites do not obey Yahweh's instructions. In the previous passage, Yahweh explained what would happen to the Israelites if the Israelites continue to disobey Yahweh. Yahweh said that Yahweh will destroy the Israelites' land and cities and force the Israelites out of their land to go live in other countries. Now in this passage, Yahweh tells the Israelites what will happen to their land and to the Israelites who survive Yahweh's earlier punishments.

When Yahweh forces the Israelite people out of their land and into their enemies' lands, the land of Israel will be empty. The land will have no people to farm the land or live on the land. During that time, the land will rest and experience the years of Sabbath rest it should have had before. Remember that in Leviticus 25:4, Yahweh told Moses that every seven years, the Israelite people were supposed to let the land rest for a year instead of farming on the land. But if the Israelites do not let the land rest for the Sabbath year, Yahweh will punish the Israelites. When Yahweh finally punishes the Israelites completely, Yahweh will remove the people from the land so that the land can finally catch up on its rest.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: How long do farmers in your culture farm in the same place without taking a break? Do farmers change the fields they plant in or plant different crops in different years? If yes, why do you think farmers do that? If not, why do you think farmers do not do that? Pause this audio here.

Then Yahweh talks about what will happen to the Israelites who survive the destruction of their cities and land. Yahweh will send these survivors away from their land into other countries. When the Israelite survivors are in the lands of their enemies, Yahweh will make the Israelites survivors so afraid that they will run away when they hear the sound of a leaf blowing in the wind. This just means that the Israelites will be so afraid that even small and safe things like the sound of moving leaves will make the Israelites run away. The Israelites will run from these small things just like the Israelites would run from someone who chases the Israelites with a sword to kill the Israelites. Even though no one is actually chasing the Israelites, the Israelites will die anyway. In fact, the Israelites will be so afraid that the Israelites will run into each other and trip over each other, even though the Israelites are not running from anyone. All of this is probably special language that shows how afraid the Israelite people will be. The Israelites may or may not literally run when the Israelites are afraid and trip over each other. The point of this special language is that the Israelites will panic and try to get away from enemies who do not even exist. Also, the Israelites will hurt each other as the Israelites panic and try to escape death. Since the Israelites will be running even when the Israelites do not have real enemies, the Israelites definitely will not be able to defend themselves against real enemies, who will defeat the Israelites.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: Think of a time when you were so scared that you were afraid of things that were not even dangerous. If you cannot think of a personal story, think of a time when someone in your community was so scared that the person was afraid of things that were not even dangerous. How do you talk about someone who is very afraid like this? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh then says that the Israelite people will die in foreign countries, and the Israelites' enemies' land will eat the Israelites. Yahweh may mean that the Israelites will just die in foreign countries. On the other hand, Yahweh may mean that the Israelites will not only die in foreign countries, but people will bury the Israelites' bodies there too.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: What do people in your community do with their dead people? What do people do to take care of the dead bodies, and where do people put the dead bodies? Now imagine that one of the people in your community died in a foreign country. What do you think would happen to their body? How would people in your community feel about that? Pause this audio here.

Finally, Yahweh says that the lives of the Israelites who survive all of this will become worse and worse as the Israelites live in their enemies' lands. This will make the Israelites feel like the Israelites are decaying.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:34–39 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has two scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh talks about what will happen to the land of Israel while the Israelite people are living in their enemies' lands.

In the second scene: Yahweh talks about what will happen to the Israelite people while the Israelite people are living in their enemies' lands.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelite people
  • And the enemies of the Israelite people.

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

Yahweh is still talking to Moses on Mount Sinai, and Yahweh has been telling Moses what will happen to the Israelites if the Israelites disobey Yahweh and do not pay attention to Yahweh's punishments. Yahweh will force the Israelites out of their land to live as exiles in their enemies' lands. Remember that the things Yahweh describes in this passage have not happened to the Israelites yet. These are things that will happen if the Israelites disobey Yahweh.

Now, in the first scene of this passage, Yahweh tells Moses what will happen to the land of Israel if Yahweh forces the Israelites to leave. There will be no one to farm the land or live in the land, so the land will rest during that time. The Israelites should let the land rest for a year every seven years, just like Yahweh told the Israelites to do in Yahweh's instructions about the Sabbath year. But if the Israelites do not let the land rest, Yahweh will remove the Israelites from their land so the land can finally rest. In this passage, Yahweh talks about the land as if it were a person who can rest. Yahweh also says in several ways that the land will rest and experience its Sabbath while the Israelites are in their enemies' lands. Yahweh talks about the land's Sabbath in several ways to emphasize that it is important for the Israelites to obey Yahweh's instructions. The Israelites need to take care of the land by following Yahweh's instructions about the Sabbath year. Otherwise, Yahweh will have to take care of the land by punishing the Israelites.

Stop here and discuss this as a group: Think of a story in your culture where a place, object, animal, or something else that is not human does something that usually only a human would do. Why do you think the storyteller talks about this thing like it is a person? Pause this audio here.

Then, in the second scene of the passage, Yahweh tells Moses about what will happen to the surviving Israelites. These are the Israelite people who are still alive after people destroy the Israelites' cities and their land. Yahweh will send these surviving Israelites away from their land to live in their enemies' lands. Yahweh will make the Israelites so afraid that the Israelites will panic because of small and unimportant things and try to get away from enemies who do not even exist. Yahweh says that the Israelites will run away like they are running away from someone attacking the Israelites with a sword. The sword represents weapons in general, and you can translate this the same way you translated it in previous passages. The Israelites will stumble over each other like people who are panicking as they run away from a dangerous thing.

The Israelites will also be so afraid that the Israelites will not be able to stand up in front of real enemies. This is special language that means that the Israelites will not be able to defend themselves against their enemies, who will defeat the Israelites. In the foreign countries that the Israelites will have to live in, the Israelite people will die in foreign countries, and people will bury the Israelites there. The Israelites who do not die yet will have worse and worse lives in their enemies' lands, so the Israelites will feel like they are decaying. This will happen because of the Israelites' iniquity. In other words, the Israelites have continued to disobey Yahweh, and now the Israelites are guilty. The Israelites' ancestors were also guilty because the ancestors disobeyed Yahweh.

Stop here and discuss this as a group: How will you talk about the land in this passage? At the beginning, Yahweh talks about the Israelites' land resting. Now Yahweh talks about the enemy land devouring or eating the Israelites, which symbolizes people burying the Israelites in the enemy land. Is there a way in your language to talk about land doing human things? How else can you emphasize in your translation that Yahweh cares about the land as well as about people? Pause this audio here.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:34–39 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has two scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelite people
  • And the enemies of the Israelite people.

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

Before this story, Yahweh told Moses some things that are important to this story. Before you act out this story, have the person playing Yahweh tell the person playing Moses that when the Israelite people keep refusing to obey Yahweh, even after Yahweh punishes the Israelites, then Yahweh will force the Israelites out of their land to go live in their enemies' land. Also, have the person playing Yahweh tell the person playing Moses that every seven years, the Israelites are supposed to let their land rest for one year during the Sabbath year of rest. But Yahweh describes what will happen if the Israelites do not obey. You can choose an area to represent the land of Israel, and have the people playing the Israelites act out farming and working in that land during the Sabbath year instead of letting the land rest. To represent the Israelites not obeying, you may choose an area to represent other lands. Have the person playing Yahweh tell the person playing the enemies to force the people playing the Israelites to leave the land of Israel and go to the other lands. Now, have the person playing the enemies act out how the enemies force the people playing the Israelites out of the Israelites' land.

Now, for the first scene of this passage, have the person playing Yahweh tell the person playing Moses what will happen to the land of Israel while the Israelite people are in other lands. No one will farm the land or live in the land, so the land will rest. Have the people playing the Israelites stay away from the area that represents the land of Israel so the land can rest.

Pause the drama.

Ask the people playing the Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I regret not obeying Yahweh about letting the land rest; or
  • I am sad that it was bad for the land for my people to live there; or
  • I miss my land and want to go back.
Continue the drama.

Then, for the second scene in this passage, have the person playing Yahweh tell the person playing Moses what Yahweh will do to the Israelite people. Have the people playing the Israelites act out what will happen to the Israelites. Yahweh will make the Israelites so afraid that the Israelites will panic over small things like quiet noises and run away, even though no enemies are chasing the Israelites. The Israelites will also hurt each other as they try to run away from their enemies, so have the people playing the Israelites pretend to run into each other and fall over.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am upset that I need to punish the Israelites, but I want the Israelites to turn back to me; or
  • I am sad that my people are so afraid; or
  • I am willing to punish my people because I know that I will bring the Israelites back into a relationship with me.
Continue the drama.

The Israelites will not be able to defend themselves against their enemies, so have the person playing the enemies pretend to fight the people playing the Israelites, and have the enemies win. The Israelite people will die in foreign countries, and people will bury the Israelites there, so have one of the people playing the Israelites pretend to die, and have the other person playing the Israelites act out burying the dead person. The people who do not die yet will have worse and worse lives in their enemies' lands, so have the remaining Israelites act out being sad in the enemies' lands. All this will happen because of the Israelites' and their ancestors' guilt. Have the people playing the Israelites act out how they realize that they are guilty because the Israelites have disobeyed Yahweh.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing the remaining Israelites, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am upset that Yahweh is letting our enemies defeat us; or
  • I am grieving for my fellow Israelites who are dying in our enemies' lands. We cannot bury these people with honor in our ancestors' graves; or
  • I am sad because my life here in my enemies' land is terrible. Our enemies are cruel to us, and I miss my home.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 26:34–39 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

In the last few passages, Yahweh has explained how Yahweh will punish the Israelite people if the Israelites keep disobeying Yahweh after Yahweh punishes the Israelites. For more information on Yahweh or Israelites, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same words or phrases for Yahweh and Israelite as you used in previous passages.

One of the punishments is that Yahweh will force the Israelites out of their land and into their enemies' lands. Then the land of Israel will be empty, and there will be no people to farm the land or live in the land. For more information on Israel, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same word or phrase for Israel as you used in previous passages.

During that time, the land will rest and experience the years of Sabbath rest it should have had before. So when Yahweh removes the people from the land, the land can finally catch up on its rest. For more information about Sabbath, refer to the Master Glossary. For more information on the Sabbath year, you may also refer to Leviticus 25:4. Use the same word or phrase for Sabbath as you used in previous passages.

Then Yahweh talks about the Israelite people who survive when Yahweh punishes the Israelites. When the Israelites are in the lands of their enemies, Yahweh will make the Israelites so afraid that the Israelites will run away from even small things as if those things were trying to kill the Israelites. Yahweh says he will do this by bringing despair to the Israelites' hearts, which will make the Israelites afraid. For more information on heart, refer to the Master Glossary. You may use the same word or phrase for heart as you used in previous passages. Or, if there is a more natural way to talk about Yahweh making the Israelites very afraid that does not use the word or phrase for heart, you may use that word or phrase.

The Israelites will stumble over each other like people who are running away from a sword. If you use the word for sword in your translation to represent war or danger, use the same word for sword as you have used in previous passages.

The Israelite people will die in foreign countries among people from non-Israelite nations. People will bury the Israelites there, where the Israelites' enemies live. For more information on nations, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same word or phrase for nations as you used in previous passages.

And lastly, for the Israelite people who survive all of this, their lives will become worse and worse as the Israelites live in their enemies' lands, so the Israelites will feel like they are decaying. This will happen because of the iniquity of both the Israelites and the Israelites' ancestors. For more information on iniquity, refer to the Master Glossary. Use the same word or phrase for iniquity as you used in the previous passage.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.

title: Leviticus 27:1–8
content:
Hear and Heart

In this step, hear Leviticus 27:1–8 and put it in your hearts.

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 27:1–8 three times, in three different translations, if possible.

Pause this audio here.

Now, as a group, discuss the following questions:

  1. What do you like in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  2. What do you not like or not understand in this passage? Pause this audio here.
  3. What does this passage tell us about God? Pause this audio here.
  4. What does this passage tell us about people? Pause this audio here.
  5. How does this passage affect our daily lives? Pause this audio here.
  6. Who do you know who needs to hear this passage?

Setting the Stage

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 27:1–8 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this passage, Yahweh tells Moses to talk to the Israelites about vows. Remember that a person who makes a vow asks God to do something for that person and offers to do something in return. Sometimes people would offer to dedicate or give a person to Yahweh as part of their vow. A person may give themselves or another person in their household, such as a family member or a slave. The dedicated person would perhaps help the priests or Levites with jobs other than the ones that only priests or Levites can do.

Yahweh tells Moses how the Israelites can redeem or set free a dedicated person when the Israelites pay certain amounts of money. Then the dedicated person will no longer have to serve, while the person who made the vow still keeps the vow. It is also possible that Yahweh might mean that Yahweh will not allow the Israelites to give a person to Yahweh. Instead, when someone promises to give Yahweh a person in a vow, Yahweh wants the Israelites to pay a certain amount of money instead.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, when people desperately need something, how do those people ask gods or spirits for help? When are some times when people may promise to do something in exchange for help? Pause this audio here.

Stop here again and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, would a person ever dedicate themselves to God or a god or spirit? If people do this, is there ever a way to redeem that person or end the service in an honorable way? Pause this audio here.

Yahweh then tells the Israelites what the value for each person is, based on that person's age and whether they are a male or a female. A person needs to pay 50 shekels to pay for a male who is between 20 and 60 years old. A shekel was a unit of measurement that people used as money. A shekel was often a piece of silver that weighed a certain amount. Sometimes a shekel was in the form of a coin. Scholars do not know how much a shekel was worth. People may have earned about a shekel for two weeks of work. In that case, a person would earn 50 shekels in 100 weeks, or nearly 2 years. Sometimes, people used different weights for shekels, so the priests in the temple had a specific weight the priests used for shekels. Yahweh specifies that the shekels a person needs to use to pay for any human needed to weigh as much as priests in the holy place decided a shekel should weigh.

Stop here as a group and look at a picture of a shekel. Pause this audio here.

A person needs to pay 30 shekels to pay for a female who is between 20 and 60 years old. Yahweh probably tells the Israelites to pay less money for women because if the Israelites buy a woman as a slave, the Israelites pay less money. Yahweh does not think women are less valuable than men.

A person needs to pay 20 shekels to pay for a male who is between 5 and 20 years old. A person needs to pay 10 shekels to pay for a female who is between 5 and 20 years old. A person needs to pay 5 shekels to pay for a male who is between 1 month and 5 years old. A person needs to pay 3 shekels to pay for a female who is between 1 month and 5 years old. A person needs to pay 15 shekels to pay for a male who is older than 60 years old. A person needs to pay 10 shekels to pay for a female who is older than 60 years old. Yahweh probably had people pay less money for people who were older or younger because if the Israelites bought someone of that age as a slave, the Israelites would pay less money. Yahweh does not think old or young people are less valuable.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, what are some situations when a person would pay a worker a different amount for a job based on the worker's age or if they are male or female? Pause this audio here.

If a person who makes the vow cannot afford to pay the price for someone that they gave in a vow, then that person needs to bring the person that they gave in a vow to a priest. The priest will examine the person that someone gave in a vow and decide how much the person who made the vow needs to pay for the second person based on how much the first person can afford.

Defining the Scenes

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 27:1–8 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will define the scenes, characters, and setting of this passage. Then the group will visualize this passage.

This passage has two scenes.

In the first scene: Yahweh tells the Israelites how much money to pay for someone whom a person vowed to give to Yahweh.

In the second scene: Yahweh explains that if someone cannot afford to pay to get someone back, the priests can decide a lower price.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelites
  • A person making a vow
  • A man between 20 and 60 years old
  • A woman between 20 and 60 years old
  • A boy or a man between 5 and 20 years old
  • A girl or a woman between 5 and 20 years old
  • A boy between 1 month and 5 years old
  • A girl between 1 month and 5 years old
  • A man older than 60 years old
  • A woman older than 60 years old
  • A person who cannot afford to buy back someone the person vowed to give to Yahweh
  • And a priest

As a group, pay attention to these parts of the passage's setting:

In previous passages, Yahweh told Moses what the Israelites need to do so that the Israelites can prosper, and what Yahweh will do to the Israelites if the Israelites do not obey Yahweh. In this passage and the next few passages, Yahweh will talk about people or things that people might give to Yahweh.

In the first scene, Yahweh tells Moses to tell the Israelites how much money to give to Yahweh to redeem, or buy back, someone that a person vowed to give to Yahweh. The person who vowed to give someone to Yahweh will probably have to take the money to the priests at the tabernacle and give the money to the priest. Yahweh starts with people between 20 and 60 years old, because the Israelites considered that age range the most standard age range people talked about. Then Yahweh tells the Israelites what the Israelites need to pay for people who are younger than 20 who someone gave in a vow. Finally, Yahweh tells the Israelites what to pay for people who are older than 60.

Stop here and discuss this question as a group: In your culture, how do you group people by age? What is the best way for your language to order these groups of people? Pause this audio here.

A person needs to pay 50 shekels to pay for a male who is between 20 and 60 years old. A person needs to pay 30 shekels to pay for a female who is between 20 and 60 years old. A person needs to pay 20 shekels to pay for a male who is between 5 and 20 years old. A person needs to pay 10 shekels to pay for a female who is between 5 and 20 years old. A person needs to pay 5 shekels to pay for a male who is between 1 month and 5 years old. A person needs to pay 3 shekels to pay for a female who is between 1 month and 5 years old. A person needs to pay 15 shekels to pay for a male who is older than 60 years old. A person needs to pay 10 shekels to pay for a female who is older than 60 years old. Remember that a person may have earned about a shekel every two weeks for a regular job. This was a lot of money for someone to pay.

Stop here and do this activity as a group: Gather at least 50 small items or units of money. Practice this passage by giving the right amount of items for each age range and gender that Yahweh talks about. Pause this audio here.

In the second scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites what to do if the Israelites cannot afford to pay the amount of money Yahweh says to pay to buy back a person that an Israelite has vowed to dedicate to Yahweh. The Israelite who made the vow must take the person they want to give for the vow to a priest. The priest will then decide how much the Israelite needs to pay for the person the Israelite vowed to give to Yahweh, based on what the Israelite can afford.

Now, the group should storyboard, draw, or use objects to visualize the passage and the action in it.

Embodying the Text

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 27:1–8 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will dramatize the passage.

This passage has two scenes.

The characters in this passage are:

  • Yahweh
  • Moses
  • The Israelites
  • A person who makes a vow
  • A man between 20 and 60 years old
  • A woman between 20 and 60 years old
  • A boy or a man between 5 and 20 years old
  • A girl or a woman between 5 and 20 years old
  • A boy between 1 month and 5 years old
  • A girl between 1 month and 5 years old
  • A man older than 60 years old
  • A woman older than 60 years old
  • A person who cannot afford to buy back someone the person vowed to give to Yahweh
  • And a priest

As a group, act out the passage twice. You should act out the passage in your own language.

First, act out the passage without stopping. Pay attention to the dialogue, flow, plotline, and chronology of the passage. Make sure you do not skip acting out the difficult or important parts of the passage. Help each other remember every part of the passage.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage.

The group should act out this passage a second time. At certain points in the drama, pause the drama and ask the person playing the character, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person playing the character should answer what they would be feeling or thinking if they were that character. Then continue the drama.

Pause this audio here and act out the passage a second time.

The following is an example of the drama and possible responses.

In the first scene, Yahweh tells Moses to tell the Israelites how much money an Israelite needs to pay to buy back a person whom that Israelite gave to Yahweh in a vow.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing a person who makes a vow, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I was so grateful to Yahweh that I vowed to give my child to Yahweh; or
  • I really needed Yahweh's help, so I vowed to give my child to Yahweh; or
  • I am glad I can buy back the person I vowed to give to Yahweh; or
  • It is going to be really hard to afford to pay for the person I vowed to give to Yahweh; or
  • I know that I cannot really give someone to Yahweh, so I will pay this money instead.
Continue the drama.

A person needs to pay 50 shekels to pay for a male who is between 20 and 60 years old. A person needs to pay 30 shekels to pay for a female who is between 20 and 60 years old. A person needs to pay 20 shekels to pay for a male who is between 5 and 20 years old. A person needs to pay 10 shekels to pay for a female who is between 5 and 20 years old. A person needs to pay 5 shekels to pay for a male who is between 1 month and 5 years old. A person needs to pay 3 shekels to pay for a female who is between 1 month and 5 years old. A person needs to pay 15 shekels to pay for a male who is older than 60 years old. A person needs to pay 10 shekels to pay for a female who is older than 60 years old.

In the second scene, Yahweh tells the Israelites what to do if an Israelite cannot afford to pay the amount of money Yahweh tells the Israelites to pay. The person who made the vow must take the person they wanted to give for the vow to a priest. The priest will then decide how much the person needs to pay for the person they vowed to give to Yahweh. The priest decides based on what the first person can afford.

Pause the drama.

Ask the person playing a person who cannot afford to pay for someone that they vowed to give to Yahweh, "What are you feeling or thinking?" The person might answer things like:

  • I am glad I can pay for the person I vowed to give to Yahweh; or
  • I am poor, so I can only pay a little bit of money; or
  • Yahweh is so kind to make this easier on me.

Filling the Gaps

Listen to an audio version of Leviticus 27:1–8 in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this step, the group will discuss key terms and words in this passage.

In this passage, Yahweh talks to Moses. Yahweh is the personal name that the one true God gave to the Israelites to call God. Use the same words or phrases for Yahweh and Israelites as you used in previous passages. For more information on Yahweh and Israelites, refer to the Master Glossary.

Yahweh talks about when someone makes a vow to give Yahweh a person. A vow is a promise someone makes to someone, or so that the other person will do something for that person. Use the same word or phrase for vow as you used in previous passages. For more information on vow, refer to the Master Glossary.

A person has to pay using shekels. A shekel is a weight that people use to measure silver or gold. People used silver to pay for things, and people weighed the silver that people used to pay for things in shekels. Use the same word or phrase for shekel as you used in previous passages. For more information on shekel, refer to the Master Glossary.

The shekels need to weigh what the priests in the holy place, or sanctuary, say the shekels should weigh. The holy place was the place where people went when people wanted to make a sacrifice to Yahweh. Use the same word or phrase for holy place as you used in previous passages. For more information on holy place, refer to the Master Glossary.

If someone who vows to give a person to Yahweh cannot afford to buy the person back, the first person can take the person that he vowed to give to Yahweh to a priest. Priests were responsible for offering sacrifices to Yahweh on behalf of the people, and the priests also taught the people how to worship Yahweh. Use the same word or phrase for priest as you used in previous passages. For more information on priest, refer to the Master Glossary.

Speaking the Word

Listen to an audio version of the passage in the easiest-to-understand translation.

Pause this audio here.

In this session, retell the passage, as a group, in your own language.

First, the whole group should practice telling the passage in your own language. Remember to include the things you decided in previous steps, like chronology, words, phrases, emotions, or anything else you discussed.

One group member should tell a few sentences of the passage and pause. Another group member should tell the next part of the passage and pause. Do this until the group has retold the whole passage. The group members can correct each other in this step.

Pause this audio here.

Next, each member of the group should tell the whole passage without interruption at least one time. A group member can use random objects, motions, or their storyboard to help them remember the passage.

Pause this audio here.

Next, the group can decide whose version of the passage you like the most. You may decide that you liked the way one group member told one scene but you liked the way a different group member told another scene.

Pause this audio here.

Finally, the group can put together a final version of the passage that everyone agrees on. Each group member should practice telling this final version of the passage.
